jobs.title: Salesman
jobs.description:
tempo scan group (distribution division) membuka lowongan pekerjaan untuk posisi salesman penempatan di denpasar, bali. posisi ini bertugas untuk menangani penjualan produk distribusi di industri farmasi atau fmcg, mencapai target penjualan yang ditentukan perusahaan, serta bersedia melakukan mobilitas dinas di area bali.

pria, status single. pendidikan minimal s1. berpengalaman sebagai salesman di bidang farmasi atau fmcg. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi dan attitude yang baik. mampu bekerja mencapai target penjualan. bersedia melakukan dinas lapangan di wilayah bali. memiliki kendaraan roda dua pribadi serta sim c yang masih aktif.

jobs.title: Sales Internet Rakyat
jobs.description:
bertanggung jawab mempromosikan dan menjual produk layanan internet rakyat di wilayah kota dan kabupaten bandung. menjalin hubungan kerja sama yang baik dengan para calon pelanggan, memberikan layanan terbaik, serta memenuhi target penjualan yang ditentukan perusahaan. fasilitas mencakup gaji, komisi, dan bonus bulanan.

berusia antara 18 hingga 50 tahun. wajib memiliki kendaraan bermotor pribadi dan sim yang masih aktif. memiliki smartphone android untuk operasional kerja. memiliki pengalaman di bidang sales diutamakan, namun terbuka bagi pemula tanpa pengalaman.

jobs.title: Crew Outlet
jobs.description:
bosfa coffee & japanese food sedang mencari crew outlet untuk ditempatkan di meteseh, semarang. posisi ini bertanggung jawab dalam operasional harian outlet, termasuk persiapan makanan dan pelayanan pelanggan dengan jam kerja pukul 13.00 hingga 22.00.

pria atau wanita dengan rentang usia 18 hingga 35 tahun. kandidat harus jujur, ramah, disiplin, berkomitmen, dan bertanggung jawab. mampu bekerja secara mandiri maupun dalam tim, bersedia bekerja di bawah tekanan, tidak sedang menempuh pendidikan kuliah, serta bersedia terikat kontrak kerja selama 1 tahun. diutamakan bagi yang menyukai dunia masak-memasak dan memiliki kemauan untuk belajar.

jobs.title: Admin
jobs.description:
pt. trans indonesia superkoridor membuka posisi admin untuk penempatan kerja di sangatta, kutai timur. tugas utama mencakup tanggung jawab mengurus alat pemasaran dan keperluan kantor, menangani administrasi pemasaran, serta memberikan dukungan umum termasuk melakukan koordinasi lintas divisi sesuai kebutuhan perusahaan.

kandidat perempuan dengan usia maksimal 28 tahun. pendidikan minimal d3. memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. memiliki pengalaman kerja di bidang yang relevan. terampil dan mahir dalam mengoperasikan microsoft office.

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
kami mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk bergabung dengan tim kami. bertanggung jawab untuk meningkatkan penjualan dan mencapai target penjualan. melakukan analisis pasar dan kompetitor, serta membangun hubungan dengan merchant.

laki-laki/wanita usia maks 35 tahun, minimum pendidikan sma sederajat, memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, memiliki komunikasi skill yang baik, memiliki kendaraan roda dua, memiliki sim c aktif, pengalaman menjual mesin edc & akuisisi

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
bukuwarung sedang mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk melakukan akuisisi merchant dan penjualan mesin edc di berbagai wilayah di jawa tengah dan diy. posisi ini bertanggung jawab untuk memperluas jaringan merchant dengan dukungan gaji pokok, tunjangan pulsa dan transportasi, serta jaminan bpjs.

pria atau wanita dengan usia maksimal 35 tahun dan pendidikan minimal sma sederajat. kandidat wajib memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, serta memiliki kendaraan roda dua dan sim c aktif. pengalaman dalam menjual mesin edc dan akuisisi sangat diutamakan.

jobs.title: Sales
jobs.description:
pt pd tempo (tempo scan group divisi distribusi) membuka lowongan untuk posisi sales penempatan depok. bertanggung jawab mencapai target penjualan produk distribusi fmcg dan farmasi serta menjaga komunikasi dengan klien dan mitra dagang.

pendidikan minimal s1. pengalaman kerja minimal 3 tahun di perusahaan distribusi atau fmcg. mampu mencapai target penjualan yang ditetapkan. memiliki kendaraan bermotor roda dua dan sim c aktif. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia ditempatkan di depok.

bertanggung jawab mengelola toko online di shopee, mencakup upload produk serta kelola stok dan harga. menangani komunikasi dengan membalas pesan konsumen secara ramah, cepat, dan solutif. memproses pesanan masuk harian dan mengoordinasikan pengiriman barang. membantu optimasi fitur promosi di platform shopee seperti flash sale, voucher, campaign, dan iklan shopee.

wanita berusia maksimal 28 tahun. memiliki pengalaman dalam mengoperasikan shopee seller centre. terbiasa menggunakan canva atau aplikasi edit foto dasar menjadi nilai tambah. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, teliti, jujur, dan berorientasi pada pencapaian target penjualan.

jobs.description:
posisi sales executive di spx express bertanggung jawab untuk secara proaktif mencari peluang bisnis baru guna meningkatkan angka penjualan. anda akan berperan dalam membangun hubungan jangka panjang dengan klien, memastikan target penjualan tercapai, serta berkoordinasi dengan tim internal untuk memberikan layanan yang melampaui ekspektasi klien. selain itu, anda bertugas memantau tren pasar dan kompetitor untuk terus memperbarui strategi penjualan perusahaan.

jobs.title: Gestor/a de Casos de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG) - Guasdualito
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Gestor/a de Casos de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG)** altamente calificado con sede en **Guasdualito, Edo. Apure.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**:

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Gerencia de Protección de la base, el/la **Gestor/a de Casos de VBG** apoyará la implementación en terreno del componente de respuesta y atención a la Violencia Basada en Género (VBG) en el marco de las intervenciones humanitarias de DRC Venezuela. La persona seleccionada será responsable de brindar atención individualizada directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG y personas en riesgo bajo el modelo de **Gestión de Casos de VBG**, garantizando el cumplimiento de los principios rectores (enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, confidencialidad, seguridad, respeto y no discriminación).

Asimismo, integrará un enfoque diferencial de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), interseccionalidad y derechos humanos, asegurando el adecuado mapeo, articulación y derivación con servicios especializados (salud, legal, protección infantil, apoyo psicosocial) y actores institucionales locales (Consejos de Protección de NNA, Defensoría del Pueblo, Ministerio Público, Centros de Salud), contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de los entornos de protección comunitarios y a la calidad de la información del programa.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

- Implementar el ciclo completo del modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG (evaluación, plan de atención, seguimiento y cierre), brindando Primera Ayuda Psicológica bajo principios de estricta confidencialidad y consentimiento informado.
- Elaborar planes de seguridad individualizados junto con las personas sobrevivientes para mitigar sus factores de riesgo.
- Gestionar derivaciones seguras y oportunas a servicios especializados (atención médica/atención postexposición, asesoría legal, atención en salud mental y apoyo psicosocial y/o alojamiento).
- Mantener actualizado el mapeo local de actores y rutas de atención (CPNNA, Fiscalía, Defensorías, centros de salud, etc.).
- Facilitar sesiones comunitarias de sensibilización sobre prevención de VBG, derechos humanos y rutas de atención, promoviendo la inclusión de mujeres, niñas, personas con discapacidad y población OSIEGD.
- Registrar de manera oportuna, segura y confidencial la información de los casos en las plataformas internas (KoBo, bases de datos), garantizando la entrega de insumos mensuales para reportes programáticos y donantes.
- Garantizar la aplicación transversal de la Política de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), la Rendición de Cuentas (AAP), el enfoque de No Hacer Daño (Do No Harm) y los estándares de Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS).
- Participar en reuniones de seguimiento técnico, supervisión de casos y coordinación interinstitucional según los requerimientos operativos de la base.

**REQUISITOS, EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

**Educación:**

- Pregrado / Titulación universitaria en Ciencias Sociales, Salud o Humanidades (Psicología, Trabajo Social, Sociología, Orientación o áreas afines).

**Experiencia laboral:**

- **Mínimo dos (2) años** de experiencia práctica relevante en atención directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG, gestión de casos de VBG o implementación de programas de protección de género/apoyo psicosocial.
- Experiencia demostrable en el trabajo con comunidades en situación de vulnerabilidad, población en movilidad/migración, comunidades rurales, indígenas o personas OSIEGD.
- Mínimo un (1) año de experiencia en contextos humanitarios o de cooperación internacional (deseable en el contexto venezolano).

**Conocimientos técnicos:**

- Dominio del modelo de **Gestión de Casos de VBG** y de las Directrices del IASC para la integración de intervenciones contra la Violencia Basada en Género en la Acción Humanitaria.
- Conocimiento del marco normativo nacional venezolano (Ley Orgánica sobre el Derecho de las Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia, LOPNNA, entre otros) y de los servicios de atención institucionales y comunitarios.
- Manejo del enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, enfoque de derechos, interseccionalidad y diversidad (AGD).
- Conocimiento del contexto socio-humanitario específico de la base a la que postula (**Apure/Guasdualito, Zulia/Maracaibo, Zulia/ Sur del Lago o Sucre/Carúpano**).
- Manejo intermedio de herramientas ofimáticas (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint) y plataformas de recolección de datos (KoBoToolbox).

**Habilidades Personales:**

- Altas habilidades relacionales, comunicación asertiva, escucha activa, empatía y confidencialidad.
- Capacidad de resolución de conflictos y toma de decisiones en situaciones complejas.
- Capacidad de trabajo en equipo multidisciplinario y adaptabilidad al trabajo de campo/terreno en zonas de difícil acceso.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 22 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio aproximada:** Noviembre 2026

jobs.title: Republicado - Asistente de protección (género)
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados. Actualmente incorpora actividades en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Nariño y Norte de Santander.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

Bajo la supervisión de la Gerencia de Protección, apoyará la implementación de las acciones y actividades de transversalización del enfoque de género en el programa de acción contra minas (AMC) y educación en riesgo de minas (ERM). Apoyará la implementación en terreno de los objetivos de Protección dentro de los proyectos en curso de DRC, integrando un enfoque diferencial de edad, género y diversidad, e identificando acciones específicas para mitigar los riesgos de VBG y/o para evitar la perpetuación de patrones patriarcales en los territorios, así como para promover la integración del enfoque de género en todas las actividades. Participará de otras actividades de protección en el marco de las acciones conjuntas de la Unidad de Protección de DRC Nariño según sea requerido.

Desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes, actores institucionales y actores humanitarios, que permita facilitar y garantizar adecuadamente las actividades de Protección de DRC. También se destaca la importancia de tener habilidades para el trabajo en equipo.

Contribuirá a garantizar la calidad de la planificación, implementación y seguimiento de las actividades de protección en los municipios de intervención.

**Responsabilidades:**

•Implementar las acciones y actividades de transversalización del enfoque de género en los municipios de intervención de acuerdo con las metodologías desarrolladas, los procedimientos operativos estándar (SOP) y la política de edad, género y diversidad (AGDM) de DRC, bajo la coordinación de la Gerencia de protección y con el acompañamiento técnico del/la especialista del área y del/la oficial de protección (género).

•Garantizar la incorporación de los principios rectores de género y VBG en las actividades de ACM y ERM, bajo los cuales incorpore el enfoque diferencial, interseccional y de derechos humanos.

•Apoyar a la/el oficial de protección (género) en la elaboración y actualización del mapeo de actores y servicios disponibles, identificando nuevas ofertas de servicios, con el fin de garantizar el acceso a atención integral para los casos identificados.

•Apoyar a la/el oficial de protección (género) en los espacios de formación y capacitación del equipo de ACM/ERM de DRC.

• Implementar actividades de grupos de apoyo para víctimas directas e indirectas de Minas Antipersonal (MAP), Municiones Sin Explotar (MUSE) y Artefactos Explosivos Improvisados (AEI), promoviendo en estas actividades la rehabilitación emocional y psicológica de las personas, brindando primera ayuda psicológica cuando fuese necesario.

•Implementar acciones de prevención de VBG, a través de actividades de sensibilización sobre género, VBG y temáticas relacionadas, en los municipios de intervención.

•Acompañar círculos de mujeres en los territorios de intervención, orientados a promover la equidad de género y mitigar la reproducción de estereotipos de género asociados al trabajo de cuidado y a los roles de género tradicionales dentro del hogar, tomando como base el enfoque de las 3R (Reconocer, Reducir y Redistribuir) en las cargas de cuidado no remunerado.

•Mantener buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas y otros actores externos para apoyar y facilitar la implementación adecuada de las actividades.

•Recopilar y gestionar adecuadamente la información de las personas de interés, garantizando la confidencialidad, la protección de datos personales, el consentimiento informado (cuando aplique), y el registro oportuno y preciso en las bases de datos y sistemas de información de DRC, conforme a los procedimientos internos para el reporte de las actividades.

•Contribuir al desarrollo y la contextualización de metodologías, protocolos y herramientas técnicos, incluyendo metodologías para sesiones grupales, grupos de apoyo, círculos de mujeres, así como el material requerido para cada una de las actividades.

•Mantener una comunicación y coordinación constante con la/el oficial de protección (género), la Gerencia de Protección y el equipo técnico, para asegurar una planificación eficiente y garantizar la calidad y coherencia de las intervenciones de protección en los municipios de intervención, en línea con la estrategia general y los proyectos en curso o propuestos.

•Participar en la implementación de actividades generales de protección de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados y las necesidades identificadas.

•Participar activamente en las reuniones de equipo y en los espacios de seguimiento técnico con el/la especialista del área, así como en procesos de formación y retroalimentación, aportando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas para fortalecer la calidad de las acciones de ayuda legal y protección.

•Demás funciones asignadas que se consideren necesarias para la ejecución del cargo.

**Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo**

- Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
- Participar activamente en la conformación del COPASST – Comité de Convivencia Laboral –Brigadas de emergencia, así como las actividades que los mismos realicen.
- Cumplir con las normas reglamentos e instrucciones del SG SST.
- Informar oportunamente de los peligros y riesgos latentes con su sitio de trabajo.
- Asistir a las capacitaciones en SST definidas por el programa de capacitación del SG-SST.
- Velar por el mantenimiento del orden y aseo de su puesto y área de trabajo.
- Suministrar información clara, veraz y completa sobre su estado de salud.
- Reportar inmediatamente al área de SST y su jefe inmediato los accidentes de trabajo que se presenten, incidentes (casi Accidentes) y enfermedades diagnosticadas como laborales.
- Reportar al jefe inmediato la necesidad de tomar acciones correctivas o preventivas, que correspondan ante no conformidades reales o potenciales del proceso al cual pertenece.
- Participar en las actividades de capacitación, simulacros y las que sean programadas desde seguridad y salud en el trabajo
- Participar y contribuir con el cumplimiento de la política y los objetivos del SG-SST.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

• Mínimo un (1) año de experiencia en trabajo comunitario, trabajo social, derechos humanos, prevención de violencia basada en género, atención a personas en riesgo y sobrevivientes de VBG, trabajo con personas OSIEGD

• Conocimiento del contexto y la situación humanitaria del departamento de Nariño.

• Conocimiento en enfoques diferenciales (AGD) y trabajo con comunidades étnicas.

• Optimas habilidades en comunicación oral y escrita

• Optimas habilidades en MS Word y Excel

• Voluntad y habilidad de aprender

**Deseable:**

- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con refugiados, migrantes, desplazados internos, comunidades étnicas.
- Experiencia en primeros auxilios psicológicos y apoyo psico social.
- De carácter tranquilo y diplomático.
- Buen trabajo en equipo; habilidad para crear buen ambiente.
- Dominio de inglés es una ventaja

**Requisitos en términos de Formación Académica y conocimientos técnicos:**

- Pregrado con titulación en Ciencias Sociales y Educación (Trabajo Social, Psicología, Pedagogía, Licenciatura, Sociología y afines)

**Idiomas:**

• Castellano (obligatorio)

• Comprensión escrita de lenguaje inglés (es una ventaja)

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

• Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes

• Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación

• Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación

• Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad

• Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONG's a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Salario iniciando en $ 2.462.000 más Auxilio de Transporte según experiencia y competencias del candidato.
- Fecha de inicio: octubre 2026
- Tipo de contrato: Obra Labor
- Horario: Ciclos operativos de seis semanas de trabajo de lunes a sábados de 8:00 a 5:30 p.m., al final del ciclo operativo se disfruta de 2 semanas de descanso (esta información se ampliará en el proceso de entrevistas).
- Fecha de inicio: Octubre 2026
- Medicina Prepagada: al 100% para el trabajador.
- Alimentación: Servicio de alimentación en base.
- Alojamiento: Alojamiento compartido en base
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina principal Nariño donde inician y finalizan los ciclos operacionales, con disponibilidad de traslado por necesidad programática a los municipios del triángulo del telembi.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida

actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes:** 15 de noviembre a las 11:59 am Hora Local.

*¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!*

*En DRC creemos que la diversidad nos fortalece y que cada persona aporta talentos, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Promovemos un entorno de trabajo inclusivo donde todas las personas sean bienvenidas y valoradas por su talento, experiencia y potencial.*

*Invitamos a postularse a todas las personas que cumplan con el perfil del cargo, sin distinción de género, identidad o expresión de género, orientación sexual, edad, origen étnico o nacional, creencias, condición socioeconómica o cualquier otra característica que contribuya a la diversidad de nuestro equipo.*

***Nota: Esta vacante está sujeta a subordinación de fondos por parte del donante.***

***Nota 1:** El postulante que aplique a esta convocatoria autoriza a DRC a validar la información personal suministrada en la hoja de vida. Su identificación será comprobada en las bases de datos públicas y privadas con el uso exclusivo de convalidar la información, de acuerdo con nuestras políticas antifraude, lavado de activos y financiación del terrorismo.*

***Nota 2:** El/la postulante que de forma libre y voluntaria deseen hacer parte del proceso de selección para ocupar la posición de la presente convocatoria, deberán observar un estricto apego a las normas que apliquen para la materia (idoneidad en los títulos presentados, ejecución de pruebas de forma personal e individual y veracidad en la información) adhiriéndose a los manuales y Políticas anti fraude de DRC, so pena de declarar descalificado el postulante que incurra en cualquier irregularidad a juicio de la organización, aún por la mera sospecha, e incluso en posibles conductas de tipo penal conforme a la legislación colombiana.*

jobs.title: Network Development Associate-Asia Pacific
jobs.description:
**Location:** Nepal, Pakistan and Thailand

**Department:** Global Impact - Network Development

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Network Platform Manager

**Responsible for(Line managing):** N/A

**Grade:** Grade A or an equivalent based on the country of hire

**Contract Type:** Open-ended contract

## **About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives.

**About the Job**

The Network Development Associate based in the Asia Pacific region will play a key role in strengthening engagement, communication, and coordination across the HelpAge Global Network. This is an exciting opportunity to support a growing and strategically important area of work that helps connect members, amplify their voices, and enable collaboration across regions.

## **Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities**

**Network Engagement and support to the Network Platform (50%)**

- Working with the Network Platform Team, strengthen communication and coordination between HelpAge and network members, particularly across Asia Pacific, alongside the Regional Adviser and Thematic Advisers.
- Support and facilitate knowledge sharing, collaboration and peer learning across the network.
- Support the curation, management and updating of the HelpAge digital portal, providing administrative backend support and first line user support.
- Help organize and facilitate regional convenings, thematic sessions, webinars, peer learning events, and cross‑network exchanges.
- Support in the development of newsletters and additional communications content for network members and other stakeholders.
- Support member applications, onboarding, and induction processes.
- Maintain and frequently update overall documentation including, accurate member information and mailing lists on HelpAge CONNECT (Hosted by salesforce) and SharePoint.
- Support the coordination of Network Development Team meetings and provide other administrative support to the Regional Advisor and Network Development Team as needed.
- Support in tracking engagement and participation trends across the membership.

**Regional Network Engagement, Communications and Administrative Support for the Regional Adviser, Asia Pacific (50%)**

- Support communication and engagement with potential and existing network members across the region, helping maintain strong information flows between members, the Regional Adviser and cross organisational teams and the wider network.
- Participate in meetings and discussions with network members in the region, document meeting proceedings, provide logistical and administrative support for regional meetings, webinars, learning events and member engagements.
- Prepare and disseminate agendas, invitations, briefing materials and meeting notes, and maintain agreed records and documentation.
- Support communications, member liaison and event administration for regional initiatives, including Conferences.
- Collect and maintain member engagement data, feedback and participation information to support reporting, learning and continuous improvement.
- Coordinate translation and interpretation arrangements for regional communications and events where needed.
- Gather stories, case studies and learning content from network members and partners across the region
- Develop communications and visibility materials that strengthen member engagement and showcase network impact across the region, including ensuring up-to-date information in digital and website platforms.
- Maintain regional communications channels including social media pages and support knowledge sharing within the region and across the wider HelpAge network.
- Monitor and compile relevant national and regional developments to support the Asia Pacific Regional Adviser’s planning and reporting activities, and assist with the implementation of the regional communications and knowledge management plan.
- Share relevant funding opportunities with network members and maintain follow-up records, keeping the Regional Adviser and relevant colleagues informed.

## **Skills and experience required**

- At least 3–5 years of Experience supporting network coordination, member engagement, communications and administrative activities, ideally in international development, civil society, humanitarian or multi-stakeholder environments.
- Experience in supporting logistical planning and coordination of sub-regional, regional and global meetings, workshops, webinars, learning events and strategic convenings.
- Good IT skills and familiarity with digital collaboration, communication and data visualization tools.
- Strong written communication skills with the ability to produce clear, concise documents, including meeting minutes and action points.
- Experience supporting online events, webinars, virtual meetings and knowledge‑sharing processes.
- Basic design and editing skills; familiarity with Canva, WordPress and Mailchimp is desirable.
- Experience producing and supporting newsletters, digital communications and managing social media channels.
- Ability to draft and edit news updates, communication content and articles in English.
- Ability to troubleshoot basic digital platforms, connectivity or login issues during online meetings and events.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken). Proficiency in at least one relevant regional language is essential, depending on the location of the role. Additional languages spoken within the region will be considered an asset.
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work under pressure and meet deadlines.
- Strong organizational and time‑management skills.
- Good interpersonal skills and experience working in cross‑cultural settings.
- High level of discretion when handling sensitive information.
- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
- Cultural sensitivity and respect for diversity.

**Key Behavioural Competence**

Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Policies and Code of Conduct**

As a HelpAge International employee, you are expected to comply with all organisational policies and standards, and to conduct yourself in a manner consistent with our values at all times.

This includes, but is not limited to:

- Code of Conduct
- Safeguarding Policy and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Anti-Fraud and Bribery Policy
- Anti-Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy
- Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy
- Raising a Concern (Whistleblowing) Policy
- Social Media Policy

All staff are required to familiarise themselves with these policies, complete any mandatory training, and adhere to them throughout their employment with HelpAge International.
**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
- Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
- Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
- Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

jobs.title: Development Supervisor
jobs.description:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview**: The Development Supervisor leads corporate and community engagement efforts that generate financial contributions, sponsorships, in-kind resources, volunteer support, and long-term partnerships for IRC programs in Georgia and Florida. Reporting to the Development Director, this position develops and stewards’ relationships with businesses, civic and faith-based organizations, community leaders, and other supporters; advances local visibility and mission-aligned engagement; and translates these relationships into measurable fundraising and resource-development outcomes. The Supervisor directly supervises the Development Specialist and works collaboratively with program teams, local leadership, and IRC headquarters.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Corporate Partnerships, Sponsorships & Revenue Development**

- Identify, research, cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate and community prospects for cash gifts, sponsorships, workplace giving, matching gifts, cause-marketing partnerships, and other philanthropic support.
- Develop tailored sponsorship proposals and partnership opportunities for events, program priorities, and special initiatives; negotiate and fulfill approved partner benefits and recognition commitments.
- Build and support third-party fundraising opportunities led by businesses, civic organizations, community groups, and individual supporters; coordinate with the Development Director on approvals, messaging, and gift processing.
- Manage a defined portfolio of corporate and community relationships, maintain prospect pipelines and stewardship plans, and contribute to annual revenue and engagement goals established with the Development Director.
- Identify and refer major-gift, individual donor, corporate foundation, and institutional funding prospects to the Development Director and grants lead; collaborate on cultivation and introductions.

**Community Engagement, Advisory Council & External Representation**

- Manage, maintain, and expand relationships with faith-based organizations, civic groups, businesses, and community partners.
- Represent IRC Georgia and Florida at selected chambers, networking events, civic meetings, community forums, and presentations; proactively recommend engagements that support strategic visibility and resource development.
- Coordinate and help lead engagement of the IRC in Atlanta Economic Empowerment Advisory Council, including member cultivation, meeting preparation, partnership activation, and fundraising participation.
- Collaborate with leadership and program teams on mission-aligned community education and advocacy-related engagement, consistent with IRC policies and approved organizational positions.
- Work with Site Directors and program leads to coordinate event planning, partner orientations, and in-kind giving across Georgia and Florida.

**In-Kind Giving, Match & Volunteer Partnerships**

- Create and execute an in-kind acquisition strategy, from identifying needs and soliciting donors through stewardship, valuation, documentation, and outcome tracking.
- Work directly with program leads to identify priority client and program needs; coordinate drives and work with Supply Chain/Operations to track receipt, storage, and distribution in accordance with IRC and funder policies.
- Coordinate the office’s raising of Match support through eligible in-kind donations, volunteer time, and cash donations; prepare monthly Match Grant status reports and recommend strategies to address shortfalls.
- Lead the strategy and partner solicitation for seasonal and special-purpose giving drives, including Holiday Giving; oversee implementation with support from the Development Specialist and program/operations teams.
- Provide oversight and direction for volunteer engagement, including corporate group opportunities, while the Development Specialist supports recruitment, onboarding, scheduling, and day-to-day coordination.
- Administer AmeriCorps and fellowship partnerships across Georgia and Florida offices, including recruitment, onboarding, and funder reporting; confirm annual service-member targets and operational responsibilities with leadership.

**Campaigns, Events & Communications**

- Work with the Development Director and relevant headquarters/RAM teams to support annual and seasonal giving campaigns, including year-end, Give Miami Day, Georgia Gives Day, and other approved appeals.
- Work with the Development Director, Deputy Director of Programs, and Economic Empowerment Advisory Council to plan and execute Dinner Together and other fundraising events, with responsibility for sponsorship acquisition and partner engagement; event revenue goals are set annually with leadership.
- Plan and oversee donor-facing components of donation events, fundraising events, and partner activations, delegating event logistics to the Development Specialist as appropriate.
- Coordinate donor and partner communications, impact updates, testimonials, and stewardship materials with appropriate communications colleagues and headquarters teams; ensure accuracy, consent, and brand alignment.
- Coordinate with responsible communications staff to keep Georgia and Florida local web content and stories current, subject to IRC website governance and approvals.

**Data, Reporting, Collaboration & Supervision**

- Maintain accurate donor cultivation, solicitation, giving, and recognition records in Salesforce for cash and in-kind donors; analyze reports to inform donor moves and pipeline priorities.
- Track and report partnership activity, sponsorship revenue, in-kind support, eligible Match contributions, and other agreed-upon development metrics; prepare required partner and in-kind donor reports.
- Supervise, coach, prioritize work for, and evaluate the Development Specialist; establish clear division of responsibilities and support consistent volunteer, event, engagement, and data workflows.
- Collaborate with the Development Director and grants lead to identify funding opportunities and supply corporate/community introductions or partnership information for proposals.
- Liaise with IRC headquarters/RAM staff on national corporate, in-kind, and volunteer opportunities relevant to Georgia and Florida.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**: Bachelor’s degree in business and/or Communications or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field, fundraising, corporate partnerships, sponsorship sales, business development, community engagement, or related relationship-management work strongly preferred; prior supervisory or team-lead experience desirable. minimum of 2-5 years’ experience strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Demonstrated ability to solicit financial support, build persuasive sponsorship proposals, steward partners, and manage multiple prospects toward measurable results.
- Comfort with public speaking, external representation, cross-functional coordination, and supervising/delegating work.
- Experience with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), donor data quality, reporting, and pipeline tracking.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, hybrid work (3 days office) and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional domestic (non-local) travel required; up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate starting at $60,131.30/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Communications Officer (Graphic Design & Social Media)
jobs.description:
## **Job Specific Context**

UNOPS has signed an agreement with the United Nations to implement the activities for the United Nations Youth Office.

The United Nations Youth Office was established by General Assembly resolution 76/306 as a dedicated entity for youth affairs within the United Nations Secretariat. The Office leads system-wide coordination on youth, advances advocacy and policy coherence on youth issues, and promotes the meaningful engagement of young people in United Nations processes and decision-making.

Within the Office, the Partnerships, Communications and Advocacy Section leads strategic communications, public advocacy and external engagement to strengthen awareness of theOffice's mandate, amplify youth voices, support the implementation of key initiatives and partnerships, and promote youth participation across the United Nations system. The Section manages the Office's global communications portfolio, including strategic campaigns, digital communications, social media, multimedia storytelling, executive communications, editorial products, newsletters, events communications and media engagement.

## **Role Purpose**

As part of the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section, the Communications Officer will support the development of graphic design and social media management for the United Nations Youth Office. The role will support the development and implementation of the Office’s visual identity and digital communications, producing high-quality, engaging and accessible graphic design materials and social media content that advance its strategic priorities and flagship initiatives. The position will oversee the planning, creation and publication of content across the Office’s digital platforms and printed products, ensuring consistency in messaging, branding and visual presentation. Through creative direction, audience-focused storytelling and effective digital engagement, the Communications Officer will strengthen the visibility of the Office’s work, amplify youth voices and support the Office’s efforts to advance meaningful youth participation and engagement with the United Nations. The Communications Officer will monitor Social Media performance, align tactics and engage in strategic communications discussions.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

1\. Graphic Design and Visual Identity Development

- Support the development, refinement and consistent application of visual identities for the UN Youth Office and its flagship initiatives, campaigns and advocacy efforts.
- Develop and expand branding systems through the creation of visual concepts, illustrations, campaign branding, graphic design templates and merchandise designs.
- Produce high-quality, youth-friendly communication materials for digital and print platforms, including social media assets, presentations, publications, event signage and other communications products.
- Ensure visual communications are cohesive, engaging and aligned with the UN Youth Office’s communications strategy, established visual identities and target audiences.

2\. Social Media Management and Content Production

- Contribute to the planning and coordination of the UN Youth Office’s social media presence across platforms, maintaining oversight of content calendars, editorial priorities and publishing workflows.
- Provide support in content development and the timely preparation, review and publication of social media outputs, ensuring consistency in messaging, tone, visual identity and editorial standards.
- Develop and produce engaging, platform-appropriate social media content, combining graphic design, visual storytelling and written copy to communicate the Office’s priorities, initiatives and impact.
- Coordinate with and provide guidance to interns and other contributors on content development, copywriting, editorial standards and the preparation of social media materials, ensuring quality and consistency across channels.
- Support audience engagement and amplification efforts to strengthen the visibility of the UN Youth Office’s work and amplify youth voices, initiatives and perspectives.

3\. Campaign, Event and Advocacy Communications

- Facilitate coordination in visual and digital communications for the UN Youth Office’s flagship initiatives, global campaigns, major events and advocacy activities, ensuring alignment with communications objectives and campaign messaging.
- Support development of communications materials and social media content for key advocacy moments, including flagships on Youth Mental Health and Well-being, UN Youth Compass, Young Leaders for the SDGs, and others.
- Support communications planning and on-the-ground content production and coordination for major events, missions and engagements involving the Assistant Secretary-General for Youth Affairs, including capture and dissemination of content.
- Contribute to storytelling and digital outreach around the Office’s activities, highlighting youth leadership, meaningful youth participation, partnerships and results across relevant platforms.
- Support content production and publication to ensure timely and consistent coverage before, during and after major events and advocacy moments.4. Digital Communications Strategy and Audience Engagement
- Support the continuous refinement and implementation of the UN Youth Office’s digital communications approach, ensuring that content remains youth-friendly, relevant and tailored to the intended audiences and platforms.

4\. Digital Communications Strategy and Audience Engagement

- Support the continuous refinement and implementation of the UN Youth Office’s digital communications approach, ensuring that content remains youth-friendly, relevant and tailored to the intended audiences and platforms.
- Monitor social media trends, audience engagement patterns, emerging content formats and changes in platform features and algorithms to identify opportunities to strengthen the Office’s digital presence.
- Monitor performance, support in establishing key performance metrics and analyze traffic across channels.
- Provide input and implement improvements to social media content formats, publishing approaches and amplification strategies, particularly in support of major campaigns, events and advocacy priorities.
- Contribute to the development and application of effective digital storytelling and visual communications approaches that strengthen the visibility and reach of the UN Youth Office’s work among young people globally.

## **Education Requirements**

**Required**

- Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in information technology, communications, fine arts, social sciences, or any related field is required, with 2 years of relevant experience OR
- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in any of the above related fields with 0 years of relevant experience.

**Desired**

- A globally or nationally recognized professional certificate in graphic design is desired.

## **Experience Requirements**

**Required**

- Relevant experience is considered work in communications, graphic design or related fields.
- Demonstrated proficiency in the use of design software and programmes (eg. Adobe Suite, Canva, Figma, etc.) to create digital cards, gifs, icons, logos, charts, publications, etc.
- Previous experience developing content for major social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram,

jobs.title: Director of Operations (f/x/m) – Brussels – MSF Belgium
jobs.description:
## CONTEXT

As Director of Operations, you will provide strategic leadership for the operational portfolio of MSF Operational Centre Brussels (OCB), ensuring that interventions remain relevant, responsive and accountable to the people we assist. You will lead OCB’s operational response in complex and rapidly changing environments, steering priorities and allocating resources across countries and over multiple years in line with OCB’s Strategic Ambitions 2026–2031.

OCB has two Directors of Operations (DOs), who jointly oversee and manage operations currently spanning 35 countries, with an annual budget of €400 million. Working closely with your fellow Director of Operations, the Medical Director and the wider leadership team, you will bring together humanitarian analysis, medical priorities and operational capacity to enable access to care, deliver effective programmes with an oversight of operational risks and opportunities.

You directly report to the General Director of MSF OCB and are member of the OCB CODIR (*Comité des Directeurs*), thereby actively contributing to the broader delivery of OCB Strategic Ambitions and leadership of the organization.

Together with the other Directors of Operations, you provide strategic operational leadership for the MSF movement, as part of MSF’s RIOD and in the Medical Operational platform (platform of the Operations & Medical Directors). You also represent MSF in external fora to negotiate, advocate and enable donor trust.

Both Directors of Operations (DOs) lead the Operations Department of MSF OCB.

The department consists of six managerial and technical teams called Cells, each in charge of a portfolio of countries and an Emergency Team (E-Pool) for the management of highly volatile emergency interventions. These teams are in Brussels, Abidjan and Rio. They supervise, empower and support Country and Project Teams to deliver MSF OCB medical humanitarian action.

The department also includes the Security Risk Management Unit (SRMU) and teams working on transversal management functions, including operational monitoring, information and knowledge management, and duty of care. These functions are coordinated and implemented through delegated responsibilities and dedicated support structures, ensuring coherent operational management, institutional learning and support to decision-making.

The DOs and operations department colleagues have a critical role in championing wider aspects of the quality of our social mission including bearing witness, safeguarding, climate adaptation, diversity, equity and inclusion, empowering teams and optimally and ethically collecting and using our data.

The DOs jointly manage the department and ensure operational continuity. Each supervises designated teams and leads agreed dossiers covering OCB issues, the MSF movement and external stakeholders. Team assignments may shift between DOs to balance workload. Both DOs share accountability for the strategic direction, performance, resource allocation and adaptation of the overall OCB operational portfolio, regardless of their individual responsibilities.

At the time of publishing, there is an ongoing review on the review of OCB’s operations structure, leadership and governance to propose feasible adjustments that strengthen accountability, decision-making, emergency responsiveness, cross-department coordination and Movement-level engagement. In 2027, it is anticipated to have a Deputy Director of Operations joining the departmental leadership, and a plan to have one cell re-locate to Nairobi.

## MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

- Lead, together with the other DO, strategic decision-making across OCB’s global operational portfolio and define the multi-year operational vision, priorities and resource choices
- Lead, together with the other DO, the operational translation of OCB’s Strategic Ambitions 2026–2031 into clear priorities and resource choices, and steer the development, implementation and monitoring of the Strategic Priorities and OPS action plans with operational teams and relevant departments
- Define, elaborate and follow up operational and medical strategies with CODIR colleagues and operational leadership
- Steer OCB’s operational portfolio in line with its Strategic Ambitions and geographical focus, lead regular reviews of relevance, results and resource use to guide prioritisation, adaptation and resource allocation, and decide on exploratory projects and project openings, reorientations and closures within the agreed decision-making framework
- Oversee the annual operational budget approved by the Board of Directors and its follow-up, and decide on the allocation of funding and human resources in line with the Operations Department’s decision-making processes, multi-year and annual budgets, and human resources framework, while balancing planned operational investments, emergency response capacity and flexibility to respond to emerging humanitarian needs
- Manage, support, coach and evaluate the Operations Coordinators and Head of E-pool, ensuring effective leadership, strategic decision-making and accountability for their operational portfolios, and provide guidance or intervene at country level when required by major operational challenges or escalated decisions, while respecting the responsibilities delegated to Operations Coordinators
- Manage, support, coach and evaluate the Coordinator of the Security Risk Management Unit, and retain institutional responsibility and decision-making authority for security risk oversight across the operational portfolio, including final authority, with the General Director, over critical decisions concerning the continuation, suspension or withdrawal of teams operating in insecure environments
- Ensure, in close collaboration with the Security Risk Management Unit, strategic oversight of security policies and their implementation across operations, while differentiating the DO’s global decision-making authority, the Operations Coordinators’ accountability for day-to-day security management at country level and the SRMU’s technical advisory role
- Ensure that critical security decisions are informed by SRMU technical advice and supported by appropriate security risk assessments, mitigation measures and monitoring arrangements
- Manage, support, coach and evaluate the Operations Monitoring & Management Support Officer, Duty of Care Coordinator and future Deputy DO
- Ensure that the Operations Department has the organisational structure, management capacity, competencies and resources required to deliver its operational priorities, including identifying capability gaps and developing management and leadership capacity
- Ensure the implementation of Duty of Care, Safeguarding, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, and an anti-racist approach for all staff, with active support to reduce barriers for women in the workforce
- Ensure coherence between operational ambitions and OCB resource policies within the DO team, foster a cohesive, collaborative and supportive departmental culture, exchanges among cells and a horizontal peer culture, and lead strategic meetings with departments to strengthen interdepartmental cohesion and collaboration
- Ensure effective operational governance and management systems, including coherent operational planning, monitoring, review and decision-making processes, consistent implementation across operational teams and continuous improvement based on operational experience and organisational learning
- Support and follow up specific dossiers agreed within the DO team, and work on internal dossiers to enhance operational debate, interdepartmental collaboration and collective reflection within strategic platforms and departmental and cross-departmental meetings
- Contribute actively as a CODIR member and participate in regular meetings of the OCB Board of Directors, MSF Belgium and OCB partner sections
- Contribute, together with the other DO, as an active member of RIOD and MedOpDir, supporting the successful strategic leadership of these MSF platforms
- Represent OCB at internal and external meetings, on MSF international platforms and with the media

## REQUIREMENTS

**Education and Experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent professional experience
- Medical, para-medical profile and / or degrees in Public Health, Epidemiology is a strong asset
- Minimum 7 years of international experience with Médecins Sans Frontières in and across multiple countries of operations
- At least 5 years of senior management experience, including at country level (eg. Country Coordinator or Country Medical Coordinator) and headquarter levels

**Competencies**

- Excellent context and humanitarian analysis skills and proven security management
- Analytical and strategic thinking with demonstrated talent for identifying, and improving complex work processes and set-ups
- Demonstrated ability to manage complex operational portfolios & crisis situations, assess performance, prioritise investments and make strategic resource allocation decisions.
- Dynamic and proactive, problem-solving aptitude, creativity and initiative
- Strong communication skills (both oral and written) at various levels, for often non-experts (pedagogical skills)
- Strong ability to be an active team leader and player; to manage and organize teamwork, promoting trust and enthusiasm
- Demonstrated capacity to negotiate with different internal and external stakeholders
- Ability to remain effective and exercise sound judgement under pressure
- Adaptability across diverse operational contexts, cultures and working environments
- Demonstrable commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion and cross-cultural awareness
- Ability to lead organisational changes, strengthen management systems and foster organisational learning and continuous improvement
- Adherence to MSF principles and to our values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust, Empowerment
- All MSF staff are required to uphold MSF’s Behavioural Commitments and safeguarding principles, ensuring that their conduct reflects respect, integrity, accountability, and a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, and abuse of power. They must contribute to a safe and inclusive working environment and apply MSF’s “do no harm” principles in all interactions
- MSF’s position recognises safe abortion care is an essential medical act to save lives and reduce suffering, and all candidates must feel at ease to support this

**Languages**

- Proficiency in **English,** both written and spoken, is mandatory
- Other commonly used languages in MSF (French, Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese) are a strong asset

**Other**

- Willingness and availability to travel frequently; essential mobility between headquarters and project locations, including travel to partner sections and other Operational Centres

## CONDITIONS

- Expected start date: **10th of May 2027**
- Location: **Brussels** (Belgium)
- Mobility: up to 30% in different contexts of intervention
- Type of contract: Open-ended contract with a **4-year mandate (extendable for max. 2 more years)** – Full-time
- Salary according to OCB Head Office salary grid
- Meal Vouchers – Hospital Insurance – Pension Plan – 100% reimbursement for public transportation costs

Deadline for applications: **1st of December 2026**

jobs.title: Cell 1 Intern
jobs.description:
## Join MSF OCG as a Cell 1 Intern!

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 9 months at 100%

### Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

### Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

At MSF OCG, field operations are supported by multidisciplinary teams based in Geneva, known as operational cells. These teams provide operational support to field missions and facilitate coordination with the different departments at headquarters. Cell 1 now supports operations in Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Eswatini.

As part of the HR function's evolution towards a more strategic partnership with operations, the Cell Intern supports the Operational HR Partner (HROP) by taking on specific delegated HR activities and files. The intern acts as a focal point for these files, ensuring their follow-up, supporting the HROP's daily activities and facilitating interactions with other departments at headquarters, field missions and members of the Cell Team. In addition to these HR-related responsibilities, the Cell Intern provides operational and administrative support to the Cell Team, contributing to its day-to-day functioning.

### Tasks & Responsibilities

To support the HROP's focus on strategic HR mentoring and support to missions, the Cell Intern contributes to the management and follow-up of specific HR files delegated by the HROP, under their supervision. The Cell Intern’s responsibilities are divided as follows: 60% of the time is dedicated to HR and administrative support, and 40% to operational support (including medico-operational dossiers).

Under the supervision of the Cell HROP, the Cell Intern supports the Cell as follows:

**HR and Administrative Support**

Translation of operational ambitions into HR needs & planning of the IMS positions:

- Follows up with the missions on the job descriptions of international staff (MI), brings missing or outdated MIs to the missions’ attention, and files received MIs. Step by step, the intern will be expected to have a critical eye on the MIs and the capacity to raise an alert if some information is missing.
- Supports the updating of the international staff tracking table (HR Update) (mission dates, job openings, obtaining documents).
- Compiles a table of the cell's mission positions to be opened on a weekly basis.
- If necessary, supports the management of IMS job openings, particularly in emergency situations.
- Supports missions and GPOs with IMS propositions and the matching process, based on requests/needs.
- Participates in discussions about the optimal setup requested by the field to ensure that staffing is sufficient in number and coherent in composition to meet operational and institutional ambitions, especially during MYR and POA.
- Reviews MYR and POA matrices, reports any issues (technical, settings-related, analytical, etc.) to the HROP, and provides the HROP with initial feedback on the forecast and variances compared to the last validated budget.
- Supports the verification of IMS staffing requests formalized by the HRCos (compliance with planning, accuracy, and clarity of the request).
- Follows up on updates by the missions (at least every 3 months) to the missions’ HR restrictions table, detailing the profiling decisions in place.

HR and administrative management of international mobile staff (IMS):

- Monthly, as part of the IMS salary payment process, supports the verification of changes to the start and end dates of IMS contracts, amendments, positions and project allocations, and the preparation of monthly IMS payroll information for confirmation to FAR.
- Follows up with Field Movement Referents (FMRs) and acts as a focal point in case of specific movements or visas.
- Participates in HR briefings and debriefings and, when appropriate, carries them out under the guidance of the HROP, in accordance with the policy, ensuring that the HROP is alerted when needed.
- Welcomes international staff before departure, introduces them to current operations and ensures they have the necessary documents.
- Follows up with international staff on documents required for their departure (informed consents BIC, proof of life).
- Consolidates, monitors and updates pre-departure briefing materials for international staff.
- Follows up on anticipated returns of IMS and files documents related to them.
- Follows up on other specific HR procedures as needed.

Information / Reporting:

- Ensures that statistics and indicators are collected and passed on, and participates in their analysis at least during PoA and MYR and at the end of the year (HRNS).
- Develops HR statistics with the assistance of the HROP.

Meetings and specific platforms:

- Participates in the monthly "Tour du Monde" meetings to open IMS positions and present the cell's HR/operational news.
- Participates in HR department meetings when deemed relevant by the HROP.
- Participates in POA, MYR and HR Days (if/when possible).
- Maintains links with other OCG Cells’ interns to ensure consistent management of mandatory IMS documents (POA, BIC), Kompas management, etc.

**Operational Support to the Cell**

- Supports the cell in the organization of meetings (i.e. the weekly cell meeting (Mini Desk), Plan of Action discussions with field teams), including the preparation of agendas, taking minutes and archiving meeting documentation.
- Supports the cell in the management of information, such as cell archiving; acts as the focal point for online platforms such as Kompas and SharePoint; and manages key tools for the organization of the cell (i.e. presence, field visit preparation).
- Coordinates the organization of Cell events as needed (and keeps the cell calendar updated).
- Supports the preparation of key operational documents and presentations for either internal or external use.
- Organizes group BIC briefings by RP/ARP when needed.
- Follows up on material to be sent to missions and the ordering of maps via the GIS centre, as agreed with the RLO (Logistic Referent) of the cell.
- Provides support to the FINOP (Finance Referent) to prepare Powers of Attorney for mission teams. If needed, follows up on contracts and partnership agreements and manages information related to audits.
- Provides ad hoc support to the Directorate of Operations, such as meeting management, minute-taking and the coordination of operational and planning documents (portfolio reviews, emergency updates).
- When delegated by the RP, may support the preparation and delivery of operational updates to HQ (Point Info).
- In case of IMS briefings/debriefings in Geneva, welcomes international staff, presents the Cell 1 setup to them and ensures they have the necessary documents; supports the organization of their arrival and stay if needed.

**HR - Operational Dossiers**

- Each Cell Intern, during the period of employment is expected to work on an HR - Operational Dossier. The dossier selected should combine (a) the operational needs of the Cell/Missions, (b) academic requirements, such as the need to complete a thesis, and (c) if possible, a link to the future career of the Cell Intern.
- The topic needs to be selected within the first month of employment and agreed upon with the HROP and RP, ensuring that there is a clear deliverable (written report, thesis, etc.).
- The final deliverable MUST be presented to the Operations Department at the end of the period of employment.

### Your profile

*Education*

- Master’s degree in Humanitarian Studies, Development Studies, HR Management, Business Administration, or another relevant field.

*Experience*

- No specific work experience is required, but previous employment or engagement with NGOs or charities is considered an advantage.

*Languages*

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
- Knowledge of French is an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Capacity of analysis and synthesis,
- Planning and organization.
- Knowledge of key issues of the humanitarian environment.
- Excellent writing skills.
- Excellent knowledge of the MO environment (Powerpoint, Excel, Word).

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Team player; ability to coordinate with numerous stakeholders.
- Ability to work autonomously.
- Pro-active and solution-oriented.
- Flexible and capacity to adapt quickly.

### Terms of employment

- A tripartite internship agreement is mandatory.
- 6 to 9 months, according to internship agreement.
- Full time (40h/week).
- Based in Geneva, Switzerland
- Start date : 11th of January 2027
