jobs.description:
Do you have what it takes to lead a dynamic team of humanitarian and mine action professionals, addressing urgent needs in one of the most challenging regions of the world? This is your chance to make a lasting impact in Mali.

**About the Role**
As Country Director, you will lead DCA’s established programme in Mali, guiding its strategic direction and ensuring high-quality, accountable implementation. You will lead approximately 40 national and 2 international staff, prioritising staff wellbeing and a supportive working environment. Working closely with national partners, you will guide a programme combining humanitarian response, protection, mine action and resilient livelihoods.

Key responsibilities include:

- Supporting staff welfare and creating an enabling work environment.
- Nurturing relationships with national authorities, donors, and other stakeholders, including humanitarian coordinator actors, and international NGOs in Mali.
- Ensuring effective and proactive security management in a volatile and insecure context.
- Identifying fundraising opportunities to sustain and grow the programme.

- Risk Education on Explosive devices (Mines and Explosive Remnants of War)
- Victim assistance, and protection mainstreaming
- Emergency response (RRM) and cash-based programming
- Livelihoods and food security to enhance economic resilience
- Conflict prevention and peacebuilding

DCA supports and empowers local civil society networks to represent their communities effectively, address safety concerns, and engage with local authorities. You will lead this programme as it continues to build on its strong reputation.

**Key Responsibilities**

Your leadership will encompass:

**Leadership and Strategy**

- Lead the development and implementation of DCA’s Mali strategy, ensuring a relevant, high-quality and financially sustainable programme.

**Programme Quality Assurance and Security Management**

- Ensure the quality of DCA programming through engagement with donors and , and stakeholder,and through engagement in development, and reviews/approval of proposalsand donor reporting.

**Team Leadership**

**Stakeholder Engagement**

- Representing DCA to local authorities, international and national humanitarian stakeholders, and local communities.
- External representation in humanitarian coordination fora, including HCT, Cluster coordination, and the international NGO coordination body (FONGIM)
- External representation and regular engagement with current and prospective donors
- Maintaining constructive dialogue with relevant units and technical advisors at HQ.

**Your Profile**

We are looking for a leader with:

- Minimum 5 years’ leadership experience in humanitarian assistance and/or mine action.
- Strong programme implementation skills and expertise in financial, administrative, security, logistics, and operational management.
- Proven experience in safety and security management in volatile contexts.
- Demonstrated success in fundraising, networking, and donor liaison.
- Strong ability to mentor and develop staff while fostering a positive team environment.
- Cultural sensitivity, maturity, and excellent communication skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken French and English.

**What We Offer**

- A competitive salary package, including hardship allowance, to be negotiated based on experience level

**Application Process**
DCA is committed to diversity and inclusion. We warmly welcome applications from qualified individuals regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, religion, or background.

**Please note the following requirements:**

jobs.title: Global Fund Project Finance Director
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Global Fund Project Finance Director**, you will oversee the full accounting and financial management, budget monitoring, and compliance of the Global Fund grant and all related sub-recipients (SRs) and sub-contractors. You will establish strong internal controls and financial reporting procedures to safeguard Global Fund investments, manage risks, and ensure compliance with grant agreements, approved workplans and budgets, Global Fund regulations, World Vision policies, and local laws. You will also coordinate capacity assessments and development, support the Ministry of Health (UGP) and SRs in strengthening grant financial management, and implement financial strategies to reduce compliance-related risks and liabilities.

**30% of time – Grant Financial Management and Budget Oversight**

You will coordinate grant agreements and amendments, maintain grant documentation, and ensure timely, accurate donor reporting. You will review management letters, address compliance issues, lead budget and compliance training, monitor spending and budget execution, and recommend corrective actions. You will oversee budget revisions, develop monitoring tools, coordinate with WVI CAR and US finance teams, manage cash projections and disbursements, review and approve journals and liquidations, and regularly reconcile cash balances, SR advances, and non-cash assets.

**30% of time – Financial Management, Compliance and Grant Close-out**

You will ensure all financial processes and reports comply with WVI CAR, Global Fund, local, and international requirements. You will maintain audit-ready financial records, strengthen grant financial management capacity, and ensure effective cost allocation, accounting, internal controls, and asset monitoring. You will oversee grant and SR accounting, verify expenditure eligibility, ensure compliance with Blocked Parties Screening (BPS) and Labour Distribution Reporting (LDR), and maintain appropriate support-cost recovery. You will also monitor spending with Supply Chain and programme teams and lead the grant close-out process in coordination with the Chief of Party and Finance Director.

**25% of time – Audit, Monitoring and Capacity Strengthening**

You will oversee planned audit and monitoring visits, ensure assessments are properly documented, and coordinate corrective action plans and follow-up. You will ensure Finance and programme staff conduct financial monitoring of SRs, review monitoring reports, assess internal controls and segregation of duties, and strengthen SR capacity in financial management and compliance. You will facilitate Financial Management Working Groups (FMWGs) for the Global Fund GC7 consortium and collaborate with the Global Integrated Investigation Team on fraud and corruption allegations when necessary.

**10% of time – Financial Monitoring and Technical Support**

You will ensure the Finance and Compliance Officer provides capacity-building support to Global Fund Finance and Programme teams on relevant policies and procedures. You will oversee real-time monitoring of key activities, periodic assessments of financial systems and processes, and implementation of risk mitigation measures. You will approve liquidations, verify supporting documentation, and maintain professional networks with the Regional Deputy Finance Director and WVUS Finance Manager.

**5% of time – Leadership and Staff Management**

You will lead, mentor, and coach Finance and Grants Compliance staff to achieve Global Fund programme objectives. You will establish annual finance and compliance targets, incorporate responsibilities into staff performance plans, conduct regular performance reviews, and strengthen staff motivation, commitment, capacity, and teamwork.

**Requirements include:**

- Master’s degree in accounting, Finance, Management or related field like international business management.
- CA, ACCA, CPA or another professional accreditation equivalent.
- A minimum of 10-15 years of progressive experience in grant finance management.
- At least 7-10 years of direct experience managing Global Fund grants, with demonstrated responsibility for financial oversight, compliance, budgeting, reporting, and grant performance.
- Fluency in both English and French is required, with excellent verbal and written communication skills in both languages.
- Proven experience serving as a Principal Recipient (PR) for Global Fund grants, with substantial accountability for grant implementation, governance, risk management, and stakeholder engagement. Experience solely at Sub-Recipient (SR) level will not be considered sufficient.
- Demonstrated experience managing and overseeing grants across multiple Global Fund funding cycles, including but not limited to New Funding Model 2 (NFM2), New Funding Model 3 (NFM3) and Grant Cycle 7 (GC7).
- Proven track record of managing complex grant portfolios with cumulative values ranging from USD 50 million to USD 150 million or more.
- Extensive experience across the full Global Fund grant life cycle, including grant making, implementation, performance management, closure, transition, and sustainability planning.
- Strong working knowledge and practical experience in managing C19RM (COVID-19 Response Mechanism), RSSH (Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health), PSM (Procurement and Supply Management), and Health Systems Strengthening (HSS) grants and interventions.
- Demonstrated ability to ensure compliance with Global Fund regulations, financial management requirements, audit standards, and performance-based funding frameworks while delivering programmatic and financial results.
- Willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 20% of the time.

**Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Senior Partnership Advisor, Foundations & Private Sector (Re-advertisement)
jobs.description:
The overall purpose of Danish Red Cross’ (DRC) international engagement is to increase and strengthen humanitarian impact, inspire and act for human dignity, and enhance resilience and social cohesion in contexts of poverty, conflict and disaster.

The Global Partnership unit leads the coordination and strategic direction of the Danish Red Cross’ international partnerships, external and within the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement. The Unit is responsible for global resource mobilization efforts and initiatives and provides support to countries and regions. The Unit hosts the Danish Red Cross’ core donor specialization knowledge and capacity on compliance and strategies. Furthermore, the unit supports and quality assures proposals to core donors.

**The position**

As part of the Movement relations and private partnerships team (MOPS), the Partnership Advisor will drive Danish Red Cross’ strategic engagement with Danish and international foundations and private sector actors, with the objective of growing and diversifying non-institutional funding and strategic partnerships. The role combines new partnership development with strategic management and growth of high-value, multi-year partnerships. It focuses on senior-level relationship building, development of innovative partnership models, negotiation of multi-year agreements, and strong partnership stewardship across the full lifecycle. The Advisor will position DRC as a preferred humanitarian partner among Danish businesses, corporate foundations, family foundations, and selected international private sector actors through collaboration within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

**Main responsibilities:**

- Develop and implement a multi-year strategy for Danish and international private sector and foundation engagement aligned with DRC’s international priorities.
- Build and convert a qualified pipeline of high-value partnership opportunities, with clear income and partnership-growth ambitions.
- Lead the strategic management of one or more high-value, multi-year foundation partnerships, including relationship management, governance, internal coordination, delivery oversight and identification of opportunities for growth.
- Ensure strong partnership stewardship throughout the grant lifecycle, working closely with programme, finance and operational colleagues to support delivery, reporting, compliance and proactive management of risks and partner expectations.
- Develop partnership models beyond traditional grant funding, including strategic co-creation and multi-stakeholder alliances.
- Support country and regional teams to identify, shape and pursue high-potential private sector and foundation partnerships.
- Work closely with Business Development Advisors, Fundraising, and Operations to align private sector engagement with programming priorities.
- Represent DRC in relevant private sector and foundation networks and relevant Movement platforms related to private sector engagement.

**We expect you to have the following qualifications:**

- A master’s degree or MBA in Business, International Affairs, International Development or related
- Significant experience (7-10 years) in business development, resource mobilization, partnership development, preferably in the humanitarian or non-profit sector
- Demonstrated success in securing high-value, multi-year private sector or foundation partnerships
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, high-value, multi-year and/or multi-stakeholder partnerships including stakeholder engagement, negotiation, renewal and growth
- Strong established network in Denmark and ideally internationally
- Solid understanding of private sector CSR strategies, corporate foundations, and philanthropic trends
- Strong strategic account-management skills, including experience balancing partner expectations with organisational priorities and operational realities
- Experience coordinating complex partnerships across multiple internal teams, technical areas and geographies
- Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, Danish is an advantage

**As a person you have the following competences:**

- High level of strategic thinking and diplomatic and political judgement
- Ability to lead processes and engage people across functions and geographies
- Results-oriented and entrepreneurial mindset and ability to turn opportunities into concrete action.
- Collaborative team player with the ability to build trust and work in a multicultural environment

**We offer**

A full-time position of 37 working hours per week in an inspiring workplace. You will have the opportunity to work in a diversified motivated team of donor experts and be part of Danish Red Cross’ large global humanitarian action. You will refer to the Head of Global Partnership in Copenhagen.

The position is based in Copenhagen with potential 4-8-week travel. Salary and employment conditions will comply with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargain agreement with AC.

**Application and further information**

We look forward to receiving your application via the Red Cross home page [www.rodekors.dk/job](http://www.rodekors.dk/job)

In case you have questions to the position please contact Head of Global Partnerships, Marie-Chantal Legendre Dahl mcd@rodekors.dk or Team coordinator Vivian Pucher vipuc@rodekors.dk

Application deadline is 20th November 2026; Interviews will take place soon thereafter. The expected date of commencement is as soon as possible, preferably no later than January 1st.

jobs.title: Climate Change Capacity-Building Programme for PWP Partners in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI)
jobs.description:
## Climate Change Capacity-Building Programme for PWP Partners in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI)

Duhok, Iraq
19 - 20 November 20261

Background and Context:
The PROSPECTS Partnership (Partnership for Improving Prospects for Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Persons) was launched in 2019 by the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The partnership brings together the International Labour Organization (ILO), the International Finance Corporation (IFC), UNHCR, UNICEF, and the World Bank to deliver complementary interventions in education, skills development, employment, and protection.

PROSPECTS is implemented across eight countries—Egypt, Ethiopia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Sudan, and Uganda. The current Phase II of the partnership covers the period 2024–2027.

Iraq has experienced decades of conflict, instability, and governance challenges that have significantly weakened infrastructure, institutional capacity, and social cohesion. Despite ongoing reconstruction and stabilization efforts, substantial development needs remain, particularly among refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and vulnerable host communities living in remote and underserved areas with limited access to quality public services.

Within this context, PROSPECTS supports the implementation of the Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) in Duhok Governorate, using the EIIP approach to create decent employment opportunities while rehabilitating and improving community infrastructure through labour-based, local resource-driven approaches.

Under PROSPECTS Phase I, EIIP interventions implemented in Duhok and Nineveh Governorates generated more than 46,000 working days while integrating decent work principles into infrastructure development. Between 2021 and 2025, EIIP activities in Duhok focused primarily on green infrastructure interventions, including the rehabilitation of irrigation systems, land restoration, afforestation, and solid waste recycling. These initiatives contributed to environmental sustainability, climate change mitigation, and improved livelihood opportunities for refugees, IDPs, and host communities.

Building on these achievements, under PROSPECTS Phase II, the ILO will support the pilot implementation of a National Public Works Programme (NPWP) in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, applying the EIIP approach to promote decent employment, sustainable infrastructure development, and improved access to livelihood opportunities for vulnerable populations.

As part of this effort, the ILO will deliver a capacity-building programme on climate change and climate-resilient public works targeting government institutions, youth, and social partners. The programme will strengthen participants’ knowledge and practical skills in integrating climate change adaptation, environmental sustainability, and resilience considerations into public works planning and implementation. Through targeted training and practical learning, participants will be better equipped to identify climate-related risks, promote sustainable infrastructure solutions, and contribute to the effective implementation of the PWP. This initiative will also strengthen collaboration among key stakeholders and support the development of local capacities for more inclusive, climate-resilient, and sustainable public works in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.

Purpose of the Assignment:
The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified service provider to organize and manage all logistical arrangements for a Capacity-Building Workshop on Climate Change and Climate-Resilient Public Works under the National Public Works Programme (PWP), to be held in Duhok on 19–20 November 2026.

The selected service provider will be responsible for planning and coordinating all event logistics, including, but not limited to:

• Venue arrangements;
• Accommodation for participants;
• Transportation services;
• Catering and refreshments;
• Conference equipment and audio-visual services;
• Printing and branding materials;
• Event signage and visibility items;
• Registration and participant management; and
• All other logistical requirements specified in the scope of services and the table below.

The workshop aims to strengthen the capacities of key stakeholders involved in the implementation and institutionalization of the PWP in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, with a particular focus on integrating climate change adaptation, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience into public works planning and implementation.

The workshop will bring together representatives from relevant government institutions, ministries, governorates, technical directorates, youth, social partners, and other key stakeholders to enhance their knowledge, technical skills, and understanding of climate-resilient public works and the application of the Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) approach.

The specific objectives of the workshop are to:

1\. Strengthen participants’ understanding of climate change adaptation, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience in the context of public works and infrastructure development.
2\. Enhance the technical capacities of government institutions, youth, and social partners to integrate climate considerations into public works planning, design, implementation, and monitoring.
3\. Promote the application of the EIIP approach in developing inclusive, sustainable, and climate-resilient infrastructure while generating decent employment opportunities for vulnerable populations.
4\. Facilitate knowledge exchange and collaboration among government institutions, youth, social partners, and other stakeholders on climate-resilient infrastructure and employment-intensive public works.
5\. Support the effective implementation and institutionalization of the PWP by strengthening local capacities and promoting a shared understanding of stakeholders’ roles in delivering sustainable and climate-resilient public works interventions.
Conditions that must be met in the hall:
1\. The halls should have enough space for sitting, including registration table at the entrance, per each day
2\. The hall should have easy access to a minimum of 2 toilets
3\. The hotel should have full considerations for disability access
4\. The Hall should be sufficiently bright with good light and air conditions.
5\. The hotel shall arrange for fully functional electronic and audio-visual equipment and workshop materials (such as banners and/ or flags banners, data shows, wireless microphones, audio systems, teleconference equipment, etc.)
6\. Flipcharts with stands, whiteboard with paper, and markers
7\. Meeting signage includes company logo to guide your guests.
8\. 4 stars hotel and they must be approved by UNDSS.
9\. Room on ground floor or higher (not basement floor) Meeting room picture required to be attached
10\. Free Wi-Fi internet connection in the training room.
11\. Pens and notepads per participants.

The company will liaise and report to Ms. Gashaw Shareef, shareef@ilo.org , Mr. Miran Bakragha at bakragha@ilo.org , and Marina Rai at marina@ilo.org
Payment
According to the ILO policy, the payments of services are performed 30 days after receipt of service.
The payment schedule will consist of a single payment, issued after the completion of the service and upon receipt of the invoice and required documents from the supplier, in line with ILO's satisfaction with the service.
Means of payment: the payment will be paid via wire transfer to the designated bank account of the supplier.
Important Notes:
The supplier will be billed to ILO based on the actual number of participants and service.

jobs.title: Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist
jobs.description:
**Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist**

Africa (multi-country; remote and field-based assignments) | Framework-based consultancy | Subject to contract award and individual assignments

**About Voluntās (Latin: will, goal, purpose, meaning)**

Voluntās was created from the fundamental belief that all human beings have the inherent right to live a meaningful life. **That is why we exist: to realize human potential in all corridors of life** – making every workplace, community, and country on the planet full of hope and dignity. Philosophers by heart and advisors by profession, we use our insights to provide evidence-based inspiration, tools and recommendations for our partners around the world.

Voluntās has established offices in Beirut, Copenhagen, Dakar, Kyiv, Mumbai, Nairobi, Port Sudan, and Tunis. We build on a track record of over 270 projects across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, serving more than 150 clients. We advise private and public sector actors, including international organizations, government agencies, civil society and foundations, on how to drive meaningful change in societies and organizations.

Our field of expertise is providing fact-based recommendations and policy options grounded in extensive research and data collection in volatile regions and tailored to increase the impact and sustainability of our partners’ efforts.

Voluntās offers a wide range of services across research, policy and governance, including context and thematic analysis, public perception surveys and policy briefs. Under monitoring and social impact, we provide program design, third-party monitoring, evaluations, and social impact measurement. We work across thematic areas including agriculture and food, children and youth, economic development, education, gender, health, migration, governance, media, peace and security, and sustainability.

**About the Role**

Voluntās is preparing a proposal for a multi-year framework covering monitoring, evaluation, reporting and learning (MERL) services for development finance programs in Africa, including agricultural finance, climate resilience and risk financing.

We are seeking an experienced **Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist** to support the design and implementation of climate-sensitive and gender-responsive MERL frameworks, ensuring that climate adaptation, gender equality and inclusion outcomes are effectively measured, monitored and reported across multiple programs and countries.

The framework is anticipated to begin in late 2026 and run for five years. Specific assignments, timelines and levels of effort will be confirmed through individual work orders; appointment and mobilization are not guaranteed.

**Your Responsibilities**

- Develop and harmonize climate adaptation, gender equality and inclusion of indicators within MERL frameworks and theories of change.
- Define indicator reference sheets, baselines, targets and measurement methodologies, including climate resilience metrics and gender-disaggregated indicators.
- Support the application of climate adaptation measurement frameworks and gender-lens investment standards, including the 2X criteria.
- Develop data collection and reporting approaches, including aggregation and attribution rules, to assess climate and gender-related outcomes.
- Support climate and gender analysis across agricultural finance, climate resilience, and risk financing programs.
- Contribute to evaluations, impact assessments, portfolio-level and climate-fund reporting, and knowledge products.
- Provide technical guidance and capacity building to implementing partners on climate-sensitive and gender-responsive MERL.

**Main Competencies**

- Master's degree in environmental sciences, climate change, gender studies, development studies, economics, or related fields.
- **Minimum 7 years of relevant experience integrating both climate adaptation and gender indicators into MERL or results of measurement frameworks.**
- Proven experience designing and applying climate-sensitive and gender-responsive indicators, measurement methodologies, and reporting systems.
- Demonstrated application of climate adaptation and resilience measurement approaches, and familiarity with gender-lens investment standards, including the 2X criteria.
- Strong knowledge of climate resilience, gender equality, women's economic empowerment, and inclusive development.
- Experience supporting multi-country development programs in Africa, preferably in climate adaptation, agricultural finance, or related sectors.
- Strong analytical skills and experience with quantitative and qualitative research, evaluations and results reporting.
- Excellent written and spoken English; French and/or Arabic is an asset.

jobs.title: Program Quality Technical Advisor II - JWBG
jobs.description:
**About CRS**

Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. CRS works to *save, protect, and transform* lives in need in more than 100 countries, and has been present in Jerusalem, West Bank, and Gaza (JWBG) since 1961. In JWBG, CRS manages programming through its field offices in Jerusalem, Gaza, Ramallah and Bethlehem. At present, CRS JWBG provides rapid emergency assistance, recovery efforts and resilience support to conflict affected communities in Gaza and the West Bank in the sectors of multi-purpose cash; shelter; psycho-social support; food assistance; water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) and livelihoods.

**Job Summary**

The Jerusalem-based Program Quality Technical Advisor II provides program quality support in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices across the Jerusalem, Gaza, and West Bank (JWBG) Country Program (CP), to advance the delivery of high-quality programming to the conflict-affected, poor and vulnerable. Your technical knowledge in program quality, grants management, and business development will support quality programming, responsible growth, and effective grants management across the emergency response and recovery portfolio.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Working closely with Program Managers, ensure effective grants management for the emergency portfolio. Develop and update the CRS grants management tracker and prepare BD and funding overviews for internal audiences.
- Coordinate development of high-quality CRS progress and final reports to donors in support to the Program Managers and ensure communication to donors is timely and aligned with requirements.
- Provide program quality management support to Program Managers related to program start-up, implementation, close-out, and other key deliverables. When required, act as gap-filling for senior Program Mangers.
- In close coordination with the Head of Programming (HoP), Country Representative (CR) and PMs, co-lead the development of the CP strategy for emergency response and recovery for Gaza and the West Bank, and keep it updated over time reflecting changes in needs and gaps.
- Keep abreast of internal displacement trends, multi-sectoral needs assessments, and key UN-led coordination meetings, and organize recurrent meetings with the program team to feedback key information. Identify information gaps and co-lead multi-sectoral assessments.
- Contribute to CP efforts to pre-position CRS for growth opportunities. Coordinate and lead the development of the technical design for large and/or complex proposals, including design workshops with CRS and partners’ program teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach. Act as lead writer for complex proposals and as needed, develop other proposal annexes.
- Provide technical support, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction.
- Contribute to capacity strengthening initiatives for CP staff through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curricula, conducting trainings and workshops, and mentoring and coaching to CP staff.
- In close coordination with the MEAL Manager, contribute to knowledge management and learning through assisting with measuring program impact, capturing and sharing lessons learned and best practices, and research and internal reports. Co-lead cross-program learning sessions and support Program Managers in after action reviews and reflection events.
- Support establishing and maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research, and other institutions. Participate in relevant forums to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work. Contribute to communication materials for internal and external communications and events.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Master's Degree in International Relations or a related field required.
- Minimum of five years relevant international working experience in an advisory or management role with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO.
- Experience with grants management and project management, ideally with an international NGO.
- Previous experience providing technical assistance and developing successful proposals for external donor funding is required.
- Demonstrated application of technical principles and concepts. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Experience in business development, project design and proposal development including technical writing.
- Experience in mentoring, coaching, facilitation and training applying adult learning principles and practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including applying data collection tools and methodologies, data analysis, and data presentation.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based and civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.
- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Excellent relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings.
- Strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment.
- Strong written and oral communication skills.
- Strong presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills.
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented.

**Required Languages:** English fluency (written and verbal) is required, knowledge of Arabic is an advantage.

**Travel:** Up to 30% travel to the West Bank and Gaza (if required/desired and feasible)

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** No

jobs.title: Graphic Designer
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

Marketing & Mobilization (M&M), a part of External Relations (ER) is a dynamic team, tasked with overseeing and creating communications and marketing, building the IRC’s global profile and brand, increasing private revenue from deeper donor engagement and partnerships, and influencing our target audiences. In alignment with our Strategy100 commitments, M&M has launched ambitious multi-year campaigns that raise funding, profile and influence and will improve our share of voice and resonance in key geographies and globally.

The Content and Creative team, a part of M&M, consists of award-winning creative specialists and idea partners, developing powerful communications and experiences to engage audiences and ultimately to deliver on ER ambitions and objectives. Our mission is to be a leading provider of brand creative and storytelling products about the IRC’s clients, staff and programs.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is seeking a skilled Graphic Designer to support our Impact at Scale work within the Creative Studio Design Team. This full-time role is focused on producing high-quality donor facing deliverables—primarily presentation decks, data visualizations, proposals and reports—that communicate the IRC’s humanitarian impact with clarity and precision.

The ideal candidate plays a pivotal role in securing support for the IRC’s most ambitious and impactful priorities. This individual brings the IRC’s Impact at Scale vision to life—translating complex program strategies into clear, compelling communications that motivate giving across Trusts & Foundations, High Net Worth Individuals (HNWI), Global New Business prospects, and Corporate partners. Working closely with the Strategy Unit, program teams, and External Relations colleagues, the Designer develops high quality proposals, reports, and pitch materials that show donors the meaningful impact their investment can make.

This designer thrives in a fast-paced creative environment, brings exceptional expertise and a sharp eye for typographic systems and layout hierarchy, and can translate complex data and narratives into polished, compelling visual documents. Must be experienced in the Adobe Creative Studio systems including InDesign, Photoshop and Illustrator. Figma and Figma Slides knowledge are a bonus but not required.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Reports & Long-Form Documents**

- Design and lay out high-quality impact reports, funding propositions, and donor collateral in Adobe InDesign
- Build and maintain paragraph and character styles, master pages, and grid systems to ensure typographic consistency and layout integrity
- Apply meticulous attention to type hierarchy, spacing, and detail across multi-page documents
- Produce print-ready and digital PDF outputs optimized for various distribution contexts

**Data Visualization & Infographics**

- Transform raw data and statistics into clear, meaningful charts, diagrams, and infographics
- Design visuals that communicate impact metrics at a glance for high-value donor audiences
- Work within established brand frameworks while bringing a strong visual sensibility to each piece

**Presentations & Decks**

- Design and produce executive-ready presentation decks (PowerPoint and/or Google Slides) aligned with IRC brand guidelines
- Develop scalable deck templates and systems that are easily reused and adapted across teams
- Collaborate with stakeholders to clarify goals, audience needs, and key messages; refine content structure for clarity, pacing, and emphasis
- Translate complex data, technical concepts, and program results into logical, digestible visual flows that guide understanding

**Collaboration & Brand Stewardship**

- Partner with the Creative Studio team and front-line fundraisers on bespoke HV donor projects
- Maintain strict brand consistency across all deliverables and seek approval through the Creative Studio as appropriate
- Manage multiple concurrent projects with tight turnarounds while maintaining exceptional quality and attention to detail

**Essential Qualifications:**

- 4–5+ years of professional graphic design experience, with a strong portfolio demonstrating print and digital publication work
- Expert-level proficiency in Adobe InDesign, including master pages, paragraph/character styles, and grid-based layout systems
- High-level proficiency in Adobe Creative suite including Photoshop and Illustrator
- Strong command of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop
- Demonstrated experience designing presentation decks in PowerPoint and/or Google Slides. Figma Slides knowledge is a preference but not required.
- Exceptional typographic skills and a meticulous eye for layout hierarchy, spacing, and detail
- Experience creating data visualizations and infographics that communicate complex information clearly
- Ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and adapt quickly in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
- Passion for the IRC’s mission and commitment to humanitarian work

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Presentation Narrative & Content Strategy: ability to collaborate with stakeholders, identify key messages, and structure content for clarity and impact
- Typographic Excellence: deep understanding of type hierarchy, grid systems, and design consistency across long-form documents
- Data Visualization: skill in transforming quantitative information into intuitive visual formats for non-specialist audiences
- Attention to Detail: unwavering precision in design execution, file management, and brand application
- Communication: clear, concise communicator capable of working across teams and managing feedback constructively
- Time Management: proven ability to prioritize and deliver high-quality work across multiple concurrent projects

**Desired Qualifications:**

- Experience working in the nonprofit, humanitarian, or fundraising sector
- Familiarity with IRC’s brand guidelines and design system
- Experience with Figma or other UI/UX tools

**Working Environment:**

This role may require working remotely full- or part-time (i.e., telecommuting). Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation: (**$73,000 - $85,000/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Senior Youth Program Specialist
jobs.description:

A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of August 31, 2027.***

**IRC Background:** IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:** The vision of the IRC Washington Youth Program is that youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds will have the skills and resources necessary to pursue a future of opportunity. The Youth and Education Program works towards this vision by providing educational and enrichment opportunities to help school-aged youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds catch up on missed education, adjust to a new school, accelerate English language development, and build positive relationships in the school and community. This program supports school-age youth and their families, and also provides support to teachers and school administration to better connect and serve these students.

The Sr. Youth Program Specialist is responsible for teaching and implementation of IRC’s Youth and Education Programs in Spokane, WA.

The Virtual Ready to Read (VR2R) program promotes enjoyment of reading, literacy skills, language acquisition, social and emotional asset development, and positive cultural identity for students in grades 3–8. Upon enrollment, students receive a device, a learning kit with craft materials and art supplies, a workbook, and a set of books. Parents and students attend an orientation to ensure they know how to use their device and the video call platform. Each student attends one-hour online classes twice a week from January through May. Students read a book as a group and engage in themed lessons with vocabulary and grammar content, discussion questions, and activities. Students also take part in virtual field trips to institutions such as the Pacific Science Center, Woodland Park Zoo, and Seattle Aquarium. Two consecutive 1-hour classes are led by an IRC teacher on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 pm – 6:00 pm (a slightly later start at 4:15 pm can be accommodated if your schedule does not allow an earlier start). The program runs from January to May. Classes are small with typically under 15 students in attendance for each class.

The Individualized Tutoring Program matches K-12 students and families with an IRC-screened, trained, and supervised tutor who supports English language acquisition, literacy and fluency, math skills, general homework, and social-emotional learning. Tutors meet with students in their homes once a week after school for 1–2 hours over a period of 3–6 months. Tutoring is one of IRC’s long-standing programs, and IRC is committed to providing high-quality tutoring in alignment with the standards of Stanford University’s National Student Success Accelerator. Tutoring appointments are typically scheduled on weekdays between 4:00 pm – 7:00 pm or weekends.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Virtual Reading Program**

- Schedule: 6–10 hours per week, including Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 pm – 6:00 pm (a 4:15 pm start can be accommodated if needed). The program runs from January to May.
- Teach and manage the online classes in the Virtual Reading Program, which is the primary responsibility of this position.
- Prepare lesson plans and materials tailored to students’ needs.
- Send reminder texts and make reminder calls to families to keep attendance high.
- Provide support to students who are having issues with their devices.
- Support the Youth and Education team in collecting and maintaining student and family records, documents, and case notes, while maintaining confidentiality.
- Conduct outreach phone calls to invite families to participate in programs.
- Conduct enrollment sessions with new families to ensure they understand the program and to collect all necessary documentation.
- Provide ongoing support to volunteers, including problem-solving, answering questions, coaching, and sharing teaching and learning resources and best practices.

**In-home Tutoring Program**

- Provide direct, in-person instruction to students in their homes through the Individualized Tutoring Program.
- Prepare lesson plans and slides tailored to students’ needs using the Virtual Ready to Read curriculum. The materials have already been selected, and a scope and sequence has been created for Virtual Ready to Read, however, the Sr. Specialist will need to create slides for each session based on a template.
- Provide ongoing support to volunteer tutors, including problem-solving, answering questions, coaching, and sharing teaching and learning resources and best practices.
- Assist the program coordinator with regular supervision of community tutors to ensure quality instruction, safeguarding, and accountability, including support with tutor observations and feedback and quarterly feedback calls with families and students.

**Other Youth Programs and Duties**

- Provide in-person support to other youth programs and events, including Summer Camp, the Youth Roots teen summer program, and field trips.
- Assist the Tutoring and Elementary Education Program Coordinator, as needed, with the following:
- Collecting and maintaining student and family records, documents, and case notes while maintaining confidentiality.
- Conducting outreach phone calls to invite families to participate in programs.
- Conducting enrollment sessions with new families to ensure they understand the program and to collect all necessary documentation.
- Program planning.
- Documenting attendance records and entering students into the database.
- Conducting feedback calls with families.
- Comply with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to: Youth Program Coordinator**

**Position directly supervises: Interns, volunteers**

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal*****:** ***Youth Program Specialists, Youth Program Team, other IRC Seattle staff***

***External*****:** ***Teachers at partner school districts, Contacts at partner organizations***

**Job Requirements:**

- Relevant degree in Education, Teaching, Child/Youth Development or related field, or 2-4 years relevant experience in teaching, tutoring, or youth development programming. TESOL certificate a plus.
- Cross-cultural experience; connection and experience working with people from refugee and/or immigrant communities
- Experience working with multi-lingual students and families
- Committed to anti-racism and continual learning and growth
- Demonstrated ability to use a variety of instructional strategies appropriate for individual student needs
- Commitment to creating safe and healing learning spaces for newcomer students and utilizing trauma informed practices with students and families
- Flexible and adaptable – able to quickly problem solve and change plans and activities according to student need or unexpected circumstances
- English proficiency, both spoken and written. Bonus if the candidate has professional proficiency in predominant language of local client base desired (Dari, Pashto, Arabic, Somali, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Ukrainian etc.)
- Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
- Proficiency in MS Office suite including Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams
- Ability to work well with people of diverse cultural backgrounds
- Ability to work well independently and as part of a team
- Ability to maintain responsibility for multiple tasks in the context of a diverse, fast-paced work environment
- Willing to be First Aid/CPR certified upon hire

**Working Environment*****:***

- Hybrid: Staff will work at the IRC office, in the homes of refugee families, and remotely. The Virtual Reading Program can be taught remotely from home as long as there is a reliable Wi-Fi connection. Staff are expected to travel to students’ homes for in-person tutoring.
- **Schedule:**

**1. Part-time: 20 hours / week:**

- Must be available on Tuesday and Thursday between 4:00 pm – 6:30 pm PST (If schedule does not allow, 4:15 pm start could be accommodated)
- AND Must be available 2 other weekdays between the hours of 4:00 pm – 6:30 pm OR on weekends

**2. Monday – Thursday,** 1:30 pm – 6:30 pm is the ideal schedule. However, we are open to discussing alternative schedules as long as the candidate is available to work during the days and times outlined in bullet point 1 above.

- Limited Term. The position ends on August 31, 2027.
- Access to reliable high-speed internet from home office.
- Access to reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the Spokane Public School district area.

**Compensation:** **($25.50- $27.50 / hour).** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.company: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
**Department:** Program

**Position:** WASH Field Engineer

**Direct Manager:** WASH Program Manager

**Contract duration:** 8 Months (with the possibility of renewal).

**Duty Location:** Idleb, Lattakia, Hama, Deir Ez zor, Aleppo

## **About AMAL Organization for Relief & Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war torned.

Amal Organization is a relief and development organization, was established in early 2013 in the northern countryside of the city of Homs on 6/6/2014 and the organization was licensed and registered in Turkey – Gaziantep

**POSITION PROFILE:**

The WASH Engineer will work within the project areas and in its host communities with possible travel to needed areas. The main responsibilities will include working to design and improve the technical engineering implementation aspects of Amal’s WASH program and sanitation technology including designing, quantifying, specifying boreholes, preparing contractual documents and managing them, managing geophysical studies, submersible and hand pump installation and repairs, submersible, and hand pump repair and maintenance training, designing and constructing water distribution systems, pump testing, water quality testing, hand-dug well construction, and/or paving road. The WASH Engineer will also be responsible in coordinating and leading any emergency relief situations involving WASH efforts, creating and drafting technical designs, and submitting regular reports on the work being completed.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

1. **Assess needs for WASH interventions (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene facilities) at the community level including public schools and Health facilities.**
2. **Ensure the project will satisfy the needs of the beneficiaries and provide oversight of water source construction and sanitation projects to ensure quality:**

- Preparation of drawings (AutoCAD), BoQ/Cost Estimates and Tender documents for all WASH infrastructures
- Ensuring the training staff of water station in technical areas including water quality testing, and building and maintaining quality water point structures;
- Help design and revise the construction/rehabilitation works component of the project work-plan, and monitor that the implementation of the construction/ rehabilitation activities respects the time-table milestones and deadlines
- Conduct trainings regarding operation and maintenance of water supply and sanitation facilities for beneficiaries and Water management committees
- Develop and maintain good relationships and lines of communication with relevant local authorities and communities, prior to intervention explaining Amal’s role as an NGO and liaising with them during all phases of the project.
- Regular monitoring of ongoing construction activities to ensure that all the activities are executing as per design, specifications and work schedule
- Extend all possible technical support to other team members and contractors when and where required
- Keep close coordination with contractors through regular meetings
- Preparation of weekly, monthly work plans and construction progress reports
- Preparation of feasibility studies/ reports, borehole pumping tests analysis & reporting and completion certificates
- Verify the work done at the site and recommend for the payments to contractor(s)/casual labors etc
- Working in harmony with all other project staff and field team for the effective and efficient day-to-day management of the WASH project.
- Coordinate with other stakeholders on the ground for smooth, efficient and effective implementation of the activities.

1. **When need be, Represent Amal in coordination meetings such as WASH cluster and other cluster meetings.**

**QUALIFICATIONS / EXPERIENCE:**

- Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical, civil, topographic or related field.
- At least five years’ work experience in WASH and a similar role.
- Proficient in Auto CAD, Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
- Good written and spoken English.
- Able to be diplomatic in communications with all NGO, governmental, and community partners.
- Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability in an ever-changing environment.
- Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
- Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
- Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal is dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so maintaining equal opportunities and nondiscrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy. This policy underscores our dedication to safeguarding the well-being of our staff by promoting a workplace culture characterized by mutual respect and professionalism. The role holder plays a vital part in this commitment, ensuring a supportive atmosphere and actively contributing to the safeguarding of their colleagues through the promotion of positive employee relations.
