jobs.description:
**Position:** Sectoral Technical Experts / Trainers - Liberia
**Type:** Consultancy / Project-based / Roster
**Location:** Liberia
**Organization:** STOOS Consulting

**STOOS Consulting** is inviting qualified **sectoral technical experts, trainers, facilitators, researchers, and consultants in Liberia** to join its roster for upcoming humanitarian, development, research, assessment, capacity building, monitoring, evaluation, and third-party monitoring opportunities across the country.

This call is open to experienced professionals from different technical backgrounds who are interested in supporting future assignments with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, donors, development partners, local organizations, and community-based actors**.

**About STOOS Consulting**

**STOOS Consulting** is an international consulting firm specialized in **Third-Party Monitoring, MEAL, research and assessments, evaluations, data collection, capacity building, conflict and gender analysis, market systems research, and economic empowerment studies**. STOOS works in complex humanitarian and development contexts to produce practical, field-based, and evidence-driven findings that support programme quality, accountability, learning, and decision-making.

Through its network of national and international experts, STOOS supports assignments in areas such as **needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, final evaluations, outcome monitoring, technical training, capacity building, qualitative and quantitative research, community consultations, and field monitoring**.

**Profile of Experts Sought**

STOOS is looking to expand its Liberia roster with qualified experts and trainers in a wide range of sectors, including but not limited to **WASH, health, nutrition, protection, GBV, child protection, education, food security and livelihoods, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, shelter, social protection, TVET, economic empowerment, migration, gender, disability inclusion, peacebuilding, conflict sensitivity, and MEAL**.

STOOS also welcomes applications from experts with experience in **research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection, training facilitation, curriculum development, institutional capacity building, market assessments, youth employment, entrepreneurship, community engagement, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and humanitarian/development programme quality**.

**Main Areas of Work**

Selected experts may be contacted for future assignments involving **technical training, capacity building, sectoral assessments, programme evaluations, field research, tool development, data collection supervision, contextual analysis, report writing, quality assurance, and technical advisory support**.

Depending on the opportunity, experts may support **KIIs, FGDs, surveys, community consultations, workshops, technical reviews, training delivery, data analysis, and preparation of practical recommendations** tailored to the Liberia context.

**Liberia Context and Relevant Experience**

Candidates with strong knowledge of Liberia's humanitarian and development context are encouraged to apply, especially those with experience related to **public health, WASH, education, food security and livelihoods, nutrition, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, environmental and natural resource governance, social protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, youth employment, economic empowerment, migration, and community resilience**.

Experience working with communities in **urban, rural, forested, coastal, border, or hard-to-reach areas** is highly valued. STOOS particularly welcomes experts who can work respectfully with **women, youth, children, persons with disabilities, rural communities, returnees, migrants, farmers, fisherfolk, low-income households, and other vulnerable groups**.

**Key Skills and Qualifications**

Candidates should have relevant professional experience in one or more technical sectors and a strong understanding of the **Liberia context**, including local institutions, community structures, civil society actors, government partners, access dynamics, and humanitarian/development priorities.

Applicants are encouraged to apply if they have worked with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, local organizations, government partners, donor-funded programmes, academic institutions, consulting firms, or community-based initiatives**.

Strong candidates will demonstrate practical experience in **training, facilitation, technical advisory work, assessments, monitoring and evaluation, field research, community engagement, or programme implementation**.

Knowledge of **Do No Harm, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, ethical research, confidentiality, conflict sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations** is highly desirable.

Experience using digital tools such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, NVivo, or similar platforms** is considered an asset, depending on the assignment.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in **English** is required for most field-based and community-level assignments.

Strong **written English** is preferred, especially for assignments involving technical reports, donor documentation, training materials, data analysis, and communication with international teams.

Knowledge of local languages such as **Liberian English, Kpelle, Bassa, Dan/Gio, Mano, Kru, Grebo, Loma, Mandingo, Vai, Gola, Kissi, or other local languages** is a strong advantage, especially for assignments in specific counties, remote or forested areas, coastal communities, or border areas.

jobs.title: Oman M&E and Research Field Manager
jobs.description:
**Introduction**

**STOOS Consulting** is an international research and consulting firm providing research, assessments, evaluations, third-party monitoring, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity-building services to humanitarian and development organizations. STOOS is seeking an experienced **Research and M&E Field Manager based in Oman** to support field implementation across its current and future projects.

**Position Overview**

This is a **field-oriented, project-based role** supporting a diverse portfolio of research, monitoring, evaluation and third-party monitoring assignments in Oman. The Field Manager will coordinate local fieldwork, teams, logistics, stakeholder engagement and data quality, working closely with STOOS project managers, team leaders, technical specialists and data analysts.

**Role Purpose**

The Field Manager will organize and oversee day-to-day field activities, helping ensure that project work is implemented safely, ethically and in accordance with approved methods, timelines and quality standards.

**Key Responsibilities**

The Field Manager will:

- Plan and coordinate field activities, including surveys, interviews, focus groups, observations, site visits and monitoring activities, as required by each project.
- Coordinate local permissions, access arrangements and stakeholder engagement with relevant authorities, institutions, partners and communities.
- Recruit, brief, train and supervise enumerators, field researchers, supervisors and other field personnel.
- Support training on approved protocols, sampling procedures, research tools, safeguarding, confidentiality and data security, as applicable.
- Support translation or adaptation of materials between **Arabic and English**, ensuring substantive changes are approved by the project team.
- Coordinate field logistics, including schedules, transport, communications, devices and contingency arrangements.
- Monitor field progress against approved plans, samples, deliverables and timelines; provide regular updates on progress and operational risks.
- Conduct or coordinate data-quality checks, including form reviews, spot checks and follow-up on missing or inconsistent records.
- Maintain fieldwork documentation, including contextual observations, access constraints, protocol deviations and unresolved data queries.
- Escalate operational or data-quality issues promptly and implement changes only with the required project approval.
- Support timely and secure submission of complete data and field documentation to the project team.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

Candidates should have:

- A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Statistics, Economics, Public Health, Monitoring and Evaluation or a related field.
- At least **five years of relevant experience** in research coordination, field data-collection management, M&E, assessments, evaluations, third-party monitoring or humanitarian and development operations.
- Experience coordinating fieldwork and engaging with authorities, institutions, civil society organizations, service providers or community stakeholders in Oman.
- Demonstrated ability to recruit, train and supervise field teams and coordinate assignments across multiple locations.
- Familiarity with digital data-collection platforms such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, CommCare** or similar systems.
- Strong Arabic and English communication skills. Knowledge of additional languages used in Oman is an asset.
- Strong planning, reporting, problem-solving and interpersonal skills, with close attention to detail.
- Availability and willingness to travel within Oman according to project requirements.

Experience across humanitarian and development sectors is an advantage.

**Engagement Modality**

The successful candidate will be engaged through a **project-based consultancy arrangement**, depending on STOOS assignments and operational requirements in Oman. The level of effort, responsibilities and field locations will be confirmed for each assignment.

jobs.title: Endline Survey (es)/Evaluation of the Advancing Climate-resilient Livelihoods and Disaster Preparedness for Extreme Poor Families in BARMM Project
jobs.description:
**BACKGROUND**

This evaluation should be conducted in accordance with agreed internal policies, specifically the IRW MEAL Framework, as well as the external policies and requirements of the donor. Its primary purpose is to assess the overall performance of the project against its intended outputs and outcomes, while also identifying key lessons to inform the design and implementation of future similar interventions for IR-PH.

The evaluation will be undertaken in a systematic, objective, and impartial manner, examining both expected and unintended results. It will analyse the project’s results chain, implementation processes, contextual factors, and causal linkages using internationally recognized evaluation criteria, including relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability. In line with the UNDP Evaluation Guidelines (2019), the evaluation aims to generate credible, evidence-based, and practical findings that can be timely integrated into organizational and stakeholder decision-making processes.
Consistent with the ALNAP Evaluation of Humanitarian Action Guide (2016), the evaluation will serve as an independent assessment of the project’s value and significance, with the dual objectives of strengthening accountability and improving policy and practice. Ultimately, the evaluation will provide reliable and useful insights that support learning and inform future programming.

In addition, the ES of the advancing livelihood project will consider the nine (9) Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) Commitments as a reference framework for assessing the quality, relevance, effectiveness, accountability, and inclusiveness of the project interventions.
Attention was given to the CHS Commitments most relevant to the project’s livelihood and DRR interventions. These included:
**Relevance**
• CHS Commitment 1: Rights, Participation and Inclusion
• CHS Commitment 2 - Timely and Effective Support according to specific needs and priorities
• Commitment 7 - Adaptation based on feedback and learning
**Coherence:**
• CHS Commitment 6 - Coordinated and Complementary Support
• CHS Commitment 3 - Resilience and Locally Led Action
• CHS Commitment 2 - Appropriate Support and Referrals
**Effectiveness**
• CHS Commitment 2: Timely, Accessible and Quality Support
• CHS Commitment 7 - Feedback, Learning and Adaptation CHS
• Commitment 5: Complaints are welcomed and addressed.
• CHS Commitment 8: Staff is supported to do their job effectively and are treated fairly and equitably.
**Efficiency**
• CHS Commitment 6: Humanitarian Responses are Coordinated and Complementary.
• CHS Commitment 9: Resources are managed and used responsibly for their intended purpose.
• CHS Commitment 8 - Competent and Well-managed Staff and Volunteers
The evaluation will provide an assessment of how the intervention performed against each of the nine CHS commitments as above.

**OBJECTIVES**
**General Objectives:**
To evaluate the project’s performance against the logical framework and assess in accordance with Project’s Result Framework and OECD-DAC evaluation criteria—relevance, coherence, effectiveness, impact, sustainability, and inclusiveness and to examine the extent to which the project interventions benefited the lives of the targeted communities or households.
**Specific Objectives:**
1\. To assess the extent to which the project achieved its intended outputs, outcomes, and targets as outlined in the project's Logical Framework and Results Framework, with analysis disaggregated by age, gender, and disability.
2\. Assess the effectiveness, efficiency, coherence and implementation strategies, including the utilization of assistance, the methodologies and approaches applied.
3\. Assess the effectiveness of livelihood interventions in enhancing the knowledge, skills, resources, and capacities of households and SHG members to establish or strengthen diversified, sustainable, and climate-resilient livelihood activities.
4\. Determine the contribution of livelihood interventions to household economic resilience, particularly in terms of income generation, livelihood diversification, savings, access to productive resources, collective economic activities, and capacity to cope with economic and climate-related shocks.
5\. Evaluate the effectiveness of community-based disaster risk reduction interventions in developing, validating, and disseminating gender-responsive and inclusive Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (BDRRM) Plans and establishing functional disaster preparedness measures.
6\. Assess improvements in disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation knowledge and preparedness among targeted schools and communities, including the integration and implementation of enhanced preparedness mechanisms in updated School DRRM Plans.
7\. Examine the inclusiveness and responsiveness of project interventions to the needs and participation of women, persons with disabilities, extremely poor households, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups in livelihood development and disaster preparedness initiatives.
8\. Determine the sustainability and potential for replication or scaling up of the livelihood initiatives, SHG mechanisms, BDRRM Plans, and school-based preparedness measures beyond the project implementation period.
9\. To assess the evaluation findings against the relevant Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitments.
10\. Identify key lessons learned, good practices, implementation challenges, and recommendations to inform future livelihood, climate resilience, and community-based DRR programming.
11\. Examine the effectiveness of beneficiary selection, targeting processes, and implementation of IR Policies.

**SCOPE OF THE ES/EVALUATION AND KEY EVALUATION QUESTIONS**
**Locale of the ES/Evaluation:**
The activity will cover Municipalities of Pahamuddin and Rajah Buayan.
**Target Respondents:**
The respondents will consist of project rightsholders and beneficiaries, partners from Local Government Unit (LGU) at both the Municipal and Barangay levels, key stakeholders, as well as other individuals considered relevant to the activity.

**CONSULTANCY DETAILS**
**Required Competency:**
The successful team will have the following competencies:
• Demonstrate evidence of experience in evaluating humanitarian action/development project
• Demonstrate experience in evaluating livelihood or graduation models/project
• Possess sectoral experience and knowledge in evaluating DRR, Climate Change, protection and inclusion etc.
• Possess deep knowledge and practical experience of using quality standards such as CHS and Sphere
• Possess strong statistical/quantitative and qualitative research skills
• Have excellent written skills in English
• Be able to communicate fluently in English and the local languages. If local translators are required, this should be budgeted.
The chosen evaluation team will be supported by IR Philippines MEAL Team.
**Expected Output of the Assignment for the Consultant:**
The consultant is expected to produce:
1\. A detailed Work Plan and Inception Report developed with and approved by IR Philippines set out the detailed methodology, data collection tools (survey questionnaire), data collection protocols/guidelines, and checklists for FGD, KII, and Observation, reporting structure, and deliverables prior to commencing the review.
2\. The work plan, inception report, draft report, final report, presentation, etc., and communication language must be in English.
3\. Conduct interviews (FGD, KII, In-depth interviews,) with project stakeholders (rightsholders, local government authority and stakeholders, project staff, etc.).
4\. Orientation of local survey team/volunteers for the data collection process and questionnaire and data collection protocol.
5\. Develop quantitative data collection tools (questionnaire), Kobo design, data quality checking, support the data collection team, data quality management, and data editing and analysis.
6\. Collation and analysis of evaluation data including cost-benefit analysis for specific interventions and submission of the first draft to IR Philippines /IRW for comments and share the initial presentation of findings.
7\. Final report submitted to IR Philippines, IRW. A full report with following section,
a) Title of Report
b) Consultancy Organization and Any Partner Names
c) Name of person who compiled the report including summary of role/contribution of others in the team
d) Period during which the review was undertaken
e) Acknowledgements
f) Abbreviations
g) Table of contents
h) Executive summary (max 4 page)
i) Main report – max 40 pages – (Standard reporting structure will be shared at inception
stage, but consultant is invited to propose most suitable report structure layout)
j) Annexes
• Terms of reference for the review
• Profile of the review team members
• Review schedule
• Documents consulted during the desk review
• Persons participating in the review
• Field data used during the review
• Additional key overview tables, graphs or charts etc. created and used to support
analysis inform findings
• Bibliography
8\. Anonymised copies of all data collected in Excel or appropriate format which would enable cross-checking and any additional analysis.
9\. The consultant requires facilitating and documenting 1-day lessons learned workshop with key project stakeholders.
10\. The evaluator will present the evaluation findings and recommendations to:
• IR Philippines team.
• Regional desk, IRW and Donor

**QUALITY ASSURANCE PROTOCOLS**
The ES/Evaluation report should represent a thoughtful, well-researched and well-organized effort to objectively benchmark outcome and address study questions which ultimately should identify gaps and potential project integral approach in maximizing the impact:

1. The report shall address all questions included in the scope of work/ToR.
2. The report should include the scope of work as an annex. All modifications to the scope of work, whether
in technical requirements, consulting team composition, methodology or timeline need to be agreed
upon in writing by the technical person.
3. The study’s design and methodology shall be explained in detail and all tools used in conducting the study
such as questionnaires, checklists and discussion guides will be included in an Annex in the final report.
4. Study’s findings will assess outcomes and impact on men, women and youth where possible. Limitations
to the study shall be disclosed in the report, with particular attention to the limitations associated with
the study methodology (selection bias, recall bias, unobservable differences between comparator groups,
etc.). Study’s findings should be presented as analyzed facts, evidence and data and not based on
anecdotes; findings should be specific, concise and supported by strong quantitative or qualitative
evidence. Sources of information need to be properly identified and listed in an annex. Recommendations
need to be supported by a specific set of findings. Recommendations should be action oriented, practical
and specific, with defined responsibility for the action

jobs.title: Enumerador - Carabobo
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. La misión de Acted es aportar asistencia humanitaria inmediata a aquellos que se encuentren en situación de necesidad al mismo tiempo que genera oportunidades a largo plazo para un crecimiento durable. Acted opera en contextos de catástrofe natural, conflicto armado y crisis socioeconómica.

Actualmente, Acted está buscando un/a enumerador/a para integrar nuestro equipo en la misión de Venezuela.

Bajo la supervisión del/de la Asistente MEAL el/la enumerador/a se encargará de la recolección de información mediante el levantamiento de encuestas y serán responsables del adecuado levantamiento, carga y resguardo de dichas encuestas y de la información contenida cumpliendo con los estándares de transparencia, calidad y normativas de la organización.

**Funciones**

- Velar por la calidad de los datos levantados en el terreno: registro de encuestas, seguimiento de los planes diseñados para el levantamiento de la data.
- Contribuye al logro de las metas establecidas por Acted sobre el número de encuestas a levantar.
- Reporta oportunamente problemas técnicos-operativos que puedan presentarse durante el levantamiento de las encuestas y propone soluciones para gestionarlos, en coordinación con el gerente de proyecto, asistentes y lideres de terreno.
- Vela por el adecuado manejo de los equipos tecnológicos dispuestos por Acted para el levantamiento de las encuestas.
- El/la Enumerador/a asegura la adherencia con los principios humanitarios, políticas, herramientas, procesos, manuales, directrices y códigos de Acted.
- El Enumerador/a guardará estricta reserva de toda la información a la que tenga acceso y conocimiento a razón del desarrollo de encuestas y que sea de naturaleza privada, confidencial o cuya comunicación pueda causar perjuicio, asegurando el pleno cumplimiento de la política de protección de datos y los procedimientos operativos estándar de Acted. A su vez, deberá seguir los lineamientos técnicos y metodológicos que impartirá el equipo de Acted durante sus capacitaciones.
- Sera responsable de la digitalización, limpieza y aseguramiento de la calidad de la información generada durante la ejecución del proyecto. Este rol es esencial para mantener la organización y fiabilidad de los datos, contribuyendo directamente a prevenir errores y respaldar la toma de decisiones informadas.
- Transcripción de datos: realizar la transcripción fiel y eficiente de información contenida en diversos formatos (documentos físicos, actas, formularios, encuestas, audios, etc.) a bases de datos y hojas de cálculo, asegurando la integridad de los registros.
- Limpieza y normalización de datos: identificar, depurar y corregir datos erróneos, inconsistentes o duplicados. Estandarizar la información para garantizar uniformidad en formatos, terminología y estructuras, facilitando así su procesamiento y análisis posterior.
- Aseguramiento de la Calidad de los datos: implementar y ejecutar rigurosos procesos de verificación y validación (doble entrada, cotejo) para asegurar la exactitud, completitud y fiabilidad de la información transcrita, realizando auditorías periódicas.
- Mitigación de errores: desarrollar e implementar estrategias proactivas para prevenir la introducción de errores durante el proceso de digitalización.
- Gestión documental: planificar y ejecutar la organización, clasificación y archivo de documentos fuente (físicos) y registros digitales vinculados al proyecto, asegurando su trazabilidad, resguardo seguro y disponibilidad oportuna.
- Comunicación: mantener una comunicación fluida, clara y proactiva con el equipo del proyecto, especialmente con el Asistente MEAL, para aclarar dudas, reportar anomalías y asegurar la consistencia en el flujo de información.
- Apoyo Adicional: llevar a cabo cualquier otra tarea o actividad relacionada con la gestión y procesamiento de la información que le sea asignada por el Asistente MEAL, contribuyendo al logro de los objetivos del proyecto.

**Perfil deseado**

**Requisitos**

**Obligatorios:**

- Estudiante universitario/a en curso o egresado/a con título profesional, preferiblemente en áreas administrativas, ciencias sociales, técnicas u otras disciplinas afines al ámbito del proyecto.
- Experiencia previa en recolección, digitación o transcripción de datos (mínimo 1 año).
- Sólidos conocimientos de Microsoft Excel para el manejo de bases de datos.
- Capacidad de resolución de conflictos, control de multitudes y gestión del tiempo.

**Competencias:**

- Precisión y atención al detalle: demostrar una capacidad excepcional para la minuciosa revisión y verificación de datos, asegurando la exactitud y minimizando errores en la transcripción.
- Organización y proactividad: habilidad para gestionar eficientemente volúmenes significativos de documentación e información, manteniendo un sistema de archivo lógico y accesible.
- Capacidad para anticipar necesidades y tomar la iniciativa en la optimización de procesos de trabajo.
- Discreción y confidencialidad: compromiso absoluto con el manejo ético y la protección de la información sensible o confidencial del proyecto y la organización.
- Comunicación efectiva: capacidad para expresar ideas de manera clara y concisa, tanto de forma oral como escrita, facilitando la interacción con el equipo y la resolución de dudas sobre la documentación.
- Orientación a Resultados: fuerte enfoque en el cumplimiento de objetivos y plazos, manteniendo un alto estándar de calidad en todas las tareas asignadas y contribuyendo activamente al éxito del proyecto.
- Comunicación asertiva en entornos multiculturales, manteniendo principios de transparencia y rendición de cuentas

**Condiciones**

- Contrato de prestación de servicios a destajo bajo la figura de Honorarios Profesionales, con una modalidad de pago por día trabajado.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Carabobo
- Prestación de servicios de forma presencial con traslados recurrentes a las zonas afectadas por el doblete sísmico.

**Marketing & Communications Coordinator**

Location: Arequipa, Peru

Start date: March 2027 (flexible)

As the **Marketing & Communications Coordinator** you will be responsible for the authentic representation of Intiwawa for the public in various media channels. In this position, you create marketing materials for Intiwawa and its projects, such as social media posts, newsletters, blog articles, photo and video marketing content, as well as manage our website and social media platforms. You will report to the General Director and work closely and collaboratively with all areas of the German and Peruvian teams to promote Intiwawa’s image, projects, campaigns, media content as well as develop a communications strategy to further develop Intiwawa’s objectives.

**Responsibilities**

● Establish a communications strategy for stakeholders

**Requirements**

● Excellent English and Spanish skills, written and spoken

● Experience in Marketing Strategy and Social Media Management

● Excellent writing skills

● Photography, videography, and digital editing skills (desirable)

● Excellent self-management and organization skills

● High level of independence, creativity and responsibility

● Ability to work in a multicultural and collaborative environment

● Minimum 6 months commitment

**Details**

● The position is **voluntary** (unpaid) and full-time **(around 30 hours/week)**

● Flexible, unconventional schedule

● Low-cost housing available

● Work-related expenses are covered

● A certificate will be provided at the end of the term and letter of references can be requested

jobs.title: Chief of Party II, Honduras
jobs.description:
**NOTE: This recruitment is contingent upon donor approval.**

CRS seeks Chief of Party II candidates for the anticipated USDA Non-Emergency Food for Peace projects. These multi‑year, development-focused projects seek to combat chronic and acute malnutrition especially in children and mothers, strengthen early recovery and resilience, and support communities.

The Chief of Party II will provide vision, leadership and overall management of these large and complex projects to serve the poor and vulnerable. The incumbent’s strategic leadership, management and technical knowledge will ensure the delivery of high-quality programming and advance the position of CRS as a leading agency in the respective field. As a senior leader, the Chief of Party II will proactively manage security and mitigate security risks.

Honduras is a Central American country with Caribbean Sea coastlines to the north and the Pacific Ocean to the south. In Honduras, CRS promotes sustainable economic growth, youth empowerment, more peaceful and just societies, and help communities protect the environment while preparing for and responding to natural disasters.

CRS Honduras leads and implements programs in education, water-smart agriculture, emergency response, disaster risk resilience, youth development, peacebuilding, local partner capacity strengthening, and water. In 2024, CRS´ programs benefited more than 500,000 vulnerable individuals in Honduras in 16 departments. CRS partners with the USDA, BHA, FAO, foundations, private sector, the Government of Honduras and 12 local organizations to create transformational and lasting change in the lives of Honduras´ most vulnerable families.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Lead all aspects of the development, implementation and consolidation of the assigned project, including sharing how the project contributes to the thought leadership of the industry. Serve as the primary point of contact with the donor as well as public, private and non-government stakeholders.
- Ensure the project is designed and implemented to meet donor expectations in terms of timely and quality results and budget, including strategies for phase out and sustainability. Lead coordination efforts between program and operations leads to ensure CRS program quality standards are adhered to.
- Effectively lead senior programming and operations talent. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching and mentoring. Strategically tailor individual development plans and complete performance assessments for direct reports. Oversee the development of staffing plans and the recruitment process of senior staff.
- Proactively manage and mitigate risk by monitoring national and regional issues that may impact staff and programming. Ensure all CRS staff safety and security policies and plans are regularly updated and all staff understand and adhere to these policies.
- Promote, uphold and model a commitment to the efficient use of agency and donor resources.
- Ensure compliance with donor grants, including financial tracking and oversight of partner budgets, finance, administration and donor reporting. Approve program expenditures, budget adjustments, and cost modification requests to donors.
- Represent CRS programming in international circles, highlighting innovative work. Publish program results and deliver presentations. Oversee the development of communication strategies and materials, complying with donor and CRS’ branding and marketing requirements and procedures.
- Manage relationships with consortium partner organizations, including organization of review/planning workshops. Coordinate the roles and activities of staff from other consortium member organizations to ensure implementation is in line with CRS partnership principles.
- Create and maintain proper conditions for learning. Establish a safe environment to share ideas, solutions, and difficulties. Build the internal capacity to detect, analyze and respond quickly to deficiencies.
- Identify performance gaps and training opportunities for CRS and partner staff and ensure the design and delivery of high-quality training and technical assistance.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, International Relations or a relevant technical area.
- Minimum of 8 years of relevant management and technical experience.
- Minimum of 7 years’ experience managing donor funds, including multi country grants. Excellent knowledge and experience in budget management.
- Minimum of 5 years of staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Experience coaching and mentoring senior program staff.
- Demonstrated experience of successful program management, including management of complex, high-value, multi-activity projects, with complicated logistics.
- Established leader in sector as demonstrated by peer reviewed publications, conference presentations etc.

**Preferred Qualifications**
- Master’s degree in a related field.
- Experience engaging partners and strengthening partnerships. Knowledge of CRS partnership strategy.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
- Ability to represent and present at high levels.
- Excellent knowledge of MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems.
- Excellent strategic, analytical, systems thinking, andproblem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big pictureand ability to make sound judgment and decisions.
- Excellent relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Ability to strategically approach each relationship.
- Team leadership abilities with diverse and multi-disciplinary teams. Coaching/mentoring skills.
- Strong communication and presentation skills. Ability to develop tailored and persuasive messaging for varied audiences.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented mindset.
- **Required Languages:** Fluency in English and Spanish is required.
- **Travel:** Must be willing and able to travel up to 35%.
- **Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: Oficial de Cadena de Abastecimiento y Compras
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Barranquilla y Bogotá, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

El Oficial de Cadena de Abastecimiento y Compras es responsable de las compras requeridas en las bases, así como de la debida gestión de los activos, manejo del inventario, almacenamiento, transporte de bienes y personas, gestión de flotas de vehículos y apoyo logístico general al programa general en Ocaña Norte de Santander y municipios asignados de conformidad con el marco interno de Danish Refugee Council – DRC y las regulaciones impuestas por los donantes.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Compras**

- Garantizar la correcta ejecución de los procesos competitivos de compras para todas las solicitudes requeridas en la base.
- Realizar procesos de compras para la generación de acuerdos marco según la necesidad identificada en el plan de compras de la base.
- Asegurar la recepción de compras requeridas para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC.
- Realizar seguimiento y control de todas las solicitudes de compras.
- Asegurar el respaldo documental de todos los procesos de compras en sharepoint, con el fin de asegurar transparencia y trazabilidad en nuestros procesos de compras.
- Correcto registro de proveedores locales de acuerdo con los lineamientos de DRC
- Gestionar el desarrollo e implementación de contratos marco y estrategias de abastecimiento que generen eficiencias operativas para la base.
- Monitorear el avance de los procesos de compras en la base e identificar cuellos de botella o riesgos operativos, proponiendo medidas correctivas.

**Logística**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).
- Coordinar con el equipo de seguridad para asegurar una distribución logística acorde con las condiciones operacionales y de contexto.
- Planificar y asegurar la disponibilidad de kits humanitarios para respuesta de emergencia en los programas de DRC.
- Brindar soporte logístico a las operaciones de la base y a los municipios asignados, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos y los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Apoyar el mantenimiento y adecuado funcionamiento de las instalaciones de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Implementar mecanismos de control, seguimiento y verificación de los bienes y elementos asignados al personal y a los programas.
- Apoyar los procesos de verificación física, auditorías internas y revisiones operativas relacionadas con la gestión logística cuando sea requerido.

**Gestión de Inventarios y Activos**

- Control, seguimiento y aseguramiento del inventario de kits humanitarios de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios periódicos y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Implementación de mecanismos de control, conciliación y seguimiento de inventarios.
- Identificar riesgos, inconsistencias o desviaciones en la gestión de activos e inventarios, recomendando e implementando acciones correctivas y preventivas.
- Asegurar que toda la información relacionada con inventarios y activos esté actualizada y alineada con las directrices de Oficina Nacional y los donantes en el sistema ERP Dynamics.
- Asegurar el registro oportuno, la trazabilidad y la disponibilidad de los activos fijos, reportando y documentando cualquier incidente, pérdida, daño o baja de activos.
- Realizar verificaciones físicas periódicas de los activos y conciliarlas con los registros del sistema.
- Garantizar el adecuado respaldo documental de los movimientos de inventario y activos, asegurando transparencia, trazabilidad y cumplimiento de auditorías internas y externas.
- Coordinar las transferencias, asignaciones, préstamos y bajas de activos de acuerdo con las políticas y procedimientos vigentes de DRC.

**Gestión de Flota**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de gestión de flota de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Garantizar la disponibilidad de los vehículos requeridos para la ejecución de las actividades programáticas y operacionales.
- Coordinar las revisiones periódicas, mantenimientos preventivos y correctivos de los vehículos, y reportar oportunamente cualquier novedad o falla identificada.
- Mantener actualizada toda la documentación legal y operativa de la flota, gestionando oportunamente renovaciones de seguros, SOAT, revisiones técnico-mecánicas, permisos y demás requisitos aplicables.
- Monitorear el uso y consumo de combustible de la flota de la oficina local, identificando desviaciones y proponiendo acciones correctivas cuando sea necesario.
- Realizar seguimiento periódico a los logbooks y demás registros de flota, verificando la calidad de la información registrada, analizando tendencias de uso, kilometraje, consumo y mantenimiento para anticipar riesgos y establecer medidas correctivas o preventivas.
- Garantizar que los expedientes físicos y digitales de los vehículos se encuentren completos, organizados y disponibles para procesos de auditoría interna y externa.
- Promover el cumplimiento de las políticas de seguridad vial y uso adecuado de los vehículos por parte de los conductores y usuarios autorizados.

**Administración**

- Colaboración con la unidad de finanzas para el correcto registro de la cadena de abastecimiento.
- Coordinación con la unidad de finanzas para la oportuna ejecución de los pagos.
- Otras actividades que requiera la organización relacionada con la gestión logística en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en logística humanitaria, adquisiciones, transporte y distribución, almacenamiento y gestión de stocks para emergencias humanitarias.
- Buena comprensión de las normas y regulaciones de adquisiciones de los principales donantes internacionales.
- Buen conocimiento de la normatividad local a nivel de contrataciones.
- Excelentes conocimientos de MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Dominio intermedio de inglés será un valor agregado en el proceso.
- Capacidad analítica y resolutiva.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Seguridad Operacional (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Oficial Nacional de Seguridad Operacional tendrá las siguientes funciones y responsabilidades orientadas al fortalecimiento de la seguridad y el acceso institucional:

- Realizar análisis de contexto de riesgos para la seguridad operacional a nivel nacional y participar activamente en la construcción de procedimientos, protocolos, guías y herramientas para el acceso más seguro y seguridad operacional.
- Elaborar y dar seguimiento a las acciones propuestas por la sede central a ser implementadas en las Filiales, promoviendo su fortalecimiento a través de la implementación de la Política y Estrategia de Seguridad.
- Participar proactivamente en las comunicaciones con el Sistema Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos de Desastres junto con los programas de Socorro y otros pertinentes, para mantener a la Sociedad Nacional incluida en el sistema como auxiliar de los poderes públicos con funciones de complementariedad y manteniendo una participación en el seguimiento de las operaciones a nivel nacional.
- Garantizar la réplica de toda la información que se obtenga a través de formaciones, cursos, talleres u otros, para conformar una Oficina Nacional de Seguridad con un equipo técnico que garantice la continuidad de la información, así como la sostenibilidad de esta a lo largo del tiempo.
- Brindar asesoría en Acceso más Seguro al órgano de gobierno, gestión y operación de las Filiales para lograr una mayor aceptación, acceso y seguridad en las actividades, coordinando oportunamente las actividades y cronogramas de trabajo vinculados a la estrategia.
- Mantener una comunicación activa con los Componentes del Movimiento presentes en el país (CICR, IFRC) para generar espacios de trabajo articulado y complementario que apoye el fortalecimiento de la Sociedad Nacional aprovechando las fortalezas de cada enfoque.
- Participar en espacios de coordinación de la temática para implementar acciones de alcance nacional e intercambiar experiencias con otras Filiales.
- Garantizar estrictamente la confidencialidad de la información institucional.
- Trabajar activamente hacia el logro de los objetivos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumpliendo y trabajando bajo los Principios Fundamentales del Movimiento y realizando cualquier otra responsabilidad relacionada con el puesto asignado.

Reporte

El/La Oficial Nacional de Seguridad Operacional le reportará al/a la Director(a) General como supervisor inmediato.

Lugar de trabajo

Caracas, con disponibilidad requerida para movilizarse por el territorio nacional.

Requisitos y Perfil del Cargo

**Experiencia Requerida:**

- Haber sido personal rentado o voluntario de la institución por un período mínimo de dos (2) años.
- Demostrar capacidad de convocatoria y movilización dentro de la Sociedad Nacional.

**Cursos y Formación Obligatoria (Requerido):**

- Contar con los cursos aprobados de la plataforma E-learning en: Acceso Más Seguro, Stay Safe (los 3 niveles) y WORK.

**Conocimientos y Habilidades Requeridas:**

- Buenas habilidades analíticas y enfoque centrado en la resolución de problemas.
- Responsabilidad demostrable y excelente manejo del estrés.
- Capacidad para trabajar eficientemente en un equipo multicultural bajo presión y con flexibilidad de horarios.
- Capacidad para trabajar con precisión y cuidado en los detalles mínimos.
- Conocimiento y manejo en el uso de paquetes informáticos (Office, Adobe, etc.).
- Disposición constante al aprendizaje, de adquirir nuevos conocimientos e interés explícito de desarrollarse en un ambiente humanitario e internacional en el ámbito de seguridad.

**Aspectos Deseables:**

- Tener capacidad analítica y habilidades de trabajo en equipo, integrando a distintos niveles de la Sociedad Nacional.
- Haber realizado el curso **BSAFE** en la Plataforma de la ONU ([https://training.dss.un.org/](https://training.dss.un.org/)).
- Hablar otro idioma oficial del Movimiento (inglés, francés, portugués o árabe).

jobs.title: Field Documentation Officer || موثق/ـة ميداني/ـة
jobs.company: Syrian Center for Media and Freedom of Expression
jobs.description:
Announcement Date: 06/11/2026

Employer: Syrian Center for Media and Freedom of Expression (SCM)

Vacancy code: 05/Vdc2026

Application deadline: 15/11/2026

Program/ Project / Department: VDC Project –Reports to the Field Coordinator

Job title: Field Documentation Officer

Number of positions available: 4

Workstation: Syria

Expected starting date: 01 December 2026

Type and duration of contract: Temporary contract 8 months, renewable With a renewable three-month probationary period

**Roles and responsibilities**

- Conduct field-based documentation of human rights violations within the assigned geographical area, including identifying and documenting incidents and collecting information from victims, witnesses and other credible sources in accordance with SCM’s methodologies and documentation standards.
- Conduct interviews with victims, survivors, witnesses,family members and other relevant sources, ensuring informed consent, confidentiality, sensitivity and adherence to SCM’s protection and do-no-harm principles.
- Collect, verify and document testimonies and other relevant information and materials, including documents, photographs, videos and other available evidence, and ensure their proper entry and archiving in SCM’s documentation system.
- Maintain regular field presence and follow developments within the assigned geographical area, identifying incidents and documentation needs and reporting relevant developments to the Field Documentation Coordinator.
- Build and maintain a reliable network of local contacts and sources, including victims and affected communities, local actors and other relevant stakeholders, to support access to information and effective documentation.
- Coordinate with the Field Documentation Coordinator and other members of the documentation team, including OSINT investigators, to support verification, corroboration and follow-up of documented incidents.
- Undertake field missions and travel within the assigned geographical area as required for interviews, documentation and follow-up activities, taking into account relevant security and protection procedures.
- Ensure the confidentiality, security and protection of victims, witnesses, sources and information throughout the documentation process.
- Undertake other documentation-related tasks assigned by the direct supervisor in line with the objectives and methodologies of the project.

**Required skills and qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in law, human rights, social sciences or another relevant field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Previous experience in documenting human rights violations, field research, or related work is strongly preferred.
- Experience conducting interviews with victims, survivors, witnesses or other sources, including the ability to conduct sensitive interviews professionally and ethically.
- Good understanding of human rights documentation principles and methodologies.
- Ability and willingness to conduct regular fieldwork and travel within the assigned geographical area, including to locations required for documentation and interviews.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to build trust and engage respectfully with victims, witnesses and affected communities.
- Ability to assess information critically, identify inconsistencies and documentation gaps, and conduct appropriate follow-up with sources.
- Ability to use digital tools and documentation/database systems and to learn new technical tools required for the position.
- Ability to work independently in the field while maintaining effective coordination with the documentation team and coordinator.
- Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple documentation tasks and priorities.
- Commitment to confidentiality, professionalism, impartiality and human rights principles.
- Knowledge of International Human Rights Law and International Humanitarian Law is an asset.
- Experience with open-source research and verification is an asset.
- Fluency in Arabic
- Good command of English is an asset.

جهة العمل: المركز السوري للإعلام وحرية التعبير (SCM)

رمز الوظيفة: 05/Vdc2026

مهلة تقديم الطلبات: 15/11/2026

القسم/ البرنامج/ المشروع (التبعية الإدارية): مشروع توثيق الانتهاكات– يتبع للمنسق الميداني

اسم الوظيفة: موثق ميداني

عدد الشواغر المعلن عنها: 4

مكان العمل: سوريا

تاريخ المباشرة المتوقع: 01 ديسمبر 2026

نوع العقد وفترة التعاقد: عقد مؤقت
8 أشهر قابلة للتجديد مع فترة تجريبية 3 أشهر

**الدور والمسؤوليات**

- إجراء عمليات توثيق ميدانية لانتهاكات حقوق الإنسان ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، بما يشمل رصد الحوادث وتحديدها وتوثيقها، وجمع المعلومات من الضحايا والشهود وغيرهم من المصادر الموثوقة، وذلك وفقاً لمنهجيات المركز السوري للإعلام وحرية التعبير (SCM) ومعايير التوثيق المعتمدة لديه.
- إجراء مقابلات مع الضحايا والناجين والشهود وأفراد أسرهم وغيرهم من المصادر ذات الصلة، مع ضمان الحصول على الموافقة المستنيرة، والحفاظ على السرية، ومراعاة الحساسية في التعامل، والالتزام بمبادئ الحماية ومبدأ عدم إلحاق الضرر المعتمدة لدى المركز.
- جمع الإفادات والمعلومات والمواد ذات الصلة والتحقق منها وتوثيقها، بما في ذلك الوثائق والصور ومقاطع الفيديو وغيرها من الأدلة المتاحة، وضمان إدخالها وأرشفتها بشكل سليم في نظام التوثيق المعتمد لدى المركز.
- الحفاظ على حضور ميداني منتظم ومتابعة التطورات ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، ورصد الحوادث واحتياجات التوثيق، وإبلاغ منسق التوثيق الميداني بالتطورات ذات الصلة.
- بناء شبكة موثوقة من جهات الاتصال والمصادر المحلية والحفاظ عليها، بما يشمل الضحايا والمجتمعات المتضررة والجهات الفاعلة المحلية وأصحاب المصلحة المعنيين، بما يسهم في تسهيل الوصول إلى المعلومات وتعزيز فعالية عمليات التوثيق.
- التنسيق مع منسق التوثيق الميداني وأعضاء فريق التوثيق الآخرين، بمن فيهم المحققون المختصون بالاستقصاء مفتوح المصدر (OSINT)، لدعم عمليات التحقق من الحوادث الموثقة ومطابقة المعلومات والأدلة وتعزيزها ومتابعتها.
- تنفيذ المهام والزيارات الميدانية والتنقل ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، حسب الحاجة، لإجراء المقابلات وعمليات التوثيق وأنشطة المتابعة، مع مراعاة إجراءات الأمن والسلامة والحماية ذات الصلة.
- ضمان سرية وأمن وحماية الضحايا والشهود والمصادر والمعلومات طوال مراحل عملية التوثيق.
- تنفيذ أي مهام أخرى ذات صلة بالتوثيق، بما يتماشى مع أهداف المشروع ومنهجيات العمل المعتمدة.

**الشهادات والكفاءات المطلوبة**

- شهادة جامعية في القانون أو حقوق الإنسان أو العلوم الاجتماعية أو أي مجال ذي صلة، أو خبرة مهنية عملية معادلة في مجال ذي صلة.
- تُفضّل الخبرة السابقة في توثيق انتهاكات حقوق الإنسان أو إجراء البحوث الميدانية أو العمل في مجالات ذات صلة.
- خبرة في إجراء المقابلات مع الضحايا والناجين والشهود أو غيرهم من المصادر، بما في ذلك القدرة على إجراء المقابلات الحساسة بمهنية وأخلاقيات عالية.
- فهم جيد لمبادئ ومنهجيات توثيق انتهاكات حقوق الإنسان.
- القدرة والاستعداد للعمل الميداني بشكل منتظم والتنقل ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، بما في ذلك الوصول إلى المواقع اللازمة لأغراض التوثيق وإجراء المقابلات.
- امتلاك مهارات تواصل وتفاعل شخصية قوية، بما في ذلك القدرة على بناء الثقة والتعامل باحترام مع الضحايا والشهود والمجتمعات المتضررة.
- القدرة على تقييم المعلومات بشكل نقدي، وتحديد أوجه التناقض والثغرات في التوثيق، وإجراء المتابعة المناسبة مع المصادر.
- القدرة على استخدام الأدوات الرقمية وأنظمة التوثيق وقواعد البيانات، والاستعداد لتعلّم الأدوات التقنية الجديدة اللازمة لأداء مهام الوظيفة.
- القدرة على العمل بشكل مستقل في الميدان، مع الحفاظ على التنسيق الفعّال مع فريق التوثيق والمنسق المسؤول.
- امتلاك مهارات تنظيمية قوية والقدرة على إدارة مهام وأولويات متعددة متعلقة بالتوثيق.
- الالتزام بمبادئ السرية والمهنية والحياد ومبادئ حقوق الإنسان.
- تُعد المعرفة بالقانون الدولي لحقوق الإنسان والقانون الدولي الإنساني ميزة إضافية.
- تُعد الخبرة في البحث والتحقق باستخدام المصادر المفتوحة (OSINT) ميزة إضافية.
- إجادة اللغة العربية.
- يُعد امتلاك مستوى جيد في اللغة الإنجليزية ميزة إضافية.

jobs.title: Research Manager
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUND ON REACH**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to lead our research team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 1 year, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027.

## **Country profile**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea.

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community in Somalia. Data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to directly inform humanitarian response planning, as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Key areas of focus include:

**Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA):** REACH conducts the annual MSNA, whose findings feed into the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) workshop and, through it, the annual Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

**Food Security and Nutrition:** REACH conducts food security and nutrition assessments that feed into Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition analyses.

**Cash and Markets:** REACH provides research and analytical support to the Somali Cash Consortium and conducts market monitoring analysis as part of a harmonised approach, led by the Cash Working Group.

**Ad-hoc Research:** REACH conducts ad-hoc assessments as needs arise, including rapid needs assessments following sudden-onset shocks such as flooding, drought and conflict-induced displacement.

To ensure that research findings meaningfully inform humanitarian response planning, REACH shares data through formal coordination platforms, including the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), needs analysis and planning processes, the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, among others. Partner feedback is actively integrated to validate and triangulate findings, as well as to guide research design and geographic targeting.

## **FUNCTIONS**

REACH is seeking an experienced candidate who has previously managed teams and implemented projects in a complex humanitarian setting. Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, and in close coordination with the Country Representative and HQ, the Research Manager will be responsible for overseeing the implementation, development, and strategy of the research portfolio of the REACH Somalia mission. This includes managing the teams responsible for the MSNA, food security and nutrition assessments, the Somali Cash Consortium, market monitoring, and ad-hoc assessments such as rapid needs assessments.

The candidate should be comfortable representing REACH with donors and be able to coordinate and liaise with a range of senior external partners, including OCHA, cluster coordinators, UN agencies and NGOs. This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, humanitarian cluster, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager’s responsibilities include the following:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Direct management of international and national research staff across the MSNA, food security and nutrition, cash and markets, and ad-hoc assessment workstreams, including recruitment, appraisals, and capacity building;
- Day-to-day management of the research team, including the development of work plans and performance indicators, and development and implementation of capacity training plans to improve efficiency and performance;
- Conduct regular check-ins with staff within the unit, and promote team building, productivity and staff welfare as the main pastoral focal point for research staff;
- Provide regular support and technical backstopping;
- Take on additional work streams and management responsibilities as well as advise in strategic mission decision-making as a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), as required.

***RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant project and programme objectives, and REACH’s research cycle guidelines;
- Ensure that all (Senior) Research Officers are comprehensively briefed on objectives and expected outputs of research cycles, and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood;
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation for an assessment;
- For each research cycle, review ToRs before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that ToRs are validated before data collection begins;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning, data collection, and management;
- Monitor data collection, ensuring correct implementation in line with agreed ToRs, and keep track of progress and delays of all assessments throughout the research cycle;
- Work closely with the Field Manager and Ops teams to ensure logistics, finance, administration, security and HR processes directly related to REACH are appropriately implemented, alongside the relevant Acted departments.

***PORTFOLIO OVERSIGHT***

- Oversee the timely delivery of the annual MSNA, ensuring that findings are available in time to feed into the JIAF workshop and the HNRP, and support the team in preparing for and participating in the JIAF process;
- Oversee food security and nutrition assessments, ensuring that methodologies, timelines and outputs are aligned with IPC requirements and that data is made available to IPC analyses as planned;
- Oversee REACH’s research support to the Somali Cash Consortium, ensuring that deliverables meet consortium and donor requirements and timelines;
- Oversee market monitoring analysis, ensuring consistent, timely outputs that are used by Cash Working Group partners;
- Lead the planning and rapid deployment of ad-hoc assessments, such as rapid needs assessments, in response to emerging crises and partner information needs, in coordination with OCHA and the clusters.

***ANALYSIS AND DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure research staff maintain regular communication with HQ on progress and deadlines for written products;
- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs (i.e. reports, factsheets, briefs, presentations, etc.), complying with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Review all research products before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- Under supervision of HQ, ensure that research products are uploaded to relevant data portals, as specified in research ToRs;
- Under the direction of the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, engage in the dissemination of research products, including emails, presentations to coordination bodies, and bilateral meetings, such as with donors;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in conducting monitoring and evaluation as specified in the research ToRs and in line with REACH guidelines.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- With the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, identify information gaps in line with humanitarian priorities in Somalia, and identify advocacy and dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of REACH’s work;
- Lead on formalising synergies with other assessment and knowledge management actors, as well as strategic partnerships with key humanitarian stakeholders and decision makers;
- As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Somalia country strategy.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Represent REACH at the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG) and in other inter-agency coordination forums, and act as a key REACH focal point for OCHA on needs analysis and humanitarian programme cycle processes;
- Represent REACH in cluster and multi-sector meetings and technical working groups, including the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, and follow up on technical issues identified in these forums;
- In coordination with the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, present research findings to relevant partners to enhance their use and impact;
- Ensure that external communications with partners and key stakeholders, including UN agencies, local and national authorities, and NGOs, are conducted and documented as appropriate;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in external engagement on REACH strategy and, when requested, in fundraising and grants management.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs, and will ensure that the research team does the same. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

The Research Manager is also responsible for ensuring that all interactions with crisis-affected populations are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner, and that communities are adequately consulted and informed about REACH programme objectives, activities and methodologies.

## **REQUIREMEnTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international relations, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, social research, or similar).
- **Years of work experience** At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis.
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative research experience, including sampling, methodology design and analysis. Ability to provide technical oversight of research products to a high standard.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Experience with the humanitarian programme cycle (HNRP/JIAF) and with humanitarian coordination forums (e.g. ICCG, clusters) is strongly preferred.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA-type research, food security and nutrition assessments and/or IPC processes, and cash and markets research is highly desirable.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high-level presentations and briefings to senior external audiences.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to manage multiple research cycles in parallel with tight deadlines in a complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the Horn of Africa region is desirable, or in any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’660 **CHF** and 3’720 **CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 **USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees
