jobs.title: Senior Project Officer - Private Sector Engagement and Markets
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Senior Project Officer - Private Sector Engagement and Markets

**Reports to:** Program Manager - Church Lands and PSE

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by November 20, 2026 no later than 11:59pm.

**Background**

Under its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation strategic priority area, CRS Uganda supports nature-based solutions, climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods. Forest Flavors (FF) is a 3-year initiative (FY26 - FY29) that applies a market systems development (MSD) and private-sector-led approach to strengthen inclusive, commercially viable and nature-positive agroforestry value chains, with an initial focus on coffee, cocoa, vanilla and spices. The project seeks to improve smallholder and dioceses market participation and returns, support enterprises to test and scale inclusive business models, and strengthen climate-resilient agroforestry landscapes.

Forest Flavors will work mainly across 3 regions namely; Central region covering Luwero, Masaka and Lugazi, Western region covering Kasese and Northern region covering Gulu directly engaging with private sector actors, smallholder farmers and their organizations, service providers, financial institutions and relevant public and civil-society stakeholders to address market-system constraints and crowd in sustainable investment. Church and diocesan assets where feasible will contribute to viable business and landscape models where land tenure, governance, user rights, market demand and the business case are validated. The project will use a diagnose, prioritize, co-create, invest, learn and scale approach, with decisions guided by commercial viability, inclusion, environmental contribution and the potential for replication.

**Job Summary:**

Based in CRS Uganda’s Kampala office, **the Senior Project Officer (SPO)** **- Private Sector Engagement and Markets** will coordinate and support the implementation of Forest Flavors (FF) activities under the Church Lands and Private Sector Engagement (CL3) project. The role will focus on diocesan and private sector engagement, business development service delivery, and facilitating linkages to key market enablers, including finance, technical assistance, standards and certification bodies, and other relevant service providers.

The SPO will identify and engage potential private sector actors (PSAs), in coordination with the Project Manager - CL3, and facilitate the co-creation of commercially viable, inclusive and nature-positive agroforestry business models. This will include identifying partnership opportunities to address systemic market constraints, coordinating business case development and tailored business development services, and supporting capacity strengthening in marketing, financial management and inclusive business practices. The SPO will also coordinate and follow up on activities implemented through private sector partners, verify and manage milestones, budgets and deliverables, and ensure timely activity implementation and reporting.

Through effective coordination, facilitation and relationship management, the SPO will support market linkages, strengthen enterprise, diocese and smallholder participation in priority agroforestry value chains, and contribute to continuous learning and improved project results.

The role will work closely with the Project Manager - CL3 and the wider FF team, as well as relevant technical, MEAL, finance and operations colleagues. This is a technical coordination role and has no direct staff supervisory responsibilities.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead the planning, coordination, and high-quality implementation of assigned activities in alignment with approved annual workplans, budgets, and CRS program quality standards. This includes mapping and onboarding potential Private Sector Actors (PSAs), collaborating with stakeholders to co-create commercially viable business models across priority value chains (coffee, cocoa, vanilla, and spices), and maintaining rigorous activity trackers to manage deliverables, risks, and implementation milestones.
- Coordinate technical assistance and business development support for private sector partners / MSMEs and, dioceses based on identified needs and follow up on agreed actions to strengthen commercial performance, market access and investment readiness.
- Ensure, gender equality, youth inclusion and social inclusion are considered in partner diagnostics, business model design, service delivery, access to assets and finance, and tracking of economic benefits.
- Coordinate implementation follow-up with PSAs and project stakeholders, including periodic partner check-ins and targeted monitoring visits when required; document bottlenecks and agree practical corrective actions.
- Support portfolio reviews and learning processes to assess whether supported models should be expanded, adapted, paused or discontinued based on evidence of commercial viability, inclusion, environmental contribution and scale potential.
- Coordinate stakeholder engagement and represent the project, as delegated, in technical meetings with PSAs, service providers, financial institutions, relevant government and sector actors, and Church/diocesan stakeholders.
- Work with the Project Manager and relevant CRS colleagues to monitor activity expenditure against approved budgets, flag resource or implementation risks early, and support timely planning of procurement, logistics and technical assistance.
- Coordinate technical inputs and support for assigned activities to ensure deliverables are completed to agreed standards and within approved timelines.
- Work with finance, operations, technical colleagues and partners to ensure required resources and administrative processes are planned in time to support implementation.
- Compile and review activity progress updates, maintain evidence of milestone completion, and provide timely inputs to consolidated project progress reports.
- Maintain complete and organized documentation for assigned activities, including partner engagement records, due diligence, business cases, agreements where applicable, milestone evidence, lessons learned and case studies, in line with CRS and donor requirements.
- Strengthen partnerships and engagement with church and partner staff using CRS partnership principles, tools, and approaches, ensuring mutual accountability, collaboration, long-term impact and proactively address partnership challenges,

***Required Languages*** - English fluency, including excellent oral and written skills, required. Fluent in local Ugandan languages from the Central or Western or Northern regions would be an added advantage.

***Travel*** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 50 %.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

- Analysis and problem-solving skills with ability to make sound judgment
- Good relationship management skills and the ability to work closely with local partners
- Proactive, results-oriented and service-oriented
- Attention to details, accuracy and timeliness in executing assigned responsibilities
- Deep commitment to land restoration

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** None

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Internal:** Pram Manager – Church lands and PSE (CL3), Program Manager -Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Head of Programs, Snr. Ag, Markets and Livelihoods Advisor, Head of Operations, MEAL team, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI), Operations and Finance team, Regional and HQ Forest Flavors teams

**External:** Church and Diocese focal points, local partner staff and relevant national, district, and other government stakeholders, community leaders

*\*\*\*Our Catholic identity is at the heart of our mission and operations. Catholic Relief Services carries out the commitment of the Bishops of the United States to assist the poor and vulnerable overseas. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.*

*Disclaimer: This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.*

**CRS' talent acquisition procedures reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.**

**CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.
- **Agency Leadership Competencies:**
- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: Collective Sudan (CCS) Capacity Sharing and Localization Manager, Sudan
jobs.description:
**Location:** Darfur (roving), Sudan

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) ☐ **Level 3** X **Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

**About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

**The Program / Department / Team**

Prosper Global's Sudan crisis response seeks to meet the humanitarian needs of vulnerable Sudanese and other conflict-affected people across the country. Prosper Global Sudan is recognized as a leader in market systems, agricultural, and food security and building on this experience, the MC Sudan humanitarian program will layer in resilience and other program activities where appropriate and feasible to do so. Assistance is delivered with a focus on needs, in partnership with local actors and civil society.

Collective Sudan is an innovative nexus Consortium platform formed in August 2023, bringing together 19 organizations committed to delivering more effective assistance through a harmonized cash-plus approach. Guided by local knowledge, global best practice and evidence-based adaptation, Collective Sudan works across the country – including hard-to-reach areas – to provide inclusive, scalable, and integrated interventions that meet urgent needs while supporting foundations for recovery and resilience. By leveraging cash and markets to address multi-sectoral basic needs, Collective Sudan strengthens local agency, civil society and promotes economic stability while catalysing more coordinated, efficient and impactful humanitarian action and recovery.

By positioning cash as the default modality, Collective Sudan enables choice and dignity aligned with accountability and people-centred design, while reducing harmful coping strategies and supporting local markets. CVA is faster, more cost-efficient than in-kind aid, and strongly preferred by communities. Through CVA and complementary interventions, Collective Sudan addresses complex, multi-sectoral needs, supports localization, and promotes economic recovery.

**The Position**

The Capacity Sharing Manager provides strategic and technical leadership for the design, coordination, and delivery of capacity strengthening across the Collective Sudan (CCS), with a strong emphasis on advancing localization and partner-led programming. This role ensures a coherent, consortium-wide approach to strengthening national NGO partners across technical (CVA), organizational, and systems capacities, combining strategic oversight with targeted hands-on support where needed. The Manager leads the development of capacity strengthening strategies, frameworks, tools, and workplans, ensuring alignment with CCS program priorities, donor expectations, and global best practice.

The Manager works closely with the Deputy Chief of Party, Partnerships Manager, Programs Advisor and other members of the CCS Secretariat, as well as all partner organizations to ensure that capacity strengthening is contributing to improved quality, accountability, and sustainability of programming.

**Essential Responsibilities**

Program Management

- Coordinate with CCS Secretariat and national and international partner teams on planning and monitoring implementation of CCS CVA activities.

Technical Support

- Provide technical support and guidance for quality CVA implementation through active support and accompaniment with partners as needed.
- Develop and disseminate harmonized CCS tools, guidelines, and best practices to support effective CVA implementation.
- Ensure CVA program implementation is in line with sector best practice and the highest feasible quality standards while balancing current humanitarian imperatives.
- Facilitate peer-to-peer learning and knowledge exchange among consortium members.
- Collaborate with MEL teams to refine indicators and methodologies to measure the impact and effectiveness of CVA programming.
- Lead or contribute to the documentation of lessons learned, case studies, and evidence generation.

Capacity Development

- Working closely with Capacity Building and Localization Coordinator, demonstrate a focus on the capacity strengthening of national NGOs in the nascent CVA space in Sudan, ensuring sustainability of response and contributing toward localization.
- Conduct or update Cash Capacity Assessments on a periodic basis to measure progress and organizational technical development
- Develop and deliver tailored capacity-building initiatives, including training, mentoring, and on-the-job accompaniment support for staff.

Strategy

- Continuously review and advise on adaptations and adjustments to the CCS CVA programming for growth and sustainability, considering access and liquidity environment.
- In collaboration with INGO national, regional and global cash experts, support the development of a consortium-wide CVA strategy.
- Recognize opportunities for innovative action and explore implementation possibilities with the CCS, including providing technical and management support to pilot CVA programming utilizing alternative or digital financial solutions including NFC cards, mobile money, cryptocurrency, and other vouchers modalities.
- Maintain strong and transparent communication with consortium partners at all levels.

Finance & Compliance Management

- Ensure that consortium partner CVA activities are compliant with donor and grant holder rules and regulations, including strengthening national partner reconciliation and financial procedures as they relate to cash programs.
- Advise partners on the mapping, selection, management, contracting, and use of financial service providers.

Representation and Coordination

- Support Protection Manager and DCOP to scale referral intakes and outgoings to complementary sectoral services and to access MPCA.
- Assist the Cash Working Group with various technical subgroups, such as the MEB working group, FSP working group and others as needed.

**Safeguarding Responsibility**

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

**Accountable to:**

CCS Secretariat,CCS National Partner Organizations, CCS International Partner Organizations, CCS International Partner Regional and Global Cash Units, Prosper Global Programs, Operations and Finance teams, Regional and HQ Technical Support Units

**REPORTS DIRECTLY TO:** CCS Deputy Chief of Party

Workplans for the expert will be developed primarily by the CCS Secretariat team with inputs from the CCS Technical Working Group (currently made up of cash technical focal points from each of the INGO) and the CCS Steering Committee (consisting of all INGO Country Directors / Senior Management).

GENERAL

- Ensure all capacity strengthening activities uphold Prosper Globaland consortium commitments to safeguarding, gender equality, and localization, and promote these principles across partner engagement and programming.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

- Actively learns safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

None

**Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** The CVA Manager will be hosted by Prosper Global but managed within the Cash Consortium of Sudan structure. 1) They will report directly to the CCS Deputy Chief of Party for technical and day-to-day oversightwhile2)Prosper Global partnership team will act as the administrative manager – as the lead agency for the CCS and the grant holder for sub-grantees.

**Works Directly With:** CCS Secretariat,CCS Partner Organizations, Prosper Global Sudan Partnerships, Local authorities, Operations and Finance teams, Regional and HQ Technical Support Units

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

**Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, economics, business administration, international development, or related field.
- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in humanitarian or development programming, with at least 2 years supporting Localization and Capacity Strengthening or Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) or livelihood interventions.
- Demonstrated experience in training, mentoring, or organizational capacity strengthening with national NGOs or community-based organizations.
- Experience working with or through local partners, preferably in consortium or multi-agency settings.
- Sound understanding of CVA programming principles
- Strong facilitation and adult learning skills, able to adapt content to different literacy and experience levels.
- Proven ability to build trust and collaboration with diverse stakeholders, including local NGOs, community groups, and consortium partners.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills in Arabic and English (written and verbal).
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly within Sudan, including to reasonable field and hard-to-reach areas.

**Success Factors**

The successful Capacity Sharing Manager will combine deep technical knowledge of cash transfer programming with practical experience in supporting and developing partners. They will demonstrate creativity and adaptability in addressing challenges, particularly in complex or conflict-affected contexts. The officer will have strong communication and interpersonal skills to engage a range of stakeholders and foster effective partnerships. They will be experienced in designing, leading, and supporting capacity development initiatives, helping partners improve their systems and practices. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic environments with many stakeholders, manages multiple priorities efficiently, and approaches challenges with problem-solving and accountability. Clear, collaborative communication, and teamwork are central to success in this role.

**Living Conditions/ Environmental Conditions**

This position is based in Nyala, Darfur but will be roving across all Darfur states (candidate will be hosted by different partners in the consortium depending on state) .The position requires up to 60% domestic travel to support state programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

**Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

**Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work. We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

**Safeguarding & Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [**Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies**](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline **integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org**).

Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Global Purchasing Data Coordinator
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## About the Role

Seeking a data professional with 3+ years of experience to lead the SAP Purchasing Data Team. You will optimize tools, drive accurate SAP data entry, and collaborate with Procurement & Finance to empower supply chain operations for our farmers.

## Responsibilities

- Lead the SAP Purchasing Data Team to drive execution excellence by ensuring high accuracy and timeliness in processes, timely closure of purchase orders, and consistent on-time payments
- Own purchasing data team KPI. Collaborate with the team to ensure they are accurate, using them to prioritize improvements and manage team performance.
- Own purchasing data entry and Payment Flow for critical supply chain operations by working closely with Procurement, Sourcing and Finance. This will ultimately support procurement requisitions, receiving inputs, sending payments, and other data in between.
- Lead cross-functional collaboration by designing and facilitating recurring and ad-hoc meetings with Procurement, Inventory Data, Payments, and Tech teams. Establish clear agendas, track action items to closure, and optimize meeting structures to minimize duplication and enhance overall efficiency.
- Develop your team through regular check-ins, team meetings, and Performance and Development Reviews. Over time, raise the performance expectations.
- Own the Closure of Open POs (purchase orders) by leading weekly reviews and ensuring timely resolution.
- Drive Innovation in Tools & Best Practices
- Provide strategic leadership in developing tools and best practices that empower the team, strengthen process consistency, and scale operational excellence across the Department
- Lead data quality initiatives and establish standardized practices that elevate operational excellence, enhance efficiency, and strengthen customer service. Drive continuous improvement through effective project management and ensure sustainable adoption by fostering stakeholder alignment, capacity building, and change management.
- Prevent fraud and loss by implementing strong controls, conducting periodic data analysis, and escalating anomalies to leadership to proactively identify and mitigate risks of fraud or loss
- Own the cash forecasting process via a robust annual forecasting process, monthly budget updates, ongoing approval process with finance and timely payment support. Own collaboration with the payment team to flag upcoming payments, the root cause of Late payments and flag urgent payments.
- Standard costing data set up: Implementing quarterly standard costing updates in collaboration with the accounting team, in order to ensure accurate accounting books.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong data and analytical skills; Comfort with advanced Excel; experience working in SAP preferred.
- Incredible attention to detail – can pick out a mistake in a data set.
- Creativity and strong problem-solving skills; constantly looks for alternative solutions to problems.
- Excellent stakeholder coordination skills; strong writer and verbal communicator who can negotiate with internal clients and be persuasive but who is also humble and open to other viewpoints.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Nairobi, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya

## Application Deadline

2 February 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Uganda Field Operations Lead (Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Uganda program, founded in 2014, provides more than 34,000 farmers with quality farm supplies as well as fruit trees like avocados. Our team in Uganda is headquartered in Jinja, close to the districts we serve, and supported by a small presence in Kampala. One Acre Fund works in the eastern region of Uganda, primarily in the districts of Iganga, Jinja, Kamuli, and Buikwe.

## **About the Role**

As the Field Operations Lead, you will drive core seasonal activities, manage regional teams, and spearhead program expansion. You will deliver impact targets through rigorous field execution, coach Regional Leads, and represent the department.

You will report to the Head of Field Programs.

## **Responsibilities**

**Vision / Strategy:**

- Lead the field implementation of the Uganda Vision and Strategy and drive up farmer impact in the region served.
- Identify and implement the resources, processes, and systems required to achieve the vision and strategy in the region served.
- Lead the design and setting up of OKRs for the department and support the Regional Leads to set OKRs that translate the vision and strategy into executable activities.

**Season execution: coffee program execution and tree mobilisation**

- Own the season execution plan end to end by making sure every training in the season calendar is delivered on time, to standard, and at target attendance in each region.
- Lead field mobilisation for the tree programme.
- Track weekly execution against plan using KPIs and data.
- Standardise and document field protocols and tools so they are applied consistently across regions.

**Team Management:**

- Manage and coach 3+ Regional Leads on professional development, regional performance, and day-to-day problem-solving.
- Participate in all aspects of regional operations throughout the season, including staff recruitment and leadership development.
- Supervise and sign off on the monthly payroll process so that salaries, transport costs and bonuses for all field staff are paid accurately and on time.

**Expansion:**

- Lead field rollout each season and ensure programme implementation objectives are met.
- Develop a clear rollout plan for every expansion season: site readiness, staffing deployment, timelines, operational needs and risks.
- Work with Government Relations and local leadership to ensure new sites are operationally ready and authorisations are in place.
- Coordinate with Procurement and Logistics to ensure supplies, logistics and training materials are ready before rollout.

**Impact and tree programme follow-up:**

- Work with the Impact and Innovations teams to roll out new coffee agronomy practices and training topics through the field team.
- Supporting the design and implementation of impact-centric trials and interventions by working together with the Social Behavioral Change and Product Innovations teams.
- Coordinate the collection of field data that allows us to derive insights related to impact e.g. on GAP adoption or prevalence of pests & diseases in the field.
- Coordinate with the Impact team on surveys that measure training success and behaviour change.

**Budget:**

- Co-create the annual Field Operations budget and monitor it monthly through a budget-versus-actuals (BVA) review; flag material variances and look for cost-saving opportunities.
- Support donor reporting needs, including grant BVAs for the program.

**Stakeholder management and Partnerships:**

- Coordinate and take part in key regional partnership meetings.
- Handle internal and external relationships, including government, district government officials, and other external partners in liaison with other relevant teams in the organization.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 5-7 years of experience in field operations, programme delivery or a similar role, and at least ~2 years in management, ideally in agriculture, rural development or last-mile distribution.
- Demonstrated experience managing people, ideally managers or team leads.
- Experience delivering seasonal or time-bound operations at scale.
- Experience with expansion, scale-up, or new-site launches is a strong advantage.
- Willingness to travel regularly to field sites across Uganda

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Jinja, Uganda

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Contract Duration**

2 Years

## **Eligibility**

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

## **Application Deadline**

01 February 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Senior Director, Internal Audit
jobs.description:
**Location: Europe (Netherlands, France, Belgium, Switzerland)**

**Status: Full-Time, Regular**

**Starting Salary: €90,000 commensurate with professional experience and internal equity**

**Closing Date:** Submit application by **20 November**

## [**Risk Level**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en)**: X Level 3 ☐Level 2 ☐Level 1**

- (Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.
- Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.
- Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

### **The Unit**

The Internal Audit Unit (IAU) operates within the Ethics and Compliance Department (ECD) and reports directly to the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO). The Senior Director of Internal Audit also has direct access to the Chair of the Joint Audit and Risk Committee (JARC). The IAU's role is to provide objective assurance that Prosper Global's business risks are being managed appropriately and that the agency's risk management and internal control framework is operating effectively. The IAU actively reviews, among other things, the reliability and integrity of financial and operating information as well as the systems established by the agency to ensure compliance with Prosper Global's policies and procedures, donor policies and regulations, and US, UK, Netherlands and host country laws and regulations.

### **The Position**

The Senior Director, Internal Audit (SDIA) provides independent, objective assurance and strategic insight to Prosper Global's leadership and the JARC. The role manages the organization's internal audit function and helps strengthen governance, risk management, compliance, and internal control systems across a complex global operating environment.

The SDIA develops and executes a risk-based internal audit strategy that evaluates key enterprise risks. Working closely with senior leadership, country teams, and corporate functions, the SDIA identifies opportunities to strengthen accountability, improve organizational effectiveness, safeguard resources, and support mission achievement.

The position serves as a trusted advisor to leadership and the Board, providing forward-looking analysis, practical recommendations, and objective assurance regarding the effectiveness of Prosper Global's control environment.

### **Essential Responsibilities**

#### **Vision and Strategy**

- Partners with stakeholders to develop and execute the IAU strategy, ensuring the delivery of high quality, risk-based audit and advisory services that respond to organizational priorities and evolving risk.
- Evaluates the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls associated with new business models and innovative funding mechanisms.
- Ensures the IAU delivers meaningful assurance, actionable recommendations, and risk insights that strengthen internal controls, support effective risk management, and enhance organizational performance and accountability.
- Develops audit reports, presentations, and communications that are clear, concise, objective, and impactful, enabling management and governance bodies to understand key risks, make informed decisions, and take timely corrective actions.

#### **Personal Development**

- Consistently strives to exceed expectations; demonstrates flexibility, resilience, and the ability to maintain positive relationships and composure, even under difficult circumstances.
- Maintains high ethical standards and treats people with respect and dignity.
- Demonstrates an awareness of their personal strengths and development needs, modeling non-defensive behavior and openness to feedback.
- Builds a culture of feedback and learning, so IAU reports are viewed by agency management as tools for improved compliance, performance, service delivery and achievement of mission outcomes.
- Always demonstrates sound judgment and welcomes new ideas and bold thinking. Implements innovative approaches and evaluates their impact.
- Shares information proactively and appropriately, helping to create a trusting, collaborative team environment that supports reasoned risk-taking and risk assessment.

#### **Internal Audit Services**

- Documents, maintains, and periodically reviews the Internal Audit program, including audit methodologies and procedures, to ensure alignment with Prosper Global's policies and applicable donor requirements.
- Supports special scope audits as requested by the CECO, other Executive Staff or the JARC.
- Uses appropriate reporting and governance channels to bring organizational conflicts of interest and other significant internal control or compliance issues to the attention of the CECO, senior management, and, where appropriate, the JARC.
- Maintains expert knowledge of Prosper Global's policies and procedures and remains current on applicable donor rules, regulations and industry practices.
- Maintains systems and records that ensure the security, completeness and retention of Internal Audit documentation and historical records.
- Presents audit findings and recommendations to senior management and other stakeholders, as appropriate.
- Analyzes information from audit, assurance, compliance and review activities across the organization (e.g., donor audits, external reviews, and compliance monitoring) to inform the IAU's audit strategy and risk management approach.
- Provides independent advice and insight on internal controls, risk management, and governance considerations related to system design, process improvements, and organizational automation initiatives.
- Provides periodic updates to the JARC regarding audit activities, significant findings, control deficiencies, and the status of management corrective action efforts.

#### **Team Management**

- Fosters and sustains a culture of mutual respect, collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement where team members are empowered to achieve excellence.
- Sets clear expectations, promotes accountability, and supports professional growth through ongoing coaching, feedback, and performance management.
- Leads, supervises, mentors, and develops IAU staff, ensuring the team possesses the skills and resources necessary to deliver high quality audit and advisory services.
- Partners with country and regional leadership to identify and prioritize control gaps, audit findings, and other identified areas for improvement.
- Strengthens the IAU's data analytics and continuous auditing capabilities to enhance risk assessment, improve audit effectiveness, and facilitate remote testing and monitoring of international operations.
- Leverages technology and data-driven insights to increase audit coverage, identify emerging risks, and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of audit activities.

#### **Field Audits**

- Subject to risk priorities and resource availability, leads or oversees the execution of approximately 2 to 4 field audits annually, including periodic travel to international field locations.
- Conducts or directs audits and special reviews identified through the annual audit plan, emerging risk assessments, management requests, or other organizational priorities.

#### **Coordination**

- Partners closely with the COO, GC, CFO, Corporate Finance, Grant Compliance Support Unit, Global Procurement and Logistics, International Finance, Program Operations teams, Human Resources, and the Global Controller to ensure Internal Audit activities remain aligned with Prosper Global's evolving risks, operations, policies and procedures.
- Coordinates with other ECD functions to facilitate information sharing, support risk-based decision making, and ensure significant audit findings, and fraud and corruption indicators, are appropriately considered and addressed.
- Collaborates with external auditors as necessary and assists the Global Controller or International Finance Department in responding to relevant inquiries.
- Serves as a standing member of the Enterprise Risk Management Committee, providing insight regarding key risks, control effectiveness, emerging trends, and organizational risk efforts.
- Fosters strong working relationships across global and field operations.

#### **Safeguarding Responsibilities**

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

Internal Auditors (1)

### **Accountability**

- **Reports directly to**: Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO)
- **Works directly with**: Field personnel, including Country Directors, Regional Operations Directors, Regional Vice Presidents, Country Finance Managers and finance team members, and any Internal Audit team members in countries; International Finance; Grant Compliance Support Unit; Global Procurement and Logistics; Operations teams; Human Resources; Global Controller
- **Governance access**: Direct and independent access to the Chair of the JARC while continuing to report to the CECO; makes periodic presentations to the JARC

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

- A degree in Business Administration, Accounting and/or Finance and Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credentials are required. Additional certifications such as CPA, CISA, CFE, CRMA or equivalent are strongly preferred.
- At least 10 years of progressive internal audit, risk management, compliance or assurance experience.
- Significant experience leading audit functions in complex multinational organizations.
- Experience conducting audits in humanitarian, international development, non-profit or similarly regulated environments.
- Demonstrated knowledge of US government, EU, and major institutional donor compliance frameworks.
- Knowledge of international internal audit standards.
- Experience engaging directly with boards, audit committees or equivalent governance bodies.
- Excellent writing and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with both financial and non-financial audiences.
- Experience working overseas, with strong interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills.

### **Success Factors**

The successful candidate is a collaborative and highly credible leader who can balance independence with partnership. They possess exceptional judgment, resilience, and the ability to communicate complex risks in a clear and practical manner. They are comfortable engaging with senior executives, Board members, donors, and field teams operating in challenging environments.

The SDIA demonstrates intellectual curiosity, sound professional skepticism, cultural awareness, and a commitment to continuous improvement. They foster trust while holding themselves and others accountable to the highest standards of integrity and performance.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The location of the position is flexible within continental Europe where Prosper Global is registered and able to employ staff. The position will entail up to 40% travel to field locations, including program locations that may include insecure or harsh environments.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

### **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

jobs.title: Finance Intern - the Occupied Palestinian Territories
jobs.description:
**Work Context**

CESVI is an Italian NGO founded in 1985 and based in Bergamo, Italy. With a strong commitment to humanitarian aid and sustainable development, CESVI operates in over 20 countries worldwide, including Palestine. The organization focuses on supporting vulnerable communities through emergency relief and development programs, while also promoting environmental sustainability. Its mission is rooted in solidarity and the belief that development should be driven by local empowerment and global cooperation.

**Focus on oPt**

CESVI has been working in Palestine since 1994, and it has developed over the years an expertise in the WASH, Solid Waste Management (SWM), and site management sectors, implementing both emergency and development interventions in both the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. CESVI programmes are supported by strong partnerships with relevant actors in the sector and through strong commitment to coordination and collaboration.

In response to the situation in the Gaza Strip, CESVI has been expanding and consolidating its presence in the strip, through implementation of emergency response interventions. WASH and Site Management represent the core business of CESVI in Gaza, with activities implemented across multiple locations and in partnership with different local, national, and international actors.

We are currently seeking an Intern to join the OPT Mission, supporting the Finance Department, **Based in Amman – Jordan**.

**Job Description**

The **Finance Intern** will report to the **OPT Finance Manager**.

This internship offers a valuable opportunity to gain hands-on experience in finance and humanitarian field operations within an international NGO setting.

Specific tasks, Support with:

- Financial Document Control
- Audits
- Budget Monitoring
- Accounting
- Finance Systems and Process Improvement

(Specific tasks will be defined at the mission level upon arrival)

**Essential Requirements**

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field. Master's degree preferred.
- Strong understanding of financial principles, budgeting, and accounting practices.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office package, especially Excel.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate financial concepts to non-financial staff.
- Fluency in English and Italian is required.

**We offer**

- **Duration**: 12 months
- **Reimbursement**: 750 euro
- Health insurance
- VISA reimbursement
- 1 return flight and VISA run flight as needed

**SAFEGUARDING**

Cesvi has a zero-tolerance approach to any harm to, or exploitation of, a child or a vulnerable adult by any of our staff, related persons or partners.

Cesvi commitment to being a safe organization begins with the staff recruitment process which includes meticulous checks, such as criminal records checks or check disclosure of previous convictions, to ensure children and vulnerable people are safeguarded and abuse is prevented. Safeguarding checks are part of the selection process performance.

**HEALTH SAFEGUARDING**

CESVI pays particular attention to safeguarding the health of all the human resources of the Organisation. Therefore, in order to protect its staff, an assessment of their suitability for the position in each mission is carried out before departure. Such assessment is done by the Occupational Doctor of the Organisation, who will also examine the vaccination coverage.

*Due to the high volume of applications received, we are unable to respond to all candidates. Only those shortlisted and contacted for an initial interview will be updated on the status of their application.*

jobs.title: Regional Solutions Adviser - Syria & Hosting Countries
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

Candidates with management/advisory level experience within the humanitarian context, specifically those with deep understanding of the Syria context, displacement dynamics, and durable solutions frameworks.

To succeed in this role candidates will need to be strong and experienced in donor engagement, business development, and grant management, as well as experience in project management i.e. coordinating and managing programmes across multiple countries and stakeholders.

Strong strategic planning, analytical, and communication skills are also a requirement for this position.

**What you will do**

The **Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)** is seeking a strategic and experienced humanitarian professional to join our MENA Regional Office as Regional Solutions Adviser - Syria & Hosting Countries.

As the region continues to navigate displacement, return preparedness, and durable solutions for Syrians, this pivotal role will drive regional collaboration, strengthen programme quality, and support innovative, multi-country responses across **Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, and the wider MENA region**.

You will play a leading role in shaping NRC's regional Syria response by:

- Providing strategic programme support and guidance to country offices.
- Strengthening cross-country coordination, learning, and regional coherence.
- Leading the development and management of regional and multi-country grants.
- Identifying and securing new funding opportunities and donor partnerships.
- Supporting return preparedness and durable solutions initiatives for Syrian refugees and returnees.
- Coordinating scenario planning, information sharing, and regional analysis.
- Representing NRC in relevant regional forums and stakeholder engagements.
- Promoting evidence-based programming, learning, and advocacy across the Syria response.

**What you will bring**

We are seeking a collaborative and forward-thinking adviser with:

- 6-8 years of humanitarian, recovery, or development experience, including 3 years in advisory or management roles.
- Specialist knowledge and expertise equivalent to an advanced university degree in a relevant field (e.g., international development, politics, social science)
- Strong knowledge of development and other institutional donors’ strategies, priorities, and compliance requirements for relevant donors.
- Track record of successful proposal development, or similar in funding or partnerships
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts, with preference for previous experience in the region
- Understanding of, and commitment to working collaboratively with technical and operational colleagues within a matrix structure, including capacity building
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal

**Context related skills, knowledge and experience**

- Deep knowledge and understanding of the Syria context
- Experience with coordination role across different countries
- Experience working with overall strategy development and planning
- Experience of developing learning and development tools and resources to support capacity building
- Understanding of durable solutions concepts and frameworks and previous experience in working on return contexts
- Experience with project management, including budget monitoring, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting, modification requests and evaluations
- Knowledge of and interest in new business opportunities, including different partnerships modalities, grants and commercial opportunities
- Experience of working with cross-country programmes and donors

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAM0Gl5p5UvRIDRI7Z6ESKdAc0K_8qqUHKieitun5UJxOg?e=HdWSf7) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman Jordan, Syria or Lebanon. **Please note that this is a non-accompanied position.**
- Fixed term contract: Until November 2027 (extension possible if additional funding is secured)
- Travel: Up to 30% to Field locations.
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from all qualified candidates.
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

**If you're passionate about regional leadership, partnership-building, and developing solutions for displaced populations, we'd love to hear from you.**

**Apply today and help shape the future of NRC's Syria & Hosting countries' response.**

jobs.title: Malawi Credit & Repayment Data Snr Coordinator (Fixed-term)
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## About the Role

Seeking a meticulous data integrity professional to minimize operational risk and strengthen farmer trust by serving as the central manager for the integrity, accuracy, and timely reconciliation of all client credit and repayment transactions.

## Responsibilities

Financial Data Reconciliation and Integrity (Central Focus)

- Act as the primary reconciliation and quality checker for farmer credit and repayment data, ensuring accuracy across all systems.
- Proactively manage and follow up with external partners (e.g., NBS Bank, MNOs) to secure timely transaction reports (e.g., daily reports by 8:00 AM) to prevent and resolve reconciliation delays.
- Ensure accurate and timely daily MNO payment reconciliations, including correcting invalid payments.
- Investigate and resolve TNM/Airtel reconciliation issues and transaction report delays.
- Manage Monthly CLIF/Bank reconciliation and Monthly Receivable reconciliation.
- Manage Post-audit corrections on credit/repayment, Post-Audit write-offs/push to payroll.
- Conduct regular all-season CLIF data anomaly checks (weekly) to ensure accurate client data and flag all discrepancies to management.
- Manage large-scale data cleanup efforts, including coordinating the transfer of confirmed farmer payments from the COCA savings account to active loans.
- Identify and resolve Odoo and Fineract issues, specifically focusing on the elimination of duplicate loans.

Payment Reversal and Refund Processing (Key Transaction Management)

- Act as the central manager for payment reversal handling for Field Operations, unique number checks for Group Leaders (GL) payments, and refunds payment.
- Manage and process client refunds (phase 1 & 2) and conduct Refund postmortem analysis.
- Execute End of Season Defaulter and group liability banning actions.
- Perform seasonal CLIF actions such as site merging, overpayment transfers, site activation/deactivation, and input delivery locking.

Client Data & System Quality Oversight

- Monitor system performance (e.g., USSD, Fineract, FieldSmart), conduct system audits, produce reports with recommended improvements, and proactively troubleshoot and resolve system sync failures and credit mismatches between Field Smart, Fineract, and Odoo (e.g., during enrollment).
- Review and work on tickets submitted through Zendesk via the customer service hotline and complete data changes in CLIF as requested by the field team (via FO hotline or tracker submission).
- Prepare and generate Client Repayment Progress reports (CRPRs), Group Repayment Progress Reports (GRPRs), and Client Level Notices.
- Review and process Yield & funeral insurance claims following given procedures and timelines, ensuring complete documentation.
- Actively coordinate with the field team to resolve and collect missing or invalid client data points, such as National IDs, phone numbers, and gender information.

Project Support and Training

- Coordinate complex User Acceptance Testing (UAT) plans (e.g., for refund tool or CLIF) and manage stakeholders to ensure project deadlines are met.
- Train Customer Engagement (CE)/FOPS on POP search.
- Draft or revise training documents and facilitate trainings to the field team during Field Officer meetings, enrollment, and input delivery boot camps on Biz Ops-relevant topics.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Advanced Technical Data Management and Analysis Skills: Expertise in writing SQL queries, and performing complex analysis to reduce external dependencies.
- Data Quality Assurance: Expertise in ensuring data integrity and reliability across systems.
- Good knowledge of Financial and Accounting concepts.
- Experience with support platforms - Jira, Zendesk, Kissflow.
- Medium to high-level skills in analytics tools such as Rstudio, Python, and Excel.
- People Management experience.
- Bachelors Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related area
- Good knowledge of Financial and Accounting concepts.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Zomba, Malawi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

1 year

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Malawi.

## Application Deadline

04 February 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: MSF International Managing Director
jobs.description:
**Location:** Based in Geneva or within approximately +/- two (2) hours from Geneva

**Contract:** Fixed term at 100% - It is a mandated role (currently 3+3 years)

**Starting date:** 01st of March 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 26th of November 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified.

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**I. CONTEXT**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement.

Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG). MSF International also provides administrative and operational support to movement-wide initiatives and services, including MSF Access.

**II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement.

**The role ensures that MSF International:**

- Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities.
- Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee);
- Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care;
- Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems;
- Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization;
- Models MSF values in leadership, equity, duty of care, and ethical management;
- Ensures that the decisions taken by the Board of Directors of MSF International and its implementation is compliant with the Articles of Association, the internal regulations, as well as Swiss standards and Swiss laws, for as long as the registered office is in Geneva, Switzerland.

The MSF Management Director acts as a strategic partner to the International Secretary General, providing leadership on transversal and institutional topics with regards to the management of MSF International.

**III. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1. Strategic Leadership and Implementation of MSF International (Multi‑year Plan & SPARC): Lead the translation of MSF International and movement strategic priorities into clear objectives, organisational plans, policies and resourcing within MSF International; support cross‑functional initiatives required by international platforms as needed to deliver the Multi‑Year Strategic Plan and SPARC commitments.**

**Expected result:** MSF International delivers on agreed strategic priorities and SPARC commitments through coherent plans, measurable milestones and coordinated delivery across functions and movement partners.

a. Contribute to the development of MSF International Multi‑year Strategic Plan and SPARC within MSF International’s mandate and scope and translate strategic priorities into concrete organisational objectives, policies, systems and resource allocations, ensuring coherence across functions and services.

b. Supports cross‑functional and transversal initiatives required to deliver common strategic priorities and SPARC‑related commitments.

c. Contribute to movement-wide discussions on harmonization, efficiency and shared services.

d. Sets up and tracks implementation plans, including key milestones, indicators, and risks. Support the ISG in reporting to the International Board and relevant Standing Committees, and contribute to SPARC’s Monitoring & Evaluation Framework and Expense Steering Process for functions and services managed within MSF International’s scope.

e. Deputize for the ISG as required, within agreed scope and representation mandates.

f. Represent MSF International to key stakeholders, partners and external audiences as required, and build relationships that protect and advance MSF's institutional interests.

**2. Governance, legal compliance, accountability and risk management for MSF-International: Ensure robust governance implementation, statutory compliance and effective risk management systems for MSF International as a Swiss legal entity and for services delivered on behalf of the movement; prepare governance-level advice and support Board decision-making.**

**Expected result:** International Board and executive decisions are supported by timely, compliant and risk‑informed advice; MSF International statutory obligations and legal requirements are met and organisational risks are identified and mitigated.

a. Act as senior management liaison to the ISG, the International Board and Standing Committees on matters related to MSF International organisational governance, resources, risk, compliance and organisational performance.

b. Ensure robust systems of internal control, risk management and accountability, are in place and functioning for MSF International, in line with legal, fiduciary and associative obligations, including preparedness for critical incidents directly affecting MSF International.

c. Lead or support organizational responses to critical incidents directly affecting MSF International, including HR, legal, reputational, safeguarding or security‑related situations.

d. Ensure that MSF International fulfils its statutory responsibilities as a Swiss legal entity and that appropriate legal, administrative and governance support is obtained for decisions of the IB in light of the International Statutes, the Internal Regulations, and Swiss standards and law. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding daily management of MSF International.

e. Oversee compliance with GDPR and Swiss data protection law, promoting a culture of privacy and responsible data use.

f. Ensure appropriate legal review of all contracts and agreements directly involving MSF International and including those through which it delivers services to the movement, in accordance with MSF’s rules and policies, as well as Swiss law.
