jobs.title: Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services
jobs.company: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
jobs.description:
**Nature of Consultancy:** Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment (with mission travel to Port-au-Prince and designated departmental hubs). Any required mission travel, including its dates, arrangements, security requirements, and reimbursement of agreed expenses, shall be specified or separately agreed in writing.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days/hours, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, deliverables, and estimated levels of effort agreed between COAR and the Consultant.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 01 December 2026 to 31 December 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed; it does not create an obligation to provide or accept assignments, guarantee a minimum workload, or require continuous availability. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated Haiti Team Lead, acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope. This role is for assignment coordination and does not confer authority to direct the Consultant's day-to-day working methods or exercise line-management authority over the Consultant.

**Overview:** This Scope of Work (SoW) outlines the specific senior technical consultancy assignment with the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant may be commissioned to provide specialist analytical and advisory services for an in-depth study examining the systemic, historical, and multidimensional crisis in Haiti. Commissioned in the context of UNDP and UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) strategic planning, the study is intended to establish an evidence-based baseline to guide conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and sustainable recovery initiatives across Haiti. The assignment may include the preparation of a comprehensive, formally published biennial report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks, accompanied by a strategic intervention approach for the United Nations system. The Consultant's responsibility shall be limited to the agreed research, analytical, drafting, advisory, and facilitation outputs. Decisions concerning publication, institutional endorsement, strategic adoption, and implementation shall remain with COAR and the commissioning institutions.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**About COAR:** COAR is an independent social enterprise that directly supports practitioners, policymakers, and donors by facilitating humanitarian and development interventions in complex, fragile, and high-risk environments. COAR delivers neutral and objective research and analysis, which identifies - but does not influence - local stakeholders, relationships, interests, and analyzes broader political, economic, social, and security dynamics and trends. COAR research leverages social media, personal networks, field research teams, and local experts in order to map and translate the local human context; COAR analysis synthesizes and studies this data in order to inform both programmatic and strategic decision-making, reduce security and conflict sensitivity risks, and increase the impact of humanitarian, development, stabilization, peace-building, and peacekeeping initiatives.

**Objectives**

For the specific study assignment, the Consultant may be commissioned to:

- Conduct an analysis of historical trends and trajectories of Haiti’s systemic, social, community, political, and economic crisis to develop a comprehensive understanding of underlying structural dynamics;
- Analyze the multidimensional drivers of fragility and crisis across national, departmental, and cross-border domains;
- Map crises and trace underlying drivers of distinct forms of violence (criminal, gang-driven, political, and gender-based) to elucidate crisis systems;
- Evaluate crisis dynamics through intersectional gender, generational, and social inequality perspectives, highlighting the contributions and protection of women and youth in conflict prevention and mediation;
- Review and assess past and ongoing conflict prevention and peacebuilding interventions supported by the UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) and key multilateral/bilateral partners;
- Propose a tailored intervention approach for the United Nations system anchored in conflict prevention and peacebuilding principles; and
- Where included in the agreed assignment, provide substantive input into the preparation of an inclusive multi-stakeholder validation workshop, including contributing to validation discussions and moderating specified panel sessions.

**Activities and Key Responsibilities**

The following activities describe potential services under the study assignment. The specific activities to be performed, their estimated effort, and the associated outputs shall be confirmed in writing before commencement.

1\. Analytical Framing & Methodological Design

- Develop an analytical framework and research matrix tailored to the Haitian operational context, integrating OECD DAC peacebuilding criteria and UN Integrated Strategic Framework (ISF) objectives.
- Formulate and calibrate qualitative and quantitative research instruments, including semi-structured Key Informant Interview (KII) guides, Focus Group Discussion (FGD) protocols, and secondary assessment templates.
- Incorporate strict Conflict Sensitivity, Do No Harm, and data protection protocols, reflecting localized security constraints and protection considerations in gang-controlled and fragile environments.

2\. Multidimensional Fragility, Violence & Hotspot Mapping

- Trace historical fault lines, institutional degradation, and economic patterns driving instability across Port-au-Prince and outlying departments (e.g., Artibonite, Nord, Grand'Anse).
- Document geographic conflict hotspots, illicit trade flows, arms proliferation corridors, and cross-border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Assess formal and informal mechanisms, social cohesion structures, customary dispute-resolution mechanisms, and local resilience dynamics fostering community stability.

3\. Intersectional Analysis & PBF Portfolio Assessment

- Analyze structural socio-economic inequalities, youth recruitment vulnerabilities, and gender-based violence (GBV) as systemic drivers of fragility.
- Conduct a focused desk review and stakeholder assessment of UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects and partner peacebuilding programming in Haiti, evaluating impact, lessons learned, and systemic gaps.
- Identify practical entry points and age- and gender-sensitive recommendations to strengthen the leadership of women and youth in peacebuilding architectures.

4\. Report Authoring & UN Strategic Intervention Approach

- Prepare and coordinate the analytical synthesis and drafting of the formal, publication-ready baseline report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks in Haiti.
- Draft a pragmatic, forward-looking UN intervention approach that connects empirical research findings with strategic programming across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus.
- Integrate technical review comments from COAR leadership, UNDP, PBF, and institutional counterparts into final publishable outputs to the extent that such comments are provided within the agreed review process and schedule. The Consultant shall identify and discuss any material changes to the agreed scope or analytical conclusions that arise during review.

5\. Stakeholder Workshop Coordination & Panel Moderation

- Where specified in the assignment, provide substantive recommendations on the agenda and content of the national multi-stakeholder validation workshop.
- Deliver technical presentations on analytical findings, methodological approaches, and strategic recommendations to UN leadership, civil society, and international partners, at agreed events or sessions.
- Moderate thematic panel discussions during inclusive consultations to cultivate national ownership and partnership consensus where the relevant sessions, preparation requirements, and expected level of effort have been agreed in writing.

**Expected Results and Deliverables**

The primary result of this assignment will be a publicly available, formally published large-scale report examining fragilities and risks related to peacebuilding and development in Haiti. The report serves three primary purposes:

1. Understanding Haiti’s Crisis: Deepening multilateral and national understanding of the systems, drivers, and trajectories underlying the crisis.
2. Strategic & Programmatic Decision-Making: Informing conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and HDP nexus resource allocation.
3. Advocacy & Dialogue: Supporting continuous, multilevel dialogue among national authorities, civil society, and international partners.

**Required Experience and Expertise**

- Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in Peace and Conflict Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, or a related discipline required.
- UN System Experience: Required minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience advising or implementing peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and stabilization programming within or alongside the UN System (e.g., UNDP, BINUH, DPO/DPPA, IOM, or UN Country Teams).
- Country & Contextual Expertise: Desired analytical or operational track record in Haiti, with nuanced understanding of Haitian political history, gang territorial dynamics, departmental socio-economic disparities, and border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Analytical Capabilities: Proven track record conducting complex conflict analyses, fragility assessments, and intersectional studies focusing on gender, youth, and structural inequalities.
- Facilitation & Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue: Proven experience designing and moderating high-level validation workshops, roundtables, and policy panels involving government counterparts, UN leadership, and grassroots civil society organizations.
- Languages: Professional proficiency in both French and English (written and spoken) is required; fluency or working knowledge of Haitian Creole (Kreyòl) is a distinct asset.

**Safeguarding, Ethics, and Confidentiality**

In performing the Services, the Consultant shall comply with COAR’s Code of Conduct, any applicable Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), and safeguarding requirements that COAR identifies in writing as applicable to external consultants and relevant to the accepted assignment. In light of the delicate security and protection environment in Haiti, the Consultant shall conduct agreed research and stakeholder interactions in accordance with Do No Harm principles, informant anonymity, data protection protocols, and UN standards on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client. The Consultant shall promptly notify COAR of any material ethical, safeguarding, data-protection, or security concern arising in the course of the assignment, while retaining responsibility for the independent professional judgment required to perform the Services safely and ethically.

All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client, subject to the terms of the applicable consultancy agreement, including any agreed provisions concerning pre-existing materials, third-party materials, research data, intellectual property, and permitted retention of records.

jobs.description:
Lieu : Lyon, France
Date souhaitée de démarrage : 04/01/2026
Durée : 3 mois

Handicap International / Humanité & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux. Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens.

**CONTEXTE :**

Atlas Logistique est une unité opérationnelle de HI, qui soutient les acteurs humanitaires depuis 1993. Atlas Logistique (AL) facilite, optimise et accélère l'acheminement de l'aide dans les situations d'urgence et en contexte de crise chronique.

Notre mission est d'ouvrir l'espace humanitaire vers les populations les plus difficiles d'accès, et d'optimiser les chaînes d'approvisionnement humanitaire. Nous défendons une vision innovante de la logistique opérationnelle, vue non pas comme une fonction de soutien des opérations, mais comme un vecteur d'impact humanitaire.

La logistique opérationnelle rend le système d'aide humanitaire plus efficace, plus inclusif des populations isolées et plus respectueux de l'environnement. Elle peut également contribuer à l'émergence des acteurs du marché comme leviers de résilience et de développement dans les pays fragiles. Nous repensons constamment nos projets pour qu'ils servent cette vision et notre mandat d'impact humanitaire.

Le déploiement d'Atlas Logistique s'est accompagné ces dernières années d'une restructuration de nos opérations autour de quatre secteurs clés : les plateformes mutualisées de transport et de stockage, la logistique médicale, le renforcement des capacités logistiques et le génie civil léger d’accès, à la fois dans les phases préparation et de réponse aux urgences. Ils contribuent tous au positionnement de HI-AL en tant qu'acteur clé de l'accès humanitaire.

**OBJECTIFS DU POSTE :**

Sous la responsabilité du Pool & Preparedness Manager de la Direction Atlas Logistique et au sein du Pôle déploiement, le poste vise à évaluer les possibilités d’intervention en urgence et à piloter les ouvertures de projets Atlas Logistique sur de nouveaux terrains d’intervention.

1\. Mise en œuvre du projet

Planifier les activités selon la proposition de projet, les priorités et la répartition des rôles ; évaluer et compiler les besoins des organisations cibles bénéficiaires (OCB)
Développer les liens opérationnels et les accords de partenariat avec les autorités locales, les acteurs humanitaires et les OCB
Proposer, avec le référent technique siège et les services support, les procédures d’achat et formats opérationnels du projet ; mener les consultations, négociations et contractualisations des marchés transport
Assurer le suivi administratif, le monitoring et l’évaluation du projet via les outils de gestion existants

2\. Engagements bailleurs, reporting et capitalisation

Garantir l’atteinte des cibles contractuelles et superviser les outils de collecte, d’analyse et d’archivage des données du projet
Assurer un reporting régulier auprès du Manageur Opérationnel (Pack Projet / Sitrep) et contribuer aux rapports internes et bailleurs dans les délais impartis
Appuyer le Coordinateur Plateforme dans la conception et l’amélioration des outils et documents projet, en vue de capitaliser les expériences
Remettre en fin de mission un rapport de passation et participer au processus de capitalisation, au niveau terrain et siège

3\. Coordination interne et management d’équipe

Piloter la gestion administrative, logistique et financière du projet en lien avec les services support
Animer, accompagner et former votre équipe : objectifs, plans d’action, évaluations, développement des compétences, résolution des conflits
Proposer les évolutions de l’organigramme projet (descriptions de poste) avec le Coordinateur Plateforme
Veiller à l’application des politiques institutionnelles de HI (anticorruption, PEAS, protection de l’enfance, sécurité, genre)

4\. Représentation externe

Représenter HI/AL auprès des autorités, des OCB et des parties prenantes, et dans les mécanismes de coordination (clusters logistique et prioritaires), par délégation du Manageur Opérationnel, afin de positionner HI/AL comme acteur majeur du secteur

5\. Qualité, stratégie et préparation aux urgences (en lien avec le Spécialiste PTF)

Garantir la conformité des activités au cadre technique validé par les Référents Techniques siège et aux cadres logiques des projets
Mettre en œuvre la Politique Suivi Évaluation (enquêtes, évaluations terrain, indicateurs) et appuyer les N-1 sur ce volet
Proposer les solutions, outils et travaux de capitalisation améliorant la qualité ; veiller à l’efficacité des coûts
Participer aux évaluations de besoins et à la définition de la stratégie des projets Atlas, ainsi qu’au diagnostic et à la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de préparation aux urgences

6\. Sécurité et cadres légaux

Fournir au Coordinateur Plateforme et à votre N+1 les informations et le support nécessaires à la définition et à la mise en place des procédures et outils de sécurité de la mission
Collaborer avec le département sécurité et accès pour le suivi des équipes et des activités
Contribuer, avec le N+1 et le Responsable Sécurité, à la mise à jour et au suivi des outils de sécurité et d’accès sur les zones d’intervention (analyse des risques, niveaux et indicateurs, règles de sécurité) et aux outils de communication transversaux avec les OCB sur les enjeux sécuritaires
Assurer une transmission d’information régulière avec le N+1, le Responsable Sécurité et les équipes terrain, et développer un réseau de contacts propice à la collecte d’informations sécuritaires

**Exigences**

Bac +2 en gestion de projet ou logistique humanitaire, génie civil léger ou domaine technique apparenté
2 ans d’expérience en gestion de projet humanitaire en contexte d’urgence et/ou de crise chronique ; une expérience en logistique H2H, logistique programmatique ou génie civil est un plus
Maîtrise du cycle de projet, rigueur et fortes capacités organisationnelles
Sens des priorités, réactivité, flexibilité et résolution de problèmes
Excellent relationnel, goût du travail en équipe multiculturelle et capacité à fédérer
Sens de l’initiative et aptitude à travailler sous pression, dans un contexte sécuritaire volatile
Français et anglais courants (espagnol apprécié)
Environnement Windows et bonne maîtrise d’Excel (outils de collecte de données mobile appréciés)

**CONDITIONS DU POSTE :**

CDD de 3 mois

Ce que vous trouverez chez nous :

Des valeurs fortes : Humanité, Inclusion, Engagement et intégrité ! Et une proximité avec le terrain via des conférences régulières.

Statut cadre, 34 CP et 13 JRTT annuel et l'existence d'un CET permettant de concilier un équilibre vie pro/ vie perso

Une organisation flexible : carte tickets resto (prise en charge 60% par HI), charte de télétravail : 8 jours de présentiel par mois minimum

Transport : un forfait mobilité durable existe. Prise en charge 50% des abonnements transports.

jobs.title: International Fundraising Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** Full-time

**Duration:** This role is subject to two terms of 3 years each (maximum 6 years)

**Starting date:** 01.03.2027

**Deadline to apply:** 23.11.2027

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**I. CONTEXT**

MSF’s operational independence rests on its financial independence: 98 per cent of our funding comes from private sources, raised by 42 decentralised fundraising markets under the movement-wide Global Private Fundraising Strategic Framework (currently GPS 3.0, 2024–2030) and generating a private income of €2.5 billion in 2025. The International Fundraising Coordinator provides executive leadership for movement-wide fundraising coordination and chairs, as a non-voting member, the international fundraising platform (DirFund), which sets the fundraising strategy for the MSF Movement, and the Full DirFund (all fundraising directors). As a member of the International Office Leadership Team (IO-LT), the position contributes to IO direction, policy and other movement priorities, heads the International Office Fundraising Department (FR-IO), composed of 12 staff, with an annual budget of approximately €1.3 million, co-leads the International Digital Engagement Unit (IDEU, seven staff) with the International Communications Coordinator and works closely with the International Finance Coordinator, MSF’s Boards and General Directors. Moreover, the International Fundraising Coordinator represents MSF in external fora, e.g. in the International Fundraising Leadership Forum (IFLF). The role involves regular international travel.

**II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

Provides executive leadership to strategise, direct and oversee the development and execution of MSF’s global fundraising strategy and its governance across the Movement’s decentralised fundraising entities, aligning sections, offices and international platforms to secure sustainable, independent private income for MSF’s operational and organisational ambitions.

**III. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1. Lead the development, implementation, monitoring and course-correction of MSF’s global fundraising strategic framework (GPS) in line with MSF’s mission and movement-wide priorities, to ensure sustainable growth and diversification of private income.**

1. Define and steer the GPS cycle with the DirFund and fundraising directors, translating the movement’s vision into shared priorities, enablers and targets.
2. Monitor and analyse global fundraising performance, income and cost alike, and initiate corrective action where targets are at risk.
3. Provide thought leadership on global fundraising trends, innovation (including digital and AI-driven change) and emerging markets, shaping the movement’s response.
4. Advise on the fundraising potential of new markets and programmes, on fundraising investments and on organisational design for income generation across the Movement.

**2. Direct the international fundraising governance processes (DirFund and Full DirFund) as well as the Funding Coordination Community of the ODs within MSF’s federated structure, to ensure effective, timely collective decision-making and coherent follow-through across the movement.**

1. Chair and steer the DirFund and the Full DirFund, shaping their priorities, agendas and decision-making in line with MSF’s mission and organisational needs.
2. Broker alignment between sections and offices on complex fundraising-related issues, balancing local ownership of strategies with movement-wide interests.
3. Drive accountability for DirFund decisions, annual priorities and workplan, ensuring that commitments are implemented, monitored and escalated where necessary.
4. Align the fundraising agenda with other international, executive and operational platforms, Funding Units at the Operational Directorates (ODs) and relevant committees, task forces, and working groups, advancing SPARC-related and other movement-wide priorities.

**3. Develop and oversee MSF’s international fundraising policies, principles and standards within MSF’s ethical and governance framework, to safeguard MSF’s independence, reputation and donor trust.**

1. Lead the development, review and consistent application of movement-wide fundraising policies, such as the Emergency Fundraising Policy.
2. Advise on adherence to fundraising and governance regulations, ethical standards and donor compliance requirements, and strengthen them where needed.
3. Provide strategic direction on emergency fundraising and restricted-income monitoring during major emergencies, coordinating with Finance Directors, Funding Units and Operational Directorates (ODs).
4. Champion values-driven, inclusive leadership, including sponsorship of the Communications and Fundraising DEI Advisory Group.

**4. Oversee MSF’s movement-wide fundraising income, expenditure and investments, together with the International Finance Coordinator and team, to oversee and support cost-efficiency, financial sustainability and effective risk management.**

1. Oversee international fundraising forecasting and reporting, ensuring alignment between income and expenditure.
2. When needed, develop risk management strategies to mitigate financial, reputational and operational fundraising risks, in close consultation with other functions.
3. With the DirFund, monitor the performance of new fundraising entities and programmes against their business plans and advise on investment decisions.
4. Ensure that consistent internal and external benchmarking systems inform collective and individual strategic decisions and learning.

**5. Shape senior associative and executive decision-making and represent MSF externally on fundraising matters, to align fundraising with organisational priorities and strengthen MSF’s position in the sector.**

1. Based on the DirFund’s inputs, advise and support the International Board, section Boards, the Secretary General, the International President, ExCom/General Directors and Operations on strategic fundraising matters.
2. Align fundraising with Operations, Communications, Finance and Advocacy through joint strategies, work and project plans.
3. Represent MSF in international fora such as the International Fundraising Leadership Forum (IFLF), conferences and events, to enhance visibility, sector learning and new opportunities.
4. Support the fundraising community in high-value, inter-entity partnerships with major donors, corporations, institutional donors and governments.

**6. Represent fundraising in IO and movement leadership as a member of the IO Leadership Team, contributing to the strategic direction and management of the International Office, to ensure coherent delivery of the IO Multi-Year Plan and services to the movement.**

1. Contribute to IO Leadership Team decisions, organisational policy and leadership priorities as the executive lead for fundraising.
2. Build effective working relationships with IO coordinators, directors, operational leadership, communications, finance, legal and other functions.
3. Contribute to IO change processes and to SPARC-related and other movement-wide priorities.
4. Undertake field and office engagement as required to maintain operational understanding and support fundraising strategy.

**7. Direct the FR-IO department, co-lead the IDEU and strengthen fundraising leadership capacity across the movement, to ensure the right resources, skills and structures are in place to deliver the international fundraising priorities.**

1. Define the strategy, priorities, annual workplan, resources and structure of the FR-IO department, and oversee its annual budget of approximately €1.3 million, taking accountability for performance, financial stewardship, risk and resource choices.
2. Provide overall leadership for the FR-IO department of 12 staff and, together with the International Communications Coordinator, the IDEU (seven staff), directly managing and holding accountable senior staff while fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation and accountability.
3. Among other key areas like fundraising analysis, strategic partnerships, emergency fundraising, and project management, champion and oversee the international fundraising Capacity Building and Innovation Programme, promoting knowledge-sharing and best practice across sections and offices.
4. Mentor and coach fundraising leaders across the movement, supporting their professional development and succession planning.

**IV. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

They will ensure respectful management and communication at all levels and that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities with respect to required behaviour and report abuse while working for MSF by reinforcing and regularly discussing expected standards of behaviour.

They will welcome complainants, understand how to guide colleagues to appropriate channels, promote and create an environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour, and guide colleagues to the correct process without investigating. They will ensure that staff know how to complain and keep staff updated on reporting mechanisms.

**V. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Relevant university degree in business administration, non-profit management, international relations or a related field, or equivalent professional competence (essential).
- Advanced degree and/or certification in fundraising or general/executive management (desirable).

**Experience**

- Proven senior/executive leadership in international or regional fundraising or business development, including developing and executing comprehensive international fundraising strategies (desirable).
- Proven track record in private fundraising, including mass-market and one-to-one donor engagement (essential).
- Proven experience leading geographically dispersed teams in large, matrixed or federated multi-country organisations, contributing to organisational strategy, influencing executive stakeholders and coordinating across decentralised structures (desirable).
- Proven management of large, multi-million budgets (essential).
- Demonstrated strategic vision, executive leadership presence, political acumen, senior-level influencing, decision-making under ambiguity and high emotional intelligence (essential).
- MSF experience at fundraising director level (desirable).

**Knowledge**

- Strategic planning and organisational design (essential).
- Governance and federation management in a decentralised international organisation (essential).
- Financial oversight and risk management (essential).T
- Policy development, including fundraising regulations, ethics and donor compliance (essential).
- High-level stakeholder management with boards and executive leadership (essential).
- Global fundraising practices, donor motivations and market trends, and commitment to MSF’s principled approach to fundraising (essential).

**Languages**

- Fluent written and spoken English (essential); French, Spanish or Arabic (an asset).

**Other**

- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to MSF offices, operational contexts and international fora.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: SOUTH SUDAN - DEPUTY HEAD OF FINANCE - JUBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, including

refugees/returnees and IDP camp settings.

Context:

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- On top of these chronic situations, South Sudan has been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. By end of 2024, more than 1,000,000 people had entered South Sudan, the vast majority

entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- More recently, resurgence of internal tensions have led to heightened conflict and analysts are worried that the peace conditions offered by the Peace Agreement may not hold.

As a result, 9,3 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2025.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors and has been one of the first responders of the cholera

response.

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Malakal and a sub-office in Renk. The field office in Renk has been set-up to support the ongoing response to the Sudan Crisis and to ensure constant monitoring and rapid access to

affected communities. SI's long term presence in Upper Nile enables the organization to ensure proper coordination with other key players on the ground in order to provide a high-quality response and avoid duplication of

efforts. The response has focused on cholera since November 2024 while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- SI has recently closed its operations in Unity but is looking at starting interventions in Northern Bahr-El-Ghazal (Aweil): base opening planned for spring 2025.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2025, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 5+ million, and there are 70+ employees. This is the result of a scale-down following US funding cut in 2025 that are finally relaunched.

The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The Finance Deprtement is: Finance Coordinator Expatriate + 1 Chief Accountant + 1 Finance Assistant

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Deputy Head of Finance supports the Head of Finance in the overall financial management of the mission and ensures the implementation of SI financial procedures.

He/she assists the Finance Coordinator in preparing budget proposals, ensuring financial reporting complies with donor requirements, and updating the monthly budget follow-up. He/she also validates coordination expenses and ensures costs are allocated in accordance with the agreed cost-allocation methodology.

He/she supervises the Chief Accountant at the coordination level and provides technical guidance and support to the mission’s Finance Team. In the absence of the Finance Coordinator, he/she assumes delegated responsibilities to ensure continuity of finance operations.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

-Train and support the newly recruited National Deputy Head of Finance.

-Clear the accounting backlog resulting from the Deputy Head of Finance vacancy.

-Support the Finance Coordinator in managing shared cost allocations.

-Assist the Finance Coordinator in preparing budget proposals.

**Security constraints:**

Juba remains a volatile security context

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master degree in Finance

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 0/2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Similar Experience

2\. Knowledge about the accounting Software

3\. Budget Management and Financial Reporting Experience

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Clear Communication

2\. Autonomy

3\. Problem Solving

**LANGUAGES**

1\. English

2\. Arabic (Juba)

## SI will offer you...

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR XXX gross per month (2250 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

"The Deputy Finance Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and

some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.

Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.

Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars."

jobs.title: Head of Support – Bogotá, Colombia (National)
jobs.description:
**Department:** Funding and Services

**Duty station:** Bogotá, Colombia

**Contract type:** full-time (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1 year (renewable)

**Direct report:** Country Director

**Grade:** Head of (In country)

**\*Only Colombian citizens or candidates possessing a valid Colombian working permit will be considered.**\*

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this role?**

Geneva Call is seeking a highly qualified and experienced Head of Support for Colombia. Under the supervision of the Country Director (CD) and the technical supervision of functionals lead in HQ, the Head of Support is accountable for efficient management of all support functions: Finance, HR, IT, Donor Relations, Procurement, Administration, and Logistics. The position holder is accountable for compliance with local legislation and Geneva Call’s policies and procedures.

## **Work Relations**

The Head of Support reports to the Country Director (CD), with technical line management from the Head of Finance and the Head of HR. S/he line manages the functional focal points in the country: the Finance Coordinator, HR Officer, and Administrative Officer. S/he communicates and coordinates between the field and HQ and serves as the first point of contact for the Country Director and the local Senior Management Team on all matters related to the support functions. S/he also networks with Heads of Support from other organisations in the country.

## **Duties and Responsibilities**

**Finance**

- Lead the development of annual country and project budgets and donor financial reports, submitting them to the Country Director (CD) for review and approval.
- Identify and report on financial trends, working collaboratively with the CD to produce options, scenarios and corrective action plans that ensure the ongoing financial stability of the Country Program.
- Oversee all financial accounting matters, including maintenance of the general ledger, balance sheet, receipts, payments and payroll requirements, as well as the monthly accounts closing process, ensuring HQ deadlines are met.
- Oversee the cash flow requirements of the program, liaising with Geneva Call HQ to facilitate cash transfers; manage the effects of exchange rate fluctuations between local and contract currencies, highlighting upcoming issues early and identifying mitigating strategies.
- Oversee the financial management of partner delivery contracts and lead on audit matters.

**Human Resources**

- Resolve HR matters in coordination with the HR team, promoting good management practices and the Code of Conduct; ensure compliance with Geneva Call’s Code of Conduct and policies, and participate in investigations.
- Develop and manage the country HR team, in collaboration with the HR Coordinator at HQ, and develop management capacity at country level.
- Manage in-country performance management, ensuring managers set objectives and complete mid-year and year-end reviews with their team members; build managers’ capacity and ensure the process is followed.
- Manage and review the payroll reporting cycle for national staff, ensuring issues are flagged and followed up on in a timely manner and payroll deadlines are met; develop, monitor and review the national HR framework to ensure compliance with local legislation, based on legal advice.
- Ensure duty of care in country, in close collaboration with the global focal point at HQ; maintain the completeness of the staff database on a monthly basis; ensure smooth joiner and leaver processes in alignment with the global process; participate in monthly HR global connects; implement new policies and processes and engage in annual HR projects and priorities, in collaboration with HQ.

**IT**

- Supervise the need assessment and management of the procurement of IT assets following the guidance of the Head of IT at HQ.
- Ensures the correct usage of the IT systems.

**Donor Relations**

- Ensures organizational policies, procedures, and practices align with donor requirements, including grant agreements, reporting standards, and regulatory guidelines.
- Oversees the preparation and submission of timely, accurate, and comprehensive donor financial reports, including financial statements.
- Facilitates donor audits and implement mechanisms to identify, assess, and mitigate risks related to donor compliance, safeguarding the organization’s credibility and funding continuity.
- Provides guidance and training to internal teams on donor compliance requirements, ensuring consistent adherence across departments and project cycles.

**Procurement**

- Ensures that procurement actions are carried out in line with policies and procedures, and donor requirements, maintaining the right levels of procurement, appropriate controls and accountability, ensuring best value for Geneva Call.
- Supervise program procurement plans to ensure timely procurement.
- Manages the end-to-end procurement process, in line with GC procurement procedures and in collaboration with Procurement at HQ.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- Bachelors or Master’s degree in finance or business degree specialized in finance with a professional accounting qualification, as well as experience in human resources.

**Education (Desirable)**

- Qualifications in Colombian financial and accounting law and practice.

**Experience (Essential)**

- 10+ years of relevant work experience with increasing responsibilities in humanitarian organizations in a similar role.
- Experience of overseeing complex financial planning, monitoring, forecasting and reporting.
- Great understanding of Colombian financial and accounting laws and regulations.
- Good understanding of Colombian labor laws.

**Experience (Desirable)**

- Experience with Dynamics 365 Business Central is a plus.

**Job related competencies**

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate with impact, respect, and cultural sensitivity while building trustful relationships.
- Demonstrates an entrepreneurial mindset, a high level of integrity, ethics, confidentiality, accountability, and professionalism.
- Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize, manage competing demands, and deliver results under tight deadlines.
- Ability to collaborate effectively across departments, countries, and with HQ, fostering strong working relationships.
- Resilient and adaptable, with the ability to cope with change, stress, and insecure environments, and the willingness and ability to travel at short notice.

**Organisational Competencies**

- Demonstrated ability to thrive in a matrix management environment.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills tailored to different audiences and contexts.
- Entrepreneurial mindset with a proactive and solution-oriented approach.
- Ability to influence, coach, and build consensus in sensitive and complex situations.

**Languages (Essential)**

- Fluency in written and spoken Spanish and English is required.

**Additional information**

- The incumbent must be willing and able to occasionally travel at short notice and spend part of her time on the field.
- Testing and interviewing will be used as a form of screening.
- Initial appointment is subject to satisfactory professional references.
- Additional background checks may be required.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call consists of many diverse nationalities, cultures, languages, and opinions, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

By joining Geneva Call as Head of Support, you will play a key leadership role in enabling our humanitarian operations in Colombia. You will oversee the country support functions, ensuring the effective management of finance, human resources, administration, and operational systems that underpin programme delivery. You will become part of an organisation committed to protecting civilians and promoting respect for humanitarian norms, while contributing your expertise within a dynamic and multicultural environment.

jobs.title: Emergency Response Manager / Head of Programmes - Venezuela
jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
## **1. Background**

Plan International is implementing a growing humanitarian and early recovery portfolio in Venezuela, with a strong focus on children, adolescents, women, caregivers and crisis-affected communities.

The operation combines humanitarian response and early recovery programming and is delivered predominantly through Venezuelan partner organisations, with Plan providing programme leadership, technical oversight, quality assurance, MERL, safeguarding, financial and grant management, operational accompaniment and capacity strengthening.

The portfolio may include Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE), Education in Emergencies (EiE), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), WASH, Shelter/NFI, health and sexual and reproductive health, basic assistance and recovery interventions, depending on individual grants and partnerships.

The response is evolving from acute emergency delivery towards stabilisation, recovery and greater territorial and programmatic consolidation. The operation therefore requires strong leadership capable of maintaining strategic oversight while ensuring close follow-up of implementation, partners, programme quality, financial delivery, donor commitments and operational risks.

## **2. Role Purpose**

The Emergency Response Manager / Head of Programmes - Venezuela provides overall strategic and operational leadership to Plan International's humanitarian and recovery programme portfolio in Venezuela.

The postholder is accountable for ensuring that the portfolio is delivered on time, within approved budgets and in accordance with proposals, donor requirements, humanitarian standards and Plan International's commitments on programme quality, safeguarding, gender equality, inclusion and accountability to affected populations.

A central responsibility is to ensure that Plan's partner-led operating model translates into high-quality and accountable delivery at field level, supported by clear expectations, adequate technical accompaniment, effective monitoring and timely corrective action. This is a highly operational role requiring the ability to move confidently between strategic leadership and hands-on programme troubleshooting.

## **3. Key Responsibilities**

### **A. Humanitarian Strategy and Programme Leadership**

- Provide overall leadership and strategic direction for the humanitarian and recovery portfolio in Venezuela.
- Maintain an integrated overview of projects, grants, partners, technical sectors, donor commitments and geographical areas under implementation.
- Translate the Venezuela response strategy into clear operational priorities, workplans, management decisions and measurable results.
- Regularly review the relevance of the response as humanitarian needs and operating conditions evolve.
- Guide the transition between immediate humanitarian response, stabilisation, early recovery and recovery programming.
- Advise senior management on programme priorities, implementation constraints, operational risks and emerging opportunities.
- Ensure management decisions are translated into clear responsibilities, deadlines and follow-up actions.

### **B. Humanitarian Portfolio Management**

- Maintain consolidated oversight of workplans, implementation schedules, budgets, indicators, procurement requirements, partner deliverables, reporting deadlines and donor obligations.
- Monitor progress across the portfolio and proactively identify delays, underspending, implementation bottlenecks and quality concerns.
- Establish practical mechanisms for project-level and portfolio-level monitoring, including regular review meetings and action tracking.
- Ensure appropriate project start-up, implementation, modification, extension and close-out processes.
- Identify dependencies and complementarities between projects and sectors.
- Escalate significant programmatic, contractual, financial, safeguarding or operational risks with clear recommendations.

### **C. Partner Management and Localisation**

- Maintain productive, equitable and accountable relationships with national and local implementing partners.
- Ensure partners understand project objectives, deliverables, indicators, budgets, reporting obligations and technical standards.
- Coordinate programme, technical, MERL, financial, safeguarding and operational accompaniment to partners.
- Ensure implementation issues are identified early and addressed through agreed improvement measures.
- Strengthen partner capacities in programme management, humanitarian quality, safeguarding, accountability, monitoring and donor compliance.
- Support partner mapping, due diligence and engagement with potential new partners when required.

### **D. Programme Quality and Technical Leadership**

- Ensure interventions comply with Plan International standards and recognised humanitarian standards.
- Coordinate technical support across CPiE, EiE, MHPSS, WASH, Shelter/NFI, health and other relevant sectors.
- Ensure coherence and complementarity between sectoral components and promote integrated programming where it improves outcomes.
- Work with technical specialists to identify quality gaps and establish practical corrective actions.
- Ensure field monitoring assesses technical quality and safeguarding, not only activity completion.
- Ensure technical guidance is translated into practical actions by teams and partners.
- Promote programme adaptation based on evidence, community feedback and changes in need.

### **E. MERL, Accountability and Learning**

- Provide strategic oversight of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) across the portfolio.
- Ensure every project has appropriate indicators, targets, monitoring plans and means of verification.
- Ensure programme data are reliable, timely, safely managed and used for decision-making.
- Review portfolio performance and identify projects, results or indicators requiring corrective action.
- Ensure monitoring information from partners is systematically consolidated, verified and analysed.
- Ensure effective Accountability to Affected Populations, including safe and accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms.
- Promote learning through project reviews, Real-Time Reviews, evaluations, case studies and documented lessons learned.

### **F. Financial and Grant Management**

- Maintain oversight of expenditure and financial performance in close coordination with Finance and Grants colleagues.
- Regularly review Budget versus Actuals against implementation progress, forecasts and project milestones.
- Identify underspending, overspending and significant budget variances early and ensure corrective action.
- Monitor partner financial reporting and expenditure in coordination with Finance.
- Ensure donor contractual requirements are understood and met across programme teams.
- Support budget realignments, grant modifications, no-cost extensions and compliant project closure.
- Coordinate timely and high-quality narrative inputs for donor reports.

### **G. Field Implementation and Operational Follow-up**

- Conduct regular monitoring visits to project and partner locations.
- Review implementation directly with teams, partners and communities, and verify delivery against expected quality standards.
- Ensure field-visit recommendations result in documented actions and follow-up.
- Coordinate programme requirements with Supply Chain, Finance, Security, Communications and other enabling functions.
- Ensure plans adapt appropriately to access, security, logistics and contextual constraints.
- Maintain close engagement with personnel and consultants working outside Caracas.

### **H. Programme Development and Resource Mobilisation**

- Identify emerging humanitarian and recovery needs and translate them into strategic programme opportunities.
- Lead or contribute to needs assessments, concept notes, proposals, results frameworks and implementation strategies.
- Ensure programme designs are evidence-based, technically sound, operationally feasible, appropriately costed and aligned with implementation capacity.
- Support donor engagement, briefings and programme presentations.
- Ensure new funding opportunities are coherent with the Venezuela strategy and partner-led operating model.

### **I. Humanitarian Coordination and Representation**

- Represent Plan International, as delegated, with donors, UN agencies, clusters, sector groups, NGO coordination mechanisms, civil society and relevant authorities.
- Contribute to humanitarian coordination, inter-agency assessments, information sharing and response planning.
- Position Plan International appropriately and identify opportunities for collaboration, consortia and joint programming.
- Ensure information from external coordination informs internal strategy and operational decisions.

### **J. Team Leadership and Internal Coordination**

- Provide clear leadership and management direction to programme personnel under the role's responsibility.
- Establish clear roles, responsibilities, objectives and accountability mechanisms.
- Ensure regular coordination between Programme, MERL, Finance, Partnerships, Supply Chain, Security, Communications and technical specialists.
- Strengthen coordination between national personnel, consultants and regional or global technical support.
- Identify capacity gaps and coordinate appropriate mentoring, induction and technical assistance.
- Promote an inclusive, respectful, accountable and solution-oriented working culture.
- Ensure adequate handover, documentation and continuity across temporary and surge positions.

### **K. Safeguarding, Gender and Inclusion**

- Ensure safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment requirements are integrated throughout the programme cycle.
- Ensure partners understand and comply with applicable safeguarding requirements.
- Promote safe, accessible and confidential feedback and reporting mechanisms.
- Ensure programme decisions consider different risks faced by girls, boys, adolescents and other groups at heightened risk.
- Promote gender-transformative and inclusive programming where appropriate.
- Ensure implementation follows Do No Harm and protection-mainstreaming principles, and escalate concerns through established mechanisms.

### **L. Security, Access and Risk Management**

- Ensure programme planning integrates security, access and duty-of-care considerations.
- Work with relevant functions to establish practical risk mitigation for field activities and travel.
- Maintain an updated overview of strategic and operational risks affecting implementation.
- Ensure field movements and programme decisions follow applicable security procedures.
- Develop programme continuity measures where access or contextual constraints affect implementation.

## **4. Essential Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in International Development, Humanitarian Affairs, International Relations, Social Sciences, Programme Management or another relevant field.
- Minimum seven years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian and/or development programming, including significant humanitarian response experience.
- At least three years of programme management or senior coordination experience in humanitarian settings.
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-project and multi-donor portfolios.
- Strong experience across the full project cycle, including design, implementation, monitoring, financial follow-up, reporting and close-out.
- Experience managing programmes implemented through local or national partners.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles, programme quality, safeguarding and accountability.
- Experience with grant management and institutional donor compliance.
- Demonstrated ability to coordinate technical, programme and operational functions.
- Experience working in volatile, rapidly changing or operationally complex environments.
- Strong analytical, leadership, negotiation, coordination and communication skills.
- Ability and willingness to travel regularly within Venezuela.

### **Language Requirements**

- Spanish: Advanced professional proficiency, C2 or equivalent.
- English: Advanced professional proficiency, C1 or equivalent, including the ability to lead meetings, engage with donors, and draft or review high-quality technical and donor documentation.

## **5. Desirable Experience**

- Previous experience as Head of Programmes, Emergency Response Manager, Programme Director, Deputy Country Director - Programmes or in an equivalent senior role.
- Experience in Latin America and the Caribbean, particularly Venezuela or a comparable operating environment.
- Technical familiarity with one or more of the following: CPiE, EiE, MHPSS, WASH, Shelter/NFI, Cash and Voucher Assistance or integrated humanitarian programming.
- Experience working with institutional humanitarian donors, pooled funding mechanisms, consortia or multi-partner programmes.
- Experience managing localisation-focused or partner-led delivery models.
- Experience supporting humanitarian scale-up and transition to early recovery.
- Familiarity with Sphere, the Core Humanitarian Standard, Accountability to Affected Populations and relevant sector standards.

## **6. Core Competencies**

**Strategic and operational leadership:** Maintains strategic direction while engaging directly with implementation challenges and management decisions.

**Portfolio management:** Manages multiple grants, donors, partners, budgets and reporting requirements simultaneously.

**Decision-making under pressure:** Prioritises effectively and takes timely decisions in uncertain and rapidly evolving environments.

**Partner management:** Combines accountability with constructive accompaniment, capacity strengthening and respect for local leadership.

**Financial acumen:** Interprets budgets, BvAs, forecasts and expenditure trends and connects financial information with implementation performance.

**Programme quality:** Identifies technical and operational quality gaps and ensures corrective action.

**Communication and representation:** Represents the organisation credibly with donors, partners, humanitarian actors and senior management in Spanish and English.

**Collaboration:** Brings programme, technical and operational functions together around common implementation priorities.

## **7. Initial Priorities and Expected Results**

- Establish and maintain a consolidated, reliable overview of the humanitarian and recovery portfolio.
- Confirm clear project, partner and internal accountabilities.
- Strengthen alignment between implementation progress, financial execution and procurement planning.
- Ensure timely identification, documentation and escalation of programme risks.
- Ensure consistent monitoring of indicators, deliverables, budgets and donor obligations.
- Improve follow-up of partner reporting, safeguarding commitments and implementation actions.
- Establish regular field-based monitoring and practical corrective-action mechanisms.
- Ensure effective coordination between programme, technical, MERL, Finance, Supply Chain and Security functions.
- Support timely, accurate and high-quality donor reporting and programme development.
- Position the Venezuela portfolio for continuity, recovery and additional funding opportunities.

## **8. Contract Duration**

The initial contract will be for three months. It may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance, operational requirements and availability of funding.

Given the short initial contractual period and the dynamic nature of the Venezuela response, the successful candidate will be expected to assume responsibilities rapidly and provide immediate management continuity to the programme portfolio.

## **9. Safeguarding and Equal Opportunity**

Plan International is committed to safeguarding children, young people and adults from harm and to preventing sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. The successful candidate must uphold the highest standards of professional conduct and comply with all applicable safeguarding, data protection and accountability requirements.

Plan International promotes equal opportunities and values diversity. Recruitment is subject to appropriate background and reference checks in accordance with organisational policy and applicable legislation.

\[No traducido al idioma seleccionado\]

**Location: Caracas - Venezuela**

**Type of Role: 3-month fixed-term, full-time International or Local contract**

**Reports to: Head of Mission - Venezuela**

**Grade: 16**

**Closing Date: 12/11/2026**

*Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.*

*We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.*

*Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.*

*Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.*
