jobs.title: Institutional Support and Capacity Building Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The Central African region is home to the second largest tropical rainforest in the world, is sucking out about 1.5 billion tons of CO2 of the atmosphere or 4% of the world’s emissions every year and provides a habitat to more than 10,000 plant and animal species. Forest loss is accelerating despite ongoing efforts, as government action alone has not been enough to establish an effective balance between the interests of the forest and of economic development. On this basis, a coalition of donors – the European Union, the Federal Republic of Germany, the Kingdom of Norway, the Republic of France, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Republic of Korea – together with Central African partner countries – Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Cameroon, the Republic of Congo, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and the Republic of Gabon – have decided to enter into a collaborative partnership to establish the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI).

CAFI’s objective is to recognize and preserve the value of the forests in the region to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and contribute to sustainable development. This objective will be attained through the implementation of country-led, national scale REDD+ and Low Emissions Development (LED) investment frameworks that include policy reforms and measures to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and promote sustainable development. The CAFI Trust Fund is the principal means to implement the Central African Forest Initiative. It is administered by the MPTF-O, that also provides the Secretariat services. The Congo Basin, home to over 200 million hectares of tropical forest, represents one of the world’s most vital carbon sinks and biodiversity reservoirs. Sadly, the region continues to experience alarming rates of forest loss. Over one million hectares of forest is lost annually, driven by small-scale agriculture, infrastructure expansion, and unsustainable logging practices. Despite its ecological and climate significance, Central African forests receive only 11% of forest climate financing worldwide. This deforestation not only undermines global climate goals but also threatens the livelihoods of over 75 million forest-dependent communities.

3. Scope of Work

This assignment aims to strengthen the CAFI Secretariat’s strategy for policy dialogue & country engagement by addressing the institutional, governance and capacity challenges within the Congo Basin’s forest and climate agenda.

The purpose of this assignment is to support CAFI partner countries in strengthening national and subnational institutions to directly access, manage and implement financing from CAFI and other global environmental and climate funds such as the Green Climate Fund and the Adaptation Fund.

The Institutional Support and Capacity Building Specialist will lead the design, coordination and quality assurance of CAFI support through the direct-access readiness lifecycle from initial gap assessments and systems strengthening to accreditation, pipeline development, compliance and monitoring and continuous improvement. Ultimately, this tailored, country-owned support aims to ensure that partner institutions meet formal eligibility or accreditation requirements and the capacity to manage and implement high-quality investment programmes.

Under the overall guidance of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement, the Institutional Support and Capacity Building Specialist will include the following main functions:

1. Lead the Provision of Expert Support for Institutional Capacity Strengthening

• Assess institutional capacity gaps within national and subnational institutions, including government entities, public financial institutions, civil society organizations and other eligible entities seeking direct access to the CAFI Fund or other global environmental funds.

• Support the development and strengthening of policies, procedures and governance frameworks aligned with the CAFI Investment Framework, CAFI policies and procedures, country priorities and, where applicable, the requirements of the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds.

• Facilitate institutional coordination among ministries, departments and stakeholders, including institutions responsible for forestry, environment, climate, planning and finance, as well as national designated authorities and other entities involved in direct-access processes.

• Analyse institutional, governance and political economy factors that may enable or constrain direct access and the effective implementation of nationally led programmes.

• Contribute to the design and operationalization of national PES institutional frameworks, action plans and roadmaps, where relevant to the investment pipelines and delivery systems of institutions seeking direct access.

2. Ensure Fiduciary Readiness

• Support the development and implementation of fiduciary management systems and capabilities required for national and subnational institutions to directly access, manage and implement financing from the CAFI Fund and other global environmental funds. Areas of support may include;

o Financial management and accounting; budgeting and expenditure control; treasury and cash management; financial reporting; internal and external audit;

o Internal controls; procurement and contract management; grants and asset management; management of executing entities and other recipients; segregation of duties and delegated authorities; risk management; information systems, data integrity and record retention;

o Fraud and corruption prevention; conflict-of-interest management; counterparty screening; anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism; and whistleblower and witness protection.

• Guide and build capacity for institutions in documenting and demonstrating the effective application of their fiduciary systems during eligibility, due diligence and accreditation processes.

• Ensure that proposed institutional improvements are proportionate to each institution’s intended role, financing instruments, programme size, delivery arrangements and risk profile.

3. Development and Implementation of Grievance Redress Mechanisms related to Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSHEA)

• Support the development and implementation of institutional policies, procedures and operational systems relating to:

o Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanisms; ensuring mechanisms are accessible and effective; and

o Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSHEA); the prevention of and response to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

• Build capacity for institutions to demonstrate the effective application of these mechanisms as part of CAFI eligibility, due diligence and, where applicable, external accreditation processes.

4. Ensure Direct Access, Accreditation and Institutional Readiness

• Under the oversight of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement support, support institutional readiness assessments of potential national and subnational implementing entities, financial intermediaries and delivery partners against the requirements of CAFI and, as applicable, the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds.

• Assess institutions against their proposed role, mandate, financial instruments, project size, environmental and social risk profile, geographic reach, delivery model and implementation arrangements.

• Support candidate institutions in defining realistic and strategically justified pathways to direct access, including their institutional role, accreditation or eligibility scope, intended financing modalities, comparative advantage and priority investment pipeline.

• Translate assessment findings into costed, sequenced and time-bound institutional strengthening plans specifying responsibilities, milestones, evidence requirements, dependencies and residual risks.

• Support institutions in preparing accreditation, eligibility, due diligence and partnership documentation, including evidence mapping, documentary reviews, mock assessments, management responses and the closure of identified gaps.

• Maintain an institutional readiness dashboard and evidence repository for supported entities, with clear version control, confidentiality safeguards and status tracking.

• Liaise with national designated authorities, ministries of finance and environment, fund secretariats, delivery partners and technical assistance providers to ensure country ownership and avoid duplication of institutional support.

• Guide institutions during CAFI eligibility, due diligence processes and, where applicable, external accreditation reviews, including by coordinating responses to follow-up questions, supporting the establishment of legal and institutional arrangements, addressing conditions and operationalizing direct access once secured.

• Monitor changes in the policies, standards and accreditation frameworks of relevant global environmental funds and translate them into practical guidance for CAFI partner countries.

• Support both the achievement and effective operationalization of direct access, recognizing that eligibility or accreditation alone does not ensure the development, financing and successful implementation of national programmes.

• Monitor the implementation of institutional strengthening plans and support institutions in establishing continuous improvement processes following eligibility, accreditation or the establishment of direct-access arrangements.

5. Capacity-Building Management and Knowledge Sharing

• Support the Head of Secretariat, the Programming Team and the Partnership Unit in managing institutional technical assistance and direct-access readiness facilities across the CAFI Trust Fund, ensuring that institutional strengthening and direct-access support are linked to a credible and actionable investment pipeline.

• Conduct baseline studies and capability assessments to identify institutional, organizational and technical capacity gaps in entities seeking to access, manage or implement CAFI and other global environmental financing.

• Design and deliver tailored capacity-building solutions – covering fiduciary, environmental/social safeguards, gender and project management cycles including workshops, training, technical assistance and capacity-building frameworks, to support direct access to the CAFI Fund and, where applicable, the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds,.

• Develop guidance materials, standard operating procedures, training materials and toolkits related to institutional readiness, direct access, accreditation, fiduciary standards, safeguards, programme development and implementation readiness.

• Coordinate and mobilize specialized technical assistance in key areas, including institutional governance, fiduciary management, environmental and social safeguards, gender, forest governance, emissions-reduction strategies and sustainable land-use planning.

• Support the integration of PES into broader national climate policies and contributions, including nationally determined contributions, where PES forms part of the country’s investment pipeline or proposed delivery systems.

• Advise and support national access entities in identifying, prioritizing and developing forest, climate and environmental programmes or projects aligned with country priorities, CAFI objectives and, where applicable, the investment criteria of other global environmental funds.

• Prepare terms of reference, workplans, budgets and quality standards for specialized institutional capacity-building assignments.

• Monitor the performance of technical assistance providers and ensure that their outputs contribute to agreed institutional readiness and direct-access milestones.

• Assess and ensure candidate entities have, or can establish, adequate implementation arrangements involving executing entities, financial intermediaries, local governments, civil society organizations, Indigenous Peoples, local communities and private-sector partners, as applicable.

6. Promote Stakeholder Engagement

• Contribute to the development of partnership engagement plans across the Secretariat, with particular attention to country-owned direct-access strategies.

• Facilitate engagement and coordination with key stakeholders, including government agencies, development partners, non-governmental organizations, local communities, national designated authorities, candidate national access entities and the secretariats of relevant global environmental funds.

The IPSA shall perform other duties within the scope of this Terms of Reference as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will work under the direct supervision of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement.

5. Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies Core

Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Business Management - Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business management - Portfolio management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

2030 Agenda - Planet Climate : Climate Strategies and Policy: Policy and Institutional Building

Partnership management - CSO engagement: Knowledge and understanding of CSOs and the ability to engage with CSOs

Partnership management - Relationship management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Finance Due diligence management Ability to conduct a comprehensive appraisal of an organization or opportunity to be undertaken by a prospective investor or partner, especially to establish its assets and liabilities, as well as evaluate the potential opportunity and its related risks; knowledge of respective methodology and tools.

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Academic Education

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Science, Forestry, Climate Change, Natural Resource Management, Public Policy, Law, Public Administration or a related field, is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in coordination of institutional/political engagement and capacity building activities to high-level and multi-stakeholder platforms, preferably involving national and local government agencies, CSOs, and Donors.

Required skills and competencies

• Experience working in the development sector particularly working with international organizations, national and local government agencies.

• Experience with development and/or improvement, and implementation of fiduciary management systems for funding engagement of interested Parties.

• Experience in developing capacity building programs for government partners.

• Experience in working with the United Nations, including its policies and procedures pertaining to partnership engagement.

• Experience with accreditation to vertical funds or national execution of development programs (either multi or bilateral experience)

Desired additional skills and competencies

• Experience in land use, forests, climate projects.

• Relevant experience in the Congo Basin region.

• Experience in organizing training, organizational development, and strategic planning

• Proven experience managing partner and stakeholder relationships at the national or international level.

• Demonstrated experience of budget management, work planning, monitoring, and reporting.

Required Language(s) (at working level) Fluency in English and French is required.

7. The following documents shall be required from the applicants:

a) Personal CV or P11, indicating all past positions held and their main underlying functions, their durations (month/year), the qualifications, as well as the contact details (email and telephone number) of the Candidate, and at least three (3) the most recent professional references of previous supervisors. References may also include peers.

b) A cover letter (maximum length: 1 page) indicating why the candidate considers him-/herself to be suitable for the position.

c) Managers may ask (ad hoc) for any other materials relevant to pre-assessing the relevance of their experience, such as reports, presentations, publications, campaigns or other materials.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

jobs.title: Investigations Team Lead, Headquarters / Latin America and Caribbean (HQ/LAC) [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized SEAH, IT forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership.

Position Purpose

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) functionally reports to the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, under the overall supervision of the Deputy Director (Investigations). Under the supervision of the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, the primary role of the Team Lead (HQ/LAC) is to oversee, supervise and conduct investigations into alleged misconduct that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above, and that relates to UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) will supervise the work of the team, including but not limited to Investigators at the P3 level and all other personnel assigned to the investigation team covering UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean, and will complete their annual performance appraisals.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Lead investigations management and lead and manage Headquarters / Latin America and Caribbean (HQ/LAC) team

- Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Investigations, provides day‑to‑day operational leadership of the HQ/LAC Investigations Team, ensuring the effective delivery of investigative activities in line with OAI priorities, policies, and performance expectations.

- Manages the assigned investigative portfolio, including allocation of cases, prioritization of workstreams, workload balancing, and monitoring of progress to ensure investigations are completed timely, efficiently, and to a high professional standard, escalating risks and capacity issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Overseas and directs investigations, ensuring that appropriate investigative strategies are developed, all relevant lines of inquiry are pursued, and investigative resources are deployed proportionately and effectively.

- Reviews and edits of investigation reports prepared by team investigators and other relevant documents to ensure they are of a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations.

- Leads and personally conduct investigations only in complex, high‑risk, or sensitive matters, while otherwise providing technical direction, oversight, and quality assurance to investigations conducted by team members.

- Provides first line managerial and functional supervision to investigators and other personnel assigned to the team, including setting expectations, clarifying priorities, and ensuring alignment with OAI standards and values.

- Conducts regular and structured case and performance reviews with team members to assess investigative progress, identify quality or procedural gaps, and provide corrective direction where necessary.

- Holds direct accountability for the quality, timeliness, and defensibility of investigative outputs produced by the team prior to submission to the Chief, including investigation reports, findings, and recommendations.

- Identifies and addresses underperformance, skills gaps, or conduct issues at first instance through coaching, feedback, and performance management measures, escalating matters to the Chief in accordance with UNDP procedures where required.

- Ensures that investigations conducted by the team comply with international investigative standards, UNDP legal and policy frameworks, and OAI Investigation Guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures.

- Ensures due process, confidentiality, information security, and victim‑centered approaches are consistently applied, particularly in sensitive cases involving sexual misconduct, retaliation, or abuse of authority.

- Oversee the collection, handling, analysis, and safeguarding of evidence, ensuring proper chain of custody and appropriate handling of physical, digital, and testimonial evidence.

- Identifies investigative, procedural, or institutional risks emerging from casework and escalates systemic or high‑risk issues to the Chief to inform broader oversight, mitigation, or proactive responses.

- Oversees and promotes the effective use of investigative technologies, including case management systems, analytical software, open‑source intelligence tools, and artificial intelligence–enabled solutions, to enhance investigative efficiency, accuracy, and timeliness.

- Guides team members in the responsible and ethical use of AI and advanced analytics, ensuring compliance with confidentiality, due process, and information security requirements.

- Identifies opportunities to streamline investigative processes, improve workflows, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives under the strategic direction of the Chief.

- Acts as a key operational interlocutor with internal stakeholders (including legal services, HR, ethics, procurement, and management) on investigative matters, escalating sensitive or high‑impact issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Ensures that case records, databases, and documentation for matters under the team’s responsibility are accurate, complete, and up to date, supporting institutional accountability and auditability.

- Formulates and recommends case closure decisions, including assessments of evidentiary sufficiency and proportionality, for review and approval by the Chief.

- Supports the Chief through the provision of operational briefings, trend information, and case‑related inputs relevant to regional or functional oversight.

- Undertakes and, where appropriate, leads investigative missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including in hardship or hazardous duty locations, providing on‑site leadership and oversight for investigative activities.

- Sets the appropriate professional tone and workplace culture within the team, leading by example through ethical conduct, collaboration, and respect; fosters a culture of constructive, collective problem‑solving, open dialogue, and shared accountability; and actively models and reinforces behaviors that support teamwork, learning, and continuous improvement.

- Performs other duties within the functional profile as required for the effective functioning of the Investigations Section and the Office.

- Plans the work of the HQ/LAC Team and distributes workload among the HQ/LAC Team appropriately.

- Provides senior expertise and advice to the HQ/LAC Team so that the work of the HQ/LAC Team is performed in the most professional, efficient and timely manner.

- Appraises the performance of the HQ/LAC personnel.

- Recruit personnel for the HQ/LAC Team as necessary.

- Leads by example, setting the tone for the HQ/LAC Team. Consciously builds a supportive, collegiate and positive team culture within the HQ/LAC Team.

- Works collectively and professionally with peers to provide thought leadership and constructive challenge to ensure that the HQ/LAC Team is a dynamic, reflective unit that keeps pace with best practice.

- Actively engages and promotes discussions aimed at continued improvement of the HQ/LAC Team and the investigation function, ensuring highest impact and efficient, effective practices.

- Supervises staff and non-staff personnel in the HQ/LAC Team and provides clear, fair, support, and balanced performance feedback and reviews.

- Engages productively, professionally, collaboratively and efficiently with peers, team members, and parties internal and external to the Section to problem-solve as necessary, seek solutions and achieve positive and impactful collective outputs.

- Actively employs management techniques that ensure balance in prioritizing quality output of a high standard and a healthy workplace culture.

- Ensure field work and mission travel, which are mandatory for the position.

Ensure efficient Client Services.

- Maintains a role as a visible, active and accessible team leader, including by liaising with senior officials within the region and bureau; sharing insights from the caseload with senior managers; receiving and considering feedback on OAI investigation services; participating in regional or country level conferences or meetings to raise awareness of fraud and other control risk mitigation services.

- Liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, Regional Offices and counterparts, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

- Liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

- Where appropriate, provides advisory support to policy managers to help strengthen risk controls within UNDP, drawing on insights gleaned from the caseload.

Facilitate knowledge management and other tasks

- Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI.

- Assesses the potential for misconduct in UNDP offices and operations.

- Contributes to risk assessment planning.

- Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

- Keeps abreast of the jurisprudence of the United Nations Dispute Tribunal (UNDT) and United Nations Appeals Tribunal (UNAT).

- Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1 and/or Deputy Director (Investigations).

- Contributes to knowledge‑sharing, lessons‑learned, and capacity‑building initiatives within OAI, supporting the strengthening of investigative practice across the Section.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervise and manage Investigation Specialists and support staff, Non-personnel, Interns.

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

- People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

- Cross Functional and Technical Competencies:

Audit & Investigation - Investigation - Investigation management and investigative techniques: The ability to manage an investigation, choose avenues of inquiry and apply different techniques during an investigation, including investigative interviewing; seizure of documentary and electronic evidence; identification, collection, review and analysis of all types of evidence, including project, procurement and commercial business documentation and electronic communications; forensic analysis; verification site visits; open-source research.

Audit & Investigation - Investigation - Collection and analysis of evidence: Ability to extract and analyse all relevant types of evidence and be able to draw reasonable inferences and conclusions.

Audit & Investigation - Investigation - Investigative Interviewing: Ability to conduct investigative interviews with all types of investigation participants, including witnesses and subjects, using an approach tailored to the interviewee and the investigation.

Audit & Investigation - Investigation - Technology tools and applications for investigations: Ability to understand key application and system software, IT infrastructure, IT Control frameworks and the use of forensic investigation software.

Business Management - Communication:

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Portfolio Management:

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment.

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Criminal Justice or Investigations-related Specialization; Law; Management; Finance; or related field is required; or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, with an additional 2 years’ experience, which will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Formal professional training in a comprehensive range of investigation-related areas, e.g., from a national law enforcement or investigations academy, is an advantage.

Experience:

- A minimum of seven (7) years (with a master’s degree) or nine (9) years (with a bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in complex criminal and/or administrative investigations, including experience leading or overseeing investigative workstreams, acting as investigator or in an equivalent role is required.

- Demonstrated experience in conducting and overseeing investigations into administrative misconduct and/or criminal offences, including fraud and other financial crimes, sexual misconduct, and workplace standards of conduct violations, from intake through final reporting, is required.

- Demonstrated experience in providing technical and functional leadership in an investigative context, including guiding less experienced investigators, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, prioritizing workloads, and ensuring quality and timeliness of investigative outputs, is required.

- Demonstrated experience in addressing underperformance or misconduct within investigative teams, including providing corrective feedback, documenting performance concerns, supporting improvement, and escalating issues when required, is desirable.

- Specialized training in core investigative techniques, including interviewing, evidence handling, evidence analysis, and investigative report writing, is required.

- Specialized training and/or demonstrated experience in advanced investigative skills, such as interviewing vulnerable victims and witnesses, handling sensitive cases, digital forensics, and complex evidence analysis, is desirable.

- Demonstrated experience in leveraging investigative technologies, data analytics, and artificial intelligence tools to improve efficiency, accuracy, or timeliness of investigative processes (e.g., evidence review, pattern identification, case management, or reporting), while ensuring due process, confidentiality, and ethical use, is desirable.

- Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, persuasively, and with sound judgment in complex and sensitive situations, including conducting difficult interviews, managing challenging stakeholders, and briefing senior management on investigative findings, risks, and recommendations, is required.

- Experience in conducting risk assessments related to investigations, integrity risks, or misconduct trends is an advantage.

- At least one (1) year of experience in an international or multicultural investigative environment is desirable.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in Spanish is desirable.

- Working knowledge of French and Portuguese is an asset.

- Knowledge of another United Nations official languages is an asset.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto en Difusión Ambiental en ANP - San Luis Potosí
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Región Prioritaria para la Conservación de la APFF Sierra de San Miguelito, perteneciente a la Región Noreste y Sierra Madre Oriental, realizar acciones difusión de conservación de los ecosistemas y su biodiversidad, así como de apoyo logístico para la investigación, monitoreo de especies, educación para la conservación y vigilancia en el Área Natural Protegida asegurando el cumplimiento a la normatividad vigente, el Programa Operativo Anual y el Programa de Manejo del ANP. Lo anterior servirá para el establecimiento de áreas naturales protegidas y sus instrumentos para su manejo y regulación.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Elaborar y coordinar actividades de capacitación y Educación Ambiental a pobladores, productores y público en general del ANP.

- Diseñar y elaborar material de difusión del ANP.

- Participar en los diferentes eventos de difusión en los diversos medios de comunicación.

- Realizar talleres y eventos de difusión en temas de conservación de la biodiversidad y protección del medio ambiente, con escolares y pobladores locales de las comunidades del ANP.

- Coadyuvar en la formulación y operación del programa de manejo.

- Coadyuvar en la elaboración del Programa Operativo Anual.

- Coadyuvar en la elaboración de informes trimestrales.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la subdirección del ANP Sierra de San Miguelito; de la Dirección Regional Planicie Costera y Golfo de México, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de Preparatoria(Bachillerato), es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura o pasantía en: biología, comunicación, Ciencias sociales, exactas, ambientales o afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Relevante:

- Candidatos(as) con Certificado de Preparatoria (Bachillerato), se requieren 4 años de experiencia comprobable Educación Ambiental.

jobs.description:

Background

1- Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet.

In Pakistan, UNDP is working with the Government of Pakistan, civil society, national partners, and the people of Pakistan to help find solutions to persistent development challenges. Its work derives from and contributes to four outcome areas of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2023-2027) which include: governance; sustainable, inclusive and green economic transformation; climate change resilience and environment; and gender equality and women’s empowerment. Supported by enablers, UNDP uses a portfolio approach in Pakistan, triangulating structural transformation, leaving no one behind, and building resilience.

UNDP's country programme document for Pakistan envisions that all Pakistani people are educated and healthy, their well-being promoted and protected through economic opportunities, jobs and a climate-resilient future in a country where women and girls are safe and able to exercise their rights and to put their trust in and benefit from improved governance.

UNDP Pakistan works with the Government and communities to develop and implement local solutions to development challenges. In an evolving development context, UNDP supports the efforts of Government of Pakistan to build a more equitable, prosperous, peaceful, and resilient society, and to achieve its SDGs and COP25 targets.

Resilience, Environment and Climate Change Unit (RECCU) is supporting projects across the country to respond to the growing threat of climate change, to mainstream environmental concerns into national development planning processes, and to expand access to environmental and energy services for the poor. In particular, UNDP has sought to ensure that the poor have stronger capacities to manage, adapt, and monitor climate change. Climate Change is a huge development challenge as well as a huge environmental challenge. It is a growing problem and is now hitting the poorest and the most vulnerable first and hardest.

The 2022 floods in Pakistan have affected 33 million people, resulted in the loss of more than 1,700 lives, displaced around 9 million men, women, and children, and inundated almost one-third of productive agricultural land in Pakistan. These downstream challenges are compounded with institutional issues whereby the Government of Pakistan requires support for developing overarching frameworks to structure its flood response activities and technical expertise to set up and develop bankable projects, establish standardized mechanisms for monitoring and evaluation, and enhance strategic communications for public

outreach. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP.

UNDP has responded to the challenge by developing and launching a flagship Flood Recovery Programme (FRP) to support the Government of Pakistan’s flood recovery and rehabilitation efforts. The Programme has four key objectives dealing with the following thematic areas:

- Restoration of housing and access to/revival of essential community services.

- Restoration of livelihoods and income-generating capacities.

- Restoration of governance and service delivery.

- Accelerated environmental clean-up with strengthened capacities for Disaster Risk Management.

2- Scope of Work

The Procurement Officer will report to CO Procurement Specialist with a matrix reporting line to the FRP Operations Specialist and will work in close collaboration with the Programme Unit and project teams for resolving complex Procurement- related issues.

Review and perform quality assurance of TORs and specifications developed by the requesting unit and projects before initiation of procurement process. Build the capacities of staff to develop succinct, crisp and clear TORs for required services and specifications of goods giving details of deliverables, time period, qualification and experience requirements

- Ensure administration and implementation of the operational strategies focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance with procurement activities with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and strategies; implementation of effective internal control, proper functioning of a client- oriented procurement management system Elaboration of proposals and implementation of cost saving and reduction strategies in consultation with office management. Provision of researched information for formulation and implementation of contract strategy and strategic procurement in the CO including tendering processes and evaluation, managing the contract and contractor, legal considerations and payment conditions, sourcing strategy, supplier selection and evaluation, quality management, e-procurement implementation.

3- Organize procurement processes assigned to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support project team in preparation of procurement plan for the project and its implementation and monitoring.

- Organization of procurement processes including preparation and conducting RFQs, ITBs or RFPs, receipt of quotations, bids or proposals, their evaluation, negotiation of certain conditions of contracts in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations.

- Preparation of purchase orders and contracts in and outside Quantum/UNAll, preparation of Recurring purchase orders for contracting of services, vendors’ creation in Quantum/UNAll. Buyers profile in Quantum/UNAll. Review of procurement processes conducted by the project; submissions to the Contract, Asset and Procurement Committee (CAP) and Advisory Committee on Procurement (ACP). Implementation of the internal control system which ensures that purchase orders are duly prepared and dispatched. Timely corrective actions on POs with budget check errors and other problems. Presentation of researched information on procurement in the project. Preparation of cost-recovery bills for the procurement services provided by UNDP to projects. Keep Record and responsible for proper achieving of completed cases at Procurement Unit Database.

4- Ensure implementation of sourcing strategy and e-procurement tools focusing on achievement of the following results

- Development and update of the rosters of suppliers, implementation of supplier selection and evaluation.

- Conduct formal market research through Expression of Interest (EOI), Pre-Qualifications, Request for Information (RFI) and Open Announcements.

- Ensure effective contract management and risk assessment

- Establish contract management group and convene monthly meetings of group.

- Develop automated system alerting contract managers on critical contract dates and milestones and process the contract amendments/extensions/variations when and where required.

- Provide support and guidance to project personnel in contract management and resolving issues and disputes with the contractors/service providers/vendors.

- Manage the contract performance of different vendors and escalate to Head of Procurement regarding occurrences of non-performance by the vendors.

- Manage financial instruments such as bid securities, performance bank guarantees and performance bonds.

- Conduct risk assessment of complex and high value procurement actions for programme and project and devise risk mitigation measures.

- Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Organize and deliver various training/coaching sessions on different Procurement Topics to Project and other operations personnel.

- Organize learning sessions to create awareness about procurement rules and regulations.

- Develop flow charts of procurement methods to demonstrate steps involved and roles and responsibilities of staff.

- Synthesis of lessons learnt and best practices in Procurement.

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

3- Institutional Arrangement

The Procurement Officer will perform her/his duties under a matrix management arrangement. He/she will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP CO Procurement Specialist, with a secondary reporting line to the FRP Operations Specialist.

jobs.title: Information Technology Analyst - AI and Emerging Technologies, IPSA-9, New York, USA, UNCDF [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

The Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit (DTI) leads UNCDF's enterprise-wide digital transformation, including the integration of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies into UNCDF's investment, programmatic, and operational workflows, while also ensuring compliance with UN AI policy and guidelines. Under UNCDF's Strategic Framework 2026–2029, DTI is responsible for operationalizing a portfolio of AI agents and emerging-technology pilots that strengthen the quality of catalytic capital deployment, accelerate programme delivery, and expand financial inclusion in Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and fragile settings.

The Information Technology Analyst - AI and Emerging Technologies will work on the implementation and scaling of the AI portfolio, building on the foundational AI actions and the first deployed AI system (Strategic Alignment Intelligence, or SAI). The position is central to helping to translate UNCDF's strategic AI commitments into a mature, governed, and institutionally embedded ecosystem of digital solutions serving UNCDF's catalytic mandate, while aligning with UN and UNDP AI frameworks.

Duties and Responsibilities

The AI and Emerging Technologies Integration Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, UNCDF. The incumbent will collaborate closely with the Executive Secretary, Regional Team Leads (RTLs) and the Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, the Information Technology Analyst : AI and Emerging Technologies will be responsible for the following key result areas:

1. Operation and continuous development of UNCDF's enterprise AI agent portfolio

- Operate, maintain and improve the portfolio of AI agents deployed across UNCDF's investment, programmatic and operational workflows, including agents supporting investment pipeline analysis, investment proposal review and stress-testing, programme document drafting, donor reporting, market analysis, internal guidance on roles and workflows, and other operational processes..

- Design, prototype, test and deploy new agents on the enterprise AI platforms in use or under institutional adoption, including Google Gemini Enterprise, Salesforce Agentforce, agent development frameworks such as the Google Agent Development Kit, and additional frontier large language model providers and agentic platforms as they are integrated into UNCDF's technology stack, ensuring compliance with broader UN policy on AI governance and related technology.

- Support in identification and prioritizing of new use cases through structured discovery with teams at Headquarters and in Regional Offices, and translate them into technical designs and delivery roadmaps.

- Extend deployed agents beyond retrieval and analysis toward document generation, forecasting and workflow action, including production of analytical outputs and presentation materials directly from institutional data.

- Conduct iterative validation of agent outputs against historical institutional decisions and documented outcomes, record performance metrics, and refine agent reasoning logic and system instructions accordingly.

- Maintain version-controlled technical documentation and user guidance for each deployed agent, and coordinate onboarding across Headquarters and Regional Offices.

2. Enterprise AI architecture, data integration and institutional knowledge infrastructure

- Develop, test and maintain assigned components of the shared technical layer connecting UNCDF AI agents to institutional and external data, including interoperable connectors (Model Context Protocol servers or equivalent) that can be reused across enterprise AI platforms.

- Develop and maintain retrieval and grounding capabilities over UNCDF document repositories, enabling agents to use relevant institutional documentation, results, evaluations and lessons learned with appropriate source attribution.

- Integrate approved external development-finance, macroeconomic and credit-risk data sources into AI-agent workflows, including sources such as the World Bank, OECD, IMF and commercial risk-data providers.

- Contribute technical analysis to UNCDF’s enterprise AI initiatives, including assessment of platform capabilities, licensing approaches, costs, and user-access requirements, to inform management decisions on the multi-platform architecture.

- Work with UNCDF ICT, enterprise-systems teams and relevant UNDP counterparts to implement interoperability, authentication and security requirements, and identify potential duplication across platforms.

3. Integration of emerging technologies beyond AI

- Contribute to UNCDF’s technical exploration and integration of emerging technologies relevant to development finance, including distributed ledger technologies (e.g., Hyperledger Fabric), digital public infrastructure (DPI), digital identity and eKYC systems, tokenization, and programmable-finance applications.

- Design and implement defined feasibility assessments, technical pilots and proofs of concept demonstrating how emerging technologies may accelerate capital deployment, reduce transaction costs and enhance financial inclusion in LDCs, SIDS and fragile settings.

- Translate, when assigned, defined use cases from UNCDF’s priority financial, programmatic and operational areas into technical requirements, implementation options and draft roadmaps, in line with agreed strategic direction and technical architecture.

- Research selected emerging technologies relevant to development finance—such as CBDCs, blockchain-based financial infrastructure and interoperable payment systems—and prepare concise analysis on possible uses for UNCDF.

4. AI governance, responsible deployment and risk management

- Contribute to the development and implementation of UNCDF’s internal AI governance framework, in alignment with the UN’s policies and governance framework, including model-selection criteria, prompt governance, data-handling protocols, human-in-the-loop requirements and escalation procedures for higher-risk use cases.

- Review proposed AI use cases and deployments against applicable UN-system guidance, including the UN Principles for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence, the Global Digital Compact, and relevant UNDP/UNCDF data-protection and cybersecurity policies.

- Support the preparation and maintenance of responsible-AI monitoring documentation and basic evaluation materials, including benchmark results, limitation disclosures and validation records.

- Identify and document potential risks associated with AI integration, escalate significant issues to the supervisor, and contribute to practical mitigation measures and management briefings.

5. Partnerships, capacity building and knowledge management

- Support the Digital Transformation and Innovation unit in engagement with external AI and emerging-technology providers, including research, meeting coordination and follow-up related to potential partnerships and collaboration with relevant UN-system entities.

- Contribute to development and delivery of practical user-orientation, prompt-engineering and role-specific training sessions and materials to help UNCDF personnel use approved AI tools effectively.

- Prepare and maintain technical and programme documentation, including architecture diagrams, decision logs, reports, and updates to UNCDF’s AI priorities.

- Participate in relevant internal UN-system forums on AI for development finance, and support the preparation of materials presenting UNCDF’s work.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Thematic Area

Definition

Systems thinking & transformation

Understand that complex problems need a non- reductionistic, holistic approach. Ability to explore challenges from multiple perspectives by zooming in and out, with a focus on relationships and flows rather than individual elements; understand how certain dynamics and conditions are driving and influencing an

issue. Required Skills and Experience

Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos de la CONANP para fortificar la articulación interinstitucional, la congruencia de los instrumentos de política pública y el desarrollo de mecanismos estratégicos que favorezcan la conservación de la biodiversidad, el fortalecimiento de la gestión de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas (ANP) y otras medidas efectivas de conservación basadas en áreas (OMEC), mediante la integración de conocimientos científicos, técnicos y comunitarios, así como el seguimiento de resultados y el cumplimiento de los compromisos ambientales nacionales e internacionales.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

- Promover la convergencia de programas, estrategias y políticas públicas relacionadas con la biodiversidad, favoreciendo su vinculación con las prioridades de desarrollo sostenible y las agendas ambientales globales.

- Establecer criterios e instrumentos de seguimiento para valorar los resultados de las acciones de conservación y aportar información estratégica para el cumplimiento de los compromisos ambientales nacionales e internacionales.

- Incorporar conocimientos científicos, técnicos y comunitarios en los procesos de análisis y definición de prioridades territoriales para la conservación de la biodiversidad y el aprovechamiento sostenible de los recursos naturales.
