jobs.title: Director, Rome Centre [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition (the “UNDP Rome Centre”) is the key platform for the strategic engagement between UNDP and the Italian Government. It focuses on the critical policy areas of climate finance, youth engagement in climate action, and energy for development.

The central focus of the UNDP Rome Centre is to promote sustainable growth and resilient economic development through the mobilization of finance for climate mitigation and adaptation projects. This focus is shared by all the Centre’s programmes,

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of Director - BPPS, and the overall guidance of the Centre’s Steering Committee, the Director of the Rome Centre for Climate and Energy will be responsible for the strategic supervision of the Centre, for the external outreach and representational activities of the Centre, and the incumbent will be the representative of UNDP in Italy, tasked with coordinating the overall strategic partnership with Italy, with curating the partnership and strengthening the role of the Centre as the overall platform of collaboration between UNDP and Italy.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1. Provision of Technical Leadership of the Rome Centre for Climate & Energy

- Lead the conceptualization of the activities and outreach of the Rome Centre for Climate and Energy.

- Lead the organization and reporting for regular meetings with the donor(s), as appropriate.

- Promote, advocate for, and represent UNDP at key events.

- Identify new partnerships and strengthen existing ones through innovative approaches to partnership development.

- Maintains collaboration and coordination within the GPN and with relevant organizational units in UNDP to ensure programmatic integration and sharing of best practices.

- Liaise with UNDP senior management, technical partners, on interventions and initiatives on the relevant focus areas of the Centre.

2. Representation, Partnerships & Resource Mobilization

- Lead and coordinate the development of strategic partnerships and resource mobilization plans, particularly with the Government of Italy, relating to and strengthening UNDP’s position in climate action and energy transition, as well as support Strategic Plan implementation.

- Represent UNDP in relevant forums/mechanisms, as requested.

- Represent UNDP at a senior level in key policy fora and interactions, fostering close liaison and collaboration with UN system partners on climate action and energy transition issues.

- Cultivate and expand partnerships with bilateral, multilateral, emerging donors, International Financial Institutions (IFIs), and the private sector on climate action and energy transition, as well as broader development issues, actively seeking resource commitments and exploring new financing modalities.

- Identify, develop, and sustain partnerships with think tanks, academia, INGOs, NGOs, and development partners to leverage knowledge, expertise, and resources for climate and energy transition issues.

3. Provide top quality advisory services and lead knowledge building and management

- Deliver high-quality intellectual leadership on UNDP’s agenda by integrating climate action and energy transition issues into sustainable development knowledge products.

- Provide the relevant conceptual inputs related to the activities of the Centre for Climate and Energy

- Coordinate after-action reviews and draw lessons to enhance support mechanisms.

- Contribute to organizational learning in crisis knowledge domains.

- Coordinate with UN and other International Organizations in Rome to advance UNDP priorities and principles.

- Promote broader development effectiveness and the UN coherence agenda through new partnerships.

4. Oversight and Management of the UNDP Rome Centre

- Ensure effective management of Rome-based operations and full alignment with overall UNDP strategies, provide consistent and comprehensive support and advisory services for collaboration and integration (inclusive of human and financial resources, administrative, IT, and security matters).

- Ensure all personnel in Rome are effectively matrixed through proper span of control, reflecting the integrated office structure.

- Prepare and execute meetings for UNDP senior leadership when visiting Rome and facilitate contacts with Rome-based agencies, contributing as needed to agendas, related briefing notes at HQ.

- Provides Rome Centre related support to UNDP Country Offices as needed or when suitable opportunities arise

- Support the BPPS managed programmes and teams based in Rome, where required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Manage and supervise Rome Centre Team Leads and Administrative Assistant.

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: ​​LEVEL 4: Prioritize team workflow, mobilize resources, drive scalable results/strategic impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 4: Easily navigate complexity, encourage/enable radical innovation, has foresight

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 4: Create systems and processes that enable learning and development for all

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 4: Proactively initiate/lead organizational change, champion new systems/processes

- Act with Determination: ​​LEVEL 4: Able to make difficult decisions in challenging situations, inspire confidence

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 4: Construct strategic multi-partner alliances in high stake situations, foster co-creation

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 4: Create ethical culture, identify/address barriers to inclusion ​

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical:

- Business Development - Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations. UNDP Representation: Effectively represent and advocate for UNDP, its values, mission, work, and positions with various constituencies/audiences, shares UNDP knowledge and activities.

- Business Director & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

- Partnership Management - Resource Mobilization: Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities, and establish a plan to meet funding requirements.

- 2030 Agenda: Partnerships - Sustainable Energy: Just Energy Transition.

- 2030 Agenda: Planet - Climate: Climate Strategies and Policy: Policy and Institutional Building.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics, International Relations, Natural or Social Sciences or relevant disciplines related to Sustainable Development and International Policy are required. OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 15 years (with master’s degree) or 17 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant leadership work experience related to sustainable development, climate change and/or “green” transition is required.

- Demonstrated experience in achievement of substantive results at the nexus of policy and programming and tangible demonstrations in strategic programming, policy analysis and advice, resource mobilization, and advocacy are required.

- Experience in interagency and international co-operation, negotiation of partnerships, and mobilization of resources is required.

- Demonstrate experience in management of programmes is required.

- Experience in leadership positions and the ability to advocate for effective solutions are preferred.

- Proven experience and in-depth knowledge of developing countries’ contexts, managing complex situations, including the ability to influence/advance dialogue and present such material at global and regional for a is desired.

- Prior experience of working on issues related to developing countries or countries with economies in transition is an asset.

- Prior experience of working at cabinet level in national administration is an asset.

- Proven track record of sound knowledge of G7 / G20 inter – government processes is an asset.

- Experience in holding increasingly senior positions in the UN and/or other intergovernmental institutions and international entities is an advantage.

Language:

- Fluency in English and Italian is required with exceptional writing, presentation and communication skills.

- Fluency in French is desirable.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Program (UNDP) is the leading UN organization advancing sustainable development globally and in Ethiopia. As a key integrator within the UN system, UNDP plays a central role in helping countries achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates at global, regional, and country levels, combining international expertise with local knowledge to deliver practical solutions and impactful advocacy.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Program Support (BPPS) have the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working.  BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its program support efforts.

As per UNDP’s new Strategic Plan 2026-2029, four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience and healthy planet – define the organization’s strategic direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance.

The central purpose of the Rome Centre is to ensure the effective implementation and further development of the strategic partnership between UNDP and the government of Italy across the objectives of sustainable development and in doing so advancing the broader partnership between UNDP and G7 and G20 countries.

The Rome Centre focuses on the critical policy areas of youth engagement in climate action, energy for development and climate finance.

At the core of UNDP’s work is the Global Policy Network (GPN), which mobilizes world-class technical expertise to support six signature solutions: energy, poverty alleviation, democratic governance, resilience, environmental sustainability, and gender equality. These solutions are aligned to foster structural transformation, promote inclusion, and build resilience in Ethiopia and beyond.

Energy is a critical enabler of most countries’ development agenda and is one of UNDP’s flagship areas of intervention. UNDP’s energy work aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7), focusing on:

- Expanding access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services.

- Improving energy efficiency across sectors.

- Increasing the share of renewable energy in the national energy mix.

In Ethiopia, the government has set bold energy access and transition goals, including through Mission 300, which aims for universal electricity access by 2030, with a target of 65% on-grid and 35% off-grid connections. Achieving these ambitions will require substantial and sustained investment, robust planning, and strengthened public-private collaboration.

A key initiative supporting this agenda is "Energy for Growth in Africa", which aims to identify and support clean energy projects across the continent that face difficulties accessing finance. The initiative, launched in the context of the Italian G7 Presidency and promoted by the Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security (MASE) in collaboration with UNDP, provides technical assistance, risk mitigation tools, and access to concessional finance to improve project viability and attract private sector investment. Operated through UNDP Country Offices, the initiative works with governments to ensure alignment with national energy priorities and to help scale up investment-ready projects.

Currently active in twelve African countries, the initiative focuses on markets with limited access to commercial finance, working in close coordination with multilateral efforts to streamline support and enhance the delivery of sustainable energy solutions.

Scope of Work

The UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition is seeking an Energy Finance Specialist to support the implementation of the “Energy for Growth in Africa” program in Ethiopia. The Specialist will work in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office in Ethiopia and under the technical guidance of the Rome Centre’s Energy for Growth in Africa Team to accelerate clean energy investments aligned with national priorities and UNDP’s global and regional energy strategy.

The primary objective of this role is to identify, develop, and support energy initiatives that unlock financing and contribute to a just, inclusive, and sustainable energy transition in Ethiopia. The Energy Finance Specialist will provide strategic insights and technical expertise to ensure that interventions respond to national development goals while advancing regional and global objectives under SDG 7.

The Energy Finance Specialist will serve as the focal point for the UNDP Rome Centre’s “Energy for Growth in Africa” initiative in Ethiopia. The Specialist will provide technical expertise, strategic advice, and stakeholder coordination to accelerate clean energy investments that contribute to Ethiopia’s sustainable energy and climate goals, in alignment with CPD for Ethiopia (2025-2030), UNSCDF for Ethiopia (2025 – 2030) UNDP’s regional and global energy strategy. The key responsibilities include:

Ensure Project Identification and Origination

- Ensure the Implementation of the project origination framework established centrally by the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative;

- Ensure project identification is aligned with Ethiopia’s national energy priorities, in particular with the recently developed National Energy Compact.

Build Strategic Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination

- Map relevant stakeholders in Ethiopia energy landscape and maintain active communication to ensure inclusive and coordinated engagement;

- Engage and coordinate with key energy stakeholders—government entities, private investors, development institutions (including G7 partners and the Italian Cooperation System), and financial actors—to facilitate partnerships and co-investment opportunities;

- Organize and contribute to technical meetings, stakeholder roundtables, and outreach events to promote the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative and related energy access and transition programs;

- Engage directly and, if requested by the Government counterparts, support the Compact Delivery and Monitoring Unit that will be formed to deliver on the Mission 300 Compact.

Ensure Project Risk Mitigation and Investment Facilitation

- Liaise with financial institutions, investors, and multilateral partners to coordinate the deployment of financial instruments and appropriate risk mitigation tools for the successful completion of the projects;

- Identify opportunities for clean energy projects to generate carbon credits under voluntary or compliance carbon markets (e.g., Article 6 of the Paris Agreement), and support the integration of carbon revenue streams into project financing structures.

Provide Technical Assistance, Capacity Building, and Knowledge Sharing

- Offer technical inputs to clean energy project developers on feasibility studies, business models, power purchase agreements, and compliance with environmental and social safeguards;

- Advise and support clean energy project developers in structuring project financing by drawing on public and private, national and international climate finance sources, including those provided by multilateral development banks (e.g. WB, AfDB), vertical climate funds (e.g. GCF, GEF) and bilateral funds from G7 countries and Italy (e.g. Italian Climate Fund) - and support the submission of funding applications to these instruments. Facilitate the exchange of lessons learned and best practices with other participating countries under the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative.

Reporting, Monitoring, and Impact Assessment

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background/ Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end poverty, inequality and climate change, working in more than 170 countries.

The Regional Bureau for Africa (RBA) provides strategic direction, quality assurance and oversight across UNDP's 46 Country Offices in sub-Saharan Africa. Its Regional Programme Document (RPD) 2026–2029, anchored in the African Union's Agenda 2063 and the Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan — the "decade of acceleration" — pursues four outcomes: Prosperity, Governance, Crisis Prevention and Resilience, and Planet. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) — digital identity, payments and data exchange — is a foundational enabler across all four. It provides the digital rails for AfCFTA implementation and for SME and youth access to markets and credit; underpins RPD Output 2.4 on digital and AI policy for safe, secure public service delivery; enables risk-informed social protection and digital health; and strengthens natural resource governance and just energy transitions.

The Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub is UNDP's global centre of excellence for digital transformation, providing technical advisory, capacity building and programmatic support to Regional Centres and Country Offices. Within it, the DPI Safeguards Team ensures Africa's foundational digital rails are built with protection and equity at their core, so that scaling DPI does not deepen inequality or compromise human rights.

The position sits within the DPI Safeguards Team and is the operational bridge between the DAI Hub and RBA. It translates the RPD's digital ambition into country-level delivery — embedding safeguarding-by-design across the regional DPI portfolio, supporting country readiness assessments and national implementation roadmaps, and mobilizing partnerships and financing for the Africa DPI Accelerator.

Delivery spans 46 diverse country contexts — Anglophone, Francophone, Lusophone and Arabic-speaking, several fragile or crisis-affected — with uneven digital maturity, politically sensitive data governance environments, and multiple sovereign and continental stakeholders. The role is home-based and requires remote engagement across time zones.

Duties and Responsibilities

Lead strategic design and alignment of the regional DPI portfolio

- Align the Africa DPI Accelerator with the RPD 2026–2029, embedding digital ID, payments and data exchange in the Prosperity and Governance outcomes through a use-case-led approach across health, financial inclusion, livelihoods, agriculture, climate and digital trade. Contributes to: RPD Outcomes 1 and 2; AU Digital Transformation Strategy and Agenda 2063 Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan.

Lead country readiness and national implementation roadmaps

- With the DAI Hub readiness assessment lead, programme-manage DPI readiness assessments in priority countries, identify programmatic entry points to close the digital divide, and support national implementation roadmaps.

- Contributes to: Country Office programming across 46 offices; national digital transformation strategies; SDG acceleration.

Safeguarding-by-design across the DPI lifecycle

- Integrate universal DPI safeguards — data privacy, digital rights, inclusive governance — into country implementation plans from design through maintenance, and standardize repeatable protocols across Country Offices.

- Contributes to: RPD Outcome 2 (Governance) and Output 2.4; UNDP Universal DPI Safeguards Framework and the global DPI Safeguards agenda; UNDP Social and Environmental Standards.

Provide high -level technical advisory and regional intelligence

- Advise RBA leadership and Country Offices on responsible DPI and AI deployment, generate evidence on how DPI accelerates sectoral results, and track global and regional DPI trends, innovations and emerging risks.

- Contributes to: RPD target of 15 regional and national institutions strengthened by 2029; RBA knowledge leadership and UNDP's global DPI positioning.

Build strategic partnerships, knowledge management and sustainable financing

- Build alliances with the AU, RECs and Smart Africa to harmonize cross-border digital policy and interoperability standards; mobilize resources through concept notes, proposals and blended finance; and leverage timbuktoo to connect startups and tech hubs to national DPI projects and capital. Advise on knowledge building and sharing.

- Contributes to: AfCFTA implementation; RPD resource mobilization targets; timbuktoo and the Digital Public Goods Alliance, Co-Develop, GovStack and 50-in-5 communities; South-South and triangular cooperation.

Ensure Institutionalization and sustainability

- Curate regional DPI intelligence for the "State of DPI in Africa" agenda, convene a regional community of practice, and design the roadmap for transitioning the DPI Accelerator from a catalytic programme into a permanent regional facility.

- Contributes to: sustainability of the Africa DPI Accelerator beyond 2028; integration of DPI safeguards into UNDP's core service offer.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Digital Public Infrastructure Advisor – Africa reports directly to the Director, Regional Programme for Africa (RBA) and to the Director, AI Hub and Head of Digital and AI Programmes.

As an RBA-anchored position, the Director, Regional Programme for Africa is the primary supervisor, responsible for setting priorities, approving workplans and conducting performance assessment. The Director, AI Hub and Head of Digital and AI Programmes provides second-level reporting, ensuring technical coherence with UNDP's global digital, AI and DPI safeguards standards. The incumbent maintains regular coordination and information sharing with the DAI Hub, including the DPI Safeguards Team, so that regional delivery remains aligned with global methodologies and the Hub's work benefits from regional evidence.

The incumbent works in close collaboration with RBA regional programme teams and the 46 Country Offices in sub-Saharan Africa, DAI Hub technical teams, and relevant continental and regional partners. The position carries no supervisory responsibilities but is expected to lead joint RBA–DAI workstreams and task teams on a matrix basis.

The position is home-based.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

- Strategic Thinking Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

- An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in International Development, International Relations, Governance, Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Law, Human Rights, Economics, or Social Sciences is required. OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the above fields, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 10 years (with Master's degree) or 12 years (with Bachelor's degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in regional or multi-country programmes, governance, digital transformation, public policy or related development fields is required.

Required skills:

- Demonstrated experience supporting digital, data or technology programmes in a development context, including advising on their governance and implementation.

- Demonstrated experience building and managing multi-stakeholder partnerships across government, regional bodies, private sector and development partners.

Desired skills:

- Experience designing or implementing digital platforms or data-driven tools in developing country contexts.

- Experience applying safeguards or do-no-harm approaches to digital systems in fragile or conflict-affected settings.

- Experience working within the UN system, particularly UNDP.

- Experience working with the African Union and regional bodies, as well as development partners and south-south cooperation partners.

- Experience working in or with countries in the Africa region.

- Proven Familiarity with the AU Digital Transformation Strategy, Agenda 2063 and AfCFTA.

- Experience engaging start-up ecosystems, innovation financing or blended finance instruments.

- Demonstrated experience managing or leading multi-country or regional development programmes, including workplanning, delivery oversight and results reporting.

- Demonstrated experience applying governance, human rights or accountability frameworks to digital or data systems, including data protection, digital rights or responsible technology approaches.

- Demonstrated experience providing policy or technical advisory services to governments, regional institutions or continental bodies.

- Demonstrated experience in resource mobilization, including developing concept notes and funding proposals and engaging donors

- Demonstrated experience managing consultants or technical teams, including terms of reference, deliverables and quality assurance

The RBM/M&E Associate position falls under the PMSU unit within the UNDP Egypt office. By offering centralized guidance on Programme Finance, Results-Based Management (RBM) and quality assurance, the unit enhances the impact of the UNDP Egypt Country Programme (2023–2027) through systematic monitoring, evaluation, and strict adherence to corporate compliance standards.

Under the direct supervision of the Programme Management Analyst (NOA), the RBM/M&E Associate provides support to the leadership in the execution of oversight and management performance, and supports the formulation, planning and management of the country programme and integrated support team by managing data and facilitating implementation of various initiatives and activities aiming to effectively deliver development results. The RBM/M & E Associate promotes a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. In this context, the incumbent is responsible for the continuous identification and updating of project risks (strategic, operational, financial, and political) within UNDP’s enterprise resource planning system (Quantum).

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Supports timely implementation and effective management of RBM and M&E for the country office and projects focusing on achievement of the following:

Prepares project operational and administrative reports by collecting, selecting, reviewing and maintaining a wide range of information. Verifies that all projects are monitored in accordance with the monitoring plan. Informs deviations from the planned activities and identifies needs for reprogramming;

- Provides technical assistance for quality assurance of the implementation of the monitoring process, results framework and management arrangements of projects to guarantee a result-based management approach. This includes regular review of progress against set targets at project level. Assists in the provision of guidance/inputs at the design stage of projects;

- Supports the development of instruments to ensure a high quality of monitoring activities. Participates in results-oriented monitoring and evaluation training efforts in the Country Office;

- Assists in the development, updating, effective and efficient implementation of the CO programme and projects’ Monitoring and Evaluation plans;

- Assists in development of measurement and monitoring tools and identify data sources for programme and/or projects’ performance and indicators;

- Supports the programme/project team with data management and identifying programmatic/project issues and prompt corrective actions to enhance the programme/project objectives;

- Prepares necessary M&E forms and format to capture necessary data and information from the field;

- Supports and/or works to capture, document, and analyze that information and data from the projects’ activities in a results-based and timely manner;

- Provides and/or supports coordination of inputs in developing the Annual Work Plans (AWPs), projects’ implementation plans, etc.;

2. Assists the effective management and implementation of the evaluations policies, strategies and processes focusing on achievement of the following:

- Prepares reports and submits documents to the Government, UN Agencies and UNDP Headquarters by collecting and selecting relevant data from documents, legislation extracts, specialized publications and websites;

- Drafts preliminary presentation of information;

- Provides inputs in the formulation of Terms of Reference for outcome evaluations. Assists in the revision of TORs for specific project/thematic/sectorial evaluation missions and/or desk evaluations/reviews;

- Participates in consultant and evaluation team selection and technical feedback on evaluations;

- Assist in the process of carrying out evaluations (review of reports, participation in meetings, participation in the management and/or organization of seminars, meetings and other special events).

3. Provides administrative supports in preparation of reports completion of corporate online tools focusing on achievement of the following:

- Enters and/or reviews projects’ data to the data management system (Quantum, Quantum+, IMRP and other systems), updates project-related data on websites, as needed;

- Schedules and assigns responsibilities for activities/events needed for monitoring;

- Assists in the identification of potential implementation problems and bottlenecks and contributes to the common M&E activity of the UNDP Country Office;

- Supports programme/projects’ teams in conducting surveys, studies, assessments and similar activities;

- Liaises with the Field Moniroting Assistants within broader UNDP M&E activities and efforts;

- Maintains sound filing system including in the online SharePoint/MS Teams systems and appropriates use and recording of programme/project’s experience, activities and results;

- Provides inputs, information and statistics for quarterly, annual and other reports;

- Assists in the preparation of background documentation and working papers for its utilization in meetings with the Government and project authorities;

4. Facilitates knowledge building and knowledge sharing focusing on achievement of the following:

- Identifies and formulates lessons learned and documents best practices from evaluations and studies to be integrated into programme reports;

- Contributes to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Under the supervision of the Head of Unit, establishes connections, coordinates and disseminates information, in both ways, within the team, with other relevant units and the whole office;

- Contributes to regular capacity building of the programme/project(s) and CO staff on RBM, M&E and other relevant topics;

- Supports programme/project teams in the promotion of monitoring and evaluation standards, quality assurance/control and capacity development;

- Supports knowledge sharing and learning programme-wide in the MSU Team and the entire CO;

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

The incumbent will report directly to the Programme Management Analyst (NOA) and will work closely with the G7 RBM/M & E Associate. S/he will work closely with the other members of the PMSU team and the Programme team to support quality assurance and compliance of programme policies and procedures. The RBM/M&E Associate also works on project-specific tasks while ensuring compliance with UNDP Corporate Guidelines and is expected to act a liaison between project-level data collection and Country Office-level reporting, to better support Results-Oriented Annual Report (ROAR).

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est une organisation internationale avec plus de 17 000 employés travaillant dans environ 170 bureaux dans le monde pour aider les gouvernements à développer des politiques, des institutions et des partenariats solides pour atteindre le Programme de développement durable et ses 17 objectifs de développement durable à l’horizon 2030. Dans le cadre de son mandat, le PNUD contribue aux efforts des pays dans le renforcement de leurs capacités de résilience face aux effets du changement climatique et à la gestion durable des ressources naturelles.

Afin de concrétiser et de renforcer son engagement en faveur de la conservation et de la gestion durable des forêts algériennes, le PNUD met en œuvre une initiative en partenariat avec la Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF) et le soutien du Fonds pour l’Environnement Mondial (GEF), visant à promouvoir la restauration et la gestion forestière durable de l’écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie. L’écosystème de Pin d’Alep, qui s’étend sur plus d’un million d’hectares dans les Hauts Plateaux, est soumis à des pressions croissantes liées à la dégradation des terres, aux effets du changement climatique (sécheresse, incendies, attaques parasitaires) et aux activités anthropiques non durables. Face à cette situation, le PNUD Algérie soutient la Direction Générale des Forêts afin de mettre en œuvre une série d’actions visant à restaurer les paysages forestiers dégradés, renforcer les capacités de gestion durable des forêts et contribuer au développement des économies locales dans les wilayas ciblées.

À la lumière de ce qui précède, le bureau du PNUD à Alger prévoit de recruter un/e Coordinateur/trice de projet pour soutenir l’exécution et la mise en œuvre de l’initiative « Restauration et Gestion Forestière Durable de l’Écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie ». Le/la coordinateur/trice devra travailler en collaboration avec l’équipe programme Nature, Climat et Énergie et avec la Direction Générale du Projet, et devra prévoir des déplacements fréquents dans les wilayas d’intervention.

Portée des travaux

En étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et la supervision directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF.

Le/la Coordinateur/trice du projet travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le Directeur National du Projet, l’associé(e) administratif (ve) et financier (e) et Team Leader du portefeuille Nature, Climat et Énergie du Bureau Pays du PNUD ainsi qu'avec les diverses parties prenantes parmi lesquelles, principalement, la Direction Générale des Forêts et le Ministère de l’Agriculture et du Développement Rural et de la Pêche.

Résumé des fonctions:

- Gestion de projet : Assurer la gestion administrative et financière du projet selon les règles et procédures du PNUD, et veiller à la réalisation des activités et l’atteinte des résultats du projet dans les délais fixés via un plan de travail détaillé ;

- Appui et conseil technique : Veiller à la qualité des produits techniques et à la coordination des travaux techniques, au besoin ;

- Appuyer le développement de réseaux/partenariats : Appuyer la communication des résultats, le développement du réseau de parties prenantes à impliquer dans le projet, et assurer la circulation de l’information et bâtir des relations en vue de maximiser l’engagement des acteurs dans le processus de mise en œuvre du projet

Axe 1 – Gestion administrative, financière et opérationnelle du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice assure la gestion quotidienne du projet conformément aux règles, procédures et politiques du PNUD (POPP), notamment :

- Coordonner et superviser le travail des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) déployées dans les 3 wilayas ciblées par le projet

- Coordonner le travail de l’équipe chargée de préparer et réviser les plans de travail et les programmes financiers, veiller à la soumission dans les délais des rapports financiers et des rapports d’avancement trimestriels, du rapport annuel du projet et autres rapports ;

- Élaborer et mettre à jour les plans de travail annuels (PTA) et pluriannuels du projet, en coordination avec la DGF et l'équipe NCE du PNUD, et en assurer le suivi continu

- Gérer le cycle de vie du projet : planification, mise en œuvre, suivi, ajustements et clôture

- Assurer la liaison permanente entre les consultants, l'UGP, la partie nationale (DGF/MADR) et le bureau de pays du PNUD

- Planifier et coordonner les activités de terrain sur les trois sites du projet (Telagh, Beni Imloul, Senalba) et y effectuer des missions régulières de supervision

- Identifier, suivre et atténuer les risques liés à la mise en œuvre du projet

- Organiser les réunions périodiques du Comité de Pilotage (Board de Projet) et en assurer le secrétariat et le suivi des décisions

- Préparer les rapports d'avancement : rapports mensuels d'activités, rapports trimestriels, Rapports annuels de mise en œuvre (PIR) destinés au GEF, et rapport de fin de projet

- Assurer le suivi des décaissements et des dépenses par rapport aux budgets approuvés, en coordination avec l'assistant(e) administratif(ve) et financier(ère)

- Préparer et soumettre les rapports financiers trimestriels au PNUD

- Mettre à jour régulièrement les Indicateurs de Base du GEF (Core Indicators 3, 4, 6 et 11) pour les rapports d'étape et les évaluations (MTR et TE)

Axe 2 – Supervision technique et assurance qualité des livrables du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice veille à la qualité scientifique et technique des produits du projet :

- Rédiger et valider les Termes de Référence pour le recrutement de consultants, d'experts et de prestataires (experts en SFM/FLR, spécialistes en PSE, experts genre, M&E, etc.) recrutés par le PNUD

- Superviser, orienter et évaluer les travaux des consultants recrutés par le PNUD, et valider leurs livrables en coordination avec la DGF, le DNP, le PNUD et les parties prenantes concernées.

- Veiller à l'intégration transversale des questions de genre et d'inclusion sociale dans tous les livrables et activités du projet (marqueur genre GEN 2)

- Suivre la mise en œuvre des outils de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (ESMF, SESP) et veiller au respect des normes environnementales et sociales du PNUD

- Contribuer aux apports techniques permettant d'aligner les produits du projet avec la Loi 23-21 sur les forêts et des stratégies nationales de développement forestier

- Apporter un appui à la sélection des experts et consultants/prestataires du projet, et prendre part au processus de sélection en cas de besoin ;

Axe 3 – Communication, partenariats et gestion des connaissances

Le/la Coordinateur/trice est responsable de la visibilité du projet et de la mobilisation des parties prenantes :

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec l'ensemble des parties prenantes du projet

- Appuyer l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de communication du projet, en lien avec le/la chargé(e) de communication de la DGF et du PNUD

- Fournir les éléments nécessaires à la production d'articles, notes d'information, messages-clés et supports de communication relatifs aux résultats et enseignements du projet

- Assurer une veille active sur les initiatives complémentaires (FAO, IFAD, GEF SGP, programmes gouvernementaux) pertinentes pour les thématiques du projet

- Promouvoir le partage des bonnes pratiques, des enseignements tirés et des innovations du projet au sein des réseaux nationaux et internationaux pertinents

- Représenter le projet dans les forums, ateliers et réunions techniques nationaux et internationaux, au besoin

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Résultats attendus :

Sur la base de la description détaillée des tâches qui précède, les résultats attendus du/de la coordinateur/tric du projet, seront principalement :

- Mise en œuvre efficace et dans les délais du Plan de Travail Annuel du projet

- Qualité et conformité de tous les livrables techniques du projet aux standards du PNUD et du GEF

- Rapports financiers et programmatiques soumis dans les délais impartis

- Comité de Pilotage du Projet fonctionnel et réuni au moins deux fois par an

- Intégration effective du genre et des sauvegardes dans tous les aspects du projet

- Mobilisation active et constructive des parties prenantes à tous les niveaux

- Promouvoir le plaidoyer sur les tendances du développement et les opportunités de collaboration, en coordination avec les partenaires du projet, les parties prenantes et le personnel de communication du PNUD.

Dispositif institutionnel

Le/la coordonnateur/trice travaillera en étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et sera sous la supervision Directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF. Le/la coordonnateur/trice assurera la supervision de l’équipe des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) composée de trois (3) personnes déployées dans les trois wilayas visées par le projet.

Compétences :

Essentielles

Atteindre des Résultats

Niveau 2 : Faire monter en échelle les solutions et simplifier les processus, tout en équilibrant rapidité et précision dans l’exécution du travail.

Pensée Innovante

Engager et Partenaires

jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto en Estrategias para el Fortalecimiento del Sistema de ANP - Morelos
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Dirección Regional Centro y Eje Neovolcánico, asegurando el soporte técnico, cartográfico y documental para la planeación, establecimiento y fortalecimiento del sistema de áreas naturales protegidas (ANP) y esquemas alternativos de conservación en la Región Centro y Eje Neovolcánico, bajo enfoques de conectividad biológica y manejo integrado del paisaje.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Coadyuvar en la elaboración de diagnósticos territoriales socioambientales que identifiquen las oportunidades de nuevas declaratorias de áreas naturales protegidas bajo un enfoque de conectividad.

- Apoyar en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de información regional en materia de biodiversidad, cambio climático, monitoreo biológico y otros elementos socioambientales para la formulación de estudios que mejoren el manejo de las actuales ANP y soporten el establecimiento de nuevas declaratorias u otros esquemas de conservación.

- Apoyar en la elaboración e integración de expedientes de estudios y análisis de evaluación para el establecimiento y/o Modificación de Decretos en las áreas que se requiera bajo un enfoque de manejo integrado del paisaje.

- Apoyar en la coordinación intra e interinstitucional para el intercambio de información que facilite la conformación de estudios para nuevos decretos de áreas naturales protegidas otras modalidades de conservación.

- Apoyar en el fortalecimiento de los proyectos estratégicos regionales para el fortalecimiento del sistema de áreas naturales protegidas de la Región Centro y Eje Neovolcánico.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica directa del titular de la Dirección Regional Centro y Eje Neovolcánico, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Candidatos(as) con Certificado de preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Biología, Ecología, Manejo de Recursos Naturales, Geografía, Ciencias Ambientales o afín, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia:

- Para candidatos/as con Certificado de Preparatoria (Bachillerato), se requieren 4 años de experiencia comprobable.

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 1 año de experiencia en: Conservación de la Biodiversidad.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Conocimiento/experiencia en: Monitoreo.

- Conocimiento/experiencia en: Proyectos ambientales, sustentables, reforestación.

- Conocimiento/experiencia en: Capacitación del personal.

- Conocimiento/experiencia en: Trabajo en campo y con comunidades.

- Se dará ventaja si cuenta con experiencia en manejo de equipo informático: ArcGIS, Plataformas cola-borativas y herramientas digitales (Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Power point Inter-medio, Google Earth, ArcGis, Qgis, MatLab, SIG, manejo de bases de datos y experiencia en Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized SEAH, IT forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership

The Investigations Specialist functionally reports to the Investigations Team Lead, Headquarters, Latin America and the Caribbean (HQ/LAC Team) (P4), on investigation issues, under the overall supervision of the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1.

Position Purpose

Under the supervision of the Investigations Team Lead, Headquarters, Latin America and the Caribbean (HQ/LAC Team) (P4), the primary role of the Investigations Specialist is to conduct investigations into alleged wrongdoing that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above.

The primary role of the Investigations Specialist is to conduct investigations into alleged misconduct that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above, and that relates to Latin America.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Provision of Efficient Investigations Management

· Conducts case assessments and/or investigations into allegations in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures and the OAI investigation guidelines.

· Plans investigations to ensure that all appropriate lines of inquiry are identified and investigation resources are used effectively and efficiently to factually determine the issues relevant to an investigation.

· Identifies, collects and analyses information, demonstrating an understanding of information security and confidentiality issues relevant to investigation.

· Collects, records and handles evidence appropriately, ensuring chain of custody and demonstrating knowledge of handling considerations for different types of evidence.

· Uses specialist investigation services as and when appropriate (for example, handwriting analysis, document examination and computer forensics).

· Uses investigative technologies including case management systems, analytical software, open-source intelligence tools and artificial intelligence enabled solutions to enhance investigative efficiency, accuracy and timeliness.

· Interviews witnesses showing appropriate communications skills, accurate recording and verification of testimony through the use of interpreters as required.

· Interviews subjects/suspects in accordance with generally accepted best practice procedures (in order to obtain reliable information, while affording due process).

· Undertakes frequent, and at times extended, missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including areas with hazardous working conditions.

· Ensures that case records, databases, and documentation for matters under the Investigator’s responsibility are accurate, complete, and up to date, supporting institutional accountability and auditability.

· Formulates and recommends case closure decisions, including assessments of evidentiary sufficiency and proportionality, for review and approval by the Team Lead.

· Proposes action to close matters where appropriate.

· Drafts investigation reports of a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations.

· Field work and mission travel are mandatory for the position.

2.) Ensure efficient Client Services

• Under the direction of the Investigations Team Lead, Headquarters, Latin America and the Caribbean (HQ/LAC Team) (P4), liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, the Procurement Support Office, the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

• Under the direction of the Investigations Team Lead HQ/LAC, liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

3.) Facilitate knowledge management and other tasks

• Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI.

• Assesses the potential for fraud and corruption in UNDP offices and operations.

• Contributes to risk assessment planning.

• Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

• Keeps him/herself abreast of the jurisprudence of the United Nations Dispute Tribunal (UNDT) and United Nations Appeals Tribunal (UNAT).

• Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Deputy Director and/or the Chief, Investigations, Unit 3.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP has achieved significant progress in making gender equality and women’s empowerment integral to its work on human development. It’s Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029 builds on the lessons and achievements of previous gender equality strategies and advances gender equality as a core accelerator of human development. The Strategy aims to support governments in transforming the systems, institutions, and power structures that perpetuate gender inequalities by placing gender equality at the center of political, economic, and environmental decision-making.

The Gender Team (BPPS) has the leading role in the implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029. The Gender Equality Global Programme (GEGP) serves as a key vehicle for advancing this agenda, including Outcome 1: Economies are inclusive, and women are economically empowered. Under this outcome, UNDP supports countries in developing and implementing gender-responsive economic and fiscal policies, strengthening public finance systems, expanding investments in the care economy, and generating evidence on the impacts of taxation, public expenditure, and social protection policies on gender equality. Through research, policy advisory services, and capacity development, the Programme contributes to ensuring that public resources and fiscal reforms support more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable development outcomes for gender equality.

Background

This role is part of a project financed by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office. ( FCDO) and the European Union and managed by UNDP that seeks to address aspects of serious and organized crime (SOC). Tanzania faces a number of challenges with regard to Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (CSEA) and in particular online child abuse. One strand of the project seeks to strengthen Tanzania’s ability to respond to both domestic and international dimensions of human trafficking and child protection. With the SOC project support, Tanzania has established a cross agency Anti-Human Trafficking and Child Protection Task Force (AHTCPTF). This unit is conducting some of the most challenging cases in Tanzania.

The Criminal Justice Specialist will support the cases and work with the Tanzanian government and other partners to establish good practice, new techniques, processes and systems required to improve the investigation, prosecution of these cases and support to victims which can be scaled up across Tanzania for system change. The Criminal Justice Specialist will provide technical expertise to the AHTCPTF to manage the NCMEC and other intelligence source referrals into Tanzania and assist them to develop systems to prioritize the investigation of high-risk cases and ability to investigate and prosecute resulting cases.

Duties and Responsibilities

Mentor the Head of the Task Force and other leaders to lead a team responsible for developing and progressing investigations through methods including traditional and technical evidential capture

- Provide strategic mentoring and leadership support to the Head of the Task Force and supervisory officers.

- Strengthen leadership capacity in the planning, prioritization, and oversight of investigations.

- Guide investigators in the effective use of traditional investigative techniques and digital evidence gathering methodologies.

- Support the development of operational plans and investigative strategies for complex cases.

Mentor the Task Force to manage complex investigations and prosecutions to ensure that they are carried out thoroughly in accordance with international human rights standards and relevant Tanzanian legislation.

- Provide case-based mentoring on the management of serious and complex investigations.

- Support investigators and prosecutors in applying human rights-based approaches throughout the investigative and prosecution process.

- Advise on compliance with relevant Tanzanian laws, policies, and procedural requirements.

- Promote best practices in evidence management, case documentation, and prosecution preparation

Guide and support the Task Force to triage online reports, assess intelligence, and carry out investigations and prosecutions against individuals assessed as high-risk online offenders targeting vulnerable persons.

- Guide and support in the assessment and prioritization of online reports and intelligence referrals.

- Support the identification and development of investigative leads from digital intelligence sources.

- Mentor Task Force personnel in conducting online investigations targeting high-risk offenders.

- Strengthen coordination between investigators and prosecutors to facilitate effective case progression

Guide and support the Task Force to secure international evidence and its successful use in court proceedings.

- Advise on processes for obtaining evidence through international cooperation mechanisms.

- Support the preparation of requests for mutual legal assistance and other international evidence-gathering measures.

- Guide investigators and prosecutors on evidentiary requirements for admissibility in court.

- Facilitate engagement with relevant international law enforcement and judicial counterparts, where appropriate

Guide and support the continued use and implementation of new investigative techniques and assist the Task Force to address barriers to their effective application.

- Promote the use of video-recorded interviews of suspects, witnesses, and victims in accordance with legal requirements.

- Support the application of forensic and scientific evidence, including DNA, where appropriate.

- Assist in the standardization and effective use of investigation files, procedures, and case management tools

- Identify and recommend solutions to operational, legal, or institutional barriers affecting the use of innovative investigative techniques

Guide and support the NPS prosecutors assigned to the Task Force to prepare online cases for prosecution, including cases involving online child sexual exploitation and abuse, and strengthen the use of new evidential techniques.

- Mentor prosecutors on the preparation and presentation of digital evidence in court.

- Support the development of prosecution strategies for online-facilitated offences.

- Strengthen the use of emerging evidential techniques and digital forensic products in prosecutions.

- Identify challenges affecting successful prosecution outcomes and support the development of practical solutions

Guide and support the Head of the Task Force in developing performance monitoring systems and mechanisms for capturing lessons learned.

- Guide and assist in establishing performance monitoring and reporting frameworks for the Task Force.

- Support the conduct of quarterly case review and case management meetings.

- Facilitate the identification, documentation, and dissemination of key lessons, challenges, and good practices.

- Support the preparation of periodic performance reports and recommendations to inform criminal justice system reforms and improvements.

The Specialist will closely work with the leadership of the Task Force in Mainland, the technical lead NPS and other LE as relevant.
