- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the United Nations’ lead agency for international development. It works with countries and partners to address interconnected development challenges, strengthen institutions and resilience, and advance sustainable development. UNDP operates through a global network of headquarters, regional and country offices and delivers programmes across development, humanitarian, crisis and post-crisis contexts.

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is one of the key UNDP corporate Bureaus that provides the corporate management architecture, policies, systems, advisory support and operational services that enable UNDP to deliver results with accountability and effective stewardship of resources.

Within BMS, the Office of Human Resources (OHR) is responsible for UNDP’s people management function, with a focus on enabling UNDP to have the right capacity and organizational culture to deliver on its mandate and enable people who work for the organization to perform at their best in the environment of inclusion and respect.

UNDP is currently operating in a period of significant institutional transformation, requiring OHR to strengthen strategic people leadership, modernize HR service delivery and enable the organization to adapt with agility while sustaining performance and accountability. In this context, OHR is seeking a high-caliber leader with a strong HR management background and the capacity, commitment and mindset to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship and transformative results in the role of Deputy Director, OHR.

Duties and Responsibilities

As a member of OHR’s leadership team, working under the direct supervision of the Director, OHR and in close partnership with the Chief, HR Services, the Deputy Director, OHR provides substantive leadership for the continued development and implementation of an integrated talent management system that connects strategic workforce planning, organizational and job design, talent acquisition and deployment, succession management, career and leadership development, performance management, workplace experience, organizational culture, health and wellbeing. The Deputy Director fosters innovation across this system by using workforce data, artificial intelligence, automation and other digital solutions responsibly to improve decision quality, user experience, operational efficiency and organizational agility.

The Deputy Director ensures that integrated talent management strategies, policies, capabilities and service delivery arrangements are aligned with UNDP’s strategy and priorities and evolving business, operating and funding models. This includes shaping talent solutions that respond to changing programme and operational requirements, resource trends and the needs of different organizational contexts, while safeguarding fairness, inclusion, accountability and the effective management of institutional risk. The Deputy Director is accountable for strategic coherence and operational excellence across the talent lifecycle and for enabling a high-performing, adaptable and healthy workforce capable of delivering sustainable development results.

The Deputy Director serves as the Director’s principal strategic partner and deputizes for the Director, including representing OHR in senior management and inter-agency and staff-management forums.

The Deputy Director champions organizational excellence and professionalism and models inclusive and supportive people leadership by promoting accountability, collaboration, innovation and high performance and creating an environment in which personnel can perform, develop and thrive.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks and crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to strengthen horizontal collaboration.

1. Provide Strategic Leadership, Portfolio Oversight and Deputy Direction for OHR

- Provide strategic direction and oversight for the teams in the Deputy Director’s portfolio, ensuring integrated, client-focused delivery aligned with UNDP’s People Strategy and organizational priorities.

- Build and sustain strategic partnerships with UN entities, Member States, donors and external institutions, and mobilize resources to advance UNDP’s people priorities, programmes and services.

- Lead the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies across the portfolio to improve decision-making, service quality and operational efficiency.

- Ensure the quality, coherence and consistent delivery of corporate integrated talent management programmes across headquarters, regional and country offices.

- Represent OHR and deputize for the Director as assigned, including supporting the Director and UNDP in negotiations with staff representatives.

- As required, represent UNDP in senior-level HR forums, inter-agency bodies and strategic working groups, shaping system-wide dialogue, policies and practices.

2. Oversee Strategic Workforce Planning and Workforce Architecture

- Shape and lead the corporate workforce planning function, ensuring alignment with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, People Strategy, business and funding models and evolving business priorities.

- Lead the governance and continued evolution of UNDP’s workforce architecture, including job design, ensuring coherent job families, role profiles, position titles, career pathways and job design standards across the organization.

- Provide advice on complex workforce and organizational design matters, including reorganization, workforce optimization, as well as functional and HR alignment processes.

3. Provide Leadership to Talent Acquisition and Deployment

- Provide strategic oversight of UNDP’s talent acquisition and recruitment strategies, ensuring timely, transparent and effective outcomes of related processes.

- Ensure development and continuous improvement of talent acquisition, recruitment and deployment policies, procedures and practices across UNDP, and compliance with these across UNDP.

- Oversee senior-level recruitment and selection processes, ensuring sound governance, institutional rigor and the identification of high-caliber and diverse leadership talent.

- Provide strategic direction for talent deployment and mobility, including the Internal Talent Marketplace.

- Engage relevant stakeholders to anticipate talent needs and continuously improve talent acquisition and deployment strategies, policies and practices.

- Ensure UNDP leverages workforce analytics, digital platforms and innovative sourcing approaches to strengthen talent pipelines.

4. Oversee Succession Management and Talent Development

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the succession management function, ensuring leadership continuity, robust pipelines for critical and senior-level roles, and effective management of succession risks.

- Oversee the design and implementation of people and leadership development strategies that build a skilled, diverse and adaptable workforce aligned with UNDP’s evolving priorities.

- Ensure succession and talent development strategies are integrated with strategic workforce planning, career development, mobility, performance management and other functions in the integrated talent management cycle.

5. Oversee Performance Management, Workplace Experience and Culture

- Provide strategic leadership for UNDP’s organizational culture, ensuring that organizational values, leadership practices, people systems and ways of working reinforce inclusion, collaboration, accountability and high performance.

- Shape UNDP’s performance management, workplace experience and employee engagement approach.

- Lead organizational efforts to promote gender parity, diversity, equity and inclusion and to sustain a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, sexual harassment and abuse of authority, in coordination with relevant policy, ethics, oversight and support functions.

- Ensure that evidence from employee engagement, workplace experience and performance management informs leadership action, workforce planning, talent development, succession management, recognition and the continuous improvement of people policies and programmes.

- Oversee organizational approaches to mental health, psychosocial support, wellbeing and workforce resilience.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent directly oversees five HR Advisors (P5) and one HR Specialist (P4).

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

Within the Global Policy Network (GPN), the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for SDGs. As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

Through SFH, UNDP’s Istanbul Center for Private Sector in Development (ICPSD), one of the five Global Thematic Policy Centers of UNDP, acts as an enabler for the private sector and foundations to become more active partners in development, encouraging them through policy advice and technical services on how to contribute towards the achievement of the 2030 Agenda. ICPSD was established in 2011 in partnership with the Government of Turkey. The Center’s work to engage foundations and the private sector focuses on delivering policy advice and technical services in four thematic areas:

- Private sector engagement through South-South cooperation for the SDGs

- Digital transformation and private sector engagement in skills development

- SDG Financing and Private Sector Development

- Resilience and crisis response

Under its “SDG Financing and Private Sector Development” thematic area, the Center offers research, advocacy and multi-stakeholder partnership services to diversify sources of financing for the sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with a focus on attracting private impact capital. Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will support UNDP ICPSD’s SDG Financing and Private Sector Development portfolio Country Offices and in advancing strategic knowledge management objectives, leading research, content development, partnership building and project management for the design and implementation of projects and activities in coordination and collaboration with the COs, RBx and SFH teams. Under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Lead, SDG Finance and Private Sector Development, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will provide technical support to the design and implementation of technical assistance products across the portfolio's multi-country pipeline, including credit guarantee mechanisms, and energy-sector investment facilitation, drawing on engineering experience in the energy sector and private sector engagement experience in post-conflict and crisis-affected settings.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance of and reporting directly to the SDG Financing and Private Sector Development Portfolio Lead, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will be responsible for performing and contributing to the following:

Research, Partnership Intelligence and Knowledge Generation:

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis and technical due diligence on energy infrastructure and energy transition investments to inform new project design and partnership development across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct desk research and analytical work on energy markets, tariff structures, and generation/grid technologies to inform the design and operationalization of new private sector engagement initiatives.

- Develop and quality-assure evidence-based briefs, concept notes, strategy papers, partnership proposals, and programme documents on energy and private sector engagement in support of new project pipelines, including partnership agreements/MOUs and monitoring and evaluation frameworks, ensuring readiness for management approval and external engagement.

- Contribute to the implementation of ICPSD's knowledge management activities in the energy and private sector development area, including maintaining an updated repository of technical data, research, and partner intelligence to support ongoing partnership identification and pipeline development.

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis on energy-sector investment opportunities, private sector engagement modalities, and blended finance mechanisms as they relate to the identification of new partnership and co-financing opportunities across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct other research and information collection tasks related to energy and private sector engagement as required by ICPSD.

Programme, Partnership and Event Management:

- Lead end-to-end coordination of ICPSD programme and partnership-related activities on energy and private sector engagement, including identifying and securing venues, speakers, and guests; drafting and distributing outreach and invitations; managing event registration; and performing other related event management tasks.

- Develop and quality-assure the full suite of event documentation including press kits, logistics notes, briefing materials, and background papers on energy investment and private sector engagement, for stakeholder workshops and partner engagements.

- Design and deliver substantive research inputs for events, trainings, and workshops, including speaker briefings and evidence syntheses on energy investment, private sector development, blended finance, and partnership and resource mobilization opportunities.

- Support the content development and organization of national and international conferences, workshops, retreats, partner and donor engagement events, and other events organized by ICPSD in support of new energy and private sector engagement project and partnership development.

Management Coordination, Partnership Development, facilitate knowledge management and Strategic Support:

- Prepare and quality-review notes, presentations, and strategic summaries on energy and private sector engagement for senior management and external advisory functions, exercising independent judgment on framing, accuracy, and positioning.

- Identify and escalate emerging issues, risks, or opportunities relevant to ICPSD's energy and private sector engagement project and partnership pipeline, providing management with timely, evidence-based situational assessments.

- Lead the development of knowledge management products including methodologies, reports, and thematic briefs on energy and private sector engagement, ensuring outputs meet ICPSD quality standards and are fit for external dissemination.

- Participate in events and organizations related to energy and private sector engagement, actively identifying and cultivating new partnership and project development opportunities.

- Participate in project and partner/donor coordination meetings on energy and private sector engagement, as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will work under the guidance of and reporting directly to the UNDP ICPSD SDG Financing and Private Sector Development Portfolio Lead.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies:

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management

- Results-based Management Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- Partnerships Management Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Working with Evidence and Data Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Partnership management

- Private sector engagement Ability to identify, conduct outreach, and manage relationships with the private sector.

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Sustainable Energy Hub Energy Finance

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Engineering or related field is required , OR;

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned field of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) and 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of extensive working experience in private sector engagement and energy areas

Required skills:

- Experience in private sector engagement through partnerships with DFIs, multilateral development banks, governments or other institutions particularly in post-conflict, crisis, or fragile-state country contexts

Desired skills:

- Experience in sustainable energy investment analysis, including feasibility assessment of sustainable energy projects.

- Previous experience in engagement with energy companies and energy-sector institutions, both public and private.

- Experience conducting analytical research, stakeholder consultations, and preparing high-quality publications, practitioner case studies, policy papers, or other knowledge products for energy particularly in post-conflict, crisis, or fragile-state country contexts.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

At country level, the UNV Field Unit (FU) and/or designated UNV personnel are responsible for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes in the areas of peace, development and humanitarian assistance.  UNV Field Units/designated UNV personnel represent and position UNV in the respective countries with a focus on the UN Country Team, bringing UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners within a client service approach and collaborating with other stakeholders from government, civil society and private sector. As UNDP represents UNV at country level, UNV personnel are usually hosted within a UNDP Office and are accountable to the Supervisor and UNV Executive Coordinator for compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations

Scope of Work

1.Assist in mobilizing volunteers and developing and maintaining partnerships

- Support in the management of key accounts of assigned partnerships.

- Support and maintain relationships with assigned UN partner/s in the country/countries to ensure an understanding of UNV’s mandate, key offers and the added value that UN Volunteer assignments bring in support to the achievement of their respective mandates.

- Support in the identification of volunteer placement opportunities based on UN agency strategies and plans and present UNV value proposition and volunteer modalities with the objective of maximizing the relevance of volunteerism for impact.

- Support in the preparation of descriptions of assignment, with a focus on the assigned partners.

- Support in the development of offers and initiatives that respond to the evolving needs of partners for volunteer solutions.

- Contribute to the organization of advocacy campaigns, key events and other external communication efforts that raise awareness and foster engagement.

- Ensure knowledge is documented, systematized and fed back into volunteer mobilization, using UNV's Client Relationship Management (CRM) to track interactions and updates.

- In consultation with the Online Volunteering (OV) Programme Associate in the respective Regional Office, act as a focal point for online volunteers and accreditation of OV service organizations, focusing on supporting host entities with developing OV opportunities through advocacy engagements and promoting the concept of OV.

2. Contribute to business intelligence in support of strategic and sustained mobilization

- Support partnerships development by collecting and analyzing data of UN Cooperation Frameworks and agency programming frameworks to identify volunteer engagement areas.Record volunteer mobilization opportunities and business intelligence in CRM.

- Support in the engagement with potential partners by preparing presentations, mapping etc. on opportunities for volunteerism for internal use by UNV.

- Support the identification of opportunities for communicating on positive volunteer stories and strengthening visibility of the Agency partnership and the impact of volunteerism.

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

- Assist in gathering feedback from volunteers through surveys or informal check-ins and help compile and share insights to inform improvements in volunteer management practices.

- Support the organization of appreciation initiatives and local events to acknowledge volunteer contributions and foster a sense of belonging.

- Support the Country Coordinator in ensuring volunteers’ satisfaction with their assignment.

- Backstop other functions in the Field Unit/at country level during peak periods or personnel absences, ensuring continuity of service and contributing to a seamless and positive volunteer experience.

4. Support duty of care of UN Volunteers serving in the assigned area

- Liaise with the respective entities’ security focal points or heads of office, as applicable, and provide support to ensure a detailed and precise understanding among UN Volunteers on all security-related issues, including e.g. assistance with headcounts in emergency situations.

- Provide timely and accurate support to UN Volunteers undergoing medical evacuation, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV, while maintaining compliance with established procedures.

- Provide tailored support to UN Volunteers who do not speak the UN official language, to facilitate their understanding and providing key information, and navigate their assignment environment effectively throughout the volunteer management cycle.

- Provide host entities with comprehensive information on the enabling instruments available through UNV that support the health and wellbeing of UN Volunteers, such as insurance and related benefits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the general guidance of the Regional Manager, with day-to-day reporting to the Country Coordinator, the Client Engagement Assistant supports the identification, development, and cultivation of select partnerships with UN Agencies / Host Entities at country level. This includes managing the relationship with priority partners, gathering and sharing data and information that influence mobilization opportunities, ensuring client satisfaction with volunteer services, and bridging the delivery of services from centralized functions of the volunteer management cycle. The critical purpose of this role is the sustained mobilization of volunteers to the designated partners (clients) and support to the duty of care for serving volunteers.

The role involves regular contact and liaison with counterpart UN personnel at all levels, including senior level staff. Within UNV, all personnel are expected to work across multiple units, functions, and teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Core

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Knowledge Generation

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- A university degree in Social Sciences or related area will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with high school diploma) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of practical and relevant experience at national or international level in partnership engagement, advocacy, management, client service or related areas.

- Experience in preparing presentation materials, including PowerPoint slides and talking points, as well as minute-taking and report drafting.

- Experience in the use of computers, oﬃce software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Previous experience with international or development organizations is considered an asset.

- Knowledge and experience of ticket-based service management systems (e.g. Salesforce/UNALL, or equivalent) is considered an asset.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Arabic.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

At country level, the UNV Field Unit (FU) and/or designated UNV personnel are responsible for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes in the areas of peace, development and humanitarian assistance.  UNV Field Units/designated UNV personnel represent and position UNV in the respective countries with a focus on the UN Country Team, bringing UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners within a client service approach and collaborating with other stakeholders from government, civil society and private sector. As UNDP represents UNV at country level, UNV personnel are usually hosted within a UNDP Office and are accountable to the Supervisor and UNV Executive Coordinator for compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations

Scope of Work

1. Assist in mobilizing volunteers and developing and maintaining partnerships

- Support in the management of key accounts of assigned partnerships.

- Support and maintain relationships with assigned UN partner/s in the country/countries to ensure an understanding of UNV’s mandate, key offers and the added value that UN Volunteer assignments bring in support to the achievement of their respective mandates.

- Support in the identification of volunteer placement opportunities based on UN agency strategies and plans and present UNV value proposition and volunteer modalities with the objective of maximizing the relevance of volunteerism for impact.

- Support in the preparation of descriptions of assignment, with a focus on the assigned partners.

- Support in the development of offers and initiatives that respond to the evolving needs of partners for volunteer solutions.

- Contribute to the organization of advocacy campaigns, key events and other external communication efforts that raise awareness and foster engagement.

- Ensure knowledge is documented, systematized and fed back into volunteer mobilization, using UNV's Client Relationship Management (CRM) to track interactions and updates.

- In consultation with the Online Volunteering (OV) Programme Associate in the respective Regional Office, act as a focal point for online volunteers and accreditation of OV service organizations, focusing on supporting host entities with developing OV opportunities through advocacy engagements and promoting the concept of OV.

2. Contribute to business intelligence in support of strategic and sustained mobilization

- Support partnerships development by collecting and analyzing data of UN Cooperation Frameworks and agency programming frameworks to identify volunteer engagement areas. Record volunteer mobilization opportunities and business intelligence in CRM.

- Support in the engagement with potential partners by preparing presentations, mapping etc. on opportunities for volunteerism for internal use by UNV.

- Support the identification of opportunities for communicating on positive volunteer stories and strengthening visibility of the Agency partnership and the impact of volunteerism.

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

- Assist in gathering feedback from volunteers through surveys or informal check-ins and help compile and share insights to inform improvements in volunteer management practices.

- Support the organization of appreciation initiatives and local events to acknowledge volunteer contributions and foster a sense of belonging.

- Support the Country Coordinator in ensuring volunteers’ satisfaction with their assignment.

- Backstop other functions in the Field Unit/at country level during peak periods or personnel absences, ensuring continuity of service and contributing to a seamless and positive volunteer experience.

4. Support duty of care of UN Volunteers serving in the assigned area

- Liaise with the respective entities’ security focal points or heads of office, as applicable, and provide support to ensure a detailed and precise understanding among UN Volunteers on all security-related issues, including e.g. assistance with headcounts in emergency situations.

- Provide timely and accurate support to UN Volunteers undergoing medical evacuation, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV, while maintaining compliance with established procedures.

- Provide tailored support to UN Volunteers who do not speak the UN official language, to facilitate their understanding and providing key information, and navigate their assignment environment effectively throughout the volunteer management cycle.

- Provide host entities with comprehensive information on the enabling instruments available through UNV that support the health and wellbeing of UN Volunteers, such as insurance and related benefits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the general guidance of the Regional Manager, with day-to-day reporting to the Country Coordinator, the Client Engagement Assistant supports the identification, development, and cultivation of select partnerships with UN Agencies / Host Entities at country level. This includes managing the relationship with priority partners, gathering and sharing data and information that influence mobilization opportunities, ensuring client satisfaction with volunteer services, and bridging the delivery of services from centralized functions of the volunteer management cycle. The critical purpose of this role is the sustained mobilization of volunteers to the designated partners (clients) and support to the duty of care for serving volunteers.

The role involves regular contact and liaison with counterpart UN personnel at all levels, including senior level staff. Within UNV, all personnel are expected to work across multiple units, functions, and teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Required Skills and Experience

Tiered Approach

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria was created to significantly increase resources to fight three of the world’s most devastating diseases, and to direct those resources to areas of greatest need. The Global Fund attracts, manages and disburses resources in a public-private partnership that makes a sustainable and significant contribution to the reduction of mortality and morbidity caused by the three diseases and to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

UNDP is a key partner to the Global Fund to Fight HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM) and is the UN agency assuming the role of Principal Recipient of GFATM grants in South Sudan for TB and HIV/AIDS. In its role as Principal Recipient, UNDP ensures quality financial management, timely procurement of supplies, and efficient monitoring and delivery service. UNDP’s management role consists of implementing grants, ensuring financial accountability, and training of national and international counterparts on program management, financial accountability and timely programmatic reporting to the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) and Global Fund (GF) Secretariat.

Position Purpose

The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will report to the Program Manager (Global Fund) and will work within the Program & M&E unit to support the Finance & QA unit, the PSM & Procurement unit and the Warehouse/Supply Chain Management team. The Specialist will liaise with the GF Country Team, the Local Fund Agent (LFA), the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), the Ministry of Health (MOH), the South Sudan AIDS Commission (SSAC), the National TB Program, the technical working groups responsible for HIV and TB, and various other partners and stakeholders. The incumbent will be required to travel to service delivery sites for the purpose of monitoring and supporting project activities.

Scope of Work

Under the overall guidance of the Program Manager (Global Fund), the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will be responsible for the following key tasks:

Lead the GC8 monitoring and evaluation framework and plans:

- Lead the development and updating of M&E frameworks and plans for the HIV, TB and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) portfolio in coordination with MOH, SSAC and the National TB Program;

- Conduct regular analysis of grant performance against GC8 targets, identify implementation gaps and emerging risks, and recommend concrete corrective actions in coordination with program teams and sub-recipients;

- Develop M&E tools, indicator reference sheets and training materials for the PMU, SRs and implementing partners;

- Support SRs to strengthen their M&E systems for timely and accurate reporting;

- Supervise and monitor the work of any M&E consultants assigned to support the team;

- Conduct M&E capacity assessments of SRs and national partners and implement a capacity development plan;

- Review progress reports against targets and propose remedial actions for under-performing indicators;

- Monitor implementation bottlenecks and provide analytical inputs to program decision-making.

Deliver grant performance reporting to the Global Fund:

- Coordinate the preparation of Program Update, Discontinuation and Progress Reports (PUDRs), bi-annual and annual updates to the Global Fund;

- Consolidate quarterly programmatic information and ensure timely submission through corporate systems and the Global Fund transparency portal;

- Organize and document program review meetings, including preparation of background data and follow-up action points.

Assure data quality across the HIV and TB portfolios:

- Review data from HMIS/DHIS2 and program sources for completeness, accuracy and consistency;

- Plan and conduct routine data quality assessments (RDQA/DQA) and support sub-recipient site quality assurance (RSQA);

- Supervise, mentor and support the M&E Analyst (TB/HIV);

- Strengthen the use of routine program data, including DHIS2 and community-level reporting, to identify service delivery gaps, monitor coverage among key and vulnerable populations, and inform program adjustments.

Manage surveys, evaluations and learning:

- Coordinate baseline, mid-term and end-line surveys and evaluations, including drafting Terms of Reference and providing technical direction;

- Facilitate dissemination of evaluation findings and the preparation of management responses;

- Document lessons learned and promote their use in program design and grant revisions.

Build M&E capacity and support nationalization and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Deliver M&E and health information systems (HIS) training to MOH, SSAC, National TB Program staff and SRs, including NEPWU-NASOSS;

- Support the Country Dialogue Transition Plan (CDTP) and capacity transfer for progressive nationalization of the PR role;

- Develop and monitor measurable milestones for transferring M&E responsibilities to national institutions, including strengthened national ownership of data quality assurance, analysis and Global Fund reporting;

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the PMU, Country Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

The key impact of the post will be high-quality, timely monitoring, evaluation and reporting of the GC8 portfolio, sustaining the grant’s high-rating performance and enabling UNDP, the LFA and the Global Fund to verify results. The post also builds national M&E capacity, supporting data quality for HIV and TB services and the sustainability of interventions under the Country Dialogue Transition Plan. The position will be supervising M&E Analyst.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact;

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences;

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands;

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results;

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration;

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

People Management Competencies

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional/Technical Competencies

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management

- Monitoring and Evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programs, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and program management and results; Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programs and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming; Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools; Ability to make independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Working with Evidence and Data Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Statistics, Social Sciences, Monitoring & Evaluation or a related field is required. Or;

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience

- Minimum 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation of health programs, preferably including HIV and TB is required.

- Proven experience in developing and implementing M&E frameworks, performance frameworks and data quality assurance (RDQA/DQA) processes;

- Experience in designing and managing surveys, including the use of HMIS/DHIS2 and statistical analysis tools (Excel, SPSS, Stata, or R).

- Proven experience in excellent report writing and presentation

Desired skills

- Experience with Global Fund grant reporting (PUDRs and performance frameworks);

- Experience in South Sudan or a similar post-conflict setting;

- Familiarity with UNDP and/or UN systems;

- Experience in facilitating trainings.

Languages

- Fluency in English is required.

- Working knowledge of Arabic is an asset

jobs.title: Business and Human Rights Analyst
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, working in around 170 countries and territories. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, UNDP is committed to helping the country through strengthened national and local capacities to carry out political, economic and social reforms and promote development. In line with its 2026-2030 Country Programme, UNDP in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) focuses on inclusive green growth, human capital development and accountable institutions and social cohesion. UNDP is fully committed to supporting BiH in achieving its Agenda 2030 commitments and advancing its European Union (EU) integration priorities. Across all areas of work, UNDP applies conflict-sensitive, integrated, and innovative approaches tailored to the country's development needs.

Accelerating Rights-Based Trade and Investment in BiH (ARTI BiH) aims to strengthen responsible business conduct in Bosnia and Herzegovina by supporting policy dialogue, institutional capacity development and practical application of human rights and environmental due diligence standards. The project responds to the growing importance of responsible business conduct for Bosnia and Herzegovina’s EU accession process, competitiveness and participation in EU-linked value chains, particularly in light of evolving EU and international sustainability requirements. The project seeks to address existing gaps in the readiness of public institutions, the private sector, financial institutions and the broader business support ecosystem to implement responsible business conduct in practice. Particular attention is placed on strengthening capacities of SMEs and relevant support institutions to understand and apply the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD), environmental due diligence and related EU sustainability requirements.

The project is structured around three mutually reinforcing areas. First, it will support national policy dialogue and development of a roadmap for a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights. Second, it will establish a Business and Human Rights Innovation Lab and strengthen cooperation with academia and Business Development Support Organizations to develop practical knowledge products, technical guidance and the functional concept for a digital HRDD/RBC self-assessment tool. Third, the project will work with the financial sector to strengthen understanding and integration of Business and Human Rights considerations into risk assessment and advisory practices. The project applies a human rights-based and gender-responsive approach, recognizing that business operations, supply-chain changes and sustainability requirements can affect women and other groups differently. Gender considerations will therefore be mainstreamed across relevant technical assistance, capacity-building, stakeholder engagement and knowledge-development activities.

To support the implementation of the project, the Business and Human Rights Analyst will provide day-to-day coordination and substantive support to the implementation of project activities, including work planning, stakeholder engagement, monitoring, reporting and knowledge management, in close cooperation with government institutions, private sector actors, academia, financial institutions, business support organizations and other relevant partners.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Sustainable Growth Sector Leader, the Business and Human Rights Analyst will be responsible for the following functions:

a) Contribute to coordination and implementation of project activities

- Contribute to the day-to-day coordination and implementation of project activities in accordance with the approved work plan and agreed timelines;

- Contribute to the preparation and regular updating of project work plans, activity schedules and implementation arrangements;

- Coordinate with relevant government institutions, private sector actors, academia, Business Development Support Organizations, financial institutions, civil society and development partners to facilitate timely implementation of project activities;

- Support the organization and coordination of meetings, consultations, policy dialogues, workshops, trainings and other project events;

- Monitor progress of project activities and follow up on agreed actions, timelines and deliverables;

- Contribute to the preparation of project progress updates, reports, briefing notes, presentations and other implementation-related documentation.

b) Substantive and technical support on Business and Human Rights and responsible business conduct

- Provide substantive and technical support to activities promoting responsible business conduct, the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and Human Rights Due Diligence;

- Contribute to the organization and implementation of multi-stakeholder policy dialogue related to Business and Human Rights and development of the roadmap for a National Action Plan;

- Prepare and review analytical inputs, guidance materials, knowledge products and other technical documentation related to Business and Human Rights, HRDD and relevant EU and international sustainability requirements;

- Contribute to the cooperation with academia and Business Development Support Organizations in the development and dissemination of practical tools, guidance and capacity-building materials;

- Contribute to the development of the functional and operational concept for the planned digital HRDD/RBC self-assessment tool, including coordination of relevant stakeholder inputs.

c) Engagement with the private and financial sectors

- Facilitate engagement with companies, SMEs, business associations, Chambers of Commerce and other private-sector actors on responsible business conduct and Human Rights Due Diligence;

- Coordinate and support capacity-building and awareness-raising activities targeting private-sector actors;

- Facilitate engagement with the Association of Banks of BiH, the Central Bank of BiH and commercial banks in activities related to the integration of Business and Human Rights considerations into financial-sector risk assessment and advisory practices;

- Facilitate dialogue and knowledge exchange between the private sector, financial institutions, public institutions, academia and other relevant stakeholders;

- Ensure the documentation of experiences, lessons learned and emerging good practices from engagement with businesses and financial-sector actors.

d) Gender equality, monitoring and knowledge management

- Ensure that gender equality and human rights considerations are appropriately reflected in the planning and implementation of relevant project activities;

- Support gender-responsive stakeholder engagement and contribute to ensuring that project activities address relevant barriers and risks affecting women, including women-led enterprises and women-dominated workforces;

- Support collection, consolidation and analysis of project monitoring data and information in line with the project Results Framework;

- Contribute to documenting results, lessons learned, and evidence generated through project implementation;

- Support knowledge management, communication and dissemination of project results and knowledge products;

- Contribute to identifying opportunities for further programme development, partnerships and scale-up based on evidence and lessons generated through the project.

The incumbent may be required to perform other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the successful implementation of the project and the overall functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-functional & Technical competencies[IM1]

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Business Direction & Strategy

Negotiation and Influence

Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Management

Project Management

Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management

Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Partnership management

Relationship management

Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Business Direction & Strategy

System Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system.

2030 Agenda: People

Gender

Knowledge and understanding of gender equality and women’s empowerment principles and ability to integrate gender considerations into programme and project activities.

2030 Agenda: Peace – Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights

Business and Human Rights

Knowledge of responsible business conduct, the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and Human Rights Due Diligence, including their application in engagement with businesses, public institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced University degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in economics, human rights, business administration, public administration, law, international relations, political sciences, development studies, social sciences or a related field is required, or

- A first-level University degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields in combination with additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional work experience in project coordination, private sector development, business support, human rights, responsible business conduct or related fields.

Knowledge, Experience and Skills

- Previous experience in project coordination and implementation in development programmes or initiatives involving multiple stakeholders.

- Strong experience in coordinating and working effectively with public institutions, private sector actors, financial institutions, academia, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders.

- Previous experience in providing technical support to private sector actors, SMEs, business associations or Business Development Support Organizations.

- Familiarity with responsible business conduct, Business and Human Rights and/or Human Rights Due Diligence concepts.

- Experience and proficiency in the usage of computers and office software packages, including MS Word, MS Excel and PowerPoint.

Desirable criteria

- Previous experience working on Business and Human Rights, responsible business conduct, Human Rights Due Diligence, ESG, sustainability or related areas is desired.

- Strong analytical and drafting skills, including preparation of reports, briefing notes, presentations and other project documentation would be an asset.

- Knowledge of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and relevant EU sustainability and due diligence frameworks would be an asset.

- Experience in engagement with financial institutions, banks or financial-sector stakeholders would be an asset.

- Experience in mainstreaming gender equality and human rights considerations into project activities would be an asset.

- Experience working with international organizations or development partners would be an asset.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in one of the official languages of people in BiH (Bosnian, Croatian or Serbian) is required.

- Fluency in English is required.

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Objetivo do Cargo e Contexto Organizacional

O Projeto Justiça 4.0 constitui uma das principais iniciativas de transformação digital do Poder Judiciário brasileiro e uma referência internacional em inovação e modernização dos serviços de Justiça. Iniciado em 2020, a partir de acordo de cooperação firmado entre o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD/ONU), o Projeto tem como objetivo desenvolver, aprimorar e disseminar soluções tecnológicas que contribuam para tornar os serviços oferecidos pela Justiça brasileira mais eficientes, eficazes, acessíveis e centrados nas necessidades da população. A iniciativa também busca otimizar a gestão e a prestação jurisdicional, beneficiando magistrados(as), servidores(as), advogados(as) e demais atores do sistema de Justiça. O Projeto está alinhado aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) e aos compromissos da Agenda 2030 das Nações Unidas.

Nesse contexto, as pessoas selecionadas atuarão como Assistentes de Projetos, prestando suporte técnico e operacional à implementação de projetos do PJ4.0. Serão selecionadas duas pessoas com atuação remota (home based).

Deveres e responsabilidades

O(a) Assistente de Projetos será responsável por prestar apoio administrativo, operacional e logístico à implementação e monitoramento das ações do Programa Justiça 4.0. O(a) profissional desempenhará atividades essenciais para garantir a conformidade processual, a eficiência dos fluxos administrativos e a correta aplicação das normas operacionais das iniciativas. Para o alcance desse objetivo, o(a) profissional desempenhará as seguintes responsabilidades principais e atividades:

1. Apoio à gestão de pessoas, onboarding e elaboração de (TR):

- Auxiliar na elaboração, revisão formal e tramitação de Termos de Referência (TR) para a seleção de pessoas físicas e jurídicas vinculadas às necessidades do programa;

- Apoiar operacionalmente as etapas de onboarding, integração e desligamento de profissionais vinculados(as) ao Programa Justiça 4.0;

- Apoiar a instrução documental de processos de recrutamento e seleção, bem como o controle de prazos de vigência, cronogramas de renovação e reajustes dos contratos da equipe.

2. Gestão, organização e tramitação eletrônica de processos e documentos:

- Acompanhar, organizar e instruir processos administrativos e comunicações oficiais por meio do Sistema Eletrônico de Informações (SEI) e demais canais institucionais utilizados pelas partes parceiras;

- Realizar lançamentos, registros e transações operacionais nos sistemas corporativos do PNUD, incluindo o Quantum, em conformidade com as orientações das áreas responsáveis;

- Organizar e manter atualizados arquivos digitais e pastas dos projetos, garantindo a padronização, a rastreabilidade, a segurança da informação e o fácil acesso à documentação.

3. Acompanhamento operacional e inserção de dados em plataformas de cooperação internacional:

- Apoiar o monitoramento de projetos de cooperação técnica internacional mediante o preenchimento, atualização e acompanhamento de dados das iniciativas no Sistema de Gestão de Convênios e Parcerias (SIGAP) da Agência Brasileira de Cooperação do Ministério das Relações Exteriores (ABC/MRE);

- Monitorar e apoiar o controle de prazos, cronogramas, metas e entregas dos projetos, identificando desvios e apoiando a articulação interna para a regularização de pendências;

- Auxiliar na compilação de informações para subsidiar o acompanhamento e as atualizações periódicas dos planos de trabalho e cronogramas gerais do programa.

4. Apoio à execução financeira, orçamentária e prestação de contas do PRODOC:

- Prestar suporte na coleta, organização e consolidação de dados orçamentários e financeiros para apoiar a elaboração de relatórios de progresso e prestações de contas periódicas do Documento de Projeto PRODOC;

- Apoiar o acompanhamento e consolidação de informações sobre a execução orçamentária, auxiliando na instrução de revisões orçamentárias e financeiras em conformidade com as normas do PNUD;

- Identificar inconsistências ou pendências financeiras e processuais, auxiliando na compilação de informações para auditorias e avaliações do projeto.

5. Apoio técnico a reuniões, instâncias de governança e documentação:

- Realizar o agendamento, envio de convites e apoio logístico geral para reuniões, oficinas, encontros tripartites e comissões técnicas das iniciativas;

- Elaborar documentos de suporte para reuniões, tais como pautas, memórias de reunião, atas oficiais, listas de presença, resumos executivos e relatórios de encaminhamentos;

- Acompanhar a execução das deliberações e recomendações acordadas nas reuniões e auditorias, monitorando os prazos de cumprimento junto aos(às) responsáveis.

6. Suporte logístico de viagens, diárias e providências operacionais:

- Apoiar a organização logística de viagens nacionais e internacionais dos projetos, incluindo cotações de passagens, reserva de hospedagens e cadastro de viajantes nos sistemas corporativos;

- Instruir, acompanhar e organizar os processos de concessão de diárias e passagens para consultores(as), parceiros(as) e equipes técnicas;

- Apoiar os fluxos de prestação de contas de diárias e passagens recebidas, realizando a conferência preliminar de relatórios de viagem, bilhetes de embarque e documentos fiscais comprobatórios.

7. Apoiar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimento relevantes para o projeto:

- Participar de treinamentos sobre procedimentos internos voltados à equipe do projeto e oferecer suporte à organização de capacitações e outras atividades de desenvolvimento de competências, conforme necessário.

- Contribuir de forma consistente para redes de conhecimento e comunidades de prática.

- Manter registros organizados de dados do projeto, atividades de campo, estudos de caso, relatos de experiências humanas, fotografias e outros documentos pertinentes que possam subsidiar o compartilhamento de conhecimento e ações de defesa de causas (advocacy).

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

O(a) contratado(a) será supervisionado(a) pelo/a Especialista de Projetos em Justiça para o Desenvolvimento de projetos do PNUD.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora seu próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes e entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curioso, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros e pede feedback.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível.

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios | Pensamento Estratégico

- Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Desenvolvimento de negócios | Comunicação

- Comunicar de forma clara, concisa e inequívoca, tanto por meio da comunicação escrita quanto verbal; adaptar mensagens e escolher métodos de comunicação dependendo do público. Capacidade de gerenciar comunicações internas e externas, por meio da mídia, redes sociais e outros canais apropriados.

Gestão de negócios | Gestão de projetos

- Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para atingir objetivos específicos.

Dados | Análise de dados

- Capacidade de extrair, analisar e visualizar dados para gerar insights significativos e apoiar a tomada de decisões empresariais eficazes.
