Background

UNRWA | United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees

The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) provides essential services and humanitarian assistance to Palestine refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Its services include education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure rehabilitation, microfinance and emergency assistance.

The Department of Legal Affairs advises on and promotes the consistent interpretation and application of international law throughout the Agency. It develops strategies to promote and implement relevant areas of public international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, refugee law and United Nations law. Particular emphasis is placed on the status and mandate of the Agency, the privileges and immunities of the Agency and its personnel, related responsibilities, and the observance of humanitarian principles.

The Department also provides legal advice and training on the interpretation and application of the Agency’s regulatory framework, including General Assembly resolutions, Staff and Financial Regulations and Rules, associated administrative issuances, and organizational directives. It advises Headquarters and Field departments on governance and management matters, particularly those involving administrative, contractual and procurement law. In addition, the Department provides technical expertise and advice on amendments to the Agency’s regulatory framework, including the drafting of regulations and rules, as well as the preparation and review of legal opinions on complex or sensitive financial matters, particularly those concerning the interpretation of the Agency’s Financial Regulations and Technical Instructions.

Furthermore, the Department reviews drafts of all types of Agency contractual instruments and arrangements, including complex contracts for the procurement of goods and services, memoranda of understanding with partners, and funding agreements. It also provides related training to strengthen the consistent interpretation, application and implementation of the Agency’s contractual and legal requirements.

Training component: Learning elements and expectations

Upon completion of the assignment the JPO will have/ will be able to:

- Legal research, analysis and application of international and general law.

- Legal drafting, advisory work and case management.

- Understanding of UNRWA’s mandate, operations and institutional framework.

- Interpersonal, communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

- Professional judgement, discretion, confidentiality and ethical conduct

The JPO training programme includes the following learning elements:

- Year 1 – Induction and practical learning: Structured induction, guided legal reading, mandatory UN training, daily on-the-job learning, progressive case management and potential Field Operations visits, followed by a review of learning needs and a development plan for Year 2.

- Year 2 – Advanced legal practice and collaboration: Increased responsibility for complex legal matters, including litigation, legal opinions, contracts and procurement, alongside participation in legal training and coordination across UNRWA and the wider UN system, strengthening legal expertise, professional judgement and stakeholder engagement.

- Year 3 – Consolidation and career development: Consolidation of legal expertise through progressively independent work, continued mentoring and feedback, and career development discussions to identify further learning needs and future opportunities within the UN system.

- Duty Travel and Training Allowance (DTTA) : An annual allowance of USD 4,000 supports relevant learning activities, duty travel and professional development related to the assignment.

Content and methodology of supervision:

- Director, Department of Legal Affairs. Purpose: direct supervision, guidance, advice, task assignment, performance monitoring and evaluation. Frequency: daily, through regular meetings, review of deliverables, and feedback on progress and quality of work.

- Heads of the General Law Unit and the International Law Unit. Purpose: substantive guidance, coordination and advice on assigned legal cases and activities across both Units. Frequency: as required, through regular interaction and review of ongoing work.

- Legal advisers and counterparts across the UN system: Purpose: professional exchange, coordination and exposure to legal practice across the UN system. Frequency: as required, through the legal advisers’ coordination mechanism.

- The Associate Legal Officer’s individual workplan will be based on the Department’s annual workplan and will define substantive activities and expected outputs. Progress will be monitored through regular discussions, review of assigned cases and deliverables, and ongoing feedback. The Associate Legal Officer will also participate in official meetings with the Director, as applicable and contribute to follow-up actions, ensuring practical exposure to the Agency’s legal mandate and the work of the Department.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Associate Legal Officer will report to the Director of Legal Affairs and work under their direct daily supervision, with full immersion in the Department’s daily work and activities. The role will have a cross-cutting focus, working closely with both the General Law Unit (covering international administrative law, commercial and institutional matters, and litigation), and the International Law Unit (covering privileges and immunities, protection, neutrality, international human rights mechanisms, and international humanitarian law). The JPO will handle a diverse portfolio of cases across both Units, participate in official meetings and related follow-up actions, gain a thorough understanding of the Agency’s legal mandate in a highly politicised context, and engage with legal advisers across the UN system.

Responsibilities (summary of duties/tasks):

1. Supports the Department’s Legal Advisory Work (30%)

• Participates in the daily work and activities of the General Law and International Law Units, gaining exposure to the full range of legal matters handled by the Department.

• Supports the Director of Legal Affairs in providing legal advice to UNRWA leadership and Directors of Divisions and Departments, including on sensitive and complex legal issues.

• Develops a comprehensive understanding of the Department’s legal functions, priorities and advisory responsibilities.

2. Manages an Assigned Portfolio of Legal Matters and Projects (30%)

• Handles an assigned portfolio of legal cases and issues across the General Law and International Law Units, under the direct supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

• Contributes to litigation and matters arising under the Agency’s internal justice system, the preparation and review of diplomatic correspondence, including notes verbal, and the provision of legal opinions on international law issues.

• Reviews commercial contracts and supports legal aspects of procurement and other operational activities.

• Undertakes designated legal projects to strengthen the Agency’s legal practices and frameworks, including the development of standard agreement templates for engagement with partners.

• Liaises with relevant Agency stakeholders, including Human Resources, Partnerships and the Executive Office, under the guidance and supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

3. Participates in Official Meetings and Follow-up Actions (25%)

• Participates in meetings led by the Director of Legal Affairs and other senior legal officers on substantive, operational and strategic legal matters.

• Contributes to meeting preparation and follow-up, including conducting legal research, drafting documentation and supporting the implementation of agreed actions.

• Develops an understanding of UNRWA’s management structures, decision-making processes and engagement with governments, beneficiaries, partners and other stakeholders.

5. Engages in Legal Coordination Across the United Nations System (15%)

• Participates, through the Director of Legal Affairs, in coordination and information-sharing with legal advisers and counterparts across the United Nations system.

• Gains exposure to the work of the United Nations Office of Legal Affairs and other UN legal offices, including inter-agency coordination mechanisms on legal matters.

• Develops an understanding of common legal issues, institutional practices and approaches to legal advice and coordination across the UN systems.

Competencies

Key competencies

- Excellent oral and written communication skills, including strong legal drafting and analytical skills.

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment, maintaining confidentiality and discretion at all times.

- Legal Research and Analysis

- Negotiation and Problem-Solving

- Stakeholder Engagement

- Teamwork and Collaboration

- Planning and Organizing

- Analytical Skills

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Master degree or equivalent in law or a Bachelor’s degree in law plus a minimum of 2 years of paid and relevant working experience. Admission to practice at a national Bar.

- In exceptional cases candidates with a Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of 4 years relevant working experience can be considered.

- Substantive parts of the candidates’ academic training (Bachelor and/or Master) must have taken place in a developing country that appears on the list of eligible countries. eligible-countries-DC-JPOs.pdf

Working experience:

- Minimum of 2 years relevant working experience after obtaining first university degree in the legal field, with an exposure to development and humanitarian activities of international organisations being an asset.

- Minimum of 4 years relevant working experience for candidates with a Bachelor’s degree.

- Specialisation in public international law and/or the law of international organisations is an asset.

- Experience in international administrative law and/or litigation is an asset.

- Work experience within the UN system should not exceed 1 year, including UNV, (paid) UN internship and UN consultancy.

- All paid work experience since obtaining Bachelor’s degree will/can be considered.

Languages:

- Fluency in English is required;

- Knowledge of Arabic or another UN official language is an asset.

Age:

Maximum age limit is 32 years as of 31 December of the year of application.

Nationality:

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in Tajikistan has been active since 1994 and is guided in its work by the Country Programme Document, which in turn builds upon the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP has made a significant contribution to developing the National Development Strategy, with an outline of policies and investments necessary to reach the SDGs by 2030. Together with the Government of Tajikistan, civil society and the people of Tajikistan, UNDP works towards identifying local solutions to global and national development challenges. Its main focus is reaching sustainable development by enhancing accountability of the current governance system, mitigating natural disaster threats, and contributing to environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.

The Climate Change, Energy and Environment (CCEE) Cluster of UNDP Tajikistan manages a diverse and growing portfolio of various projects currently under implementation across the country. The Cluster provides strategic, technical, and operational support to national counterparts in addressing Tajikistan’s key environmental, climate, and energy challenges, in line with national development priorities and international commitments. The Cluster’s programmatic focus spans several interrelated thematic areas, including climate change adaptation and mitigation, integrated water resources management, sustainable land management, urban resilience to disaster and climate risks, promotion of renewable and green energy solutions, and biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

In particular, with regard to biodiversity conservation and it’s biodiversity portfolio, UNDP's Country Office in Tajikistan is currently supporting the country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) update and implementation in alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). As countries move from updating their NBSAPs towards implementation, targeted support is required to translate national biodiversity priorities into concrete actions and address critical implementation gaps.

In this context, the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account Multi-Partner Trust Fund (NBSAP AAA MPTF) provides targeted support to countries to accelerate implementation of their NBSAP priorities and translate national biodiversity commitments into concrete action. The Fund supports high-priority interventions that address critical policy, institutional, technical and financing gaps and that have not been sufficiently covered through other available resources. Its support is intended to strengthen national readiness for sustained biodiversity action, increase implementation ambition and create foundations for further investment in achievement of national biodiversity priorities and the KMGBF.

In Tajikistan, the project directly contributes to the objectives of the NBSAP AAA MPTF by providing targeted support for NBSAP implementation, with a particular focus on operationalizing KMGBF Target 6 on invasive alien species (IAS). The project will strengthen the scientific, technical and policy basis for the prevention, monitoring and management of IAS, including through establishment of a national IAS database and development of the country’s first State Programme and Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species. These interventions will help address critical data and policy gaps, strengthen national capacities for ongoing biological risk monitoring and management, and establish a more coherent framework for coordinated action on invasive alien species.

The project further contributes to strengthening the core functions of NBSAP implementation through institutional capacity development and strategic policy support, applying a “whole-of-government” and “whole-of-society” approach. It also contributes to KMGBF Target 23 on gender equality by integrating gender-responsive approaches and promoting the equitable participation of women and vulnerable groups within IAS knowledge, monitoring and policy systems. The initiative will additionally promote youth engagement and digital innovation in biodiversity information management, thereby supporting an inclusive, sustainable and potentially scalable approach to implementation of KMGBF priorities in Tajikistan.

Under the direct supervision of UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project interventions, liaise with national partners and support effective teamwork and strong partnerships. The Project Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality project results that strengthen national capacities, data systems and policy frameworks for the prevention and management of invasive alien species, in line with Tajikistan’s NBSAP and the KMGBF.

He/she will ensure implementation mechanisms and technical working groups are established and meet regularly, that all planned workshops, technical studies and other activities are organised in a timely manner, and that they meet expected quality standards. He/she will also specifically be responsible for outreach activities to relevant stakeholders, and the preparation of synthesis reports, policy briefs, press releases and briefing notes for Government, donor, UNDP, etc.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure effective technical support to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- General coordination and liaison of project activities with national counterparts, scientific institutions and relevant stakeholders.

- Coordinate the development and validation of the National IAS Catalogue and Database.

- Facilitate the development, testing and validation of standardized IAS risk assessment protocols.

- Coordinate the development of the multi-sectoral National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Ensure alignment of the project’s technical outputs with the NBSAP, the KMGBF, national biodiversity reporting processes and other relevant national policies and strategic frameworks.

- Facilitate technical assessments, field data collection, consultations and other analytical work required for the development of the National IAS Catalogue, risk assessment protocols, IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide substantive support to project stakeholders in reviewing and validating technical methodologies, assessments, databases, policy documents and other project outputs.

- Coordinate project activities among relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry Agency, Customs Service, Food Security Committee, other relevant ministries and agencies, civil society organizations, academia and local communities, as specified in the Project Document.

- Facilitate the establishment and effective functioning of the Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group for technical coordination, policy dialogue and development and validation of project outputs.

- Ensure the elaboration of the Stakeholder Engagement and Gender Action Plan before the kickstart of project implementation, and further ensure their effective implementation and regular monitoring.

- Ensure that gender-responsive approaches and meaningful participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups are appropriately integrated into IAS assessments, data systems, consultations and policy development in line with the project’s Results Framework.

- Coordinate and follow up on implementation of relevant environmental and social safeguard measures.

- Review all technical reports as required. Fulfil substantive activities under the Project Work Plan which are not covered by consultants or other contracted experts.

- Support the timely technical review, validation, finalization and submission to relevant national authorities of key project outputs, including the National IAS Catalogue, standardized risk assessment protocols, national IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide necessary inputs to showcase project’s experience at national, regional and international forums/events as required.

- Upon request of the Programme Specialist, participate in and make presentations at conferences, working meetings, workshops, round-table discussions and other relevant events on the IAS project and its linkages with biodiversity conservation, NBSAP and KMGBF implementation.

2. Ensure effective operational and programmatic support for the project:

- Ensure operational and programmatic coordination of the project in accordance with the Project Document, approved work plans, Results Framework and applicable UNDP rules and procedures.

- Support the overall management and coordination of project implementation, ensuring timely and proper execution of activities by consultants, experts, contractors and project partners.

- Prepare Terms of Reference (ToR) for national and international consultants, experts, contractors and other service providers in line with the Project Document and relevant UNDP procedures; coordinate and guide their work and ensure compliance with agreed work plans and respective ToRs and the quality and timely delivery of outputs.

- Facilitate organization of the project Inception Workshop and support the establishment and functioning of the Project Steering Committee, Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group.

- Support communication and coordination with government institutions, scientific organizations, civil society organizations, local communities and other stakeholders involved in implementation of activities specified in the Project Work Plan.

- Prepare meeting agendas and background materials, take notes/minutes of project meetings and ensure timely follow-up on decisions and agreed actions.

- Support preparation and implementation of annual and detailed project work plans, including monitoring of implementation progress and follow-up on planned activities and deliverables.

- Monitor project progress against the Results Framework, including achievement of indicators and targets, and coordinate collection, verification and consolidation of supporting evidence.

- Collect and analyze project-related data and information from government counterparts, consultants, scientific institutions, implementing partners and other relevant sources for project monitoring and reporting purposes.

- Assume responsibility for the timely preparation of project progress reports and other required inputs in line with the reporting requirements of NBSAP AAA MPTF and corporate standards of UNDP.

- Support preparation of the project’s final report and project operational closure upon completion of project activities.

- Monitor project risks and issues in accordance with the Project Document and risk framework and ensure that emerging risks are promptly brought to the attention of the Programme Specialist and relevant project governance bodies.

- Support regular updating of project risk log and follow up on agreed risk mitigation measures.

- Monitor project expenditures, commitments and balances against approved project budget lines and work plans and bring potential deviations requiring management attention to the Programme Specialist.

- Coordinate project activities with other relevant biodiversity, climate and environmental initiatives and programmes in Tajikistan to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication and promote synergies, including with NBSAP update and national reporting.

- Provide assistance and substantive inputs to the Programme Specialist in preparation of project briefs, presentations, reports, talking points and other relevant materials.

- Ensure effective dissemination of and access to information on project activities and results, and support project outreach and communication activities in coordination with UNDP communications staff.

- Liaise with the NBSAP AAA MPTF focal point and relevant UNDP regional focal point(s) to ensure effective project implementation, seek and follow up on technical and operational guidance, address project-related issues and queries, and ensure alignment with applicable programme requirements and guidance.

- Support resource mobilization efforts by providing inputs to the new project ideas, concept notes, funding proposals, and other relevant resource mobilization materials.

3. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area.

- Organize trainings, technical workshops, consultations, awareness-raising events and capacity-building activities in a participatory manner, involving relevant government institutions, scientific / academic institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, women and youth groups, and other stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine, through its Energy and Environment Portfolio, supports national and local authorities in restoring and transforming Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in line with the principles of sustainability, resilience, and transparency. Since the onset of the full-scale war, UNDP has prioritized assistance to ensure continuity of essential services and accelerate the green recovery of Ukraine’s public infrastructure.

Within this framework, UNDP is implementing the Technical Assistance to the Renewable Energy Solutions (RES) Programme, financed through the IKI Renewable Energy Investment Grant under the European Investment Bank (EIB) facility. The Action is delivered under the Direct Implementation Modality (DIM) and coordinated with the Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine, the EIB, and GIZ.

The project aims to support the large-scale deployment of renewable energy technologies—including solar photovoltaic systems, biomass installations, and heat pumps—in public buildings such as schools, kindergartens, hospitals, and municipal facilities. This initiative is designed to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, enhance local energy resilience, and accelerate Ukraine’s alignment with EU Green Deal objectives.

The Action specifically contributes to:

- Strengthening local institutional capacity for project design, procurement, and implementation of renewable energy sub-projects;

- Ensuring technical quality, financial accountability, and environmental compliance during sub-project delivery;

- Supporting municipalities to obtain prosumer (active electricity consumer) status through the development of the net-billing mechanism;

- Enhancing transparency and governance through anticorruption and sanctions-screening systems;

- Promoting knowledge exchange, digital monitoring, and replication of successful models across Ukrainian communities.

UNDP’s Technical Assistance (TA) component serves as the enabling pillar of the RES Programme. It bridges investment, governance, and capacity development by providing:

1. Institutional support and capacity building for Final Beneficiaries (municipalities, utilities, and communal institutions);

2. Technical review of documentation provided for sub-project implementation and support for incorporating applicable environmental and social requirements into procurement and contract management;

3. Contract management for goods, works, and services financed under the EIB-BMWK framework;

4. Oversight, monitoring, and integrity assurance through red-flag tracking, sanctions screening, and compliance reviews;

5. Technical assistance for operationalizing the net-billing system and helping municipalities become self-sufficient clean-energy producers; and

6. Structured knowledge and digital platforms to enable real-time data tracking, reporting, and learning.

The project forms an integral part of UNDP’s Green Energy Recovery and Decarbonization Agenda and complements related EIB-financed frameworks.

Within this context, UNDP Ukraine is recruiting a highly qualified and experienced national professional for the position of Engineering Analyst (Renewables). The position will support the implementation of the RES Programme with a specific focus on the technical review of design documentation, support to procurement processes, and monitoring of the installation and commissioning of renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions in public facilities. The Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will help ensure the quality, safety, and compliance of implemented works, contributing to energy security, continuity of public services, and infrastructure resilience under wartime and post-war recovery conditions.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of Project Manager and in close collaboration with Project team,Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will perform the following:

1.Ensure technical review and engineering support for renewable energy and energy efficiency projects.

- Review and evaluate technical project documentation, baseline information, design calculations, drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs) and equipment specifications for solar PV, other renewable energy and energy efficiency projects under the RES Programme, assessing their completeness, consistency and suitability for implementation.

- Review project designs for compliance with national legislation, applicable regulations, technical standards and donor requirements, and recommend corrective actions to address identified discrepancies.

- Verify sub-project budgets, cost estimates and BoQs using specialised software, such as AVK, and applicable construction cost estimation methodologies.

- Support the preparation and review of technical and contract-related documentation, including scopes of work and technical specifications, ensuring that design requirements are accurately and consistently reflected in the relevant project documentation.

- Participate in technical evaluation panels, assess bidders’ qualifications and technical proposals, including the compliance of proposed equipment and materials and the completeness and consistency of BoQs, and provide recommendations in coordination with the procurement team.

- Prepare technical clarifications in response to bidders’ questions and support the resolution of technical issues related to project documentation, design solutions, equipment, materials and implementation requirements.

- Cooperate closely with GIZ and project stakeholders to identify appropriate technical solutions and provide technical advice during project planning, design review and implementation.

- Identify and assess technical requirements, constraints and implementation risks, and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.

- Review contractors’ proposed schedules for equipment supply, installation, testing and commissioning, and provide recommendations on their feasibility and alignment with project timelines.

- Support technical monitoring of contract implementation through site visits, review of progress reports and verification of equipment and works against contractual requirements, quality and safety standards, and agreed schedules.

- Review proposed changes to designs, equipment, materials or works, assess their implications for scope, cost and timelines, and provide technical recommendations for UNDP’s consideration and approval.

- Support the technical verification of completed works and supporting documentation for acceptance and payment, including records of testing and commissioning.

2.Support in contract management, construction supervision, and commissioning of the project sites.

- Monitor and supervise the implementation of construction and installation works carried out by contractors.\Manage technical aspects of contracts with construction companies and equipment suppliers.

- Ensure that installed equipment, materials, and works comply with approved project designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and quality standards.

- Coordinate and maintain effective communication with contractors, author and technical supervisions, final beneficiaries, and other relevant stakeholders.

- Conduct technical monitoring missions on sites and provide supervision throughout project implementation.

- Identify and address technical issues arising during construction and installation phases.

- Monitor compliance with UNDP and EIB social and environmental standards during the project implementation.

- Support testing, commissioning, and acceptance procedures for completed renewable energy installations.

- Verify completion of works and compliance prior to project handover.

3.Provision of operational support of the RES Project, monitoring, reporting, capacity building and facilitating knowledge sharing.

- Support final beneficiaries in obtaining prosumer status and completing related administrative and technical requirements where necessary.

- Monitor and evaluate the operational performance of installed renewable energy systems.

- Assess energy generation, energy savings, and greenhouse gas emissions reductions, including CO ₂ savings achieved through project interventions.

- Support the development and delivery of training activities for personnel of final beneficiaries to ensure proper operation and maintenance of installed systems.

- Collect, analyse, and document good practices, lessons learned, and project success stories.

- Contribute technical inputs to project monitoring, evaluation, and reporting requirements.

- Prepare and maintain technical records, performance data, and project documentation.

Support the dissemination of project results and knowledge-sharing activities.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Engineering Analyst will provide technical support for the implementation of the RES Programme, including the review of technical documentation, support to procurement, technical monitoring of contracts, and verification of completed works. The incumbent will work closely with the project team, procurement colleagues, contractors, final beneficiaries and other relevant stakeholders in accordance with the approved project document and UNDP rules and procedures

- A first university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, with a combination of additional two years of qualifying relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of professional experience in implementing energy efficiency and/or renewable energy projects for public buildings and public utilities, as well as solar power station projects in the municipal sector using national financial instruments.

- Proven ability to draft, edit and produce written proposals, advisory documents, analytical documents and results-focused reports.

- Proven track record of strong knowledge of the renewable and, in particular, solar energy equipment market, including modules, inverters, monitoring systems, and Balance of System (BOS) components, as well as battery energy storage systems (BESS), with a clear understanding of technical and logistical aspects of system integration.

- Experience and good understanding of Ukrainian legislation in the field of renewable energy, in particular, the regulatory framework governing the operation of solar power plants, grid connection procedures, net-billing mechanism, and energy storage system requirements.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Descripción de la Oficina/Unidad/Proyecto:

Esta convocatoria se realiza para dos (2) vacantes de Asistente de Monitoreo y evaluación en nivel NPSA5. Los puestos vacantes corresponden a los siguientes proyectos: Proyecto P/01004165 "Eliminación de químicos peligrosos de las cadenas de suministro en Ecuador"; y, Proyecto P/01005906 "Nature for Health Climate Promise".

Proyecto P/01005906 “Nature for Health Climate Promise”:

La iniciativa Climate Promise del Programa de Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo, busca dar una

respuesta al desafío climático, considerando el Acuerdo de París, para reducir las emisiones de los GEI

(Gases de Efecto Invernadero) que causan el calentamiento global y fortalecer la adaptación a sus

impactos. Climate Promise es la iniciativa más relevante de la cooperación internacional a nivel mundial y

opera en más de 120 países a nivel mundial.

Además, el PNUD ha trabajado también con el Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (MAE), el Ministerio de

Salud Pública (MSP) y Agrocalidad, en el proyecto “Vigilancia Integrada de la Interfaz Humano-Animal-

Ambiente bajo Mecanismos de Coordinación Intersectorial en Ecuador”, financiado por el Fondo Fiduciario

de Asociados Múltiples (MPTF) en el marco de Nature for Health (N4H) y con modalidad de implementación

DIM. Esta iniciativa busca fortalecer la prevención temprana de enfermedades zoonóticas desde un

enfoque One Health en Ecuador, así como desarrollar e implementar un sistema integrado de vigilancia

bajo coordinación intersectorial, reconociendo la interdependencia entre la salud humana, animal y

ambiental.

La iniciativa N4H, a su vez, se asocia al Plan de Adaptación al Cambio Climático del Ecuador y sus rutas

sectoriales vinculadas a salud, ambiente, adaptación y fortalecimiento institucional, guardando estrecha

relación con el ámbito de acción de Climate Promise.

En este sentido, y bajo un enfoque de portafolio, ambas iniciativas representan una oportunidad para

generar sinergias programáticas y operativas, promoviendo una implementación más articulada, eficiente

y coherente con las prioridades nacionales.

En vista del aumento significativo de actividades y de la creciente escala de iniciativas de UNDP Climate

Promise Ecuador, es necesario crear una posición especializada en Monitoreo y Seguimiento. El proyecto

articula actualmente múltiples componentes con diversas instituciones nacionales, agencias del Sistema

de Naciones Unidas, socios de desarrollo, donantes y actores privados. Esta posición permitirá fortalecer

el seguimiento integral de las actividades, resultados, indicadores y recursos, asegurando una gestión

oportuna y basada en resultados.

Adicionalmente, en coordinación con la unidad de Planificación Estratégica, Monitoreo y Evaluación de la

Oficina País, el/la Asociado/a contribuirá de manera parcial al fortalecimiento de los sistemas de

seguimiento, gestión de datos, reporte de resultados y generación de evidencia para la toma de decisiones programáticas del PNUD, promoviendo la aplicación de estándares corporativos de monitoreo,

evaluación y gestión basada en resultados.

Proyecto P/01004165 "Eliminación de químicos peligrosos de las cadenas de suministro en Ecuador":

El proyecto “Eliminación de químicos peligrosos de las cadenas de suministro en Ecuador”, en adelante denominado también como “Cadenas de valor sostenibles”, cuenta con financiamiento del Fondo para el Medio Ambiente Mundial (GEF) y es ejecutado bajo la Modalidad de Implementación Nacional (NIM) por el Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (MAE), con el apoyo de la Oficina de País del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) en Ecuador. El proyecto forma parte del Programa Integrado de Cadenas de Suministro del GEF, orientado a transformar cadenas de suministro con altos impactos ambientales mediante la sustitución de materiales y procesos intensivos en recursos y productos químicos peligrosos por alternativas sostenibles, circulares y transparentes. En Ecuador, la intervención se concentra en los sectores de la construcción, particularmente en las cadenas de ladrillos, bambú y otros materiales de construcción, y de la moda y textiles, con énfasis en las cadenas de valor del algodón y el abacá.

El proyecto tiene como objetivo contribuir a la eliminación de la contaminación asociada con productos químicos peligrosos en las cadenas de suministro de la construcción y textil en Ecuador, mediante la promoción y aplicación de principios y prácticas de economía circular, el fortalecimiento de instrumentos regulatorios, la incorporación de tecnologías innovadoras y el establecimiento de alianzas multisectoriales. La intervención responde a los impactos ambientales, sociales y económicos asociados con estas cadenas de suministro, entre ellos el uso intensivo de recursos naturales, agua y energía, la generación de residuos y contaminación, las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero y el uso de sustancias químicas nocivas o peligrosas.

Para este propósito, el proyecto implementará un enfoque integrado a lo largo de las cadenas de valor, promoviendo el diseño regenerativo y los modelos de negocio circulares; el uso de materiales innovadores, sostenibles, reciclados y reciclables; procesos de producción más limpia que reduzcan el consumo de agua, energía y productos químicos peligrosos; la creación de mercados y patrones de consumo sostenible; y estrategias de post-uso y logística inversa basadas en los principios de las 9R. Estas acciones se complementarán con el fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales, el desarrollo y mejora de mecanismos financieros, la implementación de proyectos piloto, la generación de conocimiento y la articulación entre entidades públicas, sector privado, academia, organizaciones de la sociedad civil y actores financieros.

Como resultado, se prevé beneficiar directamente a 127.268 personas, de las cuales 67.993 serán mujeres y 59.275 hombres, mejorar la gestión de 85.902 hectáreas de paisaje, evitar aproximadamente 1.017.209 toneladas métricas de CO₂, reducir 2.036 toneladas de residuos que contienen contaminantes orgánicos persistentes (COP) y disminuir 31,52 gTE de emisiones atmosféricas de COP no intencionales (COPNI). Asimismo, el proyecto contribuirá al cumplimiento de los compromisos ambientales asumidos por Ecuador en el marco de la Contribución Determinada a Nivel Nacional (NDC), el Convenio de Estocolmo sobre COP, el Convenio de Rotterdam y otros Acuerdos Multilaterales sobre el Medio Ambiente, fortaleciendo paralelamente las políticas nacionales de economía circular, producción más limpia y gestión ambientalmente adecuada de productos químicos y desechos.

En este contexto, los socios del proyecto requieren la contratación de un/a Asistente de Proyecto para Monitoreo y Evaluación, a fin de brindar apoyo a las actividades de monitoreo y seguimiento del proyecto, incluyendo la recopilación y organización de información, el seguimiento de avances, la elaboración de reportes e insumos para la toma de decisiones y la coordinación con las instituciones socias y actores vinculados a su implementación.

Alcance del Trabajo:

1.Brindar apoyo en la Implementación, asistencia a la coordinación y seguimiento:

a) Realizar el seguimiento técnico, operativo y financiero del proyecto, verificando el cumplimiento de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, metas, hitos y ejecución presupuestaria, e identificando oportunamente riesgos, desviaciones o retrasos.

b) Asistir en el seguimiento con los equipos técnicos, instituciones socias y actores involucrados, facilitando reuniones periódicas, sistematizando acuerdos y compromisos, y asegurando su cumplimiento oportuno.

c) Apoyar en la coordinación y gestión, recopilación y sistematización de información y medios de verificación, manteniendo actualizados los indicadores, herramientas y sistemas institucionales de monitoreo y generando información de calidad para la toma de decisiones y los reportes del proyecto.

d) Apoyar la gestión y difusión del conocimiento generado por el proyecto, sistematizando experiencias, lecciones aprendidas y buenas prácticas, y promoviendo su intercambio y difusión entre los actores relevantes.

e) Brindar apoyo en el seguimiento de los proyectos piloto, incluyendo la revisión de avances, productos e informes, así como la coordinación con las entidades ejecutoras, beneficiarias y socias involucradas.

2.Brindar asistencia en el monitoreo del desempeño, gestión de resultados y elaboración de reporte:

a) Dar seguimiento al cumplimiento del POA, marco de resultados e indicadores del proyecto, mediante la actualización de matrices, tableros de control y otros instrumentos de monitoreo.

b) Consolidar, analizar y validar información técnica, programática y financiera, verificando la consistencia de los avances en productos, actividades, indicadores y metas.

c) Elaborar reportes técnicos y financieros periódicos para la coordinación del proyecto, PNUD, donantes e instituciones socias, incluyendo avances, resultados, riesgos, acuerdos y acciones correctivas.

d) Apoyar procesos de auditoría, evaluación y revisión, asegurando la disponibilidad y calidad de la información requerida y el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos y estándares del PNUD y del donante.

3. Apoyar a los requerimientos estratégicos de monitoreo y evaluación de la Oficina País.

a) Contribuir a los requerimientos estratégicos de monitoreo y evaluación de la Oficina País mediante el seguimiento programático, análisis de datos, elaboración de reportes, sistematización de lecciones aprendidas y generación de evidencia para la medición de resultados e impacto, fortaleciendo la toma de decisiones y la implementación de los estándares corporativos de gestión basada en resultados (RBM), incorporando enfoques sistémicos y de portafolio que permitan analizar contribuciones a resultados de desarrollo, identificar interdependencias entre intervenciones y generar evidencia para la gestión adaptativa y el aprendizaje.

4. Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto asignado:

jobs.title: Re-advertisement Project Coordinator GCF (N-PSA 10) (Open to Tier 1, 2 & 3 applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups, and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous references and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The UNDP Multi-Country Office (MCO) current support to the Government of Mauritius in the energy sector includes several on-going and pipeline projects, which are in line with the Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement to reduce GHG emissions by 40% and increase the share of renewable energy to 60% in the national energy mix by 2030.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow @UNDP.

The UNDP Mauritius Country Office (CO) consists of two distinct units including the Environment Unit and Socio-Economic Development Unit with a diverse portfolio worth USD 65 M including the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Global Environment Facility (GEF), Adaptation Fund (AF), European Union (EU), Japan Supplementary Budget (JSB), E-Health Portfolio and TRAC projects. The Environment Unit manages a portfolio covering various focal areas such as Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, Biodiversity, Sustainable Land Management, and Chemicals and Waste.

The unit will hire a project coordinator for the “Accelerating the Transformational Shift to a Low-Carbon Economy in the Republic of Mauritius” project which is implemented under National Implementation Modality (NIM).

The project is funded by GCF with implementation initiated in 2017. The objective is to overcome identified barriers to low carbon development and support the inclusive deployment of 25MW of PV system on the electrical grid. The implementing partner is the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy and Public Utilities, the Central Electricity Board, the Outer Island Development Cooperation, and the Mauritius Renewable Energy Agency.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Coordinator (PC) will be locally recruited based on an open competitive process. His/ her responsibilities shall include:

- Overall management of the project, mobilization of all inputs, supervision of staff, consultants, and sub-contractors.

- Reporting to the Head of the Environment Unit and periodic reporting to the Project Steering Committee (PSC).

- Meeting government obligations under the project (NIM modality).

- Liaison with Government, UNDP, UN Agencies, NGOs, project partners, and donor agencies.

Summary of Key Functions

- Strategic project planning, coordination, and implementation,

- Management of the Project,

- Representation and Coordination,

- Management of communication flow,

- Partnership building and donor liaison.

Specific tasks and responsibilities:

- Ensures strategic project planning, coordination and implementation , focusing on achievement of the following results: Provides guidance and manages the overall implementation including planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring, Ensures overall efficient coordination of programmes/projects including planning processes and timely delivery of results taking into consideration agreed-upon work plans with the UNDP country office and the participating ministries/organizations, Ensures identification and promotion of joint programming and planning opportunities Identifies and develops new programme and project opportunities, Supports capacity building of national counterparts, Oversees project implementation through close monitoring of results. Ensures effective application of RBM tools, management of scorecard targets and other benchmarks, Coordinates and follows through on decentralized local evaluations. Ensures full compliance with audit requirements and timely follow-up to audit recommendations. Promotes identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learned for organizational sharing and learning.

- Responsible for effective project management focusing on achievement of the following results: Ensures smooth running of the project, builds an effective project team, promotes teamwork and an environment that is conducive to delivering results, Ensures full responsibility for the appropriate use and management of resources attributed to the project by tracking use of financial resources, ensuring the integrity of financial systems and consistent application of the Internal Control Framework and/or rules and regulations. Continually find ways to systematically identify and integrate efficiency gains and cost reductions in all operations. Approves contracts and ATLAS transactions under written delegated authority from the Resident Representative and/or Country Director. Has Atlas manager rights as delegated. Responsible for the management of the project staff, monitors their performance, completing performance assessments where necessary, Ensure timely and regular reporting, Build capacity of the project staff by identifying capacity needs and establishing training/learning programmes.

- Ensures effective management of the three components for proper implementation as per the funding proposal achieving the following: Contribute to preparation and revision of project work and financial plans, as required by UNDP, and support the operational and financial planning processes, Oversee and ensure timely submission of the Inception Report, Combined Project Implementation Review/Annual Project Report, Technical reports, quarterly financial reports, and other reports as may be required by UNDP, GCF and other oversight agencies, Contribute to the preparation and implementation of progress reports, and monitor all project activities, budgets and financial expenditures, Assist in the preparation of payments requests for operational expenses, salaries, insurances etc. as well as follow up on timely disbursements by UNDP CO, Maintain project correspondence and communication, Assist in logistical organization of meetings, training and workshops.

- Responsible for Representation and Coordination in the area focusing on achievement of the following results: Able to represent UNDP with UNCT and development partners if needed, Provides strong coordination support to national authorities and other organizations through the establishment of a wider consultation process, Ensures proper coordination and inputs to Interagency initiatives, Maintains collaboration and coordination with the other project managers to ensure programmatic integration and sharing of best practices.

- Promotes communication flow in the project focusing on achievement of the following results: Maximizes communication between the various portfolios and ensures that stakeholders (development partners, bilateral and multilateral donors, private sector, civil society, UN agencies and Government agencies) have one consistent UNDP counterpart, Ensures internal communication and coordination at project level and effective and proactive communication between relevant project units, Monitors the perception of the GCF project at the local level and suggest media activities that position the GCF project more strategically and effectively as a neutral broker for local development, Enhances local visibility for the project in development effectiveness, Ensures that local development results are effectively communicated in collaboration with Communication Office in the country office.

- Fosters partnership building and donor liaison focusing on achievement of the following results: Contributes to the development of the project Partnership and Resource Mobilization (PRM) strategy, including planning tools to implement the strategy, Identifies new partnerships and strengthens existing ones at the project level through innovative approaches to partnership development, Encourages ways of increasing project funding such as engaging in resource mobilization efforts in consultation with local counterparts and following up with donors on local opportunities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Impact of Results

- The Project Coordinator is the UNDP senior representative in the project. The results of his/her work impact on the standing and reputation of UNDP in the country and with the Green Climate Fund. When requested by the Resident Representative or Country Director, the Project Coordinator represents UNDP in international and national forums, liaises with external clients and a broad range of constituencies and UNDP counterparts in the Government, local and international media, civil society as well as counterparts from other international organizations.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will work under the general supervision of the Head of the Environment Unit (who may delegate a direct supervisory role) in the UNDP MCO for Mauritius and Seychelles and will collaborate closely with the Project Director for National Implementation Modality (NIM) Projects.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigating complex landscape, champion inter- agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management (Insert below standard sentence if the position has direct reports.)

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

People Management

• Show managerial courage

• Ability to demonstrate empathy and emotional intelligence

• Ability to motivate and direct

• Ability to build an enabling Workplace

• Ability to build capability

• Manage performance and ensure accountability

• Lead with Humility

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies (insert up to 7 competencies)

Thematic Area - Name - Definition

Business Management - Result Based Management - Ability to manage programmes and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results.

Business Management - Project Management - Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management - Partnerships Management - Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation - Ability to research and turn into useful knowledge, relevant for context or responsive to a stated need

Business Direction Strategy - Strategic thinking - Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions

Ability to leverage learning from a variety of sources to anticipate and respond to future trends; to demonstrate foresight to model what future developments and possible ways forward look like for UNDP.

Partnership Management - Strategic Engagement - Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking - Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in engineering, Environmental Science, Business Administration or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (master’s degree) or 7 years (Bachelor’s degree) of relevant working experience in the fields related to the assignment, at national is required.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.
