jobs.title: Humanitarian Affairs Officer - UNOCHA - Nationals Only
jobs.description:
Ce poste est ouvert aux ressortissants maliens uniquement.

CONTEXT

Le Bureau de Coordination des Affaires Humanitaires (OCHA) est un département du Secrétariat des Nations Unies. Il a pour mission de mobiliser et de coordonner l’action humanitaire de façon efficace en partenariat avec les acteurs nationaux et internationaux, de façon à atténuer la souffrance humaine, faire un plaidoyer pour les droits des populations dans le besoin, promouvoir la préparation et la prévention des catastrophes et faciliter la mise en place de solutions durables.

OCHA a egalement pour mandat, la coordination de l’assistance humanitaire dans des contextes d’urgence complexe ou de désastre naturel, en soutien au Coordonnateur Humanitaire des Nations Unies, la dissémination de l’information destinée à la communauté humanitaire, au Gouvernement et aux bailleurs de fonds, ainsi que dans le soutien aux efforts de mobilisation des ressources.

Dans sa structure opérationnelle, le bureau de OCHA comprend le bureau national à Bamako et des sous-bureaux de terrain a Gao et Menaka, Tombouctou, et Mopti où le présent poste est attaché pour des bésoins opérationels.

TACHES ET RESPONSABILITÉS

Sous la supervision du Chef de sous-bureau, le/la responsable des affaires humanitaires sera chargé(e) des tâches suivantes :

- Suivre, analyser et faire rapport sur l'évolution de la situation humanitaire, les secours/gestion des catastrophes ou les situations d'urgence dans le pays/la zone qui lui est assigné(e).

- Organiser et préparer des études sur l'aide humanitaire, les secours d'urgence et les questions connexes.

- Organiser le travail de suivi, y compris les réunions d'examen technique interagences pour soutenir le travail d'élaboration des politiques et la prise de décision sur les questions importantes.

- Participer à des projets complexes et de grande envergure, y compris des missions d'évaluation des catastrophes ou autres.

- Aider à la coordination de l'aide humanitaire/urgence internationale dans des situations d'urgence/catastrophe complexes et à assurer le soutien nécessaire (par exemple, personnel, financement, équipement spécialisé, fournitures, etc.

- Collaborer avec d'autres agences humanitaires pour planifier et évaluer les programmes d'aide humanitaire et d'aide d'urgence, et contribue à faire en sorte que les dernières découvertes, les enseignements tirés, les directives politiques, etc.

- Aider à la production des appels à l'aide internationale ; veiller à l'utilisation et à la dépense appropriées des contributions des donateurs acheminées par l'intermédiaire d'OCHA.

- Établir et maintenir des contacts avec des responsables gouvernementaux, d'autres agences des Nations unies, des organisations non gouvernementales, des missions diplomatiques, des médias, etc.

- Entreprendre et soutenir des missions d'assistance technique et d'autres missions sur le terrain, par exemple participer à des voyages sur le terrain pour entreprendre des examens approfondis des mécanismes de coordination de certains pays.

- Préparer ou contribuer à la préparation de divers rapports écrits, documents et communications, par exemple, rédiger des sections d'études, des documents de référence, des directives politiques, des documents parlementaires, des briefings, des études de cas, des présentations, de la correspondance, etc.

- Servir de point focal principal sur des sujets spécifiques ou des questions liées aux politiques ; se tenir au courant des derniers développements, assurer la liaison avec d'autres organisations humanitaires, donateurs, etc., garantir des mécanismes appropriés de suivi et de rapport ; fournir des informations et des conseils sur une série de questions connexes.

- Examiner et fournir des conseils sur les questions de politique liées à la sauvegarde des principes humanitaires et à la fourniture efficace de l'aide humanitaire.

- Organiser et participer à des groupes de travail, des réunions, des conférences, des consultations avec d'autres agences et partenaires sur des questions liées à l'aide humanitaire et aux secours d'urgence.

- Fournir des conseils et éventuellement superviser le personnel nouveau/junior.

- Effectuer d'autres tâches selon les besoins.

COMPETENCES

- Professionnalisme : Connaissance d'un éventail d'assistance humanitaire, de secours d'urgence et des questions humanitaires connexes, y compris les approches et les techniques permettant d'aborder les problèmes. Capacité d'analyse et, en particulier, capacité d'analyser et d'articuler la dimension humanitaire des questions qui nécessitent une réponse coordonnée des Nations unies. Capacité à identifier les problèmes et de faire preuve de jugement dans l'application de l'expertise technique pour résoudre un large éventail de problèmes. Capacité de mener des recherches, y compris la capacité d'évaluer et d'intégrer des informations provenant de diverses sources et d'évaluer l'impact de ces informations d'une variété de sources et d'évaluer l'impact sur la situation des droits humanitaires dans le pays/la zone assignée. Aptitude à travailler sous une pression extrême, parfois dans un environnement très stressant (par exemple, troubles civils, catastrophes naturelles et misère humaine). Capacité à fournir des conseils au personnel nouveau/junior. Fait preuve de fierté dans son travail et dans ses réalisations ; faire preuve de compétence professionnelle et de maîtrise de la matière traitée. Est consciencieux et efficace dans le respect des engagements, des délais et des résultats en respectant les délais et en obtenant des résultats. Est motivé par des préoccupations professionnelles plutôt que personnelles. Fait preuve de persévérance face à des problèmes ou des défis difficiles. Reste calme dans les situations stressantes. Assume la responsabilité de l'intégration de la perspective et de garantir la participation égale des femmes et des hommes dans tous les domaines de travail.

- Travail d’équipe : Travaille en collaboration avec ses collègues pour atteindre les objectifs de l'organisation ; sollicite l'apport des autres en valorisant sincèrement leurs idées et leur expertise ; est prêt à apprendre des autres ; place l'ordre du jour de l'équipe avant l'ordre du jour personnel ; soutient et agit en accord avec la décision finale du groupe, même si ces décisions ne reflètent pas entièrement sa propre position ; partage le mérite des réalisations de l'équipe et accepte la responsabilité conjointe de ces réalisations.

- Aptitude à la communication : s’exprime clairement et efficacement, tant oralement que par écrit ; écoute les autres, les comprend bien et donne suite comme il convient ; Adapte son langage et les moyens de communication utilisées selon l’audience ciblée ; Pose les questions voulues afin d’obtenir des éclaircissements et faciliter le dialogue ; Partage l'information avec tous ceux qu’elle intéresse et tient chacun au courant ; Analyse et synthétise des informations complexes pour en faciliter la compréhension par divers publics ; Maitrise divers outils et moyens de communication en vue de toucher différents publics cibles ; Fait preuve de discernement et a un jugement éditorial face à la communication d’informations sensibles.

QUALIFICATIONS

Formation:

- Diplôme universitaire supérieur (master ou équivalent) en sciences sociales, relations internationales, droits de l'homme, développement ou dans un domaine connexe est exigé. OU

- Diplôme universitaire de premier niveau (Licence) dans les domaines susmentionnés avec 2 années supplémentaires d’expérience sera dument pris en considération en lieu du master

Expérience professionnelles :

- Au moins deux (2) années d'expérience avérée (avec Master ou équivalent) ou quatre (4) années d’expérience avérée au sein des Nations Unies ou avec des organisations internationales impliquées dans l'aide humanitaire ou la coopération au développement sont requises ;

- Une expérience de participation à des réunions, conférences, consultations sur des questions liées à l'aide humanitaire et aux secours d'urgence avec d'autres agences et partenaires est requise

- Une connaissance des questions humanitaires et de l'architecture internationale de coordination humanitaire (IASC) est requise ;

- Une expérience de participation à des projets complexes et de grande envergure, y compris des missions d'évaluation des catastrophes ou autres serait un atout

- Une expérience dans le domaine de la coordination ou de la médiation humanitaire et du droit international humanitaire serait un atout

- Une expérience avérée dans la rédaction/ production de rapport est requise.

- Une bonne connaissance du système des Nations unies est un atout ;

Langues :

- La maîtrise du français (à l'oral et à l'écrit) pour ce poste est requise ;

- Une bonne connaissance des langues régionales du Mali est un atout.

- Une connaissance pratique de l'anglais est un atout.

DISCLAIMER

Égalité des chances

En tant qu'employeur souscrivant au principe de l'égalité des chances, OCHA valorise la diversité en tant qu'expression de la multiplicité des nations et des cultures où nous opérons et, à ce titre, nous encourageons les candidats qualifiés de tous horizons à postuler à des postes au sein de l'organisation. Nos décisions d'embauche sont fondées sur le mérite et l'aptitude au poste, sans discrimination.

OCHA s'engage également à créer un lieu de travail inclusif où tout le personnel est habilité à contribuer à notre mission, est valorisé, peut s'épanouir et bénéficie d'opportunités de carrière ouvertes à tous.

Harcèlement sexuel, exploitation et abus d'autorité

OCHA ne tolère pas le harcèlement, le harcèlement sexuel, l'exploitation, la discrimination et l'abus d'autorité. Tous les candidats sélectionnés sont donc soumis à des contrôles pertinents et doivent respecter les normes et principes respectifs.

Période d’essai

Pour toutes les nouvelles nominations à durée déterminée (FTA) a OCHA, y compris pour les agents transférés ou détachés a OCHA dans le cadre de l’Accord inter-organisations concernant le transfert, le détachement ou le prêt de personnel, et pour toute nomination de plus d’un an, la poursuite du contrat au-delà des 12 premiers mois est conditionnée à la réussite de la période d’essai.

Droit de sélectionner plusieurs candidats

OCHA se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cette annonce de vacance de poste. Nous pouvons également retenir les candidatures et prendre en considération les candidats qui postulent à ce poste pour d'autres postes similaires au PNUD, au même niveau et avec une description de poste, une expérience et des exigences éducationnelles similaires.

Utilisation de l’IA par les candidats

Les candidats sont invités à consulter les directives du PNUD concernant l’utilisation responsable de l’IA dans les processus de recrutement et de sélection.

Alerte aux escroqueries

Le PNUD ne facture aucune redevance à aucun stade de son processus de recrutement. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL), Analyst [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Approche Tiers

Veuillez noter le niveau approprié indiqué dans le titre de l'avis de vacance de poste et vous assurer que vous détenez le type de contrat correspondant, tel que défini ci-dessous :

- Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/UNCDF/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026

- Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/UNCDF/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA)

- Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes

- Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes

Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé de l'offre d'emploi, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions d'éligibilité pour postuler.

II. Background and Organizational Context

Depuis 2012, le Mali est confronté à une crise multidimensionnelle marquée par la persistance de l’insécurité,

la fragilité institutionnelle et les vulnérabilités socio-économiques. Malgré les réformes engagées par les

autorités de la Transition, notamment dans le cadre de la refondation de l’État et du renforcement de la

gouvernance, les groupes armés terroristes continuent de menacer la stabilité de plusieurs régions du pays.

Les causes profondes de la crise sont liées aux déficits de gouvernance et de dialogue politique, aux inégalités

socio-économiques, aux tensions autour de l’accès aux ressources naturelles et aux effets de la criminalité

transfrontalière. Ces facteurs sont aggravés par l’extrémisme violent, le terrorisme et les conflits

communautaires dans un contexte marqué par une présence limitée de l’État dans certaines localités.

Dans ces conditions, la consolidation de la paix exige des interventions intégrées favorisant la gouvernance

inclusive, le dialogue, la cohésion sociale, le développement local et le renforcement de la résilience des

communautés afin de traiter durablement les causes structurelles des conflits.

Pour accompagner les efforts nationaux, le Mali bénéficie de l’appui du Fonds pour la consolidation de la

paix (PBF) du Secrétaire général des Nations Unies. Le PBF est le principal instrument de l’ONU pour

maintenir la paix dans les pays confrontés à des conflits violents ou en phase de relèvement. Il investit

auprès d’entités des Nations unies, de gouvernements, d’organisations régionales, de banques multilatérales,

de fonds fiduciaires nationaux à donateurs multiples ou d’organisations de la société civile.

Le PBF est présent au Mali depuis 2014 et y a investi plus de 100 millions de dollars. Actuellement, le

portefeuille compte huit (08) projets en cours pour un montant de plus de 21 millions de dollar. Deux (2)

autres initiatives sont en cours d’élaboration, pour un budget total d’environ 5 millions de dollar.

Le Secrétariat du PBF au Mali, sert de lien entre la Branche de financement pour la Paix du Bureau d’Appui

à la consolidation de la paix et au maintien de la paix à Naw York (PBPSO), la Coordonnatrice Résidente de

l’ONU, le Gouvernement, la société civile et les agences des Nations Unies sur le terrain. Son rôle est

d’identifier des opportunités pour des projets financés par le PBF, de soutenir le développement de nouvelles

initiatives et de s’assurer que le portefeuille s’aligne sur les priorités stratégiques nationales et internationales.

Le Secrétariat aide également à orienter les investissements du PBF, en coordonnant, surveillant et évaluant

les projets pour garantir leur conformité aux normes de qualité et pour éclairer les investissements futurs.

Dans ce contexte, afin d’assurer un suivi, une évaluation, une redevabilité et un apprentissage efficaces, le

PBF, en collaboration avec le PNUD, cherche à recruter un(e) spécialiste MEAL.

III. Objectif du poste

Sous la direction stratégique du Coordonnateur Résident de l’ONU et la supervision directe du Coordonnateur

du Programme PBF, l'Analyste MEAL promeut la gestion axée sur les résultats et une approche axée sur

l'efficacité du programme en dirigeant la mise en œuvre de cadres, de systèmes et d'outils de suivi et

d'évaluation innovants et efficaces. L'Analyste MEAL fournit un soutien technique sur les pratiques de MEAL

et de reporting aux équipes de programme et de projet. Le cas échéant, l'Analyste MEAL soutiendra également

l'assurance qualité du programme et le développement de systèmes pertinents. L’analyste MEAL promeut une

approche collaborative, efficace, axée sur le client, fondée sur des données probantes et la gestion de

portefeuille.

Il / elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chargés de suivi-évaluation d'autres agences de l'équipe de

pays des Nations Unies au Mali et des organisations récipiendaires de financement du PBF, les responsables

gouvernementaux et les donateurs sur le suivi de la mise en œuvre des programmes/projets et les pratiques

d'évaluation.

IV. Principales tâches et responsabilités

1.) Développer, soutenir et renforcer les systèmes de planification MEAL sensibles au genre et aux

conflits

• Promotion des normes du suivi et d’évaluation du PBF, en s’assurant de la qualité et du

contrôle, ainsi que le développement des capacités pour les agences des Nations Unies

récipiendaires ;

• Renforcement des capacités de S&E des agences récipiendaires des fonds PBF, pour

l’élaboration des projets et le suivi des résultats, y compris l’appui à l’élaboration de leurs

cadres de résultats et l’organisation des ateliers de renforcement des capacités en S&E;

2.) Assurer la coordination de la collecte et de la restitution des données de suivi, et appuyer les

activités d’évaluation

• Accompagner les équipes de projet dans la collecte et l’analyse des données de suivi.

• Planifier et organiser des missions de suivi PBF, ainsi que des missions conjointes avec le

Comité Technique et le Comité National de Pilotage.

• Appuyer la mise en œuvre du plan de suivi et d’évaluation de l’exercice d’alignement

stratégique (SRF) avec les IFIs.

• Appuyer les évaluations des projets PBF notamment la revue des TDRs et l’appui technique

pour s’assurer que ces évaluations soient conformes aux exigences du PBF.

• Appui aux exercices évaluatifs indépendants organisés par le Siège ;

3.) Assurer l’exploitation des enseignements tirés du suivi et de l’évaluation et promouvoir le partage

des bonnes pratiques

• Procéder à l’archivage des différentes ressources PBF en vue de faciliter la documentation

des bonnes pratiques

• Superviser la formulation et la diffusion des enseignements pour permettre une réorientation

des projets et encourager l’apprentissage continu.

• Concevoir et animer des activités d’apprentissage au sein de la Communauté de Pratiques et

contribuer à la communauté de pratique du PBPSO.

• Fournir des conseils stratégiques aux équipes de projet pour documenter les bonnes pratiques

des projets

4.) Garantir un reporting, une recherche et une communication efficaces

• Orientation des agences récipiendaires des fonds PBF et les partenaires de mise en œuvre sur

les exigences du PBF en suivi et évaluation des projets et assurance de qualité des rapports

semestriels et annuels des agences ;

• Fournir un appui stratégique et technique au Comité National de Pilotage et aux partenaires

d’exécution des projets pour établir des systèmes de suivi et de reporting robustes.

• Accompagner les chercheurs dans la réalisation d’études de référence, d’enquêtes de

perception, de CBM&E de cartographies des partenaires et d’autres analyses contextuelles

Le titulaire exécute d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel et jugées nécessaires au bon

fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Responsabilités de supervision et de gestion : N/A

V. Exigence

Education

• Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) dans un domaine lié tel que le suivi et

l'évaluation, les études sur la paix, la transformation des conflits, la consolidation de la paix, les relations

ou affaires internationales, les affaires humanitaires ou d'autres domaines pertinents pour la consolidation

de la paix des Nations Unies est requis ou

• Un diplôme universitaire de premier niveau (Licence) dans les domaines mentionnés ci-dessus, associé à

deux années supplémentaires d'expérience qualifiante, sera dûment pris en considération en lieu et place

du diplôme universitaire supérieur.

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

• Au moins deux (2) ans (avec un master) ou quatre (4)ans (avec une licence) d'expérience pertinente

progressive en MEAL est requise.

• Expérience avérée en gestion de programmes/projets, évaluation et suivi est requise.

• Expérience en analyse des conflits et en programmation sensible aux conflits est requise.

• Familiarité avec les procédures du PBF, y compris le suivi et l’évaluation est souhaitée.

• Expérience en gestion du cycle de projet et en développement organisationnel est souhaitée.

• Expérience en traitement des données de projets/programmes, y compris le nettoyage des données est

souhaitée.

• Une expérience avérée de la conception de systèmes de suivi et d'évaluation et de la conception de projets

de développement ou de portefeuilles intégrés est souhaitable.

• Une capacité avérée à travailler avec des données quantitatives et qualitatives et à utiliser de manière

appropriée des outils de collecte de données et d'informations qualitatives de manière innovante est requise.

• Une expérience de la conception, de la mise en œuvre et/ou de la gestion d'évaluations et/ou

d'exercices/processus de collecte de données est souhaitée.

• Une expérience de la conduite de projets de recherche appliquée et de la production de rapports sur les

résultats est souhaitable

• Expérience dans le travail avec les Nations Unies est souhaitable

• Expérience de l'utilisation d'ordinateurs, de progiciels de bureau (MS Word, Excel, etc.) et de systèmes de

gestion Web, et connaissance avancée et à jour des outils de gestion de données et des progiciels de bases

de données est requise..

Exigences linguistiques

• Maîtrise du français parlé et écrit ainsi que de la langue nationale (Bambara) est requise

Connaissance professionnelle de l'anglais souhaitée

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Compétences de base

Obtenir des résultats NIVEAU 1 : Planifie et assure le suivi de son travail, veille à la

qualité des livrables et respecte les délais.

Penser de manière innovante NIVEAU 1: Ouvert aux idées créatives et aux risques connus, c'est

un solutionneur de problèmes pragmatique qui apporte des

améliorations

Apprendre en permanence NIVEAU 1 : Reste ouvert aux idées nouvelles, partage ses

connaissances et tire les enseignements de l'expérience.

S'adapter avec agilité NIVEAU 1 : Accueille positivement le changement et ajuste son

approche face à l'incertitude.

Agir avec détermination NIVEAU 1 : Fait preuve de constance et de calme face à la

pression et poursuit les objectifs fixés.

Engagement et partenariat NIVEAU 1: Fait preuve de compassion et de compréhension envers

les autres, tisse des relations positives

Favoriser la diversité et l'inclusion NIVEAU 1 : Traite chacun avec respect et valorise les différences

dans le travail d'équipe.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

coexistent au sein d'un processus ou d'un système global, et d'examiner comment la modification d'un élément peut avoir un impact sur d'autres parties du système.

jobs.title: Small Grants Programme National Coordinator- NPSA8 [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

Duties and Responsibilities

The National Coordinator will report through a matrixed structure to both the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist. The Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at the country level, including direct supervision of the SGP Programme Associate/Assistant and coordination of the National Steering Committee.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNOPS rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations ( CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

- Sound SGP programme results and impacts, in alignment with national strategies and priorities and SGP strategy and approaches, that contribute to transformational change in society and economy to conserve the global environment and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, Innovative, technically sound and socially inclusive grant portfolio is developed and implemented. Effective and efficient use of resources to create maximum project/programme impact. Increased trust by clients and donors and increased opportunities for visibility, partnerships and co-financing.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will be based in the UNDP [enter name of CO] offices;

- The incumbent will have a matrixed reporting line to the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and to the SGP Regional Programme Specialist, in accordance with SGP Operational Guidelines;

- The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision and development of the SGP Programme Associate/ Assistant {where applicable}

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for the execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be provided with a workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and access to reliable internet connection

Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core

Achieve Results

LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively

Background

The Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) serving as the implementing partner and UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project supports national and local governments in accelerating the transition toward sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, and people-centered urban development. The project promotes integrated urban planning, climate-smart infrastructure, sustainable mobility systems, resource-efficient urban services, enhanced urban biodiversity, and accessible green public spaces. It also strengthens institutional capacities and inclusive governance mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of citizens, communities, civil society organizations, the private sector, and vulnerable groups in urban development and decision-making processes. Through these interventions, the project contributes to creating greener, more resilient, and more inclusive cities that improve quality of life while advancing Mongolia's climate and sustainable development objectives.

The Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry (MOFALI) serving as the implementing partner and the UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by GEF, the project supports national efforts to reduce the use and release of hazardous chemicals across key economic sectors and supply chains.

The project seeks to strengthen the policy and regulatory framework for chemicals management, enhance institutional and technical capacities, improve industry practices, promote the adoption of safer and more sustainable alternatives, and increase transparency and accountability among public and private sector stakeholders. It also supports knowledge generation, awareness raising, and multi-stakeholder engagement to facilitate informed decision-making and responsible chemicals management throughout product life cycles. Through these interventions, the project contributes to reducing environmental pollution and health risks, advancing circular economy principles, and accelerating Mongolia's transition toward greener production systems and sustainable consumption patterns.

The Admin and Finance Associate will provide administrative, financial, and logistical support for the effective implementation of the GEF Funded projects of UNDP Mongolia. Under the direct supervision of the respective Project Managers and in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office operations team, the incumbent will support project budgeting, financial planning and reporting, travel and event logistics, asset and inventory management, records management, and compliance with UNDP, GEF, and national implementation modality (NIM) requirements. The Associate will ensure timely processing of financial transactions, maintain accurate project documentation, monitor expenditures against approved budgets, support project audits and reviews, and facilitate administrative coordination among implementing partners, government institutions, service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure efficient and accountable project delivery and achievement of project results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administrative and Finance Associate provides integrated operational, financial, and administrative support to the Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project and the Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project, ensuring efficient implementation, compliance, and coordination across both GEF-funded initiatives. Working closely with Project Managers, implementing partners, and the UNDP Country Office, the Associate supports financial management, administrative processes, logistics, and reporting to facilitate the timely and accountable delivery of project results.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Project Managers, the Admin and Finance Associate is responsible for project implementation support services, ensuring effective operational management of the project and transparent utilization of financial resources. The Admin and Finance Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. The Admin and Finance Associate works in close collaboration with the Project Implementing Unit (PIU) and the Country Office.

- Assets Management

- Administrative Travel support

- Actively contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans to support effective project implementation

- Verify the accuracy and completeness of financial documents and ensure timely resolution of financial processing issues

- Maintain effective internal controls and ensure compliance with UNDP financial rules, regulations, and procedures

- Monitor budget utilization, expenditures, cash flow, and delivery rates, and advise the NPC on variances, risks, and corrective actions

- Prepare financial forecasts, analyses, and periodic financial reports to support project planning, decision-making, and reporting requirements.

Financial Management and Budget Administration

- Monitor project financial performance and expenditures against approved GEF budgets, work plans, and results frameworks;

- Track, verify, and report co-financing contributions in accordance with GEF requirements and reporting standards;

- Coordinate with UNDP, government counterparts, implementing partners to ensure timely submission Government of Mongolia, UNDP, and GEF financial reports and supporting documentation;

- Ensure compliance with UNDP POPP, GEF, NIM, and relevant Government regulations;

- Contribute to gender-responsive budgeting and tracking of expenditures related to gender equality and social inclusion.

Assets Management:

- Ensure effective inventory and asset management in compliance with applicable Government of Mongolia, UNDP policies and procedures;

- Participate in periodic physical verification of project assets and inventories, prepare and submit inventory verification reports, and process all required asset receiving and disposal documentation;

- Manage the transfer, reassignment, and disposal of project assets in accordance with Government of Mongolia and UNDP asset management rules, regulations, and established procedures.

Administrative and Travel Support:

- Support the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans;

- Provide administrative, logistical, and travel support for project activities, including meetings, missions, training, workshops, conferences, and seminars;

- Maintain office supplies, inventory records, contract files, project documentation, and archives in accordance with established procedures;

- Prepare and monitor procurement and contractual documentation and maintain an up-to-date contract management system;

- Support the preparation of project reports and ensure proper filing, record management, and archiving of project documents;

- Facilitate coordination among projects, partners, and related initiatives to promote collaboration and synergies;

- Document, compile, and disseminate project knowledge, lessons learned, and good practices, and contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Monitor and share relevant national, regional, and international best practices to support project implementation and learning;

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Central Africa is home to the second largest tropical rainforest in the world. Forest loss is accelerating despite ongoing efforts, as government action alone has not been sufficient to establish an effective balance between the interests of the forest and of economic development.

On this basis, a coalition of willing donors – Norway, European Union, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Netherlands, and South Korea – together with Central African partner countries – Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Cameroon, the Republic of Congo, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and the Republic of Gabon – have entered in 2015 into a collaborative partnership to establish in partnership with the United Nations, the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI). The objective of this initiative is to recognize and preserve the value of the forests in the region to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and contribute to sustainable development. This objective will be attained through the implementation of country-led, national scale REDD+ and Low Emissions Development (LED) investment frameworks that include policy reforms and measures to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and promote sustainable development.

The CAFI Trust Fund is the principal means to implement the Central African Forest Initiative. It is administered by the MPTF-Office (http://mptf.undp.org/factsheet/fund/AFI00). As per the updated Fund Terms of Reference and the direct cost Secretariat project document, the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) is hosting the CAFI Secretariat providing the secretariat administrative services under the oversight of the CAFI Executive Board and other participating UN organizations (UNDP, UNCDF, FAO, UN-Habitat, UNFPA, and UNEP).

Established by the Executive Board, the CAFI Secretariat was created to support the fund management coupled with policy and programmatic dialogue and portfolio administration, strongly based on result-based management and solid reporting methods. With the intensification of CAFI presence in countries and solid increase in investment programmes and related digital innovations, including but not limited to the introduction of Payment for Environmental Services, a Technical Assistance Facility, Private Sector projects, it is fundamental that the Secretariat provides high-efficiency M&E services to support the Trust Fund objectives. This requires an M&E Unit led by an expert Head of M&E that can efficiently work across all CAFI partner countries and portfolio accordingly namely DRC, Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Gabon, embracing and helping to expand CAFI’s digital ecosystem in support of M&E in general and performance-based programming in particular.

Position Purpose

Under the strategic guidance of the Head of Secretariat, the Team Lead f the Monitoring and Evaluation and Risk Management Unit promotes results-based management and a programme effectiveness approach, by leading the design and implementation of innovative and effective monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks, systems and tools, and implements a robust approach to risk management across the investment portfolio of the Trust Fund, serving the Executive Board in risk-based decision making approach. Where relevant, the Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management will also support programme quality assurance and developing relevant systems. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management provides technical support on M&E and reporting practices to the business unit`s senior management as well as programme and project teams. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management promotes a collaborative, efficient, client-focused, evidence-based, and portfolio management approach.

The Team Lead of M&E and risk leads a team of personnel working on M&E and RBM, and as applicable, quality assurance work; collaborates closely with Programme, Operations and project teams in other branches and across partners and donors, programme staff in other UN agencies, and Government officials, technical advisers and experts, NGOs, and other organizations on programme implementation and monitoring and evaluation issues and practices.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Lead in designing and implementing the monitoring and evaluation frameworks, systems, and tools at Fund level and conduct quality assurance of the overall Fund’s portfolio.

• Develop integrated monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and results-based management (RBM) policies, frameworks, systems/tools and plans at Fund level, in line with CAFI’s Terms of Reference and CAFI’s Manual of Operations and its related policies towards programmes, projects and initiatives, to inform on their adequate implementation, and ensure their effectiveness and compliance with the Fund programming and reporting requirements.

• Development, continued improvement and implementation of CAFI M&E and Learning policy and strategies/Plans (e.g. the Fund’s evaluation strategy/plan), as well as related guidelines, minimum standards, procedures and templates.

• Develop SOPs and guidelines for CAFI Secretariat staff, partner countries and implement organizations.

• Coordinate partner countries in adapting, if and as required, CAFI’s M&E framework, procedures and tools to their context, while ensuring full alignment with CAFI’s.

• Participate in CAFI’s annual planning processes, defining targets and harmonized indicators to ensure consistency with CAFI’s policies across CAFI’s portfolio of programmes and projects.

• Contribute to the elaboration and mapping of business processes and procedures in programme and project oversight that includes providing input to establishment of quality assurance processes, guidance notes, protocols, tools, checklists, and sharing best practices.

• Provide technical, innovative and policy advice on M&E and RBM requirements and activities to programme and project managers, staff concerned with monitoring and evaluation, and consultants and/or members of the evaluation team. Collaborate with Programme and project teams on developing integrated development approaches.

• Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles are an integral part of programmes and operations and that these considerations are fully mainstreamed into programming and reflected in project design, monitoring, reporting, and evaluations in line with the UNDP Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion Strategies, UNSDG Operational Guide for Country Teams on LNOB, and available regional guidance.

• Develop the evaluation plan and ensure its timely implementation in line with CAFI standards for the CAFI funded programs/projects, Letters of Intent and the Trust Fund (such as independent evaluations, mid-term reviews, tranche releases).

• Ensure monitoring of data collection by projects, analyze and exploit data combining layers of maps, photo and satellite images, text and statistics.

• Facilitate the development and implementation of spatial monitoring through a dedicated structured geographic information system integrating data acquisition, administration, processing, analysis and dissemination, with support from specialized personnel.

• Support the implementation and growth of CAFI’s ecosystem of digital tools in support of efficiency and transparency, in synergy with colleagues from the programming and PES teams (specifically CAFI Connect and CAFI PES).

2.) Lead coordination of monitoring, reporting, evaluation and results-based management of CAFI programmes and projects.

• Oversee implementation and application of efficient and evidence-based results monitoring, and as applicable, quality assurance work for programme and project development and delivery using integrated portfolio management approach as well as the CAFI Connect tool and the CAFI PES dashboard

• Ensure timely identification of potential implementation problems and bottlenecks and advise the management and programme/project teams on strategies/corrective measures to address them.

• Lead the cross-cutting reviews, studies and evaluations of the M&E unit.

• Manage and coordinate third-party monitoring and/or any other data collection intervention.

• Review and approve all plans and Terms of Reference (TOR) for project and programme mid-term reviews, evaluations, and assessments. Participate in consultant and evaluation team recruitment and selection. Review and provide input on evaluation inception reports, evaluation methodology, and draft evaluation reports for quality assurance and compliance purposes.

• Ensure the optimal use of evaluation findings and recommendations. Provide guidance and input in the preparation of timely management responses and key actions to all evaluations; consolidate evaluation findings to assess effectiveness and impact of programmes/projects; and develop a communication/dissemination plan to incorporate into recommendations for improvement by projects and partners. Follow up on implementation of evaluation recommendations by project teams.

• Facilitate collation of monitoring and evaluation of impact results and/or data/information in a format that is relevant for evidence-based policy, communications and/or development interventions.

• Drive the application of CAFI’s social and environmental safeguards as applicable as part of the reporting exercises and the programme evaluation strategy.

• Lead the development of funded evaluation plans that accompany the development of programme documents and oversee the timely implementation of evaluations in the plan.

• Provide support, as applicable, in ensuring projects are designed, implemented, and completed in line with RBM and quality standards and programme and project management policies and procedures.

• Provide input into the independent verification of land use projects as per relevant EB decisions.

3.) Provide substantive contributions to capacity building and facilitate knowledge building and sharing on monitoring, evaluation, and results-based management

• Contribute to the assessment of capacity needs and elaboration of capacity development plans, tools, and methodologies. Design, organize and lead training activities; and participate in preparing knowledge packages on RBM, monitoring and evaluation, data collection/survey methods, gender mainstreaming and portfolio approach programme and project teams as well as national partners and key stakeholders.

• Lead the identification, synthesis, documentation, and dissemination of key lessons learned and good practices derived from monitoring and evaluation activities on what works, what does not work, and/or revised theories of change to identify innovative ideas for their scaling or replication.

• Provide sound contributions to local and global networks, communities of practice, and other knowledge management mechanisms. Proactively participate in regional and international fora on relevant thematic areas (including engaging in thematic discussions, contributing with analytical papers, etc.).

4.) Lead solid and efficient Reporting

• Ensure donor reports are timely prepared in line with established requirements. Prepare Results Reports, analysis of results of projects, and other periodic information and reports for the Executive Board, government partners, donor community and other key stakeholders. Advise on data use and interpretation to assess country programme results, improve programme quality, identify trends, and inform future decision-making processes.

• With direct support from CAFI’s Reporting Specialist, facilitate the reporting exercises across CAFI`s portfolio of funded projects, incorporation of lessons learned from previous exercises and semi-annual reporting to the Executive Board on the compliance of the reporting function. Provide regular update to the Executive Board on project and portfolio performance based on the information in the CAFI Connect and CAFI PES dashboard and narrative reports.

• Lead the organization and execution of accountability sessions with implementing partners to drive performance and reinforce a results culture

5.) Lead Implementation of Risk Management Framework across CAFI Portfolio

• Develop and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework for the Trust Fund, maintaining updated all related Policies and SOPs.

• Identify and assess risks across key categories, taking due diligence and reporting as per Risk Policies in place.

• Conduct risk assessments at portfolio, program, and country levels.

• Lead and guide funded projects in conducting risk due diligence.

• Maintain and regularly update a risk register.

• Design and implement risk mitigation strategies and internal controls.

• Advise program teams and implementing partners on risk reduction measures, compliance requirements and preventive controls such as procurement safeguards and financial oversight

• Ensure integration of risk management into program design and approval processes.

• Drive the development and oversee the implementation of contingency and risk response plans.

• Co-lead fiduciary risk oversight by working in collaboration with Management Specialist to monitor financial management reports from implementing organizations.

• Proactively track risk indicators and early warning signals to identify emerging threats; escalate critical risks to accordingly and propose corrective actions

• Contribute to the preparation of annual reports and portfolio reviews with a risk perspective.

• In collaboration with the Policy Dialogue Unit, conduct due diligence assessments of implementing partners in regard to their Institutional capacity, Governance systems and financial management capabilities

• Lead the risk due diligence for all prospective partners and new program designs to ensure risk is integrated into all approval processes

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervises M&E Specialist (IPSA) and MRV and Compliance Manager (IPSA)

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Business Management-Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment

Business Management & Monitoring & Evaluation:

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Development/Development Studies, Economics, Statistics, Business Management, Social Policy, or related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, programme and/or team management working with quality assurance instruments, results-based management models, and multiple stakeholders is required.

- Proven experience in the Monitoring & Evaluation of a large Fund is required.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

(1) Human Development

(2) Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

(3) Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

UNDP Indonesia is currently seeking a Team Leader - Nature and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) to guide its Nature, Environment, and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) pillar, a critical component of its overall country programme. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Team Leader serves as a strategic advisor to the Country Office Management, leading policy development, capacity building, and portfolio expansion in the NLCD pillar. The successful candidate is expected to grow the portfolio by strengthening partnerships, mobilizing financing from diverse and non-traditional partners, and position UNDP as a partner of choice in Indonesia. To do this, s/he will manage a team around 40 personnel, ensuring talent management, efficiencies, and impactful results.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Strategic Direction and Leadership of Nature, Environment, Climate and Low Carbon Development

- Set and continuously refine the strategic direction of the portfolio, translating global, regional and national priorities on nature, environment, climate and low-carbon development into clear programme priorities and areas of comparative advantage for UNDP;

- Position UNDP as a strategic partner and thought leader, identifying emerging policy and development trends and shaping UNDP’s value proposition and engagement with government and other key domestic and international stakeholders, in the public and private sector;

- Ensure coherence and strategic complementarity across the portfolio, connecting programmes and interventions across the NLCD unit, with other areas of UNDP such as Financing for Development, and Human Development and Responsive Governance, while identifying opportunities for scale, innovation and transformational impact;

- Steer the evolution of the programme pipeline, ensuring that new initiatives are strategically aligned, evidence-based, financially viable and capable of generating significant development results;

- Drive portfolio-level results and impact, using evidence, learning and performance information to adjust priorities, manage risks and ensure that the portfolio contributes to systemic and lasting change.

2. Strengthening Partnerships and Lead Financing Opportunities for Scale

- Proactively identify and cultivate strategic partnerships with government, development partners, international financial institutions, private sector, foundations, civil society and other actors aligned with UNDP’s strategic priorities;

- Anticipate and identify financing opportunities, including but not limited to, climate and environmental finance, blended finance and innovative financing mechanisms, and translate these into viable opportunities for the portfolio;

- Develop and articulate compelling propositions for partners and funders, demonstrating UNDP’s comparative advantage, the potential for scale and the development, climate, and economic impact of proposed interventions;

- Build and manage a diversified partnership and financing pipeline, balancing short-, medium- and longer-term opportunities and reducing reliance on individual funding sources;

- Broker strategic relationships and mobilize resources at scale, bringing together partners, expertise and financing around priority national challenges and opportunities.

3. Ensure Effective Team Management for Results and Oversees Accountability, Quality Control and Effective Oversight

- Provide clear direction, priorities and accountability to the team, ensuring that staff/personnel understand how their work contributes to UNDP Indonesia’s strategic objectives and portfolio results;

- Build and sustain a high-performing, diverse and collaborative team, fostering a culture of trust, inclusion, innovation, learning and shared ownership of results;

- Deploy people and expertise strategically, ensuring the Unit has the right capabilities, structures and ways of working to respond to evolving programme priorities and opportunities;

- Enable high-quality and timely delivery, proactively address bottlenecks, performance issues and risks while empowering team members to take ownership and make decisions within their responsibilities;

- Develop people and institutional capability, providing coaching, mentoring and opportunities for professional growth while strengthening knowledge management, collaboration and succession within the Unit;

- Provides strategic planning and oversight of the assigned portfolio of programmes/projects and ensures their compliance with programme and operations policies and procedures (POPP) and quality assurance standards.

4. Lead Policy Influence and Strategic Impact and Facilitate Knowledge Management

- Influence national policy, institutional priorities and investment decisions by bringing UNDP’s evidence, expertise and convening power to key policy and development processes related to nature and low carbon development. Identify and champion innovative approaches and solutions, anticipating emerging challenges and opportunities and testing new models, technologies, financing approaches and partnerships that can deliver greater impact;

- Leverage UNDP’s convening and thought leadership role to connect government, development partners, private sector, civil society and other stakeholders around complex, cross-cutting development challenges;

- Capture, demonstrate and communicate results and learning, using evidence and lessons from the portfolio to inform policy, influence investments and strengthen UNDP’s positioning and future programme development;

- Drive scale and systemic change, ensuring that successful interventions move beyond individual projects to influence institutions, markets, policies and broader development trajectories;

- Lead annual portfolio planning and develop integrated work, monitoring, human resources and procurement plans with Country Office units and project manager, ensures compliance with cost-recovery policies in coordination with operations and finance;

- Facilitates knowledge building and management especially between the programme and projects and facilitates training for the UNDP staff and personnel and national counterparts on relevant programme issues.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial responsibilities: Supervise the team including Technical Analyst, Programme Managers, Project Managers

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Ability to give sense of purpose and build trust, develop programmes of activities and platforms to build and strengthen relationships.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System thinking; Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

- Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Track record in managing complex programmes or portfolios within multilateral or bilateral development organizations, government institutions, NGOs or related organizations is required;

Background:

Suriname's mangrove ecosystems are among the country's most valuable natural assets. Covering nearly 86,000 hectares and accounting for approximately 0.6% of the world's mangrove area (SBB, 2023; FAO, 2023), they provide critical habitat for biodiversity, support fisheries, strengthen climate resilience, and sustain coastal livelihoods and community well-being in areas where nearly 90% of the country's population resides (ABS, 2024). They also provide a foundation for sustainable economic opportunities through tourism, research, education, and other nature-based sectors.

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994 and continues to support Suriname through its three broad programmatic areas: Democratic Governance, Social Development, Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resource Management. The three programmatic areas are interlinked, integrating nature-based solutions, justice and social services with the engagement of stakeholders that are relevant to all three programmatic areas.

UNDP in partnership with the European Union has been supporting Suriname in preservation and conservation of mangrove forests, especially through the two phases of the Global Climate Change Alliance (GCCA+) programmes; phase one: from March 2016 to August 2019 and phase 2: 2020- 2023. In 2024, UNDP and EU launched a new initiative Protection, Restoration, and Sustainable Use of Mangrove Forest (PRSUMF) project (2024 to 2027).

The PRSUMF project builds on the results achieved in strengthening mangrove protection and conservation by the GCCA+ programme. The PRSUMF project aims to support Suriname in building the resilience of target coastal communities through inclusive, gender-responsive coastal zone management, mangroves conservation, and sustainable use.

SBB. 2023. Mangrove Monitoring System: Total Mangrove Forest Area per District in Suriname (2023).

FAO. 2023. The World's Mangroves 2000-2020.

ABS. 2024. Population and Housing Census (Census 9), population distribution by district.

The project aims to achieve this objective:

a) By strengthening coordination, legal and strategic frameworks, for integrated coastal zone management, water management, coastal defense, and governance.

b) By enhancing the meaningful participation of local communities in the co-management of mangroves and Multiple Use Management Areas (MUMAs) and

c) By increasing sustainable income generation with a focus on women and youth, from mangrove-based value chains such as honey, fisheries, and mangrove ecosystem based-tourism.

Through the above approach, the project aims to support mitigation of rising sea levels impact, frequent flooding, and support the country’s population to adapt to climate change by playing a central role in mangrove protection, restoration and sustainable use through nature positive economic activities.

The project is implemented through a Project Management Unit (PMU) headed by the Project Manager. The Communications Associate will be part of the project management unit.

Scope of Work:

The incumbent will contribute to stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, visibility, and public awareness efforts that support achievement of project outputs and donor communication requirements. S/He will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, and the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Suriname. The Communications Associate will also work in close collaboration with the Technical Officer of the PRSUMF project.

The Communication Associate will design and implement specific targeted public relations (PR) and media activities highlighting project activities, results and accomplishments, including related products and articles for social media distribution.

Key functions and responsibilities of the Communication Associate include:

a. Implement and revise the Media/Communication and Visibility Plan as needed:

- Monitor implementation of and periodically update the Project Communication and Visibility Plan based on emerging communication needs, project progress, and donor requirements.

- Based on the Communication and Visibility and Communications Plan, develop a Media/Communication Action Plan and relevant budget in close collaboration with the Project Manager and supporting PMU members.

- Develop graphic designs for third party production (audiovisual and or print) in support of project branding communication and visibility, in line with UNDP and EU communication guidelines and requirements.

- Maintain and expand the network of project stakeholders and media and maintain regular contact with and provide information to media on project activities and project progress.

- Ensure and monitor visibility through the proper and correct use of logo’s during events, in photo-, audio-, and video productions and on all publication materials, equipment, materials and goods financed by the project as agreed with donors.

- Ensure that the project related information and communication materials are regularly updated on UNDP Suriname website, Facebook page, X and other social media platforms.

- Support the PRSUMF PMU in the organization and implementation of all project events and facilitate media coverage thereof.

- Advise and assist Project Manager and other project staff on aspects related to awareness and stakeholder engagement; dialogues and other stakeholder awareness activities.

b. Lead knowledge management and dissemination:

- Plan and prepare publication of articles, human interest stories, quarterly newsletters, and project results, this includes the gathering of supporting visual, audiovisual material and basic editing for publication.

- Liaise with specific sector specialists and technical resource persons for the development of folders, brochures and presentations and other communication material on climate change, mangrove conservation, sustainable use of mangroves for economic development.

- Develop and maintain a repository of communication, visibility, and knowledge products, ensuring accessibility and institutional memory for the project.

c. Support awareness and training activities of the project:

- In collaboration with project team, Support the design of behaviour-change and awareness campaigns tailored to local communities, women, youth, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholder groups.

- Assist with developing training material in general and specifically for policy makers; coastal communities, entrepreneurs and media professionals.

- Enable the production of video records of project activities and results achieved, as well as provide support for script writing; editing and formatting allowing for multiple media applications of the raw footage that will be captured.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Communications Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager of the PRSUMF project and under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office and collaborate closely with the PRSUMF project team and all other CO units.

Learn Continuously LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 1: Appreciates/respects differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond stakeholder/ partner’s immediate requests.
